Account & Setup: Account Management

Account suspension | Frequently Asked Questions

HubSpot uses automated systems to make sure that all users are following HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Policy and Terms of Service. This process is important in protecting our customers’ experience with our platform.

If suspicious activity is detected at sign-up or when using the platform, access to certain features will be temporarily suspended. When this occurs at sign-up, HubSpot may ask you for more information about your account. A member of HubSpot’s team will review the details of the suspension, the information you provide, and your account to make a final decision.

What tools can get suspended?

Tools used to collect or host information can be suspended at any time if suspicious activity is detected. This includes marketing email, files, landing pages, forms, and the calling tool.

What can I do if my account gets suspended?

If your access to any tools gets suspended, you’ll see a banner alert message in your account for the impacted tool with details about the suspension. If the suspension can be appealed, you will be prompted to complete an identity verification in Persona, HubSpot’s identity verification partner. Learn more about Persona.

What if my identity verification fails?

HubSpot uses Persona to confirm that the name in your HubSpot profile matches the name on your identification. It’s recommended to use an ID that displays your name in the language and alphabet that matches your HubSpot profile. If your verification fails, learn how to troubleshoot the ID verification process. If you need additional support, reach out to HubSpot Support.

I have more questions about Persona. Who can I contact?

If you have other questions about Persona, visit the Persona help center.

How can I learn more about best practices with my HubSpot tools?

If you want to learn more about how to follow best practices with your HubSpot tools, connect with experts on the Community or check out learning resources on the Academy.

Add and edit account currencies

You can update your HubSpot account to use your company’s primary currency. If you do business in multiple currencies, you can add currencies to your account and set an exchange rate compared to your primary company currency to more accurately track the amount of your deals.

The options available for managing currencies depend on your HubSpot subscription:

  • You can edit the account’s company currency in all accounts.
  • Accounts with a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription can use multiple currencies, but have different limits to the number of currencies allowed. Learn about the limitations in the HubSpot Product & Services Catalog.

Learn more about building custom currency solutions using the Settings API.

View existing currencies

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit account defaults permissions are required to edit the account’s default currency or view added currencies.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • Click the Currency tab.
  • At the top, you’ll see your Company Currency. This is the default currency when creating new deals, and is used by the Amount in company currency property for deal amount totals and reports that use that field.
  • If you’ve added multiple currencies, you’ll see a table with currencies you’ve added and their exchange rates.
  • To view historical exchange rates, hover over the currency and click Actions > View currency history. If you want exchange rates to update automatically, you can turn on automatic updates to currency exchange rates.

Change the account default currency

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • Click the Currency tab.
  • Hover over the currency and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Edit company currency to update your account’s default currency.
  • In the dialog box, click the Company currency dropdown menu and select a currency.
  • Click Continue.
  • Confirm the information, then click Save.

Please note: if you’ve updated the company currency, it’s recommended to update the following values if applicable:

  • For accounts with free tools, the Amount property on deals does not automatically convert when you change the company currency, so you’ll need to update the value on existing deals to the correct amount in the new currency.
  • For Starter, Professional, and Enterprise accounts with multiple currencies, if you’ve updated the company currency to a currency previously used on deals, update the Exchange rate value to 1 on affected closed deals.

Configure new currencies

Subscription required A Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to configure new currencies.

Permissions required Super Admin or Modify billing and change name on contract permissions are required to add currencies or edit exchange rates.

To add a currency:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • Click the Currencies tab, then click Add currency.
  • Click the Currency dropdown menu and select your new currency.
  • In the Exchange rate field, enter the exchange rate that converts your new currency to your company currency.
  • Click Save.

To edit an exchange rate:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • Click the Currencies tab.
  • Hover over a currency and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Edit company currency. In the dialog box, enter an exchange rate, then click Save. If you want exchange rates to update automatically, you can turn on automatic updates to currency exchange rates.

To remove a currency:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • Click the Currencies tab.
  • Hover over the currency and click Archive. In the dialog box, click Archive currency to confirm. Once a currency is archived, it’ll no longer be an option on new deals, but it’ll still be used on existing deals. For these existing deals, you can manually update the Currency property.

Use multiple currencies with deals

Subscription required A Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use multiple currencies with deals.

Once you’ve set up multiple currencies, you can:

  • Change the currency shown in a deal’s Amount property by editing the Currency property on the deal record. Learn more about how the Currency property impacts deal amount properties and deal exchange rates.

  • Create custom properties

  • that refer to each deal’s currency rather than the company currency.

  • Set user specific preferred currencies for viewing deal amounts in the board view.

Use the Currency property on deals

Set the currency of deals using the Currency property on your deal records. The Amount will then appear in the selected currency. Based on the exchange rate you’ve set for the currency, the value will then be converted to your company currency in the Amount in company currency property (Amount x Exchange rate for the deal’s currency). If the Amount field is blank, the Amount in company currency field will also be blank. This property can’t be manually edited and is calculated as follows:

  • If a deal is in an open pipeline stage, the Amount in company currency property uses the latest exchange rate you’ve set for the currency until the deal is closed.
  • If a deal is in a closed lost or won pipeline stage and contains a Close date, the Amount in company currency property will use the exchange rate that was in effect at the specified Close date.
    • If no exchange rate was in effect at the time, then the property will use the exchange rate in effect at the time nearest to the Close date.
    • If the Close date is in the future, the Amount in company currency property will update to reflect new exchange rates as the Close date approaches.
  • If a deal is in a closed lost or won pipeline stage but doesn’t contain a Close date, the Amount in company currency property will use the effective exchange rate at the time the deal was marked closed.
    • If no exchange rate was in effect at the time, the property will use the exchange rate in effect at the time nearest to when the deal was marked closed.
Use the Exchange rate property on deals

For deals using a currency other than the company currency, the Exchange rate property is calculated as follows:

  • For open deals (e.g., deals in an open pipeline stage), HubSpot automatically updates the Exchange rate value based on the most recent exchange rate you’ve set for the currency, and the property cannot be manually edited.
  • For closed deals (e.g., deals in a closed pipeline stage), the Exchange rate value will not be automatically updated based on your set exchange rate, historical exchange rates, currency code changes, or updates to the company currency. Instead, a closed deal’s Exchange rate will be set based on the exchange rate in effect at the time of closing. Moving forward, Super Admins or users with the multi-currency-write scope can manually update the Exchange rate value on individual deals or for multiple deals in bulk. The value can also be updated via workflows, integrations, or API calls that do not check for a user ID.
  • Learn how to edit the Exchange rate property on an individual record.
Create custom currency properties

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use calculated currency properties.

If your account has deals in different currencies, you can create custom currency properties that refer to each specific deal’s currency, rather than the company currency. For example, you may want to create a custom Commission amount property to track the commission for a deal directly in the deal’s currency.

Please note: when you set up a property that uses the deal currency, the property’s values do not automatically update based on exchange rates. If you update a deal’s currency, you’ll need to manually update the custom currency property value to the correct amount. Because the properties don’t account for exchange rates, it’s not recommended to use custom currency properties in reports.

To create a property that uses a deal’s currency:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Properties.
  • Click the Select an object dropdown menu, then select Deal properties.
  • In the upper right, click Create property.
  • Set the property’s basic details, then click the Field type tab. You can create either a number property or a calculation property:
    • Number property:
      • Click the Field type dropdown menu, then select Number.
      • Click the Number format dropdown menu, then select Currency.
      • Select the Use record currency instead of company currency checkbox.
    • Calculation property:
      • Click the Field type dropdown menu, select Calculation.
      • Click the Calculated property type dropdown menu, then select one of the following: Custom equation, Min, Max, Count, Sum, Average, Round down only, Round up only, or Round to nearest.
      • Click the Number format dropdown menu, then select Currency.
      • Select the Use record currency instead of company currency checkbox.
  • Once you’re done, click Create.

Please note: using a record currency only impacts how the value is displayed, and it will not automatically apply an exchange rate. If you’re building a custom equation with the formula editor, you can include the exchange_rate or dated_exchange_rate functions in your equation to apply an exchange rate. For example, [properties.amount] * exchange_rate('CAD').

Your custom property will update its currency based on the value set for Currency on each deal. If the property already has a value for a deal and you change that deal’s currency, the currency symbol will change, but the value will not be updated. You can manually update the property’s value to your desired amount.

Set a preferred currency for deal stage amounts and forecasts

When viewing deals in board view, by default, the deal stage amounts shown at the bottom of the board are displayed in the company currency. When using the forecast tool, amounts are displayed in your preferred currency. If your account has multiple currencies, each user can select a currency to view these amounts in their preferred currency instead.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Under Your Preferences, click General.
  • Click the Preffered currency dropdown and select a currency, then click Save. The amounts will now be displayed in the selected currency.
  • To view deal amounts in company currency instead, in the board view, hover over the Total and Weighted amounts and view the company currency in the pop-up box.
Edit a line item’s currency

Subscription required A Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to edit a line item’s currency.

Seats required An assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat is required to edit a line item’s currency.

If you’re associating products with your deals, you will need to edit the line item’s currency to match the deal’s.

  • On the deal record, locate the Line items card. There will be a “Missing currency” alert next to any line item that needs to be updated. Click Edit.
  • In the Your line items are missing a [currency] price. alert, click Update pricing.
  • In the Update line item price panel, select an updated currency option.
  • Click Confirm.
  • Click Save, then navigate back to the deal record. The line item currency should now match the deal’s currency.

Add and manage email signatures in the CRM

Use an email signature to automatically include your contact information in every email you send from the CRM, helping maintain consistent and professional communication. Users in a Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise account with an assigned Sales Seat, can create multiple signatures and assign different defaults for each connected email account.

If you send emails from a team email address, learn how to edit your team email signature in the conversations inbox.

Add an email signature

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General.

  • Click the Email tab.

  • In the Configure section, click Manage email signatures.

  • Enter your signature in the text box. In the Simple editor, use the icons to format the text, insert a link, or insert an image. Or, click HTML and edit the HTML of your signature.

  • Click Save.

Please note:

  • Email clients handle custom HTML differently. When adding more styling, there is increased risk of it not rendering when you compose an email. Learn more about HubSpot’s best practices for creating an HTML email.
  • If you want to customize the font of your signature, you can use the face attribute in a font tag in the HTML editor but be aware that many fonts are not supported across email clients.

Manage multiple email signatures

Permissions required A Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to manage multiple email signatures.

Seats required An assigned Sales Seat is required to manage multiple email signatures

Create and manage multiple email signatures, and assign different default signatures to each of your connected email accounts.

Add a new email signature
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General.
  • Click the Email tab.
  • In the Configure section, click Manage email signatures.
  • Click the Choose signature to edit dropdown menu and select Add new signature:
    • In the Signature name field, enter a name for your signature.
    • In the Signature text box, enter your signature. In the Simple editor, use the icons to format the text, insert a link, or insert an image. Or, click HTML and edit the HTML of your signature.
    • Click Save.
  • To set the signature as the global default, select the Use as my global default signature checkbox. The global default is used when no other signature is specified, and when using the Signature personalization token.
Edit default signatures for connected email accounts
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General.
  • Click the Email tab.
  • Hover over the connected email account and click Actions, then select Edit default signature.
  • In the dialog box, use the dropdown menu and select a signature. Then, click Set as default.

Assign and manage seats

In HubSpot, seats determine which tools a user can access based on your subscription, while permissions define the specific actions they can take, such as viewing, editing, or deleting data.

Every user on a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is assigned a seat type, ranging from View-Only to specialized Sales, Service, or Revenue seats. Choosing the right seat ensures your team has the necessary tools for their role while helping you manage your subscription costs effectively.

There are different seat types available based on your subscription that provide users with specific levels of access to tools and features in your account. Every user in a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is assigned a seat, and the type of seat determines what they can view, access, and do within your subscription services.

From View-Only Seats that allow users to view data without making changes, to Core and Sales, Service, or Revenue Seats that allow access to specific features. Assigning the correct seat ensures your team members have the right level of access for their role. Adding seats to your account and removing unused seats can affect your subscription billing.

Learn more about this feature by joining a small group coaching session

The seats-based pricing model only applies to new accounts and subscriptions created after March 5, 2024. Accounts created prior to March 5, 2024, that haven’t migrated to the new pricing model will only have access to purchased Sales or Service paid seats for Legacy Sales Hub and Service Hub Starter, Professional, and Enterprise accounts.

Permissions required

  • Super Admin or Modify billing permissions are required to assign, change seats, or transfer a Core Seat.
  • Super Admin or Modify billing permissions are required to add or remove seats.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, review the following:

  • Seats must be unassigned before they can be removed.
  • Seats can’t be reduced below your subscription’s minimum commitment. For example, if your subscription includes five seats, you can’t reduce to four seats.
  • Removing seats doesn’t change your current invoice. Learn more about how seat changes affect billing.
  • Before removing a user, reassign any records, assets, or responsibilities they own as needed. Removing or deleting a user removes their access to the account.

Seat types

Different types of seats are available based on which subscription services you purchase, and each seat type provides differing access to users.

Every user in a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription will have a seat. The following are descriptions of each seat type:

  • View-Only Seat: allows users to view your subscription services. These seats are free and unlimited for Starter, Professional, and Enterprise subscriptions. Users with a View-only Seat can:

    • View records, dashboards, customer data, and reports, and can filter reports.
    • Log notes on CRM records they can view.
    • Be granted billing admin permissions by a Super Admin.

Please note:

  • Users with a View-Only Seat can’t save reports, edit records, change settings, manage tools, create or edit content or be assigned Super Admin access. They also can’t create or edit activities, except for notes on CRM records they can view.

  • Users with a View-Only Seat can’t add information to HubSpot, including logging or tracking emails, forwarding or BCC addresses, or other email logging methods, or creating contacts from those emails.

  • If a user is changed from a Core, Sales, or Service Seat to a View-Only Seat, email logging is turned off. To restore email logging and the ability to create contacts from emails, assign at least a Core, Sales, or Service Seat and ensure Personal email access is turned on for the user.

  • Core Seat: provides access to core features and tools in the subscription services you’ve purchased.

    • For Sales Hub Starter and Service Hub Starter, users with an assigned Core Seat will have access to Sales Hub and Service Hub features respectively. Sales Hub and Service Hub seats will only apply to Professional or Enterprise subscriptions.
    • For Revenue Hub Professional and Enterprise, users with an assigned Core Seat will have access to view quotes, not create or edit them.
    • Learn more in HubSpot’s Products & Services catalog.

  • Sales Seat (Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise): provides access to all features included with Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise.

  • Service Seat (Service Hub Professional or Enterprise): provides access to all features included with Service Hub Professional or Enterprise.

  • Revenue Seat (Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise): provides access to all features included with Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise.

  • Partner Seat: a free seat that gives eligible HubSpot Solutions Partners employees access to all features in a client’s account.

  • Developer Seat: a free seat that provides access only to the developer platform.

Please note: Developer Seats can’t be combined with another seat or Super Admin permissions. If you would like to give a user with a seat access to the developer platform, a Super Admin can give the user the Developer tools access permission.

To understand the full scope of what each seat includes, learn more in HubSpot’s Products & Services catalog.

Seat billing

Your subscription includes a set number of seats, and you can purchase additional ones at any time at your subscription tier’s current rate. Once seats are purchased, the total count can’t be reduced until your next renewal date. Removing unassigned seats schedules the change for your next billing period, and your current invoice won’t be adjusted.

If you’re upgrading from HubSpot free tools to a Starter subscription, free seats are removed once you upgrade. You should select the total number of seats your team needs during the checkout process. Learn how to upgrade your HubSpot subscription.

To understand which type of seats your users need, learn more about seat types. If you need guidance about which and how many seats your users need, reach out to your Customer Success Team or Manager.

Add seats

To purchase additional seats:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • At the top, click the Seats tab. Review seat assignments, invite statuses, and last active dates for your users in your account.eview seat assignments, invite statuses, and last active dates for your users in the account.
  • To add additional seats, in the center, below the seat type you’d like to add seats for, click Add seats.
  • On the Seats purchasing page, click the up arrows to increase the number of seats, then click Continue.
  • Review the added seats at checkout and click Save & continue.
  • Click Complete purchase to confirm.

Remove unassigned seats

Remove unused seats from your subscription after they are unassigned. Seat removals are scheduled for your next billing period. Learn more about how seat changes affect billing. For further information, contact HubSpot’s Sales team or the Contract Management team.

Please note: if removing users with an assigned seat, you must first remove any Sales Hub or Service Hub access they have to sales tools or service tools in user permissions.

To remove unassigned seats:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • At the top, click the Seats tab. Review seat assignments, invite statuses, and last active dates for your users in your account.
  • To review specific users, use the search bar and filters at the top of the table.
  • In the center, below the seat type you’d like to remove seats for, click Remove unassigned seats.
  • In the dialog box, select the unassigned seats dropdown menu and select the number of seats you want to remove.
    • The Current Subscription box shows the number you currently have.
    • The Auto-Renewal box reflects the billing adjustment that’ll be effective at the start of your next subscription term.
  • Click Remove [#] seats.
  • In the dialog box, review the change in seats. Click Return to Account & Billing to close the dialog box.
  • After scheduling the removal of seats, view the confirmation banner. To cancel the seat removal, click Cancel this removal. Then, click Cancel this removal.

Please note: reassigning a seat that is scheduled to be removed before its downgrade’s effective date cancels the downgrade.

Swap unassigned seats for HubSpot Credits or a different seat type

Permissions required Super Admin access is required to swap seats for credits or other seat types.

If your account has unassigned seats, you can redirect that spend toward HubSpot Credits or a different seat type without contacting your account team.

For example, if your account has three unassigned Sales Seats, you can convert them to HubSpot Credits to use on features and agents in your account.

Understand seat swapping for HubSpot Credits or Seats
  • When you swap unassigned seats, the value of those seats is applied toward HubSpot Credits or a different seat type included in your subscription. For example, if you swap a Core Professional Seat valued at $45.00/month, that $45.00 becomes your available budget to put toward HubSpot Credits or a different seat type.
  • If the seats you’re adding cost more than the seats you’re swapping, you’ll be charged the difference at checkout. For example, if you swap one Core Professional Seat valued at $45.00/month, for two Sales Seats, valued at $90.00/month each, your bill increases by $135.00/month, the cost of the new seats minus the value of the swapped seat.
  • If you swap seats entirely for HubSpot Credits, the full value of your swapped seats converts to credits.
  • You can also split the value between a new seat type and HubSpot Credits. For example, if you swap one Core Professional Seat and one Sales Professional Seat for a total value of $135.00, you can apply $90.00 toward a different Seat type (e.g., a Service Seat, if available in your subscription) and convert the remaining balance to 5,000 HubSpot Credits.
  • If your new selections don’t use up the full value of your swapped seats, the remaining balance converts to HubSpot Credits, rounded up to the nearest credit pack.

Please note: before swapping seats for HubSpot Credits, confirm you no longer need those seats. HubSpot Credits cannot be swapped back for seats.

Swap seats for HubSpot Credits or a different seat type
  • Navigate to one of the following:
    • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right corner, then click Account & Billing. On the Overview tab, in the Swap unassigned seats for different seat types or HubSpot Credits section, click Swap seats & Credits.
    • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right corner, then click Account & Billing. On the Subscriptions tab, in the Subscription Summary section, click Swap seats & Credits.
    • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. Click Users & Teams. On the Seats tab, click Swap unassigned seats.
  • In the dialog box, review the available seats for swapping.
  • Next to the seats you want to swap, use the arrows or enter a number in the number field to set the quantity.
  • At the bottom right, click Choose what to get in return.
  • To swap your seats for HubSpot Credits, use the arrows or enter a number in the number field to set the amount of credits you want to receive.
  • To swap your seats for a different seat type, next to the seat type you want, use the arrows or enter a number in the number field to set the quantity.
  • At the bottom right, click Continue.
  • In the Review your changes section, review the breakdown of seats you’re removing and adding.
  • At the bottom right, click Continue to checkout.
  • Review your company details, payment details and new products terms and conditions. Then, click Complete Purchase at the bottom.

After completing checkout, your new seats and HubSpot Credits are immediately available in your account.

Assign, unassign, and change seats

Assigning a seat to a user changes their seat type, but changing a user’s seat doesn’t automatically change their permissions. For example, if a user’s seat is changed from a Sales Seat to Core Seat, the user Sales Hub access will be altered, so they won’t be able to access some features even if related permissions are turned on. Removing a seat from a user unassigns the seat, but you’ll continue to be billed for it. Remove the unassigned seat to adjust billing.

To assign Core, Sales, Service, or Revenue seats, you must have a paid HubSpot subscription, and be on the seats-based pricing model.

Please note: if changing a user’s seat from a Core, Sales, Service, or Revenue Seat, to a View-Only Seat, their account must be active. If the user’s account is deactivated, you can reactivate the user to unassign their paid seat, then deactivate the user again.

To assign, unassign, or change a seat:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the Users table, hover over the user and click Actions, then select Change seat.
  • In the right panel, click the Seats dropdown menu and select the seat type. The seat types available will depend on your subscription (e.g., Core and View-Only for Starter subscriptions, Sales or Service for Professional and Enterprise subscriptions).
  • To remove a seat for a user, click x next to the seat.
  • At the bottom, click Save.

You can also assign seats by navigating to the Users & Teams settings, clicking the Seats tab, hovering over a user, and clicking Change seat.

Transfer a Core Seat

To transfer a Core Seat to another user, if you only have one in your account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • At the top, click the Seats tab.
  • In the user table, hover over the user, and click Transfer seat.
  • In the dialog box, click the Choose a user dropdown menu, and select the user to transfer the seat to. Click Transfer seat. Then, click Transfer seat.

When a Super Admin, transfers their seat, Super Admin permissions will be transferred.

Change your HubSpot user’s email address

Change the email address associated with your HubSpot user account. This is useful if you get a new email address or if you want to switch to a different one for receiving HubSpot notifications.

Before you get started

  • You must be logged in to your HubSpot account to change your email address.
  • You’ll need your current HubSpot password to complete the change.
  • If you only log in with Google and your account isn’t managed through SSO or SCIM, you need to reset your password before changing your email address.
  • You can use the same email address for multiple HubSpot accounts.
  • A single email address can only be used as the login for one HubSpot user. You can’t change your email address to one that’s already in use by another HubSpot user, even if that user doesn’t have access to your account or is deactivated. The existing user must be permanently deleted first.
  • If you have SCIM turned on, you can’t change your user email address or add an email address in HubSpot, and must do it through your identity provider.
  • If SSO is turned on for your account, a Super Admin must temporarily exclude you from SSO requirement so you can update your email.
  • Only you can change your own login email from your user settings. Super Admins and HubSpot Support can’t directly change a user’s login email.

Change your email address

To change your email address:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right corner, then click Profile & Preferences.
  • At the top, click the Security tab.
  • In the Email section, click Edit email address.
  • In the dialog box, enter your new email address, and your HubSpot account password. You may be asked to verify with two-factor authentication or passkeys if they’re set up.
  • Click Save. Your email address will now be pending validation.
  • You’ll receive an email in your new email address’ inbox. In the email, click Confirm your email address to validate your new email address.
  • If you click Confirm your email address and are asked to log in to HubSpot again, enter your original login credentials to access your account.

Contact HubSpot about an account

Contact different HubSpot teams depending on what you need help with, such as using HubSpot tools, managing your account, or discussing billing or purchasing options. The support options available to you may vary based on your subscription.

Contact HubSpot Support

Contact HubSpot Support for help completing specific actions in HubSpot or troubleshooting issues with HubSpot tools.

For example, contact HubSpot Support to get help with:

  • Importing data.
  • Building or troubleshooting workflows.
  • Resolving errors or unexpected behavior in HubSpot.

If you’re looking for step-by-step instructions, search the Knowledge Base.

Learn more about the support options available based on your subscription.

Contact HubSpot Customer Success

For guidance on using HubSpot to meet your business goals or for questions about your account, contact your Customer Success Manager.

For example, contact Customer Success for help with:

  • Planning how to use HubSpot tools to support your strategy.
  • Upgrading your subscription or migrating data.
  • Answering account-related legal questions.

If you don’t have an assigned Customer Success Manager, contact HubSpot Support.

Contact HubSpot Contract Management

To discuss an upcoming renewal or contract change, contact the Contract Management Team.

If you have an assigned Contract Manager, contact them directly. If you don’t have one assigned, contact HubSpot Support.

Contact HubSpot Billing

For questions related to invoices, payments, or billing detail updates, contact the HubSpot Billing Team at billing@hubspot.com.

If you’re unsure if your inquiry should be sent to the billing team, contact HubSpot Support.

Contact HubSpot Sales

Contact the HubSpot Sales Team if you’re evaluating a HubSpot purchase or have questions about pricing, subscriptions, or available features.

If you’re already working with a HubSpot sales representative, contact them directly.

If you’re using a HubSpot trial, the trial expires after 14 days. Contact the HubSpot Sales Team or your sales representative to discuss a trial extension or reactivation. Trial extensions or reactivations aren’t guaranteed.

Copy assets to another HubSpot account with multi-account management

Asset copying, a feature of multi-account management, allows you to copy automated marketing emails, forms, segments, and workflows to other HubSpot accounts in your multi-account management organization.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required in the account that you’re copying assets from, and in the destination account that’ll receive the asset.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements
  • You must have set up and configured a multi-account management organization.
    • To access multi-account management, the main HubSpot account where you create the organization must have an Enterprise subscription. Each connected account must be a separate HubSpot account with a Professional or Enterprise subscription. Free accounts must be upgraded before connecting.
  • Once your multi-account management organization is set up, assets can be copied between accounts that have a Professional or Enterprise subscription for any product (e.g., Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, etc).
Understand limitations & considerations
  • When copying a marketing email, only automated marketing emails and their content will be copied. Non-automated marketing emails won’t be copied. Be sure to review the copied email in the destination account, as certain settings (such as a custom subscription type) will need to be set manually in the destination account.
  • When copying forms, form names and fields, but not the data collected through them, will be copied.
  • When copying segments, only the segment definition will be copied, not the CRM records that are part of the segment in the source account.
  • Multi-account management can’t be set up in sandbox accounts or trial accounts.
Copy assets

To set up asset copying:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Under Organization Management, click Multi-Account.
  • Click the Asset Copying tab.
  • Click Start copying.
  • Select the account you’d like to copy assets to. If you can’t see the account you’d like to copy to, make sure it is configured for asset copying in your organization.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the assets you’d like to copy, then click Next.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the assets you’d like to copy to the destination account.
    • If an asset uses a custom property that doesn’t exist in the destination account, there’ll be a column showing the number of custom properties that’ll be created in the destination account as part of the asset copying process. Click the number to see more information on the specific custom properties.
  • Click Next.
  • Review the assets you’re copying, then click Start copy.
  • The progress of the copy, along with previously completed asset copies will display in the Copy history table.
Copy assets from an index page

As well as being able to copy assets from multi-account management settings, you can also copy them from an index page.

To copy assets from an index page:

  • Navigate to one of the following:
    • In your HubSpot account, navigate to CRM > Segments.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the table, click the checkboxes next to the assets you’d like to copy, then click Copy to another account.
  • Choose the destination account, then click Next.
  • Review the assets you’re copying, then click Confirm.

Create a sandbox and deploy changes to production

Sandboxes give you a copy of your production account’s features and functionality, and copy supported assets during creation. Sandboxes are useful when you want to safely test changes without affecting your live account or end users. Once you’ve tested your changes in your sandbox account, you can deploy supported assets from your sandbox to your HubSpot production account.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to create a sandbox and deploy changes to production.

Please note: as of April 30, 2026, legacy standard sandboxes are no longer supported. To ease the transition, sandbox limits have been temporarily increased for accounts that still have a legacy sandbox, allowing you to create a new sandbox while your legacy sandbox remains available until you’re ready to delete it.

Before you get started

Understand requirements

You must create a new standard sandbox to use the deploy to production feature.

Deploy to production isn’t supported in legacy sandbox.

Limitations & considerations
  • Learn which users are copied to a sandbox account during creation and how user changes affect production and sandbox accounts.
  • Learn which production assets are copied to a sandbox account during sandbox creation.
  • Learn which object configurations and assets are supported in the deploy to production feature.
  • Contact, company, deal, ticket, and custom object IDs will have different IDs between sandbox and production accounts. You can consider creating a new custom property (e.g. External record ID) and use automations to copy production record IDs into this field, which you can then use in your sandbox if needed for testing purposes.
  • You can only enroll 100,000 records per day in all workflows for the entire sandbox account. Any additional workflow enrollments past the maximum will be dropped. You’ll be notified in your account when the cap has been reached, and the time you’ll be able to sync again.
  • If a certain asset type doesn’t copy to a standard sandbox account at creation, assets that are dependent on that asset type will also not sync. For example, since surveys aren’t eligible to copy to standard sandbox accounts, all workflows that use surveys as triggers or actions won’t be copied.
  • Integrations in your production account won’t be connected automatically to the standard sandbox account. For any existing integrations you want to connect to a sandbox account, HubSpot recommends connecting to the sandbox version of that integration to prevent disruptions to your CRM data.
  • You can send one-to-one test emails and marketing emails from a standard sandbox account to contact records that share the same email address as existing sandbox users.
    • If you send emails to contacts that are not sandbox users, the emails will not send because they are not users in the standard sandbox account.
    • Emails sent from a standard sandbox account will be routed over shared IP addresses that the production account uses.
  • Notetaker isn’t supported in sandbox accounts. Learn more about using Notetaker in your production account.

Understand user management in sandbox accounts

Sandbox users are managed independently from users in the production account. When you create a sandbox account, HubSpot copies users with specific permissions from the production account. After creation, some user status and permission changes in the production account are automatically reflected in the sandbox, while changes made in the sandbox don’t affect the production account.

When you create a sandbox account

By default, HubSpot copies the following users from the production account to the sandbox:

  • Super Admins
  • Partner admins with elevated access
  • Users with Developer tools access permissions

Users who don’t have one of these permissions aren’t copied to the sandbox by default. To add users after the sandbox is created, add them separately to the sandbox account.

After you create a sandbox account

Use the table below to understand how user changes affect the production and sandbox accounts.

Action

Result

Add a user to the sandbox account

The user is added only to the sandbox account and isn’t added to the production account.

Add a user to the production account after creating a sandbox

The user isn’t automatically added to the sandbox account. Add the user to the sandbox account manually.

Deactivate a user in the production account

If the user exists in the sandbox account, the user is also deactivated in the sandbox account.

Deactivate a user in the sandbox account

The user remains active in the production account.

Reactivate a user in the production account

If the user was previously added to and is currently deactivated in the sandbox account, the user is also reactivated in the sandbox account.

Reactivate a user in the sandbox account

The user remains deactivated in the production account.

Remove a user’s Super Admin or Developer tools access permission in the production account

The user loses sandbox access in production and is automatically removed from all of the account’s sandboxes.

Restore a user’s Super Admin or Developer tools access permission in the production account.

The user isn’t automatically added back to the sandboxes. Add the user to each sandbox manually.

Create a standard sandbox

To create the sandbox:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Sandboxes.
  • Click Create sandbox.
  • In the right panel, under Sandbox name, enter the name of the sandbox.
    • The Copy production assets checkbox will be selected by default as the sandbox must mimic your production account. Click the downIcon Down icon to review the list of assets that’ll be copied to your sandbox.
    • Click the What is this sandbox for? dropdown menu and select options. To remove options, click the X next to the option.
    • Select the Copy 5,000 contacts and associated records checkbox to copy your 5,000 most recently updated contacts, and up to 100 of their associated deals, companies, and tickets (per contact).

Please note: you can copy 5,000 contacts and associated records when creating your standard sandbox.If you don’t copy records during the sandbox creation, you can export and import test records to your sandbox at a later date. You can manually import up to 200,000 records for each of the following objects: contacts, companies, deals, tickets, custom objects, carts, invoices, marketing events, and orders per type record type. For the remaining record types, learn how to track your CRM data usage.

  • Click Create standard sandbox.
  • The process to create the sandbox may take a few hours, depending on how many assets, production plan features, and Super Admins, Partner admins with elevated access, and users with Developer tools access permissions need to be copied from your production account. Learn how permissions are handled in sandbox accounts.
  • The status is tracked in the Created On column. Once created, the status updtates to the creation date and time.
  • To review failed assets, click the Activity log tab. Then, click the status next to the sandbox to view the creation details.
    • Click the Failed assets tab to see any failed assets and the error details.
    • Click the Copied assets tab to see a list of created assets.

Access the standard sandbox

All Super Admins who were copied during sandbox creation can access a sandbox from their main account menu.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the upper right.
  • Hover over your account name to see a list of your recent accounts.
  • In the dropdown menu, click the name of the sandbox you want to access.
  • A banner will display at the top of the window, showing that you’re in the standard sandbox account.

Super Admins can also access a sandbox from account settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Sandboxes.
  • Click the name of the sandbox you want to access.
  • To exit a sandbox account, in the upper right, click your production account name.

Set up a production deploy

Once you have made your changes in your sandbox, you can deploy supported assets to your production account. To set up a production deploy, navigate to your production account, then:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Sandboxes.
  • In the top right, Set up a deploy.
    • In the Supported asset types column, select the assets you want to deploy. If you’re deploying objects, next to the assets, click Select configuration.
    • To understand what’s eligible to deploy with each asset, in the top banner, click View [X] deployment behaviors. In the right panel, review the information. Then, click Close.
  • Select the checkbox next to each change that’s eligible to be deployed. If you’re deploying objects, this will be in the right panel, and you must click Save selection.

Please note: you can deploy up to 300 changes at a time.

  • Click Next.

  • Any connections will display at the Connected Assets step. Connected assets are other assets that are used by your selected assets and which are required for your deployment.

    • Click View object configurations in the Name column to view what’ll be deployed, based on the connection.
    • Click x selected assets in the Used by column to view the connections.
    • To include the configuration in the deployment, click the Add x connections to my deploy to continue checkbox, then click Next.

  • Any conflicts will be automatically detected. Review the error, and resolve any conflicts to proceed with the deployment. If no conflicts are detected, click Next.

  • In the Deploy name field, enter a name for your deploy. In the Description field, enter a description. Click Next.

  • Review your production deployment. When you’re ready, click Deploy to Production.

  • In the dialog box, click Deploy to production to confirm.

  • Once the deployment has started, the production Activity log tab will show the Status column In progress. Once a deployment has started, it can’t be canceled.

  • Once the deployment is complete, the status will update to [#] deployed assets.

  • Please note: if your deployment fails, review the deploy error log to review what may have caused the failure. For further assistance, contact support.

  • Click the deployment name or [#] deployed assets to view the deployment details.

Review sandbox activities

To review a history of sandbox actions that users have taken in your account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Sandboxes.
  • Click the Activity Log tab.
  • A full list of sandbox-related activities will appear, including:
    • Sandbox creation details (i.e. assets copied and error reasons)
    • Past production deployments
    • Sandbox deletions
  • Click the Log type dropdown menu to filter between different activity types.

Sandbox best practices

Sandboxes allow users to innovate safely outside of their production accounts. It’s recommended to define a development strategy, and consider the following aspects to ensure reliable testing in sandboxes:

  • What’s the purpose of the sandbox? (e.g., active development, integration testing, training).
  • Who needs access? (e.g., consider limiting conflicts that can affect testing reliability).
  • Is there a need for more sandboxes to support various use cases?
  • What’s the best way to create and manage sandboxes to support development needs?

Clearly defining these aspects will aid reliable testing, and deployments of supported assets to production, while accommodating other use cases.

Below are examples of different purposes of sandboxes, users who should get access, and creation strategies to ensure reliable testing and development:

Sandbox use case

Purpose

Users

Creation Strategy

Active development and deployment

An agile workspace for ongoing development, testing, and deployments that supports active development cycles, rapid prototyping, and deployment to production.

Active builders and testers involved in development projects aimed to be deployed to production. Limiting sandbox access prevents disruptive changes that can impact reliable testing and deployments.

It’s recommended to regularly delete and create new sandboxes to accurately mirror supported assets of a production environment. This ensures new development takes place in an accurate environment (e.g., after completion of a major development project).

Integration Testing

A stable workspace for integrations, ideal for observing changes and carrying out rigorous testing, that supports the deployment of supported assets to production. It doesn’t include deployment of integration-specific configurations.

Teams managing or extending integrations and verifying end-to-end processes with external systems.

Less frequent sandbox deletion and creation is needed, as the primary goal is to maintain integration connections. But, over time, deleting and creating new sandboxes is recommended, so testing takes place in an accurate environment.

Sandbox for New User Training

An isolated sandbox that offers new hires a safe environment to learn the system and build confidence before using a production account.

Primarily new hires and employees undergoing training for system functionalities and role-specific business processes. Access should be limited to these individuals to maintain a controlled learning environment.

Sandbox deletion and creation will be as-needed, based on new hires or significant business workflow updates.

Sandbox for Testing New Features

A dedicated testing sandbox allowing for testing of new features or complex changes before production adoption.

Access should be limited to a core group of testers and stakeholders for feedback.

Sandbox deletion and creation will be as-needed, depending on what’s being tested.

Create multi-account reports

Use multi-account reporting, a feature of multi-account management, to select additional accounts outside of the account you’re logged into, to include in custom reports.

Multi-account reports include a multi-account data source to view data for other accounts in the multi-account organization. This can be one or multiple accounts.

Permissions required

  • Super Admin permissions are required in every account within your multi-account organization to turn on multi-account reports and to create, edit and delete them.
  • Multi-account reports access permissions are required to view reports that include data from multiple accounts.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements

You must have set up and configured a multi-account management organization.

  • To access multi-account management, the main HubSpot account where you create the organization must have an Enterprise subscription. Each connected account must be a separate HubSpot account with a Professional or Enterprise subscription. Free accounts must be upgraded before connecting.

  • Some functions within multi-account management require subscriptions to other products.

  • Multi-account management can’t be set up in sandbox accounts or trial accounts.

  • Once your multi-account management organization is set up, you’ll be able to create a multi-account report in any HubSpot account that has multi-account reporting turned on as a destination account. The report can include data from any of the accounts that are configured to be source accounts.

  • To create, edit, or delete a multi-account report you must be a Super Admin in every account in your multi-account organization.

  • To view reports that include data from multiple accounts in your organization, users need Multi-Account reports access permissions.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Accounts storing Sensitive Data can’t be a source for multi-account reporting.
  • Accounts hosting data in different locations can’t be connected for multi-account reporting.
  • Multi-account reports are limited to five accounts.
  • An object must be available in all accounts that are used in the report, to be selectable.
  • A property must be available in at least two of the accounts that are used in the report, to be selectable. For accounts for which the property doesn’t exist, that account’s data will be excluded from the report.
  • If a property has the same internal property name and property type, it’s determined that a property is consistent with another account.

Turn on multi-account management reporting

To turn on multi-account reporting:

  • If you haven’t already, set up your multi-account management organization.
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Organization Management, click Multi-Account.
  • Click Edit Account Connections.
  • Select an account from the left panel and toggle the Multi-account reporting switch on.
  • Connections are two-way by default (features work both ways between accounts). To change the connection to one-way (features work from one account to another), click One-way connection.
  • Click Next.
  • Review your changes, then click Done.

Create a multi-account report

Once multi-account management reporting is turned on, to create a multi-account report:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Reporting > Reports. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Reporting > Reports directly.
  • Click Create report.
  • In the left side panel, select Custom Report Builder, and click Next.
  • In the left side panel, select Create report on your own.
  • In the Multi-Account data sources dropdown menu, select the accounts you’d like to include in the report. The selected accounts will be available as a data source in the account.
  • Click Next.
  • Finish creating your report.
  • Once created, if the report is for an account that’s part of the multi-account organization, but isn’t only reporting on the account you’re logged into, the report will have a Multi-account tag. For example:
    • Your multi-account management organization is made up of Account A, Account B, and Account C.
    • If you’re logged into Account B and create a report just for Account B, the tag won’t display.
    • If you’re logged into Account B and create a report for just Account A (part of the multi-account organization), the tag will display.
    • If you’re logged into Account B and create a report for Account B and Account A, the tag will display.

Create multi-account workflows

If you’ve set up multi-account management, you can use multi-account workflows to automate record creation and updates across HubSpot accounts within your organization.

For example, you can use workflow actions to create contact and deal records or update existing contacts in another HubSpot account.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required for every user account within your multi-account organization to add and access multi-account workflow actions. For example, if you have three acccounts associated with your organization, you must be a Super Admin in all three accounts.

Before setting up a multi-account workflow, review the following requirements and considerations

Understand requirements

  • You must set up and configure a multi-account management organization.

  • Turn on multi-account workflows and configure the HubSpot accounts that can use workflow actions. Learn how to turn on multi-account management and configure connections between accounts.

  • Confirm that your account isn’t storing Sensitive Data. Accounts storing Sensitive Data can’t be used as the source account for multi-account workflows.

  • To add the Edit/create contact in another account or Create deal in another account workflow actions, multi-account workflows must be turned on as a source account in the connection.

  • To use an account as a target account in the Edit/create contact in another account and Create deal in another account actions, the account must be configured as destination account for multi-account workflows.

Understand limits & considerations
  • It’s your responsibility to ensure that you’re collecting the right consent for data processing and communications, if you’re creating records in the other account.
  • If the workflow creates a contact in another of your HubSpot accounts you should then set the legal basis of processing and email subscriptions in that account.
  • If you intend to market to contacts created in another account, you must create a complementary workflow in the destination account to set the contacts as marketing contacts and update their email subscriptions

Turn on multi-account management workflows

After setting up your multi-account management organization, turn on multi-account workflows:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Organization Management, click Multi-Account.
  • Click Edit Account Connections.
  • In the left panel, select an account.
  • Toggle the Multi-account workflows switch on.
  • Connections are two-way by default (features work both ways between accounts). To change the connection to one-way (features work from one account to another), click One-way connection.
  • Click Next.
  • Click Done.

Turning on multi-account workflows will introduce a new HubSpot defined property on the contact object called Cross-sell Opportunity which can be set to Yes or No.

Create and update contacts in other accounts with a multi-account workflow

After turning on multi-account management workflows, use the Edit/create contact in another account action to create or update contacts in other HubSpot accounts.

  • HubSpot determines whether a contact already exists in another account by comparing the contact’s Email property across accounts.
  • This workflow action can only create or edit contact records in the other account. But, the workflow trigger can use any type of object. For example, if the trigger uses a deal object, the action will find the contacts associated with the deal that’s enrolled in the workflow:
  • If the workflow is:
    • Editing contacts in another account: you’ll only be able to set the Cross-sell opportunity property.
    • Creating contacts in another account: you’ll be able to set the Cross-sell opportunity property, and then the Email, First Name, and Last Name of the created contacts will be automatically set, based on the values from the contact that the action is executing on.
  • You may only select one account per use of the new workflow action. To edit or create contact records in multiple accounts, add the workflow action once for each account you want to include.
  • Each Create or update record workflow action can target only one HubSpot account. To create or update records in multiple accounts, add a separate action for each destination account.

To use the Edit/create contact in another account action in a multi-account workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the left panel, define your trigger.
  • Click the + Add icon below your trigger.
  • In the left panel, click CRM, then select Edit/create contact in another account.
  • Configure your action:

    • Target contact: select the target record for this action. The record selected depends on the workflow’s trigger type.

      • If using a contact trigger is a contact trigger, select Enrolled contact.
      • If using a deal trigger, select Contact: Most recently updated to update the most recently updated contact, or Contacts: All associated to update all contacts associated with the deal.
      • Click + Add contact data source to use contact-based workflow actions the workflow.

    • Destination account: select the account where the contact will be edited, based on the trigger.

    • Create contact in the selected festination if one doesn’t exist: select this checkbox to create contacts in the account if they don’t exist. The contact record will be created with the email, first name and last name provided by the Target contact field.

    • Cross-account note: enter a note to add to the contact record that’s created or edited.

    • Cross-sell opportunity: determine if the record is a cross-sell opportunity.

    • Clear existing property value: select this checkbox to clear existing values in the Cross-sell opportunity property.

    • Select included properties: select the checkboxes next to any properties you want to be updated. Clear the checkboxes next to properties if you don’t want them to be updated.

    • Existing destination values: when updating an existing contact in your other account, choose whether to retain existing property values or overwrite these values.

    • Custom value handling: you can apply custom property values for specific properties. When doing so, select values from the target account or manually enter a value. If no custom value handling is selected for a property, source values will be used to create or update records by default. To apply a custom property value:

      • In the Custom value handling section, click Select property and select a property that you’d like to apply a custom value to. The value will appear as a new field.
      • In the field, manually enter a property value for updating or creating a new contact in the target account. Alternatively, click the field and select a token to apply as the custom value.
  • After setting up your workflow action, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Create deals in other accounts with a multi-account workflow

After turning on multi-account management workflows, use the Create deal in another account action to create new deals in other HubSpot accounts:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the left panel, define your trigger.
  • Click the + Add icon below your trigger.
  • In the left panel, click CRM, then select Create deal in another account.
  • Configure your action:

    • Target deal: select the target record for this action. The record selected depends on the workflow’s trigger type.

      • If using a deal trigger, select Enrolled deal.
      • If using a contact trigger, select Deal: Most recently updated to create based on the most recently updated deal, or All associated deals.
      • Click + More data to add additional data sources.

    • Select connected account: select the HubSpot account where the new deal will be created.

    • Pipeline configuration: select from the following pipeline options when creating your new deal.

      • Use source pipeline: when creating a deal, use a matching deal pipeline in the connected account as the selected target deal. If a corresponding deal pipeline or deal stage with the same name does not exist in the selected connected account, the deal creation will fail.
      • Select target pipeline: when creating a deal, use a pipeline from the selected connected account. You’ll need to select an existing deal pipeline and deal stage from the corresponding HubSpot account.

    • Cross-sell opportunity: determine if the record is a cross-sell opportunity.

    • Cross-account note: enter a note to add to the deal record that’s created.

    • Additional properties: select the checkboxes next to any properties you’d like to include in your new deal.

  • After setting up your workflow action, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Create tickets in other accounts with a multi-account workflow

After turning on multi-account management workflows, use the Create ticket in another account action to create new tickets in other HubSpot accounts:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the left panel, define your trigger.
  • Click the + Add icon below your trigger.
  • In the left panel, click CRM, then select Create ticket in another account.
  • Configure your action:

    • Target ticket: select the target record for this action. The record selected depends on the workflow’s trigger type.

      • If using a ticket trigger, select Enrolled ticket.
      • If using a non-ticket trigger, such as in a contact-based workflow, select Tickets: All associated or click + More data to add additional data sources. For example, you may want to use All associated tickets: First created or All associated tickets: Most recently associated instead.

    • Select connected account: select the HubSpot account where the new ticket will be created.

    • Pipeline configuration: select from the following pipeline options when creating your new ticket.

      • Use source pipeline: when creating a ticket, use a matching ticket pipeline in the connected account as the selected target ticket. If a corresponding ticket pipeline or ticket stage with the same name does not exist in the selected connected account, the ticket creation will fail.
      • Select target pipeline: when creating a ticket, use a pipeline from the selected connected account. You’ll need to select an existing ticket pipeline and ticket stage from the corresponding HubSpot account.

    • Cross-account note: enter a note to add to the newly created ticket record.

    • Additional properties: select the checkboxes next to any properties you’d like to include in your new ticket.

    • Custom value handling: you can apply custom property values for specific properties. When doing so, select values from the target account or manually enter a value. If no custom value handling is selected for a property, source values will be used to create or update records by default. To apply a custom property value:

      • In the Custom value handling section, click Select property and select a property that you’d like to apply a custom value to. The value will appear as a new field.
      • In the field, manually enter a property value for updating or creating a new contact in the target account. Alternatively, click the field and select a token to apply as the custom value.
  • After setting up your workflow action, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Example use cases

The following examples outline recommended ways to use multi-account workflows across HubSpot accounts in your organization.

  • Route form submissions to another account: collect form submissions in one account and automatically create contacts in other HubSpot accounts. For example, when marketing is centered in one account but leads should be routed to different brands, regions, or business units.
    • Trigger the workflow from a form submission. Learn how to set form submission triggers.
    • Use the Create or update record action to create the contact in the destination account if it doesn’t already exist.
  • Identify cross-sell opportunities: share customer interest or purchase activity with related HubSpot accounts for cross-selling or cross-marketing.
    • Trigger the workflow from an event that identifies a cross-sell opportunity, such as a deal moving to Closed won.
    • Use the Create or update record action to update the Cross-sell Opportunity property for an existing contact, or create a new contact with the property set to Yes.
    • Create a complementary workflow in the destination account to enroll contacts when the Cross-sell Opportunity property is updated.

Create notification profiles

Notification profiles let you standardize how users receive notifications across a HubSpot account. You can create account default notification profiles for users and assign specific notification profiles to presets so users don’t have to set them up individually.

Using notification profiles helps ensure users receive the right notifications through the right channels including email, bell, pop-up, browser, or connected apps, without requiring each user to configure their preferences individually.

For example, you can create a default notification profile for all users, then assign a more tailored notification profile to a preset for sales or support teams.

Super Admin permission are required to create and manage notification profiles.

.

Create an account default notifications profile

Account default notifications apply to any users who aren’t included in a profile by permission set. Default notifications won’t apply to users who have updated their own notification preferences. Moving forward, users can update their own notification preferences at any time, and those changes will override the default notifications.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • At the top, click the Notification Profiles tab.
  • To create a new profile, click Create notification profile.
  • Click to switches next to the notification type on or off. Users can receive notifications through Email, Bell, Pop-up, Browser, and other relevant installed apps (e.g., Slack).
  • Click on each notification group to expand them, to find the notification topic you want to edit. Select the notification checkbox to turn on a notification for the notification profile.
  • To clear all notifications selections, click Clear all preferences.
  • When you’re done, click Save.

All impacted users will be notified by email when you’ve made changes to the account default notifications.

Add notification profiles to a preset

You can use presets to set up default user preferences in their HubSpot account so that users don’t have to set them up individually. This is helpful if you’re onboarding new team members and want to help them get set up. To assign a notification profile to a preset:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • Click the Presets tab.
  • Click the name of an existing preset or create a new preset.
  • At the top, click the Notifications tab.
  • Click the Notification profile dropdown menu and select a notification profile.
  • To add users to your preset, navigate to the Users & Teams tab at the top of the editor.
  • Select users or teams in the dropdown menu.
  • Click Save preset.

Manage notification profiles

Once created, you can edit, deactivate, clone, or delete existing notification profiles.

Please note: if you deactivate a profile in a preset, edit, or delete a notification profile, the users previously included in the profile will return to receiving default account notifications. If the users have updated their own notification preferences, their own preferences will still override the default.

Edit or deactivate notification profiles
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • At the top, click the Notification profiles tab.
  • To edit a profile:
    • In the table, hover over the notification profile, and click the edit pencil icon to edit.
    • To change the channels where the permission set will receive notifications, toggle the switches next to the channel type on or off.
    • To change the topics that the permission set will be notified about, select or clear the checkboxes.
    • Once you’re done, click Update.
    • In the pop-up box, click Update notification profile.
  • To deactivate a profile in a preset:
    • Navigate to the Notifications tab in a preset.
    • Click the Notification profile dropdown menu, and select a notification profile.
    • Click Save preset. In the right panel, review the changes, and click Save.
Clone notification profiles
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • At the top, click the Notification profiles tab.
  • In the table, hover over the notification profile, and click the duplicate clone icon.
  • In the Choose a name for the new cloned notification profile field, enter a name for the new notification profile.
  • Make your changes, then click Update.
  • In the dialog box, click Update notification profile.
Delete notification profiles
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account defaults.
  • At the top, click the Notification profiles tab.
  • In the table, hover over the notification profile, and click the delete delete icon.
  • In the dialog box, click Delete profile.

Customize default region and language settings

Users with Account access permission can customize the time zone, language, currency, and date and number format of a HubSpot account.

A user can also customize their personal language, date, and number format from their profile settings.

Customize your account time zone

The account time zone setting localizes several of your HubSpot tools, including when your scheduled emails send, when scheduled social media content posts, and date and time information for your analytics.

Please note: some elements of HubSpot use the time zone set in your computer instead of the time zone set in HubSpot. This includes timestamps for logged sales activities, record timelines, and property history.

To change the account’s time zone:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Account Defaults.
  • In the General tab, click the Time zone dropdown menu and select the time zone for your account.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes, change time zone.
  • Click Save.

Customize default user language, date, and number format

You can customize the language, date, and number format for new users. Users can then update their personal settings to override these settings, if necessary.

To update user default settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Account Defaults.
  • Click the User Defaults tab.
  • To change the default account language, click the Language dropdown menu, then select a language. This setting changes the default language of the HubSpot interface. Custom properties will not be translated.
  • To change the default account date and number format, click the Date and number format dropdown menu, then select a Country.
  • Click Save.

Please note: HubSpot currently only offers phone support in English. Call-back, email, and chat support is available in English, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese and Spanish. To request a call-back in a specific language, ensure that the language is selected for your user.
