Workflows

You can export a spreadsheet containing information about all of your workflows, and you can export images of individual workflows.

Workflow spreadsheet exports will contain information such as:

  • The name of the workflow.
  • Whether or not the workflow is currently active.
  • Total enrollments and the count of records currently enrolled.
  • Total records that have joined the workflow goal list and the total conversion rate.
  • Create date and the user who created the workflow.
  • Last modification date and the user who modified it.
  • The workflow type.

Please note: workflows exports don’t include performance data or the workflow’s history. In addition, workflow exports don’t include data from emails used in the workflow. Marketing email exports do include an Associated workflows column which identifies the workflows that an email is being used in. Learn more about exporting your marketing email data.

To export a spreadsheet of all workflows not located in folders:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Table actions dropdown menu, and select Export view. The file will download automatically.

To export a spreadsheet of all workflows in a folder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the folder.
  • In the upper right, click the Table actions dropdown menu, and select Export view. The file will download automatically.

To export an image of an individual workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of a workflow.
  • In the upper left, click the File dropdown the select Export as .PNG. The export will process, then download as a .png file.

Necessary disclosure:

HubSpot will store workflow action logs data within the below time periods:

  • 180 days: all workflows action log data will be stored.
  • 180 days - 2 years: high level action log data such as object ID (which contact, company, deal, etc.), event type (enrollment, unenrollment, etc.), and action type will be stored.
  • 2 years+: historical data of enrollments will be retained in our system to enable workflow based filters.

Getting Started | Frequently Asked Questions

Find answers and general information about getting started with HubSpot.

What are the limits of my free account?

Once you’ve signed up for HubSpot and created your account, you will have access to all HubSpot’s free products. This includes the CRM (customer relationship management system), marketing tools like forms, sales tools like email templates, and customer service tools like tickets and conversations. From 18th September, the following limits will apply to new free accounts:

  • You can store up to 1000 contacts.
  • You can have up to 2 users.

Your account is free forever, but there are paid plans if you want to add extra functionality, or increase specific feature limits. Learn more about HubSpot’s products and add-ons.

Is my information safe in HubSpot? Will you read my emails or use my contacts?

Your information is safe and secure in HubSpot. You can choose which contacts to bring into HubSpot, and after authorizing HubSpot to integrate with your inbox, you can pick which emails should be recorded in the platform. HubSpot will never send emails to any of your contacts without your authorization. Learn more about how HubSpot keeps your information safe.

Will HubSpot work for my business? How customizable is HubSpot?

HubSpot is fully customizable to match your needs and industry. Once you bring your contacts into HubSpot, you can create custom properties that define what types of contacts they are, and segment them into lists for reporting and email communication. You’ll be able to customize your sales pipeline based on what works for you, and add a level of automation to help you move even faster. Browse HubSpot’s case studies to see how HubSpot has met the needs of organizations across a range of industries, from healthcare and manufacturing to e-commerce and non-profit.

Does HubSpot integrate with the other tools I’m using?

HubSpot integrates with over one hundred third-party tools, including Mailchimp, SurveyMonkey, Salesforce, Slack, and Eventbrite. Browse the list of supported integrations and check out Zapier, which helps HubSpot connect with even more apps that you may be using.

If you’re looking to build your own integrations, learn more in the developer documentation.

What can I report on in HubSpot?

HubSpot supports a robust set of standard and custom reports. You can create a report on any of the contact, company, deal, product, or ticket records you manage in HubSpot. You can create a funnel or pipeline report for your contacts or deals to track their progress through a specific deal funnel or lifecycle stage. Learn more about the reports included with a free subscription.

How do I migrate data from my current CRM or spreadsheets to HubSpot?

You can use HubSpot’s standard import wizard, which will walk you through the process step-by-step and offer you options to import from your inbox or a spreadsheet. Check out the full guide to the various objects in HubSpot and migrating your data over.

If you’re currently using Salesforce, learn how to import your records from Salesforce.

Does HubSpot have a mobile app?

Yes, HubSpot has both iOS and Android apps, so you can access your entire database on the go and stay on top of sales activity, marketing reporting, and more. Learn more about installing the HubSpot mobile app.

Does HubSpot have training resources where I can learn more or share with others?

Yes, HubSpot has a built-in HubSpot Academy Learning Center featuring online courses and short tutorials to help you learn the HubSpot platform. You can watch these training resources at your own pace and share them with your team.

You can also join Small Group Coaching sessions to build HubSpot skills, get real-time guidance from HubSpot Academy Professors, and connect with peers.

Can I send bulk email from HubSpot?

Yes. With HubSpot’s marketing email tool, you can send bulk emails to your contacts. Learn more about how to use HubSpot’s drag and drop email editor to send promotional emails for your business.

Install the HubSpot mobile app

Use the HubSpot mobile app to take HubSpot’s CRM tools on the go. You can view and edit records, make calls, manage marketing emails, and use the conversations inbox directly from your mobile device.

The HubSpot mobile app can be installed on iOS devices running iOS 17 or later or on Android devices running Android 11 and above. The latest versions of the app can be downloaded for free from App Store Connect and the Google Play Store. The minimum supported app version for Android is 4.30.1 and for iOS is 4.96.1. It’s possible, but not supported, to run the app on Macs with Apple Silicon.

Download the HubSpot app from either the App Store (iOS devices) or Google Play Store (Android devices), or by scanning the QR code below.

Please note:

  • For security reasons, the HubSpot mobile app is not supported on any jailbroken devices on iOS or rooted devices on Android.
  • If you use single sign-on to log in to the mobile app and have multiple HubSpot accounts, you’ll be logged in to the last cached account or one of your accounts by default. Learn how to switch accounts on the mobile app.

Install the HubSpot mobile app (iOS)

  • Open the App Store on your device.
  • Search for the HubSpot app, then tap Get to download and install the app.
  • Tap Open or open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • A “HubSpot” Would Like to Send You Notifications prompt will appear. If you want the HubSpot app to send you notifications, you must allow push notifications. Learn more about enabling notifications from the HubSpot app.
  • Enter your HubSpot credentials and tap Log In. If you’re a user in multiple HubSpot accounts, you’ll be prompted to select which account you want to access. Your device is now connected to your HubSpot account.

Install the HubSpot mobile app (Android)

Please note: the HubSpot mobile app can only be installed using the Google Play Store on an Android device. A list of supported devices can be found here. Installation from external sites or Android application packages (APKs) is not supported.

  • Open the Google Play Store on your device.
  • Search for the HubSpot (CRM & Sales) app, then tap Install to download and install the app.
  • Tap Open or open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • Enter your HubSpot credentials and tap Log in. If you’re a user in multiple HubSpot accounts, you’ll be prompted to select which account you want to access. Your device is now connected to your HubSpot account.

Manage your mobile app settings

In your app settings, you can manage your Account settings and Preferences, provide feedback on the mobile app, and get help from HubSpot Support.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • Tap Menu in the bottom navigation menu.
  • At the bottom of the left sidebar, tap the settings settings icon.
  • On the Settings screen:
    • You can customize your keyboard, calling settings, notifications, and Dark Mode settings.
    • You can also tap to toggle the Device lock setting on. When you close or leave your HubSpot mobile app, the next time you open the app, you’ll be prompted to verify your identity with your mobile device’s native biometrics or PIN code.

Get the latest version of the HubSpot app

You can automate app updates in your device settings, either for all your apps or specifically for the HubSpot mobile app. This is recommended to ensure you do not miss any key updates.

Instructions for iOS

There are two ways to update the HubSpot app, either automatically or manually:

To automatically update your apps:

  • On your iPhone, click Settings > Apps > App Store > App Updates.
  • Tap to toggle the App Updates switch on.

To manually update the HubSpot app:

  • Open the App Store.
  • Tap on your profile icon at the top of your screen.
  • Scroll to see pending updates and release notes. Tap Update next to the HubSpot app to update it to the latest version.
Instructions for Android

To automatically update your apps:

  • On your device, click Google Play Store.
  • Tap your Profile icon > Settings > Network preferences > Auto-update apps.
  • Select an option for when auto-updates can take place.

To manually update the HubSpot app:

  • Open the Google Play Store.
  • Enter HubSpot in the search bar
  • Next to the HubSpot app, tap Update.

Next steps

  • View and edit records
  • Make calls
  • Manage marketing emails
  • Use the conversations inbox
  • Publish and review social posts

Log in to HubSpot

You can log in to HubSpot using several authentication methods, including a password, passkeys, ChatGPT, Google, Microsoft, Apple, or single sign-on, depending on what’s turned on in your account. These options help you access your account securely and use the login method that best fits your organization’s security requirements. HubSpot determines the correct login screen based on your email address and the login methods your admin has configured.

If you’re having trouble logging in, learn how to troubleshoot common login issues or recover access to a deactivated or inactive account.

There are multiple ways to log in to HubSpot:

  • Enter an email address and password.
  • Sign in with ChatGPT.
  • Sign in with Google.
  • Sign in with Microsoft.
  • Sign in with Apple.
  • Use passkeys.
  • Use single sign-on (Professional and Enterprise only). If SSO is turned on, you’ll be signed out of HubSpot after 24 hours of inactivity.

Log in to HubSpot

To log in:

  • In your browser, go to the login page.
  • In the Email field, enter the email address of your account.
  • You’ll be directed to a login page based on which login methods are allowed and configured for your account. (e.g., if you’re set up to log in with a password, you’ll be directed to enter a password, or, if you’re set up to log in with single sign-on, you’ll be directed to log in using SSO). This applies to all login methods.
  • Password login
  • Single sign-on login
  • Log in using your account method.

After logging out and returning to the login page, if you have turned on third-party cookies on your browser, you’ll automatically be directed to the login screen based on your account configuration (e.g., if you’re set up to log in with a password, you’ll be directed to enter a password, or if you’re set up to log in with single sign-on, you’ll be directed to log in using SSO). This removes the need for you to enter your email address each time you want to log in to HubSpot.

Before you get started

Before getting started, please note the following:

  • To access a HubSpot account or sandbox, your email address must be an active user in that specific account. If your email address isn’t listed as a user in the account you need to access, ask an account administrator to add it as a new user.
  • Only HubSpot customers, free users, or trial users can log in to HubSpot. If you signed up to receive an ebook or registered for a webinar, but don’t have an active account, you will not be able to log in.
  • If you try to log in and see a You have no accounts message, your account may have been deactivated. Learn more about deactivated accounts.
  • If HubSpot doesn’t recognize your browser or device, you’ll be prompted to confirm your identity with an emailed verification code. This is separate from the confirmation code you receive when logging in with two-factor authentication. Learn more about login confirmations and account security.
  • If you’ve forgotten your password:
    • From the login page, you can reset your password.
    • If the password reset email doesn’t appear in your inbox, add hubspot.com to your email allowlist.

Troubleshoot login issues

If you’re unable to log in to HubSpot, try the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Confirm that your browser is supported by HubSpot.
  • Ensure that you’re using the email address associated with your HubSpot account if you have multiple email addresses.
  • Clear the cache and cookies in your browser and retry.
  • Check status.hubspot.com to see if there’s a known login issue. HubSpot will continue to update this page with any new information.
  • Log in from another network, such as a cellular network, to see if the issue is network-related. If you’re able to log in from another network, contact your IT department or network administrator to troubleshoot the network issue.
  • Learn how to troubleshoot if you aren’t receiving HubSpot system emails.
  • Turn on third-party cookies in your Chrome settings:
    • In the upper right of your Chrome browser, click the three vertical dots, then select Settings.
    • In the Privacy and security section, click Cookies and other site data.
    • Ensure that Allow all cookies is selected.
    • Try logging in to HubSpot again.

Unable to stay logged in

To ensure you stayed logged in across HubSpot and any extensions or plug-ins you use, such as the Outlook plug-in, it is recommended to select the “Remember Me” checkbox during login.

Additional login help

If you’re unable to log in after following the steps above, submit your information to the HubSpot support team using the link below.

Submit your email address below to get additional login help via email.

Log out of HubSpot

You can log out of your HubSpot account at any time to secure your account, switch users, or end an active session on a shared device. In addition to signing out of your current session, you can manage and log out of other active sessions across browsers and devices from your security settings.

For example, if you signed in on a public computer or no longer use a specific device, you can log out of that session remotely. You can also customize how long your account remains inactive before you’re automatically logged out.

Log out of your HubSpot account

To log out of your HubSpot account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right.
  • At the bottom of the dialog box, click Sign out.

Log out of active HubSpot sessions

To log out of active HubSpot sessions individually or for all browsers and devices:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click General.
  • At the top, click the Security tab.
  • To log out of an individual session, hover over the session and click Log out. You can’t log out of your current session with this method.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes, log out.
  • To log out of all sessions, including your current session, click Log Out of All Sessions.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes, log me out. Learn how to log in to HubSpot and troubleshoot login issues.

Please note: if you’re inactive in your HubSpot account after 24 hours (which is the default session inactivity timeout setting), you will automatically be logged out even if you selected Remember me when logging in. A warning message will display that says: Your session is not valid or has expired, please log in again. If your session remains active, and you selected Remember me, then you will only need to re-login after 28 days. This does not apply to the HubSpot mobile app.

Customize inactive session timeout

To customize how long a HubSpot account (including Outlook extensions) must be inactive before the user is logged out:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Security.
  • Under the Login tab, in the Customize session timeout length section, click the dropdown menu to select the amount of time an account must be inactive before the user is logged out.

You can also customize your inactive session timeout when configuring your login settings. Learn how to use the login settings wizard.

Manage AI settings

HubSpot’s AI settings give you control over how generative AI is used across your account. Configure access to AI features, manage which data sources are used, and ensure AI-generated content is tailored to your organization.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to manage AI settings.

Manage AI features settings

To use generative AI features in your HubSpot tools, turn on your AI settings in the Access tab. Turn off generative AI features and data access in your HubSpot account at any time by setting the corresponding toggles to Off.

If you’ve previously configured your AI settings, the options turned on will generally depend on the following:

  • Content Prompts corresponds to Give users access to generative AI tools and features.
  • Customer analysis corresponds to Customer conversation data.
  • Files corresponds to Files data.
  • Breeze Assistant remains the same.

To manage AI features settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, in the Account management section, navigate to AI.
  • On the Access tab of AI settings, configure the settings below.
Manage generative AI tools and features settings

To give the users access to generative AI features, such as generating text and media content using prompts, toggle the Give users access to generative AI tools and features switch on.

Toggle the Give users access to generative AI tools and features switch on. By default, this setting is toggled on.

  • This setting must be turned on to use any generative AI features, including Breeze Assistant.
  • To help AI generate outputs that reflect your business, you can also turn on additional data access:
    • CRM data: allows AI access to metadata and user-generated content such as CRM records and default properties. By default, this setting will be toggled on.
    • Customer conversation data: allows AI to summarize and respond to customer conversations such as call transcripts, emails, and more. By default, this setting will be toggled on.
    • Files data: allows AI to use file data from public files or files stored in your HubSpot account’s files tool. By default, this setting will be toggled off.
Manage Breeze Assistant settings

To let the users in your account access Breeze Assistant, toggle the Give users access to Breeze Assistant switch on.

  • Toggle the Give users access to Breeze Assistant switch on. By default, this setting will be toggled on.
  • To personalize Breeze Assistant, it’s recommended to turn the Give users access to generative AI tools and features switch on, and additional data access such as CRM data, Customer conversation data, and Files data.
Manage AI model training settings

Configure the AI model training settings to control if HubSpot may use your account’s customer data to train HubSpot AI models. This setting applies at the account level, and covers all eligible customer data. It must be configured separately for each account if you manage multiple accounts. Toggle changes are logged for audit logs.

When this setting is turned off, data isn’t used to train HubSpot AI models and isn’t shared with other HubSpot customers. When this setting is turned off, you can still use AI features in your account. Accounts with Sensitive Data turned on are opted out of AI model training by default and can’t opt in. Learn more about opting out of HubSpot’s AI model training

  • Toggle the AI Model Training switch on or off. By default, this setting will be toggled on.

Manage Breeze context

Configure Breeze context to ensure that the content generated aligns with your company. The context is used for Breeze Assistant responses and when generating content with other assistants and agents.

Learn more about managing Breeze context.

Manage multiple HubSpot accounts

Manage access across multiple HubSpot accounts by checking which account you’re currently logged into, switching between accounts, and setting a default account. This is useful if you work in more than one HubSpot account and need to confirm your Hub ID, move between accounts quickly, or ensure you’re using the correct account with the right subscriptions.

Learn more about HubSpot accounts.

Check your current account

If features, data, or tools are missing in HubSpot, you may be logged into the wrong account. Before troubleshooting, verify which HubSpot account you’re currently logged into:

  • In the upper right, click your account name.
  • In the dropdown menu, under Account, you can find the account name and unique Hub ID.

While signed into HubSpot, your Hub ID also appears as the numeric account identifier in the URL. For for example, the URL may look like app.hubspot.com/contacts/{HubID}/…

Switch accounts

If you’re a user that has access to multiple HubSpot accounts, switch between your HubSpot accounts after logging in. To switch between accounts, your email address must already be added as a user on each HubSpot account you want to access.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the upper right.
  • Under Account, hover over your account name and Hub ID to see a list of your recent accounts.
  • In the dropdown menu, click the account name you want to switch to.

Manage accounts

View all accounts you have access to, pin frequently used accounts, and set a default account that opens automatically when you log in.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the upper right.
  • Under Account, hover over your account name and Hub ID, and click All accounts.
  • To pin a specific HubSpot account to the top, hover over the account and click Pin.
  • To select which account will be the default account that’ll be opened when you log in to HubSpot, hover over the account and select Set as default.
  • To access a HubSpot account, click the account name.

Please note: if you are logged into a HubSpot account without a specific subscription, you will not have access to the functions until you switch to the correct HubSpot account with the subscription. View the Product column to understand which account you should switch to, to gain access to any functions you may be missing.

Switch accounts in the HubSpot mobile app

In the HubSpot mobile iOS and Android apps, switch between accounts from the settings menu.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • In the top left, tap the listView menu icon.
  • Tap your account name.
  • Tap Account.
  • Tap the account you’d like to switch to.

Migrate account data to another regional data center

If you have a HubSpot account, you can migrate your data to one of HubSpot’s other data centers. HubSpot supports two types of data migrations: opt-in migrations that you initiate yourself, and automatic migrations that HubSpot schedules on your behalf. Migrations automatically include all eligible sandboxes.

  • Opt-in migrations: after reviewing the requirements, logistics, and impact of the data migration tool, you can initiate and schedule the migration directly from your HubSpot account. There may be some required post-migration actions to take depending on the tools and features you’re using. If your desired migration location isn’t available yet, register your interest for future migrations if that location becomes available.
  • Automatic migrations: in some situations, HubSpot may determine that your account is a better fit for a different data hosting location to improve performance. In these cases, HubSpot will automatically schedule a migration for your account. All Super Admins will receive a notification about the migration 30 days in advance. You may cancel the migration or reschedule it.

If anything unexpected occurs during or after the migration, contact support.

Review the answers to some Frequently Asked Questions about migration.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to initiate, reschedule, or cancel a migration.

.

Before you get started

Please note the following limitations & considerations, which may apply to all types of data migrations, whether scheduled by you or automatically scheduled by HubSpot:

Data center locations

Learn more about where customer data will be hosted by HubSpot.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Data migrations usually take about 24 hours but can take up to 36 hours. Your HubSpot account will be unavailable to all users during that time.
  • Data migrations must be scheduled on an available date at least one week in advance.
  • A migration can be canceled up to 36 hours before it’s due to begin.
  • You can only migrate data from HubSpot’s U.S. East Coast data center (United States (East)) to another data center, not vice versa. E.g., you aren’t able to migrate from HubSpot’s EU data center to another data center.
  • If you use single-sign on (SSO) (Enterprise only), you’ll be automatically redirected to the new data center location after migration and no further action is required.
  • If your account collects payments with HubSpot payments, Revenue Hub, or Stripe, you can migrate to a different data center without disconnecting your payment account or canceling subscriptions. After the migration, your payment history, subscriptions, contracts, and payment links remain in place.
    • Automatic migrations aren’t scheduled for accounts that collect payments with the payments tool, Revenue Hub, or Stripe. To migrate one of these accounts, a Super Admin must opt in and schedule the data migration.
    • During a data migration, buyers can’t use payment links, open invoices, or payment method update links. After the migration, these links redirect to the new data center and accept payments again.
  • Accounts with associated developer test accounts aren’t eligible for automatic migrations. If opted in to a migration, the developer test account will expire after the migration completes.
Understand cancellations

HubSpot will cancel an account or sandbox migration if it doesn’t meet the technical or product requirements needed to complete the move. Super Admins will receive an email notification if the migration is canceled.

Depending on whether you opted in to the migration or your account was selected for automatic migration, different conditions can prevent the process from continuing. Review the sections below to learn why your account or sandbox migration may be canceled and what steps you can take to move forward.

Opt-in or automatic migrations cancellation reasons
  • Sensitive Data: if you have Sensitive Data turned on and haven’t stated the storage of HIPAA data, you can migrate your account.
    • HIPPA data: if you’re storing HIPPA data, you can’t migrate to another data center. To schedule the migration, you must edit your Sensitive Data settings to indicate that you aren’t storing HIPPA data.
  • Microsoft Teams and Zoom integrations: if you’re using the Microsoft Teams or Zoom integrations, they need to be connected to one account. This needs to be done before you can schedule the migration.
  • Billing changes: if your billing date changes after your migration is scheduled, the dates may conflict. If your migration is canceled for this reason, you must reschedule your migration for a different date.
Automatic migrations cancellation reasons

If HubSpot determines that your account is a better fit for another data hosting location, but any of the conditions below apply, your migration will be canceled to prevent business disruption. Super Admins can opt the account back in after reviewing the cancellation reason.

  • Snowflake integration: the Snowflake integration can’t be migrated. It must be uninstalled and reinstalled after migration.
  • Dedicated IP address: dedicated IP addresses can’t be migrated. You must reconnect them after migration.

Impact to HubSpot tools

All information in your HubSpot account including historical data will be migrated over to the new data center. Take note of the impact to the following tools, especially impact during downtime that’ll require further action after the date migration:

Tool

Impact to tool

Account and object IDs

Your HubSpot account and object record IDs will remain the same after the migration is complete.

Ads

Any ad scheduled to go live during the data migration will go live at the scheduled time.

Any data coming into HubSpot from a connected ad account (Facebook, LinkedIn, Google) during the migration will be processed when the data migration is complete.

API calls

Any API calls made to your HubSpot account from integrations will fail during the migration. If a call is made during migration, HubSpot will return a 477 status code.

After the data migration, API calls may or may not be retried depending on the app or integration that the API call originates from. HubSpot doesn’t have visibility into whether an API call will be retried.

Authentication & secrets

API authentication primarily works via OAuth. After the migration the OAuth flow will automatically take care of refreshing access credentials.

Calling

Outbound calling: outbound calls initiated directly from a HubSpot account will be dropped once the migration starts. Outbound calls initiated from HubSpot but done through a phone won’t be dropped.

Inbound calling: inbound calls won’t connect during the migration. HubSpot will play the standard message that would play whenever you can’t be reached.

All existing call data and recordings will be migrated to the new HubSpot data hosting location. All future call data and activity will take place on the new data hosting location.

Please note: Twilio keeps a record of HubSpot customers’ phone numbers on their U.S. servers.

Chatbots

Chatbots will be unavailable and hidden from website visitors beginning one hour before a data migration. Chatbots will be available for new messages when the migration is complete. If a customer has started a conversation with a chatbot before the migration starts, they’ll be able to finish it, but if the chat writes information to HubSpot, that will fail.

Customer portal

Your customers will be able to create new tickets and view existing tickets.

They will not be able to respond to or send new messages. If they try to respond to an existing message, they will see the following error: Unable to send message while system is undergoing scheduled maintenance. Check back later.

Custom and third-party integrations

During migration, custom and third-party integrations will not sync with your HubSpot account.

After the data migration, API calls may or may not be retried depending on the app or integration that the API call originates from. HubSpot does not have visibility into whether an API call will be retried.

CRM imports

Imports will be unavailable 24 hours before your scheduled migration date.

CTAs

CTAs will be available during the migration and will track activity. CTA analytics won’t be accessible during the migration.

Data sync

All syncing activity will be paused during the migration. After the migration, all syncing activity will resume normally.

Documents

During the migration, documents will not be visible to any users. Users will see the error: This document is temporarily unavailable because of scheduled system updates. It’ll be available again on [date migration ends].

Domains

  • The system domains of the account will be migrated: - E.g., [Hub ID].hs-sites.com and [domain - Hub ID].hs-sites.com will be migrated to [Hub ID].hs-sites-eu1.com and [domain - Hub ID].hs-sites-eu1.com)
  • Please note: custom SSL certificates can’t be migrated between data centers. Any domains that get migrated revert to the default SSL certificate provided by Cloudflare. To restore the your SSL certificate, you need to repeat the standard SSL custom certificate setup process.
  • If you have setup your domain as a reverse proxy, you’ll need to update the CNAME target you’re proxying to quickly after the migration. Learn more about the new CNAME target.

Marketing Emails

Once a data migration is scheduled, bulk marketing email sends can’t be scheduled that day.

Marketing emails scheduled to go out during a data migration won’t be sent and will need to be rescheduled when the migration is complete.

Incoming emails will be received, but workflow triggers, RSS emails, forms, follow-up emails, and other email-based automation will be paused until the migration is complete.

Facebook Messenger integration

Service reps will still be able to respond to incoming messages sent via Facebook Messenger or non-HubSpot email accounts.

Feedback surveys

Feedback surveys will still be able to collect submissions, but they won’t be available until after the migration. Reminder emails scheduled for the day of the migration won’t be sent, and will need rescheduling. All submission-based automation will also be paused until the migration is complete.

Forms

Forms will still be able to collect submissions, but they won’t be available until after the migration. All submission-based automation will also be paused until the migration is complete.

Anyone who submits a form during this time will see the following message: Your response was submitted. Due to system maintenance work, it might take up to a day to finish processing.

HubSpot-built integrations

For most HubSpot-built integrations, data won’t sync during the data migration. Data will sync after the integration is complete. Please review exceptions for the Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Snowflake integrations below:

Microsoft Teams:

If your Microsoft Teams account is currently connected to multiple HubSpot accounts, all of those HubSpot accounts must be in the same data hosting location. If you want to keep your Microsoft Teams account connected to multiple HubSpot accounts, you must either migrate all or none of the accounts to the new data hosting location.

If you only migrate one connected HubSpot account, Microsoft Teams will be disconnected from all accounts until:

  • All connected HubSpot accounts are in the same data hosting location. OR
  • The integration is disconnected from all HubSpot accounts in one data hosting location (e.g. disconnected from all HubSpot accounts in the U.S. data center).

Zoom:

If your Zoom account is currently connected to multiple HubSpot accounts, all of those HubSpot accounts must be in the same data hosting location. If you want to keep your Zoom account connected to multiple HubSpot accounts, you must either migrate all or none of the accounts to the new data hosting location.

If you only migrate one connected HubSpot account, Zoom will be disconnected from all accounts until:

  • All connected HubSpot accounts are in the same data hosting location. OR
  • The integration is disconnected from all HubSpot accounts in one data hosting location (e.g. disconnected from all HubSpot accounts in the U.S. data center).

Snowflake:

After the migration is done, you’ll need to uninstall and immediately reinstall and set up your Snowflake integration. Data captured before, during, and after migration will be available in the integration once it’s reinstalled.

Please note: depending on where your Snowflake account is located, you may experience a different syncing rate after migration. If your Snowflake account is in the same data center as your HubSpot account, the integration will sync data every 15 minutes. If they’re not in the same location, the integration will sync data daily.

Knowledge base

Your knowledge base will be available to all visitors during the data migration.

Landing and website pages

Website and landing pages will be available to all visitors during the migration, but users will be unable to make changes until the migration is complete.

Page views and analytics will still be recorded, but they won’t be available until the migration is complete.

The existing pages will continue to be hosted on the previous system for a limited amount of time, so if you modify the pages, you’ll need to select a new domain.

When you change a page to a new system domain, there won’t be an automatic redirect.

When a website or landing page is created in HubSpot but lives on a third-party website (e.g. Squarespace, Hostinger), you have to update the page’s web address in the third-party site after moving it. The data migration changes the web address, which will cause links to that page to break due to there being no automatic redirect. See the Domains section in the table.

Live chat

All live chat widgets will be unavailable and hidden from website visitors beginning one hour before a data migration.

Live chat widgets will be available for new messages when the migration is complete.

Meeting links

During migration, meeting links will go into offline mode. Meetings can still be requested via your link, but they won’t be automatically added to your calendar.

After the migration, you’ll receive an email for any requested meetings.

Please note: the meeting link owner will need to manually send meeting invites for the requested meetings.

Notifications

Sidebar notifications won’t be migrated. These notifications typically expire after 30 days.

Private apps

Your private app will stay the same after the migration is complete.

Public apps

Public app authorization isn’t impacted by migration. Authorization URLs should still be shared at the app.hubspot.com URL.

Quotes

If a quote requires multiple signatures, and isn’t complete, the count of signatures will reset to zero after the migration. All signers will need to resign the quote after the migration.

Sales Emails

1:1 emails will be sent after the migration is complete.

Sandboxes

Sandboxes are eligible for migration and record IDs will remain the same after the migration is complete.

Sequences

Sequences will be paused during a data migration, but contacts can still unenroll by responding to an email. Emails scheduled to be sent during the migration will go out as soon as it’s complete. All other emails in the sequences will send as scheduled.

Social tools

Any social posts scheduled to be published during the migration will be published after the migration is complete. You’ll still be able to schedule social posts during the weekend of your migration.

If you need to have a post published during the migration weekend, you can publish it using the individual social tool rather than through HubSpot. If you publish directly, make sure to delete the HubSpot-scheduled post so you don’t have duplicate posts.

Tickets

Tickets created through the chatbot won’t be available during the migration.

Tickets created through email will be created after the migration is over.

Tickets created through the ticket form will be processed after the migration.

Videos

If a video is embedded from the file manager, you won’t be able to play it until you select a new domain if the existing page was initially hosted on a system domain.

Webhooks from HubSpot

Webhooks from HubSpot to another system wouldn’t be sent during the time of migration.

Post-migration, they should continue to send, but it’s recommended to review your webhook configuration.

Workflows

Workflows will be paused, but any delayed actions will be triggered as soon as the migration is complete. All other workflow actions will resume as scheduled.

Opt-in and schedule a data migration

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Click Privacy & Consent.
  • Click the Data hosting tab.
  • The HubSpot data center where your account’s data is currently hosted is shown under Your Data hosting location.
  • Click Change to start the migration process.
  • Click the New data hosting location dropdown menu and select a location.
  • Click the Migration date dropdown menu and select a migration date.

Please note: the following may influence what dates you’re able to select:

  • Migrations are subject to availability. Most migration dates are available approximately one month in advance.

  • You can’t schedule a migration three days before, or after your bill date.

  • There is a limit to the number of migrations that can be carried out for all HubSpot customers. If no dates are available, the maximum number of migrations may have been reached.

  • Select the Confirm migration checkbox.

  • Click Schedule data migration.

The migration date and new location will be displayed on the Data Hosting tab.

Your account will be unavailable for up to 36 hours during the migration. If a user tries to access their account during this time, they will see the following message:

Data Migration in Progress

Your HubSpot account data is moving to the [data center location]. Your account will be unavailable until [date] at [time and time zone]. If you have any questions, contact [super admin name].

All Super Admins in the account will receive four email notifications about the scheduled migration:

  • After the migration has been scheduled.
  • The Monday of the week that the migration is scheduled for.
  • The day before the migration is scheduled for.
  • After the data migration is complete.

They’ll also receive an email notification if the data migration fails.

Migrate sandboxes

When an account is opted in for migration, all active, eligible, sandbox accounts are automatically included in the migration. Migrating sandboxes with your account helps prevent data loss and avoids disruption to development, QA, and testing processes. If a sanbox is ineligible, view the reason and resolve it before the scheduled migration date.

Please note: if a sandbox is ineligible when the migration takes place, it won’t be migrated and its data will be permanently lost. Your account will still be migrated. Cancel or reschedule the migration before it begins if additional time is needed to resolve sanbox eligibility issues.

Register interest for future migrations

If the desired migration path isn’t yet available or scheduled, signal interest in future migrations and receive updates when that migration option is available.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Click Privacy & Consent.
  • Click the Data Hosting tab.
  • Click Change.
  • Click the New data hosting location dropdown menu and select your desired location.
  • Click Register your interest.
  • You can withdraw your interest at any time on the Data Hosting tab by clicking Withdraw your interest.

Cancel and reschedule a data migration

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Click Privacy & Consent.
  • Click the Data Hosting tab.
  • Under Your HubSpot account is scheduled to move to a new data hosting location, click Actions, then select:
    • Reschedule to reschedule a data migration. In the dialog box, select a date for the data migration and click Reschedule. Migrations must be scheduled at least one week in advance.
    • Cancel to cancel a data migration. In the dialog box, click Yes, cancel data migration.

Post-migration checklist

When a data migration is scheduled by you, the following post-migration actions are required to fully configure the account in the new data center. For migrations initiated by HubSpot, these actions are optional, but reviewing them is recommended to confirm everything is working as expected.

Items that require immediate attention post migration

Action needed

Description

Reinstall HubSpot-built integration

Snowflake

If you use the Snowflake data share functionality, you’ll need to uninstall and immediately reinstall and set up your Snowflake integration. Data captured before, during, and after migration will be available in the integration once it’s reinstalled.

Please note: depending on where your Snowflake account is located, you may experience a different syncing rate after migration. If your Snowflake account is in the same data center as your HubSpot account, the integration will sync data every 15 minutes. If they’re not in the same location, the integration will sync data daily.

Other items that need attention post migration

Action needed

Description

Connect dedicated IP address

Connect a dedicated IP address for sending transactional and or marketing emails in your domain settings. Without taking this step, your emails will send with a shared IP address.

Connect return path domains

Connect custom return path domains. Without taking this step, your emails will send with your portal’s default return path domain.

Update SMTP hostname and SMTP port

If you use the SMTP API for transactional emails, update the SMTP hostname and SMTP port. Without this step, emails will pass through the original data hosting location before being processed in the new data hosting location.

Review changes to user accounts after data migration

Notification sounds reset to default

Notification sound preferences for each user have defaulted to playing a sound for notification pop-ups. Users can change preferences in their notification settings.

Browser notifications turned off

Browser notifications for each user have defaulted to being off. Users can change preferences in their notification settings.

Meeting links may have been updated

If a user’s meeting link wasn’t available in the new data hosting location, they are automatically assigned a new one. Users can change their scheduling page URL in their scheduling settings.

Update BCC and forwarding email address

Your BCC and forwarding email addresses for manually logging emails in HubSpot will be different after the migration. Follow the steps here to copy and set up your new BCC and forwarding email addresses.

Update the form embed code

If you use forms on your non-HubSpot website, you’ll have to update the form embed code. Without taking this step, forms are still functional and data will be stored in the new data hosting location but will continue to pass through the old data hosting location. Either update the embed code, or work with your web developers to ensure they’re updated. Learn more about HubSpot forms on external sites.

Update the call-to-action embed code

If you embed CTAs on your non-HubSpot website, you’ll have to update the CTA embed code. Learn more about CTAs on external sites.

Update the HS-scripts embed code

If your non-HubSpot website has any HS-scripts, follow the links under Update the HS-scripts embed code section to obtain new embed codes.

If you don’t update the embed codes, data will continue to pass through the old data location and you may experience delays with your landing page, website, and forms.

The embed codes that need upating are:

  • Analytics
  • Collected forms
  • Feedback
  • Conversations
  • Data privacy and consent
  • Ads
  • CTAs
  • Forms
  • Lead flows

Update the HS-scripts embed code on WordPress

Log into your WordPress site and follow the prompts to update the HS-scripts embed code. Without using new embed codes, data will continue to pass through the old data location, and you may experience delays with your landing page, website, and/or forms.

Migrate your account data to another regional data center | Frequently Asked Questions

Find general questions and answers about migrating your account data to another regional data center. Learn more about the HubSpot Cloud Infrastructure and Data Hosting | Frequently Asked Questions.

Can I migrate from another regional data center to the U.S. East Coast data center?

Data migration is only available from HubSpot’s U.S. East Coast data center (United States (East)) to another regional data center.

What does the data migration include?

Your HubSpot account will now be stored in HubSpot’s regional data center that you select during the migration process. The migration tool is built to support every feature and there is no expected data loss. This doesn’t mean that your data will never leave the regional data center. Please read HubSpot’s Data Processing Agreement and the HubSpot Cloud Infrastructure and Data Hosting | Frequently Asked Questions article for more information.

How safe is HubSpot’s migration tool? Does HubSpot have back-ups of my account?

The migration tool is safe and stable. Safeguards have been built that’ll stop the migration and revert to the United States (East) data center if serious issues are detected. HubSpot keeps back-ups of your account (created before the migration starts) in the United States (East) data center that can be used if needed. These backups are deleted after the migration is complete and once it’s been determined as safe to do so. Thereafter, Customer Data will be replicated for disaster recovery and back-up purposes to other data centers within the regional Hosting Location.

Do I need to make a back-up of my account before migrating the data?

No, you do not need to make your own back-up. You can export your account content and data if you’d like to do so.

Does someone from my team need to monitor our HubSpot account during the data migration process?

As your team will not have access to your HubSpot account during the migration, it is not necessary to have someone monitor your account during the process. HubSpot has safeguards built into the data migration process to monitor for issues.

Is there any data loss during the downtime?

While there is no data loss during the downtime, some tools are impacted. For more information review impact to HubSpot tools.

What happens if I notice an issue after the migration?

Please contact HubSpot Support and note the day you migrated from the United States (East) to the new data center.

How can I confirm if the migration is successful?

When the migration is complete you will be able to log in to your account. Your account’s super admins will also receive an email confirming that your account has either been successfully migrated, or if the migration failed.

To check which data center your account is in:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Privacy & Consent.
  • Click the Data Hosting tab where you can see where your HubSpot account is hosted.

Please note: HubSpot uses a Content Delivery Network (CDN) to route traffic into our network. If using an IP address location lookup tool post migration, the result will not be a reliable representation of where data is traveling. For this reason, please follow the above steps to confirm the migration.

Why was my account put on a specific data center?

If your HubSpot account was created before July 2021, it was automatically created on HubSpot’s United States (East) data center. Where customers have purchased the Subscription Service or are using Free Services only, and their Customer Data is hosted in the United States, they can choose to migrate their data to another data center, subject to some limitations.

If your HubSpot account was created from July 2021 onwards, customers who purchase a Subscription Service are given an option during the sign-up process to choose where their account is located. If a HubSpot sales representative created the account for you, they could select which data center to host your account on.

In cases where a customer has not selected a Hosting Location or for customers using Free Services only, HubSpot will make a Hosting Location selection to support your access to the Subscription Services.

Once the account is created, the data can only be moved between data centers through the migration process.

Mirror data between HubSpot accounts with multi-account management

With data mirroring, a feature of multi-account management, you can mirror contact and company data between different HubSpot accounts. For example, a sales representative in one account is interacting with a contact who bought something from another business entity. That business entity has a separate, unique HubSpot account. With data mirroring turned on, the user will be able to see that information in their account, even if they’re not a user in the other business entity’s HubSpot account.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements

  • You must have set and configured up a multi-account management organization.

    • To access multi-account management, the main HubSpot account where you create the organization must have an Enterprise subscription. Each connected account must be a separate HubSpot account with a Professional or Enterprise subscription. Free accounts must be upgraded before connecting.

  • Some functions within multi-account management require subscriptions to other hubs.

  • Multi-account management can’t be set up in sandbox accounts or trial accounts.

  • Contact data may include personal information. Your data handling practices and disclosures you make to your data subjects may need to reflect new data disclosure configurations.

  • For contact data mirroring, contacts must exist in both accounts, based on a shared email address.

  • For company data mirroring, companies must exist in both accounts, based on company website address.

  • Users who have permission to view the contact or company record in the destination account, and permission to use the connected data feature can view all the contact or company shared data from the source account, regardless of their permissions in the source account.

  • Super Admins who have a View-Only Seat can use the log in as another user feature to test the connected data functionality. Learn more about checking if the user has the right permissions to use data mirroring.

Permissions required Users with a View-Only seat can’t use data mirroring. Learn more about managing seats.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Accounts storing Sensitive Data can’t be a source for data mirroring.
  • The mirrored data will be limited to activities (notes, calls, meetings, emails, tasks) and associated deals.
  • Data in the destination account is read-only.
  • Each time contacts are viewed in the destination account, the information is updated and refreshed to reflect the current state of the source account.

Exclude records from data mirroring

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to exclude records from data mirroring.

Exclude contacts or companies for data mirroring by changing the value of the Excluded from cross-account data mirroring property to False. Edit records individually or in bulk.

Use data mirroring

Once data mirroring is configured for a multi-account management organization, users will be able to see connected contacts and companies on their record pages.

To view connected data of a contact or company:

  • Navigate to your records:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.
  • Click on a record.
  • If the record is a connected record, a label will display in the top-left corner, under the contact or company name.
  • Click connected [record] to view the connected data from the other account in the right panel.

Test data mirroring

Super Admins with a View-Only Seat can test data mirroring by logging in as another user in the account that has an assigned Core, Sales Hub, or Service Hub seat.

To test data mirroring:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • Hover over the user and click Edit permissions.

  • Click Choose permissions to expand the permissions.

  • On the left side, click Sales or Service.

  • Toggle the View connected record data switch on.

  • Make sure that the contact exists in both accounts, and that the user has permission to view the contact in the destination account.

  • Log in as the user.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • Click the contact.

  • Check that the connected data label shows in the top-left corner, under the contact name and email.

Not receiving push notifications in browser

HubSpot supports push notifications on Google Chrome 32+, Firefox 22+, Safari 6+ and Edge. If you are not receiving push notifications in your browser and your browser supports push notifications, check to ensure that notifications are not disabled in your browser’s settings.

Please note: ensure browser notifications are turned on through your operating system’s settings and that do not disturb is disabled.

Browser

Google Chrome

  • Click the lock icon in the address bar of your Chrome browser.
  • Click to toggle the Notifications switch on.

If Notifications does not appear in the lock menu, select Site settings, then select Allow in the dropdown menu to the right of Notifications.

Firefox

  • Click the lock icon in the address bar of your Firefox browser.
  • On the right, click the arrow symbol > beside Connection status.
  • Click More Information, then select the Permissions tab.
  • Under Send Notifications, uncheck Use Default and select Allow.

Safari

  • With your Safari window open, click Safari in the menu bar, then select Preferences.
  • Click the Websites tab (Notifications tab in older versions).
  • In the left panel, click Notifications.
  • Ensure that app.hubspot.com is set to Allow. If not, select the Allow websites to ask permission to send push notifications checkbox.

Edge

  • Click the lock icon in the address bar of your Edge browser.
  • Under Notifications, select Allow.

If Notifications does not appear in the lock menu, select Site permissions, then select Allow in the dropdown menu to the right of Notifications.

Please note: the above instructions are for the Edge browser released in January 2020.

Browsers HubSpot doesn’t support

HubSpot does not support displaying push notifications on the following browsers:

  • Internet Explorer
  • Opera

Troubleshoot push notifications

If you aren’t receiving push notifications, try the following troubleshooting suggestions:

  • Make sure you aren’t on an Incognito tab.
  • If turned on, turn off Focus or Do not disturb mode on your device.
  • Ensure website notifications are turned on for your Google Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge browser.

Overview of approvals in HubSpot

Approvals in HubSpot help teams review and authorize changes before actions are finalized. Depending on the tool, approvals can require designated users to review records, content, exports, quotes, or marketing assets before they move forward.

Using approvals ensures accountability, maintains compliance with internal processes, and reduces the risk of publishing or sharing incorrect information. For example, a sales manager can require approval before a deal moves to a closed stage, or a marketing manager can approve a marketing email before it’s sent to contacts. To follow up with an approver, send an approval reminder.

Before you get started

  • Update your notifications, Slack, or Microsoft Teams for real-time approval notifications by turning on the Approval activity notification. Learn more about managing your Slack and Microsoft Teams notifications.
  • Each feature requires different subscriptions, seats, and permissions. Refer to the individual knowledge base article below for details.

Approvals in HubSpot

Approvals are supported in the following areas of HubSpot. To follow up with an approver, send an approval reminder.

Revenue
  • Set up quote approvals (Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise): require approval before sending quotes to buyers. Learn how to manage quote approvals.
  • Set up legacy quote approvals (Sales Hub Enterprise): require approval before sending legacy quotes to buyers. Learn how to manage legacy quote approvals.
Content
  • Set up and moderate blog comments: require approval before blog comments are published.
  • Approve HubSpot content (Marketing Hub Enterprise, Service Hub Enterprise, Content Hub Enterprise): require approval before marketing content is published.
Data governance

(BETA) Require approvals for exports (Marketing Hub Enterprise, Sales Hub Enterprise, Service Hub Enterprise, Data Hub Enterprise, Content Hub Enterprise): require approval before exporting records from an account.

Object

Require approvals for deals (Sales Hub Enterprise): require approval for a deal pipeline so deals must be approved before progressing down the pipeline.

Mobile

Manage approvals on mobile devices: Requesting approvals on mobile is supported for marketing emails and social posts only. Users can cancel and approve content including social posts, marketing emails, blog posts, landing pages, website pages, and knowledge base articles using the HubSpot mobile app.

Production assets eligible to copy to a sandbox

When you create a sandbox, HubSpot copies supported assets and account configurations from your production account to provide a starting point for testing, training, and validating changes without affecting your live environment.

Not all assets and settings are copied to a sandbox. This article explains which assets are fully supported, partially supported, or unsupported during sandbox creation, along with any limitations or manual steps that may be required after the sandbox is created.

Learn more about sandbox assets eligible to be deployed to production and which sandbox assets are newly released, in beta, or in development.

Supported assets that can be copied to a sandbox

The assets listed in the tables below are copied to a sandbox when it’s created.

CRM data and schema

Asset type

What’s copied

Please note:

Object records

During sandbox creation, it’s optional to copy up to 5,000 of the most recently updated contact records, along with up to 100 associated deals, 100 associated companies, and 100 associated tickets per contact.

After sandbox creation, import up to 200,000 records for each record type.

Event data on records isn’t copied.

Standard and custom object schemas

Fully supported.

  • Record creation forms aren’t copied.
  • Custom object IDs and standard and custom object association IDs don’t match between the production and sandbox accounts.
  • If your account has integtrations that rely on object IDs, manually resolve ID mismatches.

Object associations and labels

Fully supported.

  • Standard and custom object association IDs don’t match between the production and sandbox accounts.
  • If your account has integtaions that rely on standard and custom object association IDs, manually resolve ID mismatches.

Properties

Most properties are copied, including calculated properties and rollup properties.

The following properties aren’t copied:

  • Dropdown select properties that use controlling properties with conditional options.
  • Data Agent logic (data entry, instructions, options, descriptions, smart property prompts).

View and edit access settings aren’t copied.

Property groups

Default and custom property groups are copied.

Property groups created by connected integrations aren’t copied.

Property validation rules

Fully supported.

Conditional property logic

Fully supported.

Object pipeline and pipeline stages

Pipelines, conditional logic rules, pipeline rules, and pipeline stages are fully supported.

The following pipeline assets aren’t copied:

  • Pipeline stage colors.
  • Board and card view customization.
  • Deal tags per pipeline.

Record customization

The following record customization assets are copied:

  • Default team record customizations for standard objects and custom objects.
  • Default cards from the card library.

The following record customization assets aren’t copied:

  • Preview customization.
  • Some custom cards and third-party app cards.

If a custom card depends on an unsupported asset type, for example it references a report which isn’t supported, the customization will copy without this custom card containing the report. It will need to be recreated in the sandbox.

Index page customizations

Views shared with everyone and team-based CRM views are copied.

If a view references a column or filter that is unsupported, that view will be skipped and flagged in your sandbox creation log with details.

Conversations inboxes

Inboxes and their names, team and user access, routing rules and any connected team email or form channels.

You’ll need to reconnect team email accounts in your sandbox before they can send or receive messages.

The following channels and assets aren’t copied:

  • Existing conversations
  • Chat channels
  • WhatsApp channels
  • Help desk channels
  • Channels connected through third-party apps
Automations

Please note: workflows and segments have cascading dependencies.

  • If a supported workflow depends on an unsupported asset, even indirectly, it’ll fail to copy. For example, a workflow that uses a segment that uses a lead scoring filter won’t be copied, because lead scoring is not supported.
  • To understand why an asset and any of its direct or indirect dependent assets failed to copy, review Failed assets in the sandbox creation activity log.

Asset type

What’s copied

Please note:

Workflows

Workflows that depend on supported assets are copied. This includes workflows that use automated marketing emails, segments, object definitions, and forms.

Workflows that depend on unsupported assets aren’t copied. For example, a workflow that uses a segment containing a lead scoring filter, won’t be copied.

Workflows with custom coded actions (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Workflows that use custom coded actions are copied.

If a workflows uses secrets, the secrets aren’t copied. Manually set up secrets in the sandbox after creation.

Workflows with webhooks (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Workflows that use webhooks are copied.

Update webhook URLs pointing to production endpoints in the sandbox to avoid unintended production triggers during testing.

Marketing

Asset type

What’s copied

Please note:

Automated marketing emails

Automated (including those that use drag-and-drop and custom templates and modules), A/B test automated, and automated transactional emails are copied.

Non-automated marketing emails and single send API emails aren’t copied.

Branded assets

Automated marketing emails, forms, and workflows assigned to any brand, including non-default brands, are copied.

Brand assignments are preserved in the sandbox.

Email footer addresses

Fully supported.

Email subscription types

Partially supported.

Visibility rules on subscription types aren’t copied.

Forms

Fully supported (including legacy forms).

Segments

Partially supported.

  • Some filters that depend on unsupported assets, such as lead scoring, feedback surveys, will cause the segment to fail to copy.

  • Segments that fail to copy may also cause dependent workflows to fail.

  • Review Failed assets in the sandbox creation activity log to understand why your segment failed to copy.

Sales

Asset type

What’s copied

Please note:

Playbooks

Fully supported.

If a playbook references an unsupported asset, manually add the missing dependency once the playbook is copied to the sandbox.

Sequences

Steps, associated email templates, delay logic, automation settings, and referenced assets such as documents are copied.

Enrolled contacts and performance data aren’t copied.

Content

Asset type

What’s copied

Please note:

Design folders

Fully supported.

Design Manager templates and modules.

Templates and modules are copied.

Website and landing pages, and blog posts (Sandbox creation now supports copying website, landing, and blog pages beta)

  • Page content.
  • HubSpot forms embedded in pages
  • Custom templates and marketplace templates from Design Manager
  • Custom modules.
  • Custom or standard personalization tokens.

Pages that use the following assets are copied without them. Manually add missing assets in the sandbox as needed.

  • CTAs
  • Non-HubSpot embedded forms.
  • Advanced menu type.
  • Footers
  • Campaign associations on landing and website pages and blog posts.
Account settings

Asset type

What’s copied

Please note:

Audit logs

Audit logs are available in sandboxes by default and are populated with sandbox activity.

Brands

Fully supported.

Teams

Team hierarchy are copied.

  • Users assigned to teams aren’t copied.
  • Sandbox users are managed independently from production. Super Admins can add users to sandboxes.

Users

Super Admins, Partner admins with elevated access, and users with Developer tools access permissions are copied.

Super Admins can add users to sandboxes.

Permissions and permission sets

User permissions for Super Admins, Partner admins with elevated access, and users with Developer tools access permissions are copied.

Super Admins can edit permissions in sandboxes.

Unsupported assets that can’t be copied to a sandbox

If an asset or configuration isn’t listed above, it isn’t copied to your sandbox at creation. This includes:

  • All Service Hub and Revenue Hub assets.
  • Reporting and dashboards.
  • Most account settings.
  • Connected apps and integrations.

To get these assets in a sandbox account:

  • Manually recreate it: set up unsupported assets directly in your sandbox. Because sandboxes are isolated from production, anything created there won’t affect the live account.
  • Review assets in beta and coming soon: review which asset types are in beta or coming soon.

Recover your inactive HubSpot account

If you try to log in and see a You have no accounts message, your account may have been deactivated.

Free accounts will be deactivated after 120 days of inactivity. This includes not logging in or using the HubSpot Sales extension. You then have 90 days to reactivate the account before it’s purged and can’t be recovered.

After 90 days of account inactivity, HubSpot will send you an email with a Sign in link to keep your account active. If you don’t intend to use HubSpot, you can delete your user.

If you need help with your deactivated account,submit an information form to the HubSpot support team.

Remove unused assets from your account with account cleanup

Identify opportunities to tidy up and declutter your HubSpot account with account cleanup. Use automated tools to clean up unused assets and keep your account organized. You can clean up unused assets such as marketing emails, posts, pages, and segments.

When cleanup automation is turned on, eligible assets will automatically be archived or deleted, depending on the tool. Automation will run once a month on the first of the month, automatically tidying up anything that became eligible within the last month.

Super Admin permissions are required to use account cleanup.

Understand criteria for asset cleanup

Before you set up automatic cleanup of unused assets, understand the criteria for each asset and the action that will be taken once you turn the settings on. In order for an asset to be cleaned up, all of the criteria must be met.

Asset

Criteria

Action taken

Companies

Last modified before the time you select in the Delete unused companies not modified in the last dropdown.

Companies meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Companies that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Contacts

Last modified before the time you select in the Delete unused contacts not modified in the last dropdown.

Contacts meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Contacts that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Deals

Last modified before the time you select in the Delete unused deals not modified in the last dropdown

Deals meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Deals that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Leads

Last modified before the time you select in the Not modified in the last dropdown

Leads meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Leads that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Orders

Last modified before the time you select in the Not modified in the last dropdown

Orders meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Orders that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Products

Last modified before the time you select in the Not modified in the last dropdown

Products meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Products that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Projects

Last modified before the time you select in the Delete unused deals not modified in the last dropdown

Projects meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Projects that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Tickets

Last modified before the time you select in the Not modified in the last dropdown.

Tickets meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Tickets that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Asset

Criteria

Action taken

Blog posts, landing pages, and websites

  • Last edited before time you select in the Archive draft [asset] older than dropdown menu.
  • Are in Draft status and don’t have a scheduled publish date.

Posts and pages meeting these criteria will be automatically archived (never deleted). Learn how to restore archived posts and pages.

Marketing emails

  • Last edited before time you select in the Delete unused marketing emails not mofied in the last dropdown menu.
  • Are in Draft status, don’t have a scheduled publish date, and aren’t referenced in workflows

Marketing emails meeting these criteria will be automatically deleted. Learn how to restore deleted emails within 90 days.

Reports

  • Last edited before time you select in the Not modified in the last dropdown menu.

Reports will be automatically deleted. Learn how to restore deleted reports for up to 14 days after deletion.

Segments
