Segments will be automatically deleted. Learn how to restore deleted segments for up to 90 days after deletion.

Workflows

  • Last edited before time you select in the Delete workflows older than dropdown menu.
  • The workflow is turned off.

Workflows will be automatically deleted. Learn how to restore deleted workflows for up to 90 days after deletion.

Asset

Criteria

Action taken

Custom objects

  • Last modified before the time you select in the Delete unused objects not modified in the last dropdown.

Custom objects meeting this criteria will be deleted. Learn how to restore deleted records for up to 90 days after deletion. Custom objects that meet the criteria in the future will be removed on the first of every month.

Turn on or edit automatic cleanup of unused assets

In the Monthly marketing asset cleanup section, you can view a preview of how many assets are eligible for cleanup and then set up automatic cleanup of those unused assets. You can also customize the cleanup criteria to fit your needs. Once you turn on the settings, it’ll remain on until you edit it.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Account Cleanup.
  • Click the CRM tab to locate CRM objects.
  • Click Set up or Edit for the asset you want to clean up.
  • Review the current policy in the Cleanup policy section and the assets that meet the criteria in the Monthly cleanup section.
  • Click to toggle the policy on/off.
  • To adjust the length of time that’s passed since the asset was edited:
    • Click Customize criteria.
    • Click the Archive/Delete [assets] not modified in the last dropdown menu. Change the criteria to consider assets that were last edited three months ago to three years ago.
    • To add additional filters, click + Add filter. In the pop-up box, click an option, then enter the details of the filter. Select the filter option. For example, you could archive all drafted marketing emails authored by a specific user.
    • Click + Add filter to add a filter to the existing AND group. When you set a filter with AND, assets must meet all the criteria in the filter group to be included.
    • Click + Add filter group to add a filter to a new OR group. When you select OR, assets must meet the criteria in at least one filter group to be included.
  • Click Save.

Please note: adding filters to reports isn’t available.

Review cleaned up assets

After you’ve set up automatic cleanup of unused assets, you can review which assets were cleaned up.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Account Cleanup.
  • Click the CRM tab to locate CRM objects.
  • Under each asset, you can view a total count of how many assets have been cleaned up. Click View to view the full list.
  • A new window will open on the Manage tab for that asset showing assets that were recently archived or deleted (depending on the criteria) so you can organize or restore the asset.

Revert cleanup automation

After the automatic cleanup runs, you can revert the most recent cleanup to restore archived or deleted assets. This is useful if assets were removed unintentionally or if you need to review recent cleanup changes. Only the most recent cleanup can be reverted. If an asset has been permanently deleted (e.g., after 90 days), it can’t be restored.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Account Cleanup.
  • In the top right, click Undo recent cleanup.
  • To revert the clean up and restore all assets, click Revert (#).
  • To revert the cleanup for individual assets, click the asset type to expand each asset. Select the checkboxes for the assets you want to restore. Click Revert selected (#).
  • In the pop-up box, select the Disable automation after revert checkbox to prevent the cleanup from running again.
  • Click Revert cleanup to confirm.

Review account limits

View HubSpot subscription entitlements and usage limits from the Account & Billing settings. The Other Limits page provides a consolidated view of the products, features, and usage-based capacities included with your subscription.

Use this page to understand what the account is entitled to based on subscriptions and add-ons, monitor how much capacity has been used, and identify when the account is approaching or has reached a limit.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to review account limits.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Users & Teams. You can also check each user’s permission sets and access on this page.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Account & Billing.
  • In the Account & Billing menu, select Other Limits.
  • Review information regarding features with limits depending on the account’s subscriptions and add-ons:

    • HubSpot phone numbers

    • Calling minutes

    • Conversational context

    • SMS messages

    • WhatsApp messages

    • API call usage

  • To increase the limits for the account, click Increase limits in the related section.

Review permission-related product updates

Review the latest permission-related product updates directly from Users & Teams settings. These updates appear in a side panel so you can understand recent permission changes without navigating away from the page. This helps you stay informed about updates while managing or reviewing your user permission setup.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to review permission-related product updates.

To view permission-related product updates:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • In the top right, click the campaignsIcon announcement icon.

  • In the right panel, review the update name, its priority, and the date it entered beta or went live.

    • To filter updates, click the Priority dropdown menu. By default, all priorities are selected. Clear the checkboxes next to the priorities you don’t want to view.
    • To view more details, click the name of the update.
    • To exit the right panel, in the top right, click X.

Review product updates and join beta features

The Product Updates page provides a centralized view of new and relevant updates, organized into sections with simplified navigation and direct actions. Browse updates tailored to your account activity, search for specific updates, and join betas.

This helps reduce the time spent reviewing updates and makes it easier to identify relevant changes, understand their purpose, and take action. For example, if your team frequently uses reporting tools, the page may highlight new reporting features so you can join the beta.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to opt an account into a beta feature.

Before you get started

Before reviewing product updates or enrolling in beta features, make sure you understand the requirements and limitations that apply.

  • Seeing an update on the Product Updates page doesn’t guarantee access to that feature. Beta availability can depend on your subscription, permissions, rollout stage, and approval by the product team.
  • Using or joining a beta gives you early access to functionality in your production environment under the HubSpot Beta Terms. Beta features are still being tested. Joining a beta doesn’t remove existing features or change your account settings. You may be asked to give feedback.
  • HubSpot may limit or close beta signups to control capacity, collect feedback, and avoid issues before a broader rollout. If a beta is closed or full, check its signup page periodically for availability. Enrollment may not reopen, and beta features may change or be cancelled before general release.
  • Private beta requests are reviewed manually and may be approved or denied. Approval timing varies.

Review product updates

Review product updates on the Product Updates page or with Breeze Assistant. Learn more about reviewing product updates with Breeze Assistant. Permissions-related product updates are available from your User & Team settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then select Product updates.
  • By default, you’ll be on the Discover tab. Review betas that are based on:
    • What’s trending across HubSpot accounts.
    • Feedback from your team (available when there are recommended updates).
    • Your team’s most-used tools (available when there are recommended updates).
    • Providing teams with more data.
    • What’s newly available.
  • To reorder the sections on this tab, click Customize.
    • In the right panel, click and drag the sections to the desired order.
    • Click Save.
  • Click the Your Betas tab to review the betas your account has opted into.
  • Click the Saved tab to review the betas you’ve saved.
  • Click the All Updates tab to review all betas.
  • Within the tabs:
    • To filter updates, click filtersIcon Filter icon. Click the dropdown menus to select options or select the checkboxes.
    • To search updates, enter keywords in the searchIcon search bar.
    • To favorite an update, click the star to the right of the update.
    • To view more information about an update, click the update’s name.

Opt into a private beta feature

Request access to private beta features. Requests will be reviewed by the relevant HubSpot product team.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then select Product updates.
  • At the top, click the All Updates tab.
  • Find the beta you want to join:
    • To search, enter keywords in the search bar.
    • To filter, click the filtersIconFilter icon, then select Private beta from the Stage dropdown menu.
  • In the row of the private beta feature you want access to, click Request Beta. To view more information about a feature, click the update’s name. To send a request, click Request Beta at the bottom of the right panel.
  • In the dialog box, to request the beta for only your user, select Enroll only me. To request the beta for the account (i.e. all users), select Enroll entire account.
  • Click to review the HubSpot Beta Terms.
  • Click the checkbox to acknowledge and agree to participate in the beta.
  • Click Request beta.

When your request in under review, the Request Beta button will be grayed out. Approval time varies.

If a request is approved, the feature will become available automatically in your account. If a request is denied, the Request Beta button will no longer be grayed out. Click it again to request to join the beta. Denials don’t prevent future requests.

Opt into a public beta feature

Opt your individual user or entire account into public beta features.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then select Product updates.
  • At the top, click the All Updates tab.
  • Find the beta you want to join:
    • To search, enter keywords in the search bar.
    • To filter, click the filtersIcon Filter icon, then select Public beta from the Stage dropdown menu.
  • To add the beta, click Join Beta at the bottom of the right panel.
  • In the dialog box, to opt only your user into the beta, select Enroll only me. To opt into the beta for the account (i.e. all users), select Enroll entire account.
  • Click to review the HubSpot Beta Terms.
  • Click the checkbox to acknowledge and agree to participate in the beta.
  • Click Join beta.

Please note: if you’re opted into a beta, but it’s not showing log out and log back in.

Edit beta enrollment

Leave a beta at any time or update if the enrollment applies only to you or all users in the account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then select Product updates.
  • At the top, click the Your Betas tab.
  • Click the update’s name.
  • To leave the beta, click Leave beta. In the dialog box, click Leave beta to confirm.
  • To change whether all users in the account are enrolled, click Edit access. In the dialog box, select Enroll only me or Enroll entire account, then click Save preferences.

Give feedback on a beta (BETA)

To give feedback on the betas you’re enrolled in:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then select Product updates.
  • At the top, navigate to Your betas.
  • In the row of the update, click Give feedback.
  • Select your feedback rating.
  • Enter any feedback comments in the text box (optional).
  • If you don’t want to share your feedback on a call with the HubSpot product team, clear the checkbox.
  • Click Submit.

Turn on weekly emails for product releases

To stay up to date on product updates, you can subscribe to product update emails. These emails will be sent to your user email address each week. This subscription applies only to you and will not send emails to other users in the account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account Defaults.
  • Click the Feature Releases tab.
  • Select the Turn on email notifications checkbox.

Put an account at the end of a gradual release

Subscription required An Enterprise account is required to put an account at the end of a gradual release.

Super Admins can place their accounts at the end of a gradual feature release. Gradual feature releases are when new functionality is made available to accounts incrementally over time. Placing an account at the end of a release gives you more time to test changes, update documentation, and train users.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account Defaults.
  • Click the Feature Releases tab.
  • Select the Put this account at the end of gradual feature releases checkbox. This will apply to future releases, not those currently in progress.

Sandbox assets eligible to be deployed to production

Once you have created your standard sandbox with eligible assets and tested changes, you can deploy eligible supported assets to production.

Learn which assets can be deployed, and which aren’t eligible to be deployed. You can also review this information in the Deployment behaviors banner as you’re setting up a deploy.

From the sandboxes page, view which asset types are newly released, in beta, or in development. Opt into beta features or share feedback on additional assets you’d like to be supported.

Please note: only new supported assets can be deployed to production. Edits to supported assets that were copied from production to sandbox can’t be deployed to production.

Supported assets that can be deployed to production

Asset type

What will get deployed

What won’t get deployed

Standard and custom objects

New custom properties including:

  • Property details

  • Field type

  • Rules

  • For new custom properties, the following settings aren’t copied and must be manually reconfigured in production:

    • Manage access
    • Sensitive Data settings

  • The following properties can’t be deployed, and won’t be listed as eligible:

    • Edits to HubSpot-defined properties
    • Sandbox edits to custom properties that exist in production won’t be listed as eligible

New property groups, including new custom properties belonging to the group.

Sandbox edits to property groups that exist in production won’t be listed as eligible.

New property conditional logic, including:

  • Controlling property
  • Dependent properties and required field logic.

Sandbox edits to property conditional logic that exist in production won’t be listed as eligible.

New object associations between two standard objects, a standard object and a custom object, or two custom objects, including:

  • Pair of labels logic

  • One-to-many label limit logic.

  • Custom association limits and custom association label limits.

  • Edits to standard object associations copied to the sandbox during the build process.

  • Sandbox edits to object associations that exist in production won’t be listed as eligible.

New object pipelines, including:

  • Stage name

  • Probability

  • Conditional stage properties

  • Pipeline settings:

    • Pipeline rules
    • Automate tab
    • Deal tags tab

  • Sandbox edits to object pipelines that exist in production won’t be listed as eligible.

Applicable to new custom objects:

  • Object name
  • Object description
  • Primary display property
  • Secondary display properties

Sandbox edits to custom objects that exist in production won’t be listed as eligible.

Automated marketing emails

Automated marketing emails including:

  • Marketing emails created in sandbox that are not yet present in production.
  • Newly created marketing emails that are tied to subscriptions that exist in production.

The following marketing emails can’t be deployed and won’t be listed as eligible for deployment:

  • Sandbox edits to automated marketing emails that exist in production
  • Regular marketing emails, this includes both published and drafted emails.
  • Automated marketing emails tied to a subscription that was created in sandbox.
  • Blog/RSS marketing emails
  • Marketing emails associated with Brands

Configurations on the Settings tab are not copied as part of the deployment and must be reconfigured in the production account.

Email footers

Email footer addresses or created in sandbox and not yet present in production.

Forms

Newly created forms in sandbox and not yet present in production.

Sandbox edits to forms that exist in production are not eligible for deployment.

Form settings won’t be copied as part of the deployment and may need to be reconfigured in the production account.

Segments

Active and static segments newly created in the sandbox, and not yet present in production if they use filters based on:

  • Object properties
  • Segment membership
  • Workflow enrollment

Any of the following marketing interaction filters:

  • Ads interactions
  • CTAs
  • Marketing campaigns
  • Marketing emails
  • Media interactions
  • Page view

The following segments won’t be listed as eligible to deploy:

  • Sandbox edits to segments that exist in production
  • Segments that use filters based on:

    • Import membership

    • Form submission

    • Behavioral events (Legacy)

    • CTAs (Legacy)

    • Marketing events

Segment settings aren’t copied as part of the deployment and must be reconfigured in the production account.

Workflows

Workflows newly created in the sandbox and not yet present in production that rely on:

  • New forms
  • New segments
  • New automated marketing emails
  • Object configurations

Workflows deployed to production accounts will automatically be set to Off.

The following workflows won’t be listed as eligible to deploy:

  • Workflows that are present in both production and sandbox accounts.
  • Workflows that have errors, or changes needed in the sandbox.
  • Workflows that have a direct or indirect connection with asset types not available to deploy yet (e.g., workflows that rely on feedback surveys)

Settings to organize workflows (e.g., folders, access, brand, and campaign labels) aren’t copied and must be manually reconfigured in the production account.

Search within your HubSpot account

Use the global search bar in the top left of your HubSpot account to search for assets, including CRM records, activities, blog posts, website pages, marketing emails, segments, dashboards, workflows, and campaigns. Search for and navigate to HubSpot tools, learning resources, and settings. Based on the available context for the top search result, Breeze, HubSpot’s AI, may generate a short summary and display suggested actions that help you continue your workflow.

If you’re searching the table on an object index page instead, learn more about the CRM search.

Search your HubSpot account

To search within your HubSpot account:

  • In the top left, click the search bar, then enter text to search for a specific asset or tool. If you want to find a company record, you can search by owner, industry, or address field. The companies that surface to the top are company results that you clicked on the most in the last 60 days inside global search.
  • To filter your search results, below the search bar, click an object name or tool name to include them in your search (e.g., click Contacts and Deals to include only contacts and deals in your search).
  • Click filter All filters to view all filters. Use the search bar to search for filters. Click a filter to add it to your search.
  • Recently used filters will be pinned below the search bar and in your search bar. Click filter All filters, then click the x to remove a filter.
  • To see all results for your search query, click See more categories in the bottom left. Within each category, to see more details, click See more.
  • Based on the available context for the top search result, Breeze, HubSpot’s AI, may generate a short summary and display suggested actions. Click the suggested action or breezeSingleStarIcon Ask Breeze to open Breeze Assistant.
  • Hover over the record to open a preview pane.
    • In the overview pane, for certain tools and records, you can complete quick actions:
      • To log a new call, email, or note on a record click the calling Call, email Email, or edit Add note buttons. Click the breezeSingleStar BBreeze Assistant button to summarize the record using Breeze Assistant.
      • To edit a website page or blog post, hover over the content, click the edit Edit button.
      • To access the recipients of a sent marketing email, click the lists View recipients button.
      • To analyze the performance of a list, click the generateChart View performance button.
      • To test or edit a workflow, click the test Test or settingsChange settings buttons.
  • Click the name of a returned asset to navigate to the record or tool.

Results will only appear if you search for values in searchable properties. Learn more about what data can be used to search for certain tools.

Set an account’s fiscal year in HubSpot

Set an account’s fiscal year to match your company’s financial calendar. This ensures that fiscal quarters, goals, forecasts, CRM filters, and reports use the same time periods your business uses for planning and performance tracking.

For example, if your fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, setting your fiscal year to July-June lets you filter records by the correct fiscal quarter and track sales goals and forecasts against your company’s actual reporting periods.

Change an account’s fiscal year

Permissions required Account Access or Super Admin permissions are required to change an account’s fiscal year.

By default, an account’s fiscal year is set to January to December.

To change your fiscal year:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Account Defaults.
  • Click the Fiscal year dropdown menu, then select the time frame that best represents your fiscal year.
  • In the dialog box, select the Confirm fiscal year checkbox and click Yes, change fiscal year to confirm the change.

Filter by fiscal year

Records

Use the fiscal year to filter records. For example, to review contacts that have been created during the current fiscal quarter:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Add a filter to your contact dashboard by clicking More filters.
  • In the right panel, in the is dropdown menu, select This fiscal quarter so far.
  • Click Apply filter.

The contacts dashboard will now display only the contacts who have been created so far in this fiscal quarter.

Reports

You can use your fiscal year to filter reports that were created using the custom report builder and that use a date picker property.

  • Follow the steps to create a custom report.
  • In the date picker field, select the Use fiscal year checkbox.

Set up and log in with passkeys

Passkeys offer a secure alternative to passwords. Passkeys use public and private key credentials to securely allow you to log in to your account using a compatible device with biometrics (face or fingerprints), PIN code, or a password manager. They’re fully supported by the three main platforms (e.g., Google, Apple, and Microsoft), as well as all major third party password managers and FIDO2 compatible hardware tokens like Yubikey. Unlike two-factor authentication, passkeys are generated, stored, and managed by your device, browser, or password manager, not by HubSpot or Super Admins.

Passkeys are created and managed by your device, browser, or password manager. Because HubSpot doesn’t store passkeys, recovery and management actions may require access to the device or service where the passkey is stored.

What are passkeys?

Passkeys provide an alternative login method that helps protect accounts from credential theft and phishing attacks. Passkeys address several common challenges associated with passwords

  • You don’t have to remember the password.
  • When you create a passkey through a browser or device prompt, it’s tied to where it’s stored—not directly to HubSpot, one specific browser, or your HubSpot profile name. If you use your computer password, it’s typically stored in your device’s built-in security manager, such as Mac passkeys or Windows Hello; other options include Apple Passwords or iCloud, Google Password Manager or a Google account, or another password manager.
  • Depending on the storage provider, it may sync across connected devices and apps, such as across your platform accounts like Google (Android) and Apple (iOS, MacOS), or your password manager.
  • It’s inherently multi-factor, combining something you have, and something you are. This eliminates the need for the legacy two-factor authentication methods that cause user friction.
  • It’s cryptographically generated and phishing-resistant because it is tied to the legitimate HubSpot site and can’t be reused on a fake login page.

How I use passkeys with HubSpot

How do I set up passkeys for my personal login?

To set up a passkey to use to log in to your account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General > Security.
  • Click Set up passkeys.
  • Depending on your settings, a passkey prompt will appear either natively on your device (e.g. MacOS, PC), using your browser, or a password manager.
  • Confirm your passkey setup.
  • The confirmed passkey will be displayed in your settings.
How do I use passkeys across my devices?

If using multiple devices (e.g., a MacBook and an Android device), you may need to set up more than one passkey. To set up an additional passkey:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General > Security.
  • Click Add another passkey.
  • Depending on your settings, a passkey prompt will appear either natively on your device (e.g. MacOS, PC), using your browser, or a password manager.
  • Confirm your passkey setup.
  • The added passkey will be displayed in your settings.
How do I log in with a passkey on my desktop?

Once a passkey is configured, you’ll see a passkey sign-in prompt on your login screen. To log in with a passkey:

  • On the login screen, enter your email address and click Next.
  • Click Sign in with a Passkey.
  • Confirm your passkey either through device biometrics, device PIN code, or prompt from your password manager.
How do I Log in with a passkey in the HubSpot app?

Once a passkey is configured, you’ll see a passkey sign-in prompt on your iOS or Android login screen.

Please note: passkeys can’t be set up on mobile, only on desktop. However, passkeys can be used to log in via desktop or mobile.

How do I login with a passkey in the HubSpot app on iOS?

To log in with a passkey on the iOS HubSpot app:

  • On the app, tap Log in.
  • Tap Log in with Passkey.
  • Confirm your passkey through your authentication method on your mobile device.
How to enforce passkeys as a login method for users

Super Admins can turn on passkeys as an option in allowed login methods, enforcing users to use passkeys to log in.

To turn on the passkey login method for users:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Security.
  • Under the Login tab, in the Configure allowed login methods section, click to toggle the switch on.
  • Select the Passkeys checkbox. Then click Save.
  • Select the date the login methods should be enforced from in the dialog box, then click Save. If selecting today’s date as the enforcement date, it may take up to 15 minutes before the login method is enforced.

Users affected by the change will receive an email notification of which login methods are allowed, and the enforcement date associated. The next time they are required to log in, they will be limited to the methods enforced.

Remove a passkey

The steps to remove a passkey depend on if two-factor authentication is configured in the account.

How do I remove a passkey for accounts with two-factor authentication?

If two-factor authentication is configured in your account:

  • On the passkey prompt, click Try another method.
  • Complete the login process using your configured 2FA method.
  • In your account settings, navigate to General > Security.
  • Remove the passkey from your security settings.
How do I remove a passkey for accounts without two-factor authentication?

If two-factor authentication isn’t configured in your account and you’re blocked by the passkey prompt:

  • On the passkey prompt, click Lost your passkey?
  • Complete the identity verification process using Persona on the device you usually login on.
  • After your identity is verified, in your account settings, navigate to General > Security.
  • Remove the passkey from your security settings.

Frequently asked questions

How do I know if I can use a passkey?

Nearly all current devices and browsers support passkeys. Learn more about detailed information on device and browser compatibility.

Can I use my passkey across multiple devices?

Passkeys are designed to be syncable, meaning they can span a platform ecosystem. If you use a Mac laptop, and have an iPhone, when you set up a passkey on your Mac, it saves to your iCloud keychain and syncs across so you can use them on all your Apple devices.

For those with cross-platform devices (e.g., PC and iPhone, Mac and Android), there are two options:

  • You can create multiple passkeys for your account so they can be used across your devices. So you could create a passkey on your Mac and also create one on your Android device. Both will appear in your security settings.
  • Use a cross-platform solution. Password managers are compatible across device platforms, allowing you to create one passkey to be used across all your devices.
Where can I learn more about passkeys?

It is generally recommended to use passkeys as a secure alternative to passwords. The standards we use for them come from the FIDO Alliance. You can read more about passkeys directly from them here.

Additionally, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), which produces guidelines and requirements on cybersecurity policies and controls for federal agencies, and often used as the standard for commercial organizations, published a supplement to NIST 800-63B -Digital Identity Guidelines — Authentication and Lifecycle Management. Incorporating Syncable Authenticators Into NIST SP 800-63B advises best practices on using passkeys in organizations.

I already don’t use a password for HubSpot to log in, should I switch to passkeys?

That’s a personal choice. The biggest step you can take in reducing risk and making it easier for you to access HubSpot is to not use a password. Ultimately, you’ll have to decide what works best for you and your organization.

I use Single Sign-On (SSO) to log into HubSpot, can I use passkeys?

If you are required to use SSO to login, you aren’t eligible to use passkeys. If your organization doesn’t require SSO, then you can.

Can I use passkeys on mobile (Android/iOS)?

Yes. You can use a passkey to log in to the HubSpot mobile app. Passkeys can’t be created in the HubSpot mobile app, but can be created from HubSpot desktop or through a browser or password manager prompt during login.

Are there any limitations in using passkeys with HubSpot?
  • Each user can only set one passkey per authenticator type.
  • Passkey login is not available with the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in.
I’ve lost access to my passkey, can I recover it?

If you’ve lost access to your passkey, complete the recovery process for the service where the passkey is stored. For example, if your passkey is saved in Apple iCloud Keychain, follow Apple’s account recovery steps. If you’re unsure where your passkey is stored and can still access your HubSpot account, review your saved passkeys in your security settings. If you’re unable to access your account using your passkey or 2FA, learn how to request a reset for 2FA and passkeys.

Some users may encounter errors during passkey recovery, such as:

  • Errors when removing a passkey.
  • QR code scanning issues.
  • Identity verification pages that don’t load correctly.
  • Recovery processes that complete without removing the passkey.

If you’re unable to verify your identity with Persona or the recovery process doesn’t resolve the issue, contact HubSpot Support. Account recovery may take 48 to 72 hours to help protect accounts from unauthorized access.

Why am I stuck in a passkey prompt or passkey loop?

If you’re repeatedly prompted for a passkey or returned to the passkey screen after attempting another login method, try the following:

  • Select Try another method and complete login using an available authentication method.
  • Verify that you’re using the device, browser, or password manager where the passkey was originally stored, such as Google Password Manager, iCloud Keychain, Windows Hello, or another password manager.
  • Confirm that the passkey is available and unlocked in your device or password manager.
  • If the prompt appears with a 2FA-related login error, the passkey may be conflicting with your 2FA state: this can happen when 2FA isn’t turned on for your user, or when 2FA is enforced and passkey login is prioritized for a user with both 2FA and a passkey. A known enforced-2FA/passkey issue has been fixed, but you may need to clear cache and cookies or try an incognito/private window to clear stale browser state.

If you’re still unable to access your account, click Lost your passkey? and follow the recovery process.

Why am I being asked for a passkey I don’t remember creating?

A passkey can’t be created without completing the passkey setup process. If you don’t remember creating one, the setup process was likely completed during a security prompt without recognition that it was passkey enrollment.

If you’re unsure where the passkey is stored, review the information shown in the passkey prompt. You can also check the device, browser, or password manager that you typically use to log in to HubSpot.

If login credentials are shared with multiple users, it’s possible another user set up the passkey. Passkeys are device and user-specific, so the user that set up the passkey is the only user that can login with the passkey. Sharing login credentials is against HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Terms.

Set up browser notifications

Browser notifications or push notifications appear in the corner of your browser when you’re not active in HubSpot. User notifications alert you when various actions or activities occur in your account.

HubSpot supports browser notifications from Google Chrome, Safari, Mozilla Firefox, and Microsoft Edge.
