  • ‘Your email can’t be tracked because you’re not logged in. Do you want to send your email without tracking?’
  • ‘There was an issue tracking this email. Check to make sure you’re connected to the internet and logged in to HubSpot.’

If you’re not seeing the add-in in Outlook, learn more about how to turn on HubSpot Sales in Outlook in your inbox.

Update Outlook

Ensure that your Outlook is updated and is the Click-to-run version. The Click-to-run version of Outlook is compatible with the add-in, while the Outlook installed from the Microsoft Store is not. Learn how to check the version of Outlook you are using and update your Outlook.

Configure firewall settings

Firewalls will need to allow communication with *.hubspot.com via HTTPS. Any updates will require communication with dl.getsidekick.com.

Tracking & notifications issues

Emails are not tracking

After sending a test email to hello@getsidekick.com, you may receive a response that your email was not tracked:

  • Ensure that the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in is installed.
  • Before sending your email, ensure that the Track email box is selected.
    • If the box was not selected, the tracking pixel used to track email opens will not be inserted in the email.
    • To check if the tracking pixel was inserted in a sent email, access the source content of the email and look for code similar to the following:

` img src=3D”http://t.sidekickopen69.com/e1t/o/5/f18dQhb0S7ks8dDMPbW2n0

x6l2B=9gXrN7sKj6v5 dlMTVfn3cs3M2y_-W2B89RP1pctGFW8mdf1T1k1H6H0?si=3D56803726671216=64&pi=3D01cd79e8 c6c3-455d-d1aa-5175f2b770de&ti=3Dundefined” style=3D”display:none!important” height=3D”1” width=3D”1” `

  • Emails sent in Plain Text mode cannot be tracked. If you see that emails are sent in plain text, switch to HTML mode:
    • Compose a new email in Outlook.
    • Under the Message Options tab in the Format group, click HTML or Rich Text.
  • If Outlook attaches the HubSpot tracking pixel via CID, the email will not be tracked. CIDs attach the pixel image to the email that you’re sending. Then it uses standard HTML image tags that reference the image to embed it in the email when the contact opens it. The tracking pixel therefore isn’t actually inserted into the email body, and the email is not tracked.
  • Try uninstalling, then re-installing the add-in.

After taking these steps, send another test tracked email to hello@getsidekick.com to receive a notification.

Common tracking error messages

You may encounter the following error message if you’re not logged in to your account:

Your email can’t be tracked because you’re not logged in. Do you want to send your email without tracking?

The resolve this error:

  • Log out of the Outlook desktop add-in by clicking HubSpot Sales in the inbox ribbon, then click Sign out.
  • Log back in to the Outlook desktop add-in.
  • If you’re still getting an error, follow these troubleshooting steps.

You may also encounter a general error that reads:

There was an issue tracking this email. Check to make sure you’re connected to the internet and logged in to HubSpot.

To resolve this error:

  • Log out of the Outlook desktop add-in by clicking HubSpot Sales in the inbox ribbon, then click Sign out.
  • Log back in to the Outlook desktop add-in.
  • Follow these troubleshooting steps.
  • Disconnect your device from your network, then reconnect.
  • Check to see if there are any security programs installed on your device that are blocking the desktop add-in.
Notifications are not appearing
  • Real-time notifications are sent through the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension. If you’re sending tracked emails using the Outlook desktop add-in and are not receiving real-time HubSpot Sales notifications, make sure your Chrome browser is running in the background with the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension installed.
  • Ensure that you are logged into the correct HubSpot Sales account when sending tracked emails using the desktop add-in. Learn how to change which account your email extension is connected to.

Login or loading issues

When you’re unable to log into the add-in, or the add-in does not load correctly, uninstall then reinstall the add-in.

Debug logs

When you’re working with HubSpot Support to troubleshoot the desktop add-in, you may be asked to provide debug logs. When you have the extension installed in Outlook, it will store information in report logs on your computer. These logs are saved each day the extension is used, and your file names refer to the usage date. If your extension isn’t functioning as expected, these logs help the support team take a deeper look into what’s happening with the add-in on your computer.

There are two ways to gather debug logs: from your PC’s Start menu and from your Outlook account.

Access debug logs from your PC’s Start menu
  • Copy and paste %appdata%into your Start menu in Windows, then press Enter.
  • A window will open with your debug logs. Add these logs as attachments to your support ticket.
Access debug logs from your Outlook account

  • In Outlook, click HubSpot Sales in the inbox ribbon and select Settings.

  • At the top of the settings dialog box, click Help. Then, select Send Logs.

  • This will open an email composition window with a HubSpot Outlook distribution email in the To field. Replace this with the email address of the Support specialist you’re working with and click Send.

Turn on connected inbox automation

When you connect your inbox to HubSpot, you can turn on inbox automation to use artificial intelligence (AI) features.

Permissions required Personal email access is required to connect your email account.

Understand inbox automation

These features allow the processing of data in email bodies, including email signatures, and metadata of all incoming and outgoing messages in your connected inbox.

Inbox automation powers features such as:

  • The automatic capture contact details in the CRM. Inbox automation features will attempt to read and automatically populate contact properties, such as first name, last name, and phone number. Learn more about which contact properties are populated and how to turn off this feature.
  • Recommended tasks based on email content. If an email body contains intent to follow-up, it’ll be flagged as a recommended task in your daily digest emails.

Please note: when inbox automation is turned on, only new emails will be scanned. It will not scan your past emails.

Turn on inbox automation

To turn on automation for an inbox that’s already connected:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General.
  • Click the Email tab.
  • Next to the email account you want to turn inbox automation on for, toggle the Inbox Automation switch on.

You can turn off inbox automation at any time from your email integration settings. Recommended tasks and contact details captured by automation will not be deleted if you turn off this setting.

Understand email open and click tracking

Track email opens and clicks to understand how recipients interact with your marketing and one-to-one emails. HubSpot records these interactions to help you analyze email engagement and uses tracking data in tools such as workflows, segments, and email optimization.

In this article, learn how HubSpot tracks email activity, what affects tracking data, and how to manage tracking for different email types.

Before you get started

Before you get started with email tracking, review consent requirements, limitations, and considerations.

Email tracking consent compliance

Some countries, such as France and Italy, require that your recipients provide consent before tracking email opens and clicks. These requirements apply to any sender emailing recipients in those countries, regardless of where the sender is based. Compliance responsibility sits with the sender. Review email tracking guidelines for obtaining prior consent and consult your legal team to determine the requirements and exemptions that apply to your specific situation.

If a recipient hasn’t provided consent, you can turn off open and click tracking for your account or for individual emails. The available options depend on the type of email you’re sending. Learn how to turn off tracking for marketing and one-to-one emails.

Please note: features that rely on email open or click events may have incomplete data or limited functionality when tracking is turned off. Learn more about how turning off tracking affects other HubSpot features.

Please note: while HubSpot provides these features, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific situation.

Limitations & considerations
  • If you’ve turned on data privacy settings in your account, one-to-one email opens and clicks can only be tracked for contacts with an assigned legal basis for data processing. Learn more about email tracking eligibility and data privacy settings.
  • Email client settings, forwarded emails, multiple recipients, and other factors may affect whether HubSpot records or attributes an open or click event. Learn more about factors that affect email tracking data.

Manage tracking by email type

You can track opens and clicks for both marketing emails and one-to-one emails. Tracking settings and requirements depend on the type of email you send:

  • Marketing emails: learn how to manage marketing email open and click tracking.
  • One-to-one emails: learn how to manage tracking for one-to-one emails.

How email tracking works in HubSpot

When email tracking is turned on, HubSpot applies the following methods to track email opens and clicks:

  • Email opens: HubSpot embeds an invisible one-pixel image, called a tracking pixel, in tracked emails. When the recipient opens the email, the tracking pixel loads, and the open event is recorded in HubSpot.
  • Email clicks: HubSpot rewrites links in the email using tracking URLs. When a recipient clicks a tracked link, the click event is recorded in HubSpot.

Email clicks can be tracked for both marketing emails and tracked one-to-one emails. The behavior and configuration of link tracking depend on the type of email you’re sending.

Marketing email clicks

When marketing click tracking is turned on, links included in the email are rewritten as tracking links. HubSpot generates unique tracking links for each recipient and email send. When a recipient clicks a tracked link, HubSpot records the click and redirects the recipient to the original destination.

If you’ve purchased the Brands add-on, you can manage the domain of the tracked links in your emails. Learn how to manage marketing email open and click tracking.

One-to-one email clicks

Subscription required A Sales Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to track one-to-one email clicks.

Seats required for certain features An assigned Sales seat is required to track one-to-one email clicks.

When you send a tracked one-to-one email from the CRM, a sequence, or the HubSpot Sales extension or add-in, you can track clicks on links included in the body of the email. When the recipient clicks a tracked link within the email, you can monitor the click in your activity feed, the contact’s activities, and by receiving real-time notifications.

When a link is tracked, HubSpot appends tracking information to the end of the hyperlinks included in your email. Tracked links use the following format: http://[xx].na1.hs-sales-engage[xx].com/...

When the recipient clicks a tracked link, the link temporarily redirects through a HubSpot-provided domain, [xx].na1.hs-sales-engage[xx].com, to track the click event. Then the link automatically redirects to the final URL destination (e.g., www.hubspot.com).

To use your own tracking domain for one-to-one email click tracking, connect a custom sales and service email tracking domain.

Please note:

  • You can connect only one custom sales and service email tracking domain per account.
  • To customize the domain for one-to-one email tracking, you must connect your own custom domain. HubSpot system domains are not supported for one-to-one email click tracking domain customization.

Email tracking eligibility and data privacy settings

If you’ve turned on data privacy settings in your HubSpot account, one-to-one emails can only be tracked for contacts with an assigned legal basis for data processing.

For example, if you send a one-to-one email to a contact with no known legal basis, the email may still be logged to the CRM, but email opens and clicks won’t be recorded. The logged email will display the following message: Tracking data is not available for this email. This email is logged but not tracked.

Learn more about how data privacy impacts email tracking with the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension and Office 365 add-in.

How tracking data is used in HubSpot

HubSpot uses email open and click events to report on email engagement and support other tools that rely on engagement data. How tracking data is used depends on the type of email you send and the HubSpot tools you’re using.

The following are a few examples of how tracking data can be used:

  • Analyze email engagement: use open and click events to measure metrics such as open rate, click-through rate, unique opens, and unique clicks. Learn more about analyzing marketing email performance and reporting on one-to-one emails.
  • Optimize marketing email sends: use open and click activity to support send time optimization, graymail suppression, and A/B testing.
  • Automate processes: use email opens and clicks as criteria for workflow enrollment, branches, or subsequent actions.
  • Segment and score contacts: use email open and click activity as criteria for active segments, lead scores, and deal scores.
  • Update CRM engagement data: use email open and click events to update engagement properties and record activities on contact records.
Impact of turning off email tracking

If email tracking is turned off, HubSpot doesn’t collect new open or click events for affected emails. Existing tracking data remains available, but features that depend on new open or click events may have incomplete data or limited functionality.

The following is a non-exhaustive list of features and tools that may be affected.

Feature or tool

Impact when tracking is turned off

Marketing email analytics

Metrics such as open rate, click-through rate, unique opens, and unique clicks may be missing or incomplete.

Marketing email health

Email health metrics or recommendations that depend on open or click engagement may be incomplete.

Send time optimization

Send time optimization may be less effective when new open or click engagement data isn’t available. Contacts without enough engagement data will receive the email at the beginning of the sending range.

Local time zone sending

A contact’s IP timezone may be missing or incomplete when new open or click engagement data isn’t available. This can affect marketing email time zone sending when the IP timezone is used as a fallback.

Graymail suppression

The Sends since last engagement property increases each time a marketing email is sent, regardless of tracking settings. When open and click engagement is not being tracked, graymail suppression may be less accurate.

A/B tests for marketing emails

A/B tests that determine a winner based on opens or clicks may default to the fallback version as the winning email.

Marketing email engagement optimization

Recommendations that depend on open or click engagement may be unavailable, incomplete, or less effective.

Sequences

Sequence steps or branches that rely on opens or clicks won’t be triggered by new tracking events.

Sequence email analytics

Metrics such as opens, clicks, and open/click rates may be missing or incomplete.

Workflows and automation

Workflow enrollment criteria, branches, or actions that rely on email opens or clicks won’t be triggered by new tracking events.

Workflow email trends

Workflow email performance statistics that rely on opens or clicks may be incomplete.

Active segments

Contacts won’t enter or leave active segments based on new open or click activity.

CRM engagement properties

CRM properties that rely on email open or click events won’t update with new tracking data.

Contact timeline

New email open or click activities won’t appear on the contact’s timeline. Logged emails will still appear separately.

Deal scores

Deal score inputs based on buyer engagement may be incomplete when they include email opens or clicks.

Lead scoring

Lead scores that use email open or click criteria won’t receive new tracking events for those criteria.

Attribution reporting

Marketing email click events from HubSpot click tracking won’t be available for attribution reports that rely on those interactions. Source and UTM-based attribution may still apply where configured.

Factors that affect email tracking data

Email tracking data may not always reflect a recipient’s exact behavior. Some factors can prevent HubSpot from recording an open or click, while others can affect which recipient the activity is attributed to.

Marketing and one-to-one emails

The following factors may affect tracking for both marketing and one-to-one emails:

  • Bot filtering: HubSpot doesn’t generate open and click events for one-to-one emails when activity is identified as non-human, such as bot activity or emails sent through forwarding addresses. You can also exclude suspected bot activity from email analytics by filtering bot activity. Learn more about bot filtering in marketing email analytics.
  • Forwarded emails: it’s not possible to determine whether a tracked email was forwarded to another recipient. Forwarded emails retain the original tracking pixel and tracking links. If another recipient opens or clicks a forwarded email, the activity may be attributed to the original recipient.
  • Email client settings: some email clients may block HubSpot’s tracking pixel, preventing email opens from being tracked. Opens may not be recorded in the following scenarios:
    • The email is composed or sent in plain text.
    • The recipient’s email client doesn’t automatically download images.
    • The recipient’s corporate email filter removes images from incoming emails.
    • The email is clipped before the tracking pixel loads (marketing emails only). Some email providers clip content above a certain size threshold, preventing the tracking pixel from loading until the recipient expands the full email. Learn how to review and decrease the size of marketing emails.
    • The recipient has a very strict spam filter that blocks images or link tracking from loading in emails, which may filter the email as spam.

If a recipient clicks a tracked link without loading the tracking pixel, HubSpot may infer that the recipient opened the email and record an open event.

One-to-one emails only

The following factors may affect tracking for one-to-one emails:

  • Multiple recipients: when you send a tracked email to multiple recipients, including recipients in the CC or BCC fields, each recipient receives the same tracking pixel. An open notification may be generated without identifying which recipient opened the email.
  • Self-opens: opening a tracked email from your sent folder may trigger a self-open notification. Learn how to block self-open notifications for the Chrome extension and Outlook desktop add-in.

Troubleshoot email open and click tracking

Review the following information if you experience unexpected open or click activity for tracked emails.

Why aren’t clicks being tracked in my emails?

Only hyperlinked, non-URL text can be tracked. If link clicks are not being tracked as expected, use descriptive text instead of a URL as the hyperlink text. For example, if you’re inserting a link to your website, hyperlink HubSpot website to www.hubspot.com. If you use www.hubspot.com as the hyperlink text, clicks won’t be tracked, even if the URL is hyperlinked.

Clicks in one-to-one emails can’t be tracked if the email is in plain text format.

Why is the open timestamp the same as the click or reply event?

Some email clients prevent HubSpot’s email open tracking pixel from loading. When this happens, HubSpot can’t directly record that the email was opened.

If the recipient later clicks a tracked link in the email or replies to it, HubSpot can infer that the email was opened. If the email previously had zero recorded opens, HubSpot may create one inferred open event.

The inferred open uses the same timestamp as the first click or reply because that’s the first confirmed engagement HubSpot receives. This inference only occurs when an email goes from zero opens to one open and isn’t repeated for subsequent clicks or replies, ensuring engagement metrics remain accurate.

Why am I not receiving open or click notifications for one-to-one emails?

If you’re not receiving any open or click notifications when sending a tracked email from your email inbox, learn how to troubleshoot tracking issues with your extension:

  • Troubleshoot the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension
  • Troubleshoot the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in
  • Troubleshoot the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in

To test link tracking, click the link from an email client and browser that does not have the HubSpot Sales extension installed to prevent the click notification from being suppressed. This can help you avoid notifications triggered by clicks on your own links, but this does not apply to other recipients of your email who may have HubSpot Sales installed.

Why am I getting multiple email opens for a specific one-to-one email?

If you receive more email open notifications than expected for a specific tracked email, it may indicate that the email was forwarded or that you copied and pasted a previously sent email. Because of privacy and security concerns, when an email is forwarded, HubSpot defaults to telling you that the original recipient opened the email again.

If you copied and pasted an email that you had previously sent, you also copied the original tracking pixel. The same tracking pixel would load for each recipient. It’s recommended to send personalized emails, which you can create from scratch in the CRM or your mail client, or to use sales email templates.

Sometimes, a single tracking image will load multiple times because of how the recipient views their emails. For example, a user could be on a server that dynamically changes that user’s IP address. If the image is loaded from multiple IP addresses, then the notifications may indicate that your emails were opened by multiple people.

Also, email clients like Outlook or Apple Mail have a preview pane as part of the inbox view. If recipients scroll over your email in their inbox, this can trigger an email open notification.

Why am I receiving one-to-one email notifications attributed to Someone?

If you send a tracked email to multiple email addresses (including CC and BCC), they all receive the same HubSpot Sales tracking image. HubSpot will still notify you of the email open, but HubSpot may not be able to determine which recipient opened the email.

If you also have data privacy settings turned on in your HubSpot account and a contact does not have a lawful basis for data processing, HubSpot Sales will track the multiple-recipient email, but the notifications will be anonymous. The Recent sales email open date, Recent sales email clicked date, and Last engagement date properties will also not be updated.

Please note: when you receive a Someone notification for an email open or click, HubSpot cannot attribute the corresponding email activity to a specific recipient, so it will not appear in any email activity reporting (e.g., a custom report).

Understand reply-only email logging rules

Email logging is based on your account’s contact email logging rules. If you’ve set your logging rules to Log replies only, use this guide to understand how replies are logged to the CRM.

To log all emails, learn how to configure contact email logging rules.

Requirements for a reply to log

When your contact email logging rules are set to Log replies only, replies to an email sent from your connected individual work email will log to the contact’s record in HubSpot. This includes one-to-one emails sent from the record in the CRM or using the HubSpot Sales extension or add-in.

The following must be true for the reply to log:

  • The original email was sent through the CRM or sent from your connected individual work email client with the HubSpot Sales extension or add-in installed and the Log checkbox selected.
  • The original email was not sent to an email address or domain listed in your never log list.
  • The individual work email address is connected when the reply is received.
  • The reply is sent to a individual work email connected by an active user.
  • The reply has the same subject line as the original email.

Email replies will log to the contact’s record timeline in your CRM. You can then navigate to the recipient’s contact record or one of the associated records to view the logged email.

If you receive a reply from an email address different from the original sender, the reply will be logged to the existing contact record associated with the email thread. No new contact records will be created.

One-to-one email replies sent from a record on desktop will be associated with the same records as the first email in the thread (e.g., if a contact was sent the first email, but not the thread’s replies, the contact will still be associated with the reply emails).

Requirements for attachments to log

The maximum file size for attachments to log for outgoing emails is 20 MB. This limit applies cumulatively across all email attachments, including inline attachments.

If your email server is running security software that scans attachments when receiving emails, HubSpot might not be able to log attachments that are included in email replies or incoming emails sent to your team email address. For example, if your Office 365 servers are running Advanced Threat Protection with Dynamic Delivery turned on, the attachments may not log.

Replies not logging as expected

If your reply doesn’t log as expected, learn more about some of the common reasons why this occurs. In some cases, if the reply didn’t log, you can forward it to the record timeline in the CRM.

New incoming emails

Incoming emails sent to your connected individual work email will not log to HubSpot if they do not meet the requirements for logging.

If a contact sends you a new email that is not part of an existing thread, this email will not log to HubSpot and for non-contacts, a new contact record will not be created. When you reply to this email and select the Log checkbox or include the BCC address, your outgoing reply will log but the contact’s original email will still not appear in HubSpot. Subsequent replies to this thread will log as long as your individual work email is connected.

Replies with a different subject line

If a contact replies to an email but changes the subject line, it’ll no longer be considered an email in the existing thread and won’t log.

Replies to emails after changing inbox providers

If you change inbox providers while you still have active threads using your previous email address, email replies will stop logging to HubSpot. In addition, if you’re using sequences, contacts who are currently enrolled in a sequence will not be automatically unenrolled because HubSpot can no longer detect the replies. Reconnect your inbox using the correct provider to log replies.

Learn more about reconnecting your inbox after switching your inbox provider.

Connected individual work email using wrong email provider

Make sure to connect your individual work email using the correct email provider type. Your email provider is the service that enables you to send and receive emails. Common email providers include Gmail and Office 365.

Confirm which email provider your email address is hosted with, then follow the instructions to connect to HubSpot with that provider. If you’re not sure which email provider your email address is hosted with, check with your IT administrator. If you don’t connect using the correct provider, emails won’t log.

Troubleshoot reply logging

If you meet the requirements for reply logging, and your reply does not fit into one of the situations listed above, learn how to get help from HubSpot. Before reaching out, it is recommended to have an example of a contact record where the reply did not log as expected and the email headers from the reply received in your email account. Learn how to collect the email headers from some common email providers, or work with your IT resource to retrieve the headers.

Uninstall the HubSpot Sales email extension

If you no longer want to use the HubSpot Sales email extension in your inbox, you can uninstall the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension for Gmail, the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in, or the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in following the instructions below.

Uninstall the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension

  • In the top right of your Chrome browser, click the three vertical dots icon. Then select Extensions > Manage Extensions.

  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales extension and click Remove.

  • After removing the extension from Chrome, clear your Chrome browser cache to remove HubSpot Sales completely.

Uninstall the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in

Uninstall the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in from Outlook’s add-in settings. Learn more about accessing add-ins in Outlook. If you’re using the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in on a Mac, you can also uninstall the add-in from your Office 365 account.

  • In Outlook, navigate to your add-in settings.
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Get Add-ins.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select Get Add-ins.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select Get Add-ins.
  • In the left sidebar menu of the Add-Ins for Outlook menu, click My add-ins.
  • In the Store Add-ins section, navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in. Click the three horizontal dots and select Remove.

Uninstall the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in

  • In Windows, click the Start menu.

  • Search for Uninstall a program or Add and remove programs.

  • Search for or navigate to HubSpot Sales for Outlook.

  • Click Uninstall.

  • In the dialog box, click Yes or Uninstall.

  • When the uninstallation is complete, click OK.

  • Complete the uninstallation process.

Uninstall the HubSpot Sales for Windows tray app

Please note: on Jan. 25, 2024, the HubSpot Sales for Windows tray app was sunset. Email notifications will instead be delivered through HubSpot’s browser-based notification system. Learn more about how to manage HubSpot browser notifications.

  • In Windows, click the Start menu.
  • Search for Uninstall a program or Add and remove programs.
  • Search for and select HubSpot Sales for Windows.
  • Click Uninstall.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes or Uninstall.
  • When the uninstallation is complete, click OK.
  • Complete the uninstallation process.

Uninstall remnants

You can first try deleting the HubSpotWebView2_ folders.

  • Copy and paste %localappdata% into your Windows Start menu.
  • Delete all of the HubSpotWebView2_ folders.

You can also try deleting the contents from the 2.0 folder:

  • Copy and paste %localappdata%\2.0 into your Windows Start menu.
  • From the search results, click to open the 2.0 folder and delete all contents.
  • If deleting the contents of the folder doesn’t work, you can try deleting the entire 2.0 folder. This step should only be done as a last resort:

Please note: deleting the 2.0 folder may affect other ClickOnce apps you have installed. This should only be done as a last resort.

- Navigate to the [Microsoft Registry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/registry) and locate the folder at the following path: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\Software\Microsoft\Windows\
- CurrentVersion\Deployment\SideBySide\2.0.

- Right-click the folder and select Delete.

Uninstalling the sales extension vs. disconnecting your inbox

Uninstalling the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension, the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in, or the Outlook desktop add-in is separate from disconnecting your authorized inbox in HubSpot.

When you uninstall the extension or the add-ins, you lose access to the HubSpot Sales features in your inbox. You can still manually log emails using your BCC address. With your inbox still connected, you can still send emails from contact records in HubSpot and continue using your sales tools that require a connected inbox in your HubSpot account.

Use contact profiles with the Outlook desktop add-in

Access your CRM contact information directly from your Outlook inbox with contact profiles. Use contact profiles to review contact information and recent sales activities. You can also create tasks and associate companies, deals, or tickets right from within your Outlook inbox.

This article is for the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in, which is in maintenance mode. It’s recommended to use the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in to access HubSpot’s sales tools from Outlook for Mac, PC, or Outlook on the web. Learn how to use contact profiles with the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in.

Please note: due to the significant changes introduced by Microsoft as part of the new Outlook for Windows, HubSpot will no longer actively develop or improve the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in. While the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in is still available in the legacy Outlook for Windows and will continue to be supported, it’s highly recommended that you activate the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in instead. If you’re using the Outlook desktop add-in, the HubSpot Office 365 add-in will automatically be installed if you switch to the new Outlook for Windows. Learn more in this HubSpot Community post.

Access contact profiles

To access contact profiles using the Outlook desktop add-in:

  • In your Outlook inbox, compose a new email and add a recipient.

  • At the top of Outlook, in the main ribbon, click Contact Profiles. Your recipient’s contact information will be available in the task pane if they’re already a contact in your CRM.

  • To add a new contact to your CRM, in the task pane, click Add to HubSpot.

    • Enter the contact information in the contact create form.
    • At the bottom, click Create.

  • To search for an existing contact, enter a name or email address in the search bar at the top of the task pane.

Please note: if data privacy settings are turned on in your account, the contact profiles will always be turned on in your Outlook inbox.

Use contact profiles

In a contact profile, you can review contact details and recent sales activities. You can also edit contact properties, create tasks, and associate new or existing companies, deals, or tickets.

  • In your Outlook inbox, compose a new email and add a recipient.

  • At the top of Outlook, in the main ribbon, click Contact Profiles.

  • To view contact details, click to expand the About this Contact section.

  • To edit a property, click a property to edit. Depending on the property type, edit the value:

    • For a text or number property, enter your value in the text box.
    • For an enumeration or user property, select a value.
    • At the bottom, click Save. Learn more about editing property values.

  • To view the contact’s recent sales activities, click the Activity tab. This section will only display calls, emails, email tracking activity, page views, and lifecycle stage changes.

Create tasks

You can create a task that’ll be associated with the contact directly from the contact profile. The task will also appear on the record index page and on the contact’s record in the CRM.

  • In your Outlook inbox, compose a new email and add a recipient.
  • At the top of Outlook, in the main ribbon, click Contact Profiles.
  • To review any existing tasks that you have created or that are assigned to you, click to expand the Tasks section in the side pane.
  • To create a new task, click Add.
  • In the side panel, enter the task name and select a due date for the task.
  • At the bottom, click Create Task.
Associate new or existing companies, deals, or tickets

Associate new or existing companies, deals, or tickets directly from the contact profile. The newly created record will be displayed on the contact profile in Outlook, the contact record in your CRM, and on the object’s index page.

  • In your Outlook inbox, compose a new email and add a recipient.

  • At the top of Outlook, in the main ribbon, click Contact Profiles.

  • To view records associated with the contact, scroll down to the Companies, Deals, or Tickets section.

    • Click to expand the section to view any existing records already associated with the contact.

  • To create and associate a new record, click Add.

    • On the Create new tab, enter the property values in the create form. To set up which fields appear in a create form, learn more about customizing the create form for each object.

    • Enter property values for your new record. If you want to set an association label, you’ll need to set the label after the record is created.

    • Click Create, or to create and associate another record, click Create and add another.

  • To associate a record that already exists in your CRM, click Add.

    • Click the Add existing tab.
    • Search for the record you want to associate, then select the checkbox next to the record name.
    • Click Next.
    • To label the record association (Professional and Enterprise only), click +Add association label to set labels that describe the relationship between the records.
    • Click Save.

Use sales tools in Gmail with the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension

Access sales tools directly from your Gmail inbox with the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension. Enroll a contact in a sequence, use templates, and insert meeting links without leaving Gmail. Integrating these tools into your workspace helps you streamline outreach and track communications in your HubSpot account. For example, you can send a tracked email to a lead using a template and create a follow-up task directly from your inbox.

To customize the sales tools that display when composing an email, learn how to customize the sales toolbar.

Before you get started

  • To access sales tools in Gmail, install the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension.
  • To use the sequences tool in Gmail, you must have a connected individual work email.
  • To use the meetings tool in Gmail, you must have a connected calendar.

Documents

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to insert a document into an email.

Insert a document link to track who’s viewing your documents and see the data in HubSpot.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.

  • In the sales toolbar, click the More dropdown menu and select Documents.

  • Hover over a document to access a preview of the document’s content. Select a document to add to your email body, or use the search bar to search for a document by name.

  • To navigate to your documents dashboard in HubSpot, click View all.

  • When you select a document, a link to the document will appear in the email body. To edit the hyperlink text, click the link and select Change.

  • In the dialog box, enter the link’s text in the Text to display field. Then click OK.

Meetings

Insert a meeting link in an email so your recipients can access your scheduling page. You can also insert proposed times directly into the email so recipients can select an available time slot directly from the email.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.

  • In the sales toolbar, click Meetings and select Scheduling links. Then select a meeting link.

  • The name of the meeting will be inserted into your email, and it’ll be hyperlinked with your scheduling page URL. To change the link text that recipients see, click the scheduling link in the email body and select Change.

  • In the dialog box, enter the link’s text in the Text to display field. Then click OK.

Payments

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to insert a payment link.

After you’ve set up the payments tool to share payment links with your contacts, you can insert a payment link directly into an email.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.

  • In the sales toolbar, click the More dropdown menu, then select Payments.

  • Select the payment link you want to share in the email.

  • Click Send.

The email recipient can then click the payment link to complete the checkout process. Learn more about collecting payments in HubSpot.

Prospecting agent

Subscription required A Sales Hub subscription is required to enroll contacts in the prospecting agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are consumed when a contact is enrolled for prospecting.

Permissions required Prospecting agent assignment permissions are required to enroll contacts in the prospecting agent.

Enroll CRM contacts in the prospecting agent directly from your inbox to manage outreach and execute personalized communication without navigating away from Gmail. Learn more about setting up and using the prospecting agent.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

To enroll a contact in the prospecting agent when composing an email:

  • In Gmail, compose a new email or navigate to an existing email thread.

    • The email recipient must be an existing contact in your CRM.

  • In the sales toolbar, click More and select Enroll in Agent.

  • Continue to confirm the prospecting agent guardrails to enroll the contact in the prospecting agent.

Sequences

Subscription required A Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to enroll contacts into a sequence.

Seats required An assigned Sales or Service Seat is required to enroll contacts into a sequence.

Permissions required Sequences and Communicate permissions are required to enroll contacts in sequences.

A connected individual work email is needed to enroll contacts into sequences from Gmail.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.
  • In the sales toolbar, click Sequences.
  • In the dialog box, use the search bar to search for a sequence by name, or click the Owner dropdown menu and select a filter option.
  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it will show the sequences that you last sent. To sort your sequences, click a column header.
  • Hover over a sequence and click Select.
  • In the next window, customize the body of your sequence templates and your sequence settings. Learn more about personalizing your sequence email content.
  • Specify the email template you want the sequence to start at, set delays between sequence steps, and specify times that you’d like each sequence template to send. When you’re ready, click Start sequence.

Snippets

When you’re composing an email in Gmail, insert a block of text using a snippet.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.

    • If you add an email recipient after you insert a snippet, any personalization tokens included in the snippet will update with the recipient’s information.

  • In the sales toolbar, click the More dropdown menu and select Snippets.

  • Select a snippet to add to your email body, or use the search bar to look up a snippet name or shortcut.

  • To navigate to your snippets in HubSpot, click View All.

Tasks

Create a follow up task after you send an email in Gmail.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.

  • In the sales toolbar, click Tasks.

  • Select a task to be created when the email is sent, or click Custom Follow Up Task.

  • In the dialog box, enter a name for the task in the Task Title field, then use the date and time picker to select the date and time when the task is due. Click Save.

  • Click Send to send your email and create the task.

Please note: if you use the Scheduled Send option, a task will not be created. You must manually send the email in order to create a follow up task.

Templates

Create or insert sales templates in Gmail.

  • Compose a new email in Gmail and add a recipient.

    • If you add an email recipient after you insert a template, any personalization tokens included in the template will update with the recipient’s information.

  • In the sales toolbar, click Templates.

  • To create a new template, click Create new. In the template editor, set up your template, then click Save.

  • To insert a template, click the name of a template. Recently used templates will display in the dropdown menu. You can also use the search bar to search for a template by name or click View all to view all templates.

  • To edit a template, hover over the template, then click Edit. Update the template content in the editor, then click Save.

  • Once you select a template, it’ll be added to your email subject and body.

If you notice that your Gmail email signature is removed after inserting a template, add the following HTML around your signature’s existing HTML:

<div class="gmail_signature" dir="ltr">
{Your Email Signature}
</div>
Save an email as a template

After sending an email in Gmail that you want to use again, you can save it to your HubSpot account as a template.

  • Open Gmail and locate the sent email you’d like to save as a template.

  • At the top of the email, click salesTemplates Save icon.

  • In the dialog box, enter a name for the template and make edits as needed.

  • Click Save template.

Use sales tools in Outlook with the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in

Access the HubSpot sales tools in your inbox when composing emails with the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in.

If you’re using the Outlook desktop add-in, learn how to use sales tools with the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in.

Before you get started

  • To access sales tools in Outlook, connect an individual work email and install the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in.
  • To use the meetings tool in Outlook, you must have a connected calendar.

Documents

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to insert a document into an email.

To insert a document into an email using the Office 365 add-in:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook and enter the email recipient.
  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.
  • In the task pane, click Documents.
  • In the dialog box, search for a document by name. Or click the dropdown menu beside the search bar to filter your documents by All, Created by my team, Created by me, and Recent.
  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it’ll show the documents that were last used by the user viewing the modal. You can sort your documents by the Last used at or the Created at column.
  • Select the Require an email address from all other viewers checkbox if you want to collect an email address from anyone else besides your recipient who views the document.
  • Hover over the document you want to use and click Select.
  • A link to the document will be inserted into your email.

Meetings

To insert a meeting link into an email using the Office 365 add-in so that your contacts can access your scheduling page:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook.
  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.
  • In the task pane, click Meetings and select one of your scheduling pages. You can also insert proposed times directly into the email so your contacts can select an available time slot directly from the email.

The name of your meeting will appear in your email. It’ll be hyperlinked, so when a prospect clicks it, they’ll be brought to your scheduling page.

Payments

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to insert a payment link.

If you set up the payments tool to share payment links with your contacts, you can insert a payment link directly into an email using the extension.

  • Compose a new email in Outlook.
  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.
  • In the task pane, click Payments.
  • Select the payment link you want to share in the email.
  • Click Send.

Prospecting agent

Subscription required A Sales Hub subscription is required to enroll contacts in the prospecting agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are consumed when a contact is enrolled for prospecting.

Permissions required Prospecting agent assignment permissions are required to enroll contacts in the prospecting agent.

Enroll CRM contacts in the prospecting agent directly from your inbox to manage outreach and execute personalized communication without navigating away from Outlook. Learn more about setting up and using the prospecting agent.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

To enroll a contact in the prospecting agent from Outlook:

  • In your Outlook inbox, compose a new email or navigate to an existing email thread.

    • The email recipient must be an existing contact in your CRM.

  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:

    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.

  • In the task pane, in the Contact profile section, click Enroll to agent.

  • Continue to confirm the prospecting agent guardrails to enroll the contact in the prospecting agent.

Sequences

Subscription required A Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to enroll contacts into a sequence.

Seats required An assigned Sales or Service Seat is required to enroll contacts into a sequence.

Permissions required Sequences and Communicate permissions are required to enroll contacts in sequences.

To enroll a contact in a sequence using the Office 365 add-in:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook and enter the email recipient.
  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.
  • In the task pane, click Sequences.
  • In the dialog box, use the search bar to search for a sequence by name. Or click the dropdown menu beside the search bar to filter your sequences by All, Created by my team, Created by me, and Recent.
  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it’ll show the sequences that were last sent by the user. You can sort your sequences by the Last used at or the Created at column.
  • Hover over the sequence you want to enroll your contact in and click Select.
  • In the next dialog box, customize your sequence’s content and settings.
    • If you’re a Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise user, you can use sales email recommendations and surface insights about your contact to help tailor your email content. Click the Low personalization alert to review the suggestions.
  • Specify the start email and send date/time.
  • Click Start sequence to enroll the contact.

Snippets

To insert a snippet into an email using the Office 365 add-in:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook and enter the email recipient.
  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.
  • In the task pane, click Snippets and select one of your snippets.
  • The most recently used snippets will appear. Select a snippet to add to your email body, or use the search bar to look up a snippet name or shortcut.
  • To navigate to your snippets dashboard in HubSpot, click Manage snippets.

Templates

To insert a template using the Office 365 add-in:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook and enter the email recipient.
  • Navigate to the HubSpot Sales add-in:
    • Classic Outlook for Windows or Mac: in the main ribbon, click Sales Tools.
    • New Outlook for Mac: in the main ribbon, click the three horizontal dots and select HubSpot Sales.
    • New Outlook for Windows or Outlook on the web: in the main ribbon, click Apps and select HubSpot Sales.
  • In the task pane, click Templates.
  • At the top of the dialog box, use the search bar to search for a template by name. Or click the dropdown menu beside the search bar to filter your templates by All, Created by my team, Created by me, and Recent.
  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it’ll show the templates that were last sent by the user viewing the modal. You can sort your templates by the Last used at or the Created at column.
  • Hover over the template you want to use and click Select.

Use sales tools with the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in

Access the HubSpot sales tools directly in your inbox when composing emails with the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in installed.

If you’re using the Office 365 add-in, learn how to use sales tools with the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in.

Please note: due to the significant changes introduced by Microsoft as part of the new Outlook for Windows, HubSpot will no longer actively develop or improve the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in. While the HubSpot Sales Outlook desktop add-in is still available in the classic Outlook for Windows and will continue to be supported, it’s highly recommended that you activate the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in instead. If you’re using the Outlook desktop add-in, the HubSpot Sales Office 365 add-in will automatically be installed if you switch to the new Outlook for Windows. Learn more in this HubSpot Community post.

Before you get started

  • To use your meetings tool in Outlook, you must have a connected calendar.
  • To use your sequences tool in Outlook, you must have a connected individual work email.

Snippets

To insert snippets in your emails using the Outlook desktop add-in:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook and add a recipient.
  • In the message ribbon, click Sales Tools > Snippets, then select a snippet. Click Manage snippets to go to your snippets dashboard in your HubSpot account.
  • Or, right-click in the body of your email and select Snippets, then select the snippet you wish to insert.

Templates

To insert a template using the Outlook desktop add-in:

  • Compose a new email and add a recipient.

  • In the message ribbon, click Sales Tools > Templates.

  • At the top of the dialog box, use the search bar to search for a template by name or click the dropdown menu beside the search bar to filter your templates by All, Created by my team, Created by me and Recent.

  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it will show the templates that were last sent by the user viewing the modal. You can sort your templates by the Last used at or the Created at column.

  • Hover over the template you want to use and click Select.

Documents

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to insert a document into an email.

To insert a document using the Outlook desktop add-in:

  • Compose a new email and add a recipient.

  • In the message ribbon, click Sales Tools > Documents.

  • In the dialog box, search for a document by name or click the dropdown menu beside the search bar to filter your documents by All, Created by my team, Created by me, and Recent.

  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it will show the documents that were last used by the user viewing the modal. You can sort your documents by the Last used at or the Created at column.

  • Select the Require an email address from all other viewers checkbox if you want to collect an email address from anyone else besides the original recipient who views the document.

  • Hover over the document you want to use and click Select.

  • A link to the document will be inserted into your email.

Meetings

To insert a meeting link using the Outlook desktop add-in so a contact can access your scheduling page:

  • Compose a new email in Outlook and add a recipient.
  • In the message ribbon, click Sales Tools > Meetings, then select one of your scheduling pages. Click Manage links to go to your meetings dashboard in HubSpot. You can also insert proposed times directly into the email so your contacts can select an available time slot directly from the email.
  • Alternatively, you can right-click in the body of your email and select Meetings, then select the scheduling page you wish to insert.

The name of your meeting will appear in your email. It will be hyperlinked, so when a prospect clicks it, they’ll be brought to your booking page.

Sequences

Subscription required A Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to enroll contacts into a sequence.

Seats required An assigned Sales or Service Seat is required to enroll contacts into a sequence.

Permissions required Sequences and Communicate permissions are required to enroll contacts in sequences.

To enroll a contact in a sequence using the Outlook desktop add-in:

  • Compose a new email and add a recipient.

  • In the message ribbon, click Sales Tools > Sequences.

  • In the dialog box, use the search bar to search for a sequence by name or click the dropdown menu beside the search bar to filter your sequences by All, Created by my team, Created by me, and Recent.

  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it will show the sequences that were last sent by the user viewing the modal. You can sort your sequences by the Last used at or the Created at column.

  • Hover over the sequence you want to enroll your contact in and click Select.

  • In the next dialog box, edit your sequence’s content and settings. Click the Start dropdown menu and select the first step of the sequence. Specify the start time of the first email send, then click the Advanced settings dropdown menu to specify when each subsequent email in the sequence should be sent.

  • Click Start sequence to enroll the contact.

Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension across the web

Access the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension on all web pages. When activated, a sidebar will display in your Chrome browser on every website. The sidebar will match domain names to existing company profiles, or allow you to create new company records in HubSpot. You can enroll contacts in sequences, send emails, receive calls, and view HubSpot records directly from your lead’s websites, Salesforce or Gmail.

Please note: you must be using the most up to date version of the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension to access it across the web.

Access and manage your HubSpot Chrome extension

To access the extension, click the sprocket HubSpot sprocket icon in the top right of the browser’s address bar. From here, you can view your activity feed or configure your settings.

If the HubSpot Chrome extension isn’t appearing in your browser’s address bar, you may need to pin the extension to your toolbar.

Activity feed

On the Activity feed tab, you can review a list of your sales activity notifications. Real-time notifications are triggered when a lead revisits your site, a tracked email is opened or clicked, a shared document is viewed, or a meeting is booked.

To follow up with a contact in HubSpot, hover over the activity and click Call. Or, click the More dropdown menu and select from the following:

  • Email: send a sales email to the contact.
  • Create task: create a task on the contact record.
  • Create note: log a note on the contact record.
  • Schedule: schedule a meeting with the contact.
  • Turn off thread notifications: mute new notifications for a specific email thread.

Learn more about the activity feed.

Settings

On the Settings tab, you can control where your extension is turned on, exclude websites, and select an account to use the extension with.

Extension enablement

In the Extension enablement section, you can enable the extension to work on Gmail, Salesforce and All other websites.

The extension can only access data on sites where it’s enabled. For example, if you’ve enabled the extension for Gmail and Google Calendar, it’ll only have access to data on those sites. To allow the extension to access data across other websites, you must enable the setting All other websites. You can also prevent the extension from running on specific sites.

  • Gmail: the HubSpot Chrome extension is enabled by default for gmail.

  • Google Calendar: toggle the switch on to access the HubSpot Chrome extension in your Google calendar.

  • Salesforce: to access the HubSpot Chrome extension in Salesforce:

    • Toggle the switch on.
    • In the dialog box, click Allow.

  • All other websites: to access the HubSpot Chrome extension across the web, toggle the switch on.

Website exclusions

In the Website exclusions section , you can prevent the HubSpot Chrome extension from running on specific sites:

  • Enter the URL of the website you want to exclude.
  • Click Add.
  • The following sites have been excluded by default: facebook.com, youtube.com, instagram.com, google.com, and hubspot.com.
  • To remove a website from the exclusion list, click the X beside the website URL and refresh the page.
Turn on Breeze Assistant

To access Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s AI conversational assistant, toggle the Enable Breeze Assistant switch on.

Use Breeze Assistant to request information, generate content, and perform actions. Learn more about using Breeze Assistant.

Turn on Calling

To access calling in the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension, toggle the Enable Calling switch on. When this setting is turned on:

  • Inbound calls can be received in the HubSpot browser without keeping a dedicated tab or window open. Your inbound ring preference must be set to ring in HubSpot browser.
  • Outbound calls dialed from the HubSpot browser stay active without keeping a dedicated tab or window open.

Learn more about how to set up calling.

Accounts in use

In the Accounts in use section, you’ll see the HubSpot account you’re connected to marked as In use. To select a different HubSpot account:

  • Click the Select an account dropdown menu
  • Select an account.
  • In the dialog box, click Change account.
Additional help

In the Additional help section, you can review HubSpot’s Customer Terms of Service from the extension settings, uninstall the extension or submit feedback on the extension directly from the extension settings.

Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension across the web

When you’re viewing a lead’s company website, view the company information or add a new company to your CRM without leaving the website.

Add companies

Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension to add new companies to your CRM while browsing the web. Users in a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise account can view and create companies using enriched company data.

  • On a company website, click the sprocket HubSpot sprocket icon in the upper right.
  • In the right panel, click Add to HubSpot.
  • In the Create Company form, enter the company information. If your account’s enrichment settings are configured for companies, the company information will be populated automatically (Starter, Professional, or Enterprise accounts only).
  • Click Create to save the company in your CRM.
Review and manage companies

Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension to review company details and log activities. You can also edit company properties and associate contacts, deals, tickets, or tasks.

  • On a company website, click the sprocket HubSpot sprocket icon in the upper right.

  • To create or log activities, click the icon for the activity you want to create or log.

  • To view the company in your CRM, click Open in HubSpot.

  • To update existing company information, click a property to edit. Depending on the property type, edit the value:

    • For a text or number property, enter your value in the text box.
    • For an enumeration or user property, select a value.
    • At the bottom, click Save.

  • On the Details tab, review or update the following information:

    • About this company: view the company properties that you have configured on the company record.
    • Deals: view deals associated with the company record. Click + Add to create and associate new or existing deals to the company.
    • Tickets: view tickets associated with the company record. Click + Add to create and associate new or existing tickets to the company.
    • Tasks: view tasks associated with the company record. Click + Add to create and associate new or existing tasks to the company.

  • To view the company’s logged sales activities, click the Activity tab.

  • To view contacts associated with the company, click the Contacts tab.

  • To view an existing contact, click the contact name.

  • To create a new contact, click Add.

    • On the Create new tab, enter the contact property values in the create form. At the bottom, click Create.
    • If you want to set an association label, you’ll need to set the label after the record is created.

  • To associate a contact that already exists in your CRM, click Add.

    • Click the Add existing tab.
    • Search for the contact you want to associate, then select the checkbox next to the record name.
    • Click Next.
    • To label the record association (Professional and Enterprise only), click +Add association label to set labels that describe the relationship between the records.
    • Click Save.
Access Breeze Assistant from the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension

You can access Breeze Assistant from within the HubSpot Sales sidebar. You must have Breeze Assistant turned on in HubSpot and your HubSpot Sales Chrome extension settings.

To access Breeze Assistant from the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension, click the Breeze Assistant icon at the side of any website.

Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension with records in Salesforce

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension with records in Salesforce.

After turning on the extension for Salesforce, you’ll be able to see the HubSpot Sales sidebar when using Salesforce. This will allow you to use HubSpot tools such as calling, meetings, sequence enrollments and more, directly in Salesforce and on your Salesforce contact, lead, and account records. This sidebar will match contact and company profiles in Salesforce with related profiles in HubSpot.

Please note:

  • To use the HubSpot Chrome extension with Salesforce records, Salesforce users must also be a user in HubSpot and logged in to the latter system. Users will need the View records permissions in HubSpot.
  • For the Chrome extension to display information on a Salesforce account or opportunity record, the account/opportunity must be syncing with a respective HubSpot company/deal, and that company/deal must have an associated, syncing contact.
Access the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension in Salesforce
  • From a Salesforce contact, lead, or account page, click the sprocket sproket icon.
  • In the right panel, review the corresponding HubSpot record’s details. Users can also do the following:
    • Add notes to the HubSpot record
    • Make calls using HubSpot’s calling tool
    • Create and send one-to-one emails
    • Create tasks in HubSpot
  • Users with a paid Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat will also be able to:
    • Create meetings
    • Enroll the contact in a sequence
Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension to bulk enroll contacts or leads in Salesforce

Seats required An assigned Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat is required to bulk enroll contacts or leads directly from Salesforce into a HubSpot sequence.

To bulk enroll contacts or leads directly from Salesforce into a HubSpot sequence:

  • From the Salesforce contact and lead pages, select the checkboxes next contacts or leads that you’d like to enroll in a sequence.
  • At the top left, click Enroll in sequence.
  • In the dialog box, use the search bar to search for a sequence by name, or click the Owner dropdown menu and select a filter option.
  • The Last used at column is user specific, so it will show the sequences that you last sent. To sort your sequences, click a column header.
  • Hover over a sequence and click Select.
  • In the next window, customize your sequence templates and settings. Learn more about personalizing your sequence email content.
  • Specify the email template you want the sequence to start at, set delays between sequence steps, and specify times that you would like each sequence template to send.
  • Then, click Start sequence.

View and manage contacts in Gmail with the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension

Use the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension to view and update CRM contact information directly in Gmail. From the HubSpot Sales panel, you can search for contacts, log sales activities, create tasks, and associate companies, deals, and tickets without leaving your inbox.

To access contact information on other web pages, learn more about using the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension across the web.

Search for contacts

Search for an existing CRM contact from the HubSpot Sales panel in Gmail.

  • In your Gmail inbox, on the right sidebar menu, click the sprocket sprocket icon.

    • If the right sidebar menu isn’t available, click Show side panel in the bottom right.

  • In the HubSpot Sales panel, click the search search icon.

  • In the search bar, enter the contact’s name or email.

  • Click the contact. The contact’s information will appear in the panel.

View contacts and log sales activities

From your Gmail inbox, review contact details, edit contact properties, and log sales activities.

  • In your Gmail inbox, on the right sidebar menu, click the sprocket sprocket icon.

  • To view a specific contact, search for the contact or open an existing email thread with the contact.

  • To view the contact record in your CRM, click Open in HubSpot.

  • To view contact details, click to expand the About this contact section.

  • To edit a property, click a property to edit. Depending on the property type, edit the value:

    • For a text or number property, enter your value in the text box.
    • For an enumeration or user property, select a value.
    • At the bottom, click Save.
Create or log sales activities

At the top of the HubSpot Sales panel, select the activity you want to create or log:

  • Note: click the description note icon to create a note.
  • Email: click the email email icon to draft and send a one-to-one email.
  • Call: click the calling call icon to open the calling tool and make a call.
  • Task: click the tasks task icon to open the task editor and schedule a task.
  • Meeting: click the meetings meeting icon to open the meeting scheduler and book a meeting on your calendar.
  • Sequence: click the sequences sequence icon to enroll the contact in a sequence. Sequence enrollment requires an assigned Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat.
  • Enroll to agent: click the breezeSingleStar AI icon to enroll the contact in the prospecting agent (Sales Hub only).

Associate companies, deals, or tickets

From Gmail, associate an existing company, deal, or ticket with a contact, or create and associate a new record. The associated record will appear on the contact in Gmail, on the contact record in your CRM, and on the record’s index page.

  • In your Gmail inbox, on the right sidebar menu, click the sprocket sprocket icon.
  • To view a specific contact, search for the contact or open an existing email thread with the contact.
  • Scroll to the Companies, Deals, or Tickets section.
  • Click to expand the section and view existing records associated with the contact.
    • In the Deals section, the first 10 associated deals will appear.
  • To create and associate a new record, click Add.
  • On the Create new tab, enter the property values in the create form.
    • To control which fields appear in a create form, learn more about customizing the create form for each object.
    • To apply an association label, set the label after the record is created.
  • Click Create. To create and associate another record, click Create and add another.

To associate an existing record:

  • In the object section, click Add.
  • Click the Add existing tab.
  • Search for the record you want to associate, then select the checkbox next to the record name.
  • Click Next.
  • To label the record association (Professional and Enterprise only), click +Add association label,then select labels that describe the relationship between the records
  • Click Save.

Create tasks

Create a task associated with the contact directly from Gmail. The task will also appear on the task index page and on the contact record in the CRM.

  • In your Gmail inbox, on the right sidebar menu, click the sprocket sprocket icon.
  • To view a specific contact, search for the contact or open an existing email thread with the contact.
  • In the HubSpot Sales panel, click to expand the Tasks section.
  • Review existing tasks that you’ve created or that are assigned to you, then click Add to create a task for the contact.
  • Enter the task name and select a due date.
  • Click Save.

Add email recipients as new contacts

Add an email recipient who isn’t already in your CRM as a new contact directly from Gmail.

  • In your Gmail inbox, open the email composer and add a recipient.
  • On the right sidebar menu, click the sprocket sprocket icon.
  • In the HubSpot Sales panel, click Add to HubSpot.

After you add the recipient as a contact, edit the contact’s properties from the side panel without leaving Gmail.

Troubleshoot issues when viewing contacts

If you’re consistently seeing a login message in the right sidebar of Gmail when viewing contacts, you may need to make changes to your browser and inbox settings.

First, adjust your cookies settings in Chrome:

  • In the upper right corner of your Chrome browser, click the Settings menu (three dots or three horizontal lines), then select Settings.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Privacy and security.
  • In the Privacy and security section, click Site Settings. Older versions of Chrome label this as Content settings.
  • Click Third-party cookies.
  • Ensure that the Allow third-party cookies setting is toggled on. Your changes will be saved automatically.
  • If you are unable to toggle the Allow third-party cookies switch on, click Add in the Allow section and add [*.]getsidekick.com, [*.].hubspot.com, and [*.]hsappstatic.net to explicitly allow them.
  • Refresh Gmail.

Additionally, some Gmail Labs (e.g., the Gmail Lab called Preview Pane) are incompatible with the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension because of inconsistent formatting of their beta features. Turning this off should allow the sidebar to appear:

  • Open Gmail.
  • Click the gear icon, then select See all settings.
  • Click the Labs tab.
  • Search for Preview Pane and turn off the feature.

If you’re still having trouble loading your contacts, turn off any other Labs features. Learn more about troubleshooting the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension.

View contacts and log sales activities

From your Outlook inbox, you can review contact details and log sales activities. You can also edit contact properties and associate companies, deals, tickets, or tasks.

  • In your Outlook inbox, compose a new email or open an existing email in Outlook. If composing a new email, add a recipient.
  • Open the sales tools in your inbox. This process will differ slightly depending on the version of Outlook you’re using. Learn how to access contacts for your Outlook version.
  • In the right task pane, under the Contact profile section, click View contact.
  • To view contact details, click to expand the About section.
  • To edit a property, click a property to edit. Depending on the property type, edit the value:
    • For a text or number property, enter your value in the text box.
    • For an enumeration or user property, select a value.
    • At the bottom, click Save. Learn more about editing property values.
  • To create or log activities, in the upper right, click the icon for the activity you want to create or log.
    • To create a note, click the description Note icon.
    • To create a sales email, click the email Email icon. The email editor will open for you to draft and send an email.
    • To make a phone call, click the calling Call icon. The calling tool will open for you to make a call.
    • To create a task, click the tasks Task icon. The task editor will open for you to schedule a task.
    • To schedule a meeting, click the meetings Meeting icon. The meeting scheduler will open for you to book a meeting on your calendar.
