  • Click the name of the app.

  • On the settings page, click Manage locations on the new card.

  • In the right panel, select the checkbox next to each view where you want to add the app card. Each tab will display all views for a single CRM object.

  • Click Save.

  • On the app cards page, click Manage locations on the older version of the card.

  • In the right panel, clear the checkbox next to each view on each tab

  • Click Save.

Add and use Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive files in HubSpot

Connect the Microsoft SharePoint & OneDrive app to HubSpot to attach, organize, and access Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint files across CRM records and workflows. After connecting the app, you can browse SharePoint and OneDrive files from HubSpot records and open linked files in Microsoft. You can also automate file creation and management with workflows.

The integration helps teams centralize customer-facing documents and reduce manual work when managing files across sales, marketing, service, and operations processes.

Before you get started

Permissions required The Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive integration is a user-level app in HubSpot. Each user must connect the app using their own HubSpot login. If you don’t have App Marketplace permissions, request app access following these steps.

  • If you’re a Super Admin, opt your HubSpot account into the Microsoft OneDrive & SharePoint File Integration for HubSpot Records public beta.
  • Your organization’s Microsoft 365 administrator may need to provide tenant-wide consent to connect the app.
  • The integration supports only OneDrive for Business accounts. Personal Microsoft accounts and personal OneDrive accounts aren’t supported.
  • You must have access to the OneDrive or SharePoint files and folders that you want to link to HubSpot records.
  • You can attach up to 20 items to each record.

Connect the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.

  • In the search bar, search for and select the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive app.

  • On the app page, click Install.

  • In the dialog box, select whether you want to connect SharePoint, OneDrive, or both.

  • Click Connect.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions to sign in to your Microsoft 365 account and authorize HubSpot.

  • If required, you may be prompted to ask your Microsoft 365 admin to grant tenant-wide consent to connect HubSpot with Microsoft 365.

  • Complete the connection process.

If you connected only SharePoint or OneDrive when installing the app, you can connect the other later.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive app.

  • Click the Settings tab.

  • In the Manage connections section, click Manage.

  • In the Manage connections dialog box, click Connect for SharePoint or OneDrive.

  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the connection.

Link Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive files to HubSpot records

After connecting the app, a Super Admin or a user with the Customize record page layout permission must add the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive integration card to the right sidebar of the records where you want to link files.

To add the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive card, follow the steps to add a card to a record page layout. In the record layout editor, add the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive integration card from the card library, then save your changes.

After adding the card, you can link SharePoint and OneDrive files and folders to records, and open linked files in Microsoft.

To add a new SharePoint and OneDrive file to a record in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to your records.

  • Click the name of a record.

  • On the record page, navigate to the Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive integration card in the right sidebar.

  • On the card, click +Add.

  • Browse SharePoint and OneDrive files or search for a file or folder.

  • Select the file or folder that you want to link to.

  • Click Confirm.

The SharePoint or OneDrive file or folder will be added to the integration card on the right sidebar of the HubSpot record. From there, you can open the file in Microsoft.

Use Microsoft SharePoint and OneDrive workflow actions

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

After connecting the app, use the following workflow actions to automatically create and organize SharePoint and OneDrive files for your HubSpot records.

You can also create a workflow with these actions using Breeze Assistant. Describe your use case or what you want the workflow to do, and Breeze Assistant can create a workflow that includes SharePoint and OneDrive actions.

Workflow action

Description

Example use case

Create folder in SharePoint

Create folder in OneDrive

Creates a folder in a selected SharePoint or OneDrive location.

Create a folder for a new deal in a designated SharePoint location.

Upload file to SharePoint

Upload file to OneDrive

Uploads a file from a HubSpot record to SharePoint or OneDrive.

Upload a signed agreement from a record file property to a customer folder.

Link SharePoint item

Link OneDrive item

Links existing files or folders in SharePoint or OneDrive.

Link an existing customer file or folder to a HubSpot contact record.

Copy attachments

Copies SharePoint and OneDrive attachments from one record to another.

Copy the folders linked to a deal to a new project record when the deal closes.

Please note: for all workflow actions, you can use file or folder IDs stored in a CRM object property as inputs in the action configuration fields.

To use SharePoint and OneDrive workflow actions:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of your workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon.

  • In the left panel, select a SharePoint or OneDrive workflow action:

    • To create a folder:
      • Select the Create a folder in SharePoint or Create a folder in OneDrive action.
      • Click the Microsoft account dropdown menu and select the account you want to use.
      • In the Folder name field, enter a name for the folder.
      • Under Destination, select whether you want the folder to be created in a document library or drive root, or a specific folder.
        • Document library root or drive root: enter the library or drive root you want to create the folder in.
        • Specific folder: enter the folder sharing URL or the folder identifier from a previous workflow action.

Please note: if a folder with the same name already exists in the selected destination, the action will complete successfully without creating a duplicate. The action output will include the existing folder’s ID and name.

- To upload a file:
    - Select the Upload a file to SharePoint or Upload a file to OneDrive action.
    - Click the Microsoft account dropdown menu and select the account you want to use.
    - Click the CRM object dropdown menu and select the record type from which you want to attach the file.
    - Click the File property field and select the property from which you want to upload the file.
    - Under Destination, select whether you want the file to be uploaded in a document library root or a specific folder.

Please note:

  • If the selected file property contains multiple files, all files will be uploaded as part of the action. The action output will include the IDs of all uploaded files.

  • If a file with the same name already exists in the destination, the file will be uploaded and renamed following Microsoft’s rename strategy. The action output will include the new file’s ID and updated name.

    • To link to an existing folder or file:
      • Select the Link to SharePoint item or Link to OneDrive item action.
      • Click the Microsoft account dropdown menu and select the account you want to use.
      • Click the CRM object dropdown menu and select the record type to associate with the item.
        • For the Link to OneDrive item action, in the File or folder identifier field, enter the file or folder sharing URL or the file or folder identifier from a previous workflow action.
        • For the Link to SharePoint item action, under Attachment type, select the type of item you want to link:
          • Site: enter the site you want to link.
          • Document library: enter the site and document library you want to link.
          • Folder or file: enter the file or folder sharing URL or the file or folder identifier from a previous workflow action.

Please note: if the item is already linked to the record, the action will complete successfully but no changes will be made.

- To copy attachments from one record to another:
    - Select the Copy attachments action.
    - Click the Copy from dropdown menu and select the source record that you want to copy the attachment from.
    - Click the Copy to dropdown menu and select the target record that you want to copy the attachment to.

Add HubSpot forms to WordPress pages and posts (legacy)

Once you’ve successfully installed the HubSpot – CRM, Email Marketing, Live Chat, Forms & Analytics plugin, you can add HubSpot legacy forms to your WordPress pages and posts.

Please note: this article is for reference only for existing forms built with the legacy editor only. Currently, it’s not possible to embed HubSpot forms created using the updated form editor on WordPress pages or posts. Learn more about using the updated form editor to create and manage forms.

In WordPress, you can add your HubSpot legacy forms through either the Classic editor or the Gutenberg Editor.

Before you get started

Before you get started, please note the following:

  • If you’re embedding a form on your WordPress site, you may need to apply additional CSS declarations within your external stylesheet to make the form responsive.
  • If you notice your form not working in WordPress or the embed code being altered when you view the live page, you may need to insert the form using a plugin to make sure the embed code stays intact.
  • If you’re using another form plugin, like Contact Form 7 or Ninja Forms, you can collect submissions in HubSpot. Review the table of supported forms, then learn how to use non-HubSpot forms.
  • If you’re using a supported, non-HubSpot form on WordPress, but aren’t seeing submission data in HubSpot, you may have another WordPress plugin installed that conflicts with the HubSpot-WordPress plugin. Turn off the plugin, or review frequently asked questions for additional troubleshooting steps.

Classic Editor

To embed a HubSpot legacy form to your WordPress pages and posts using the classic editor:

  • From your WordPress account, in the left sidebar menu, navigate to HubSpot > Forms.
  • Hover over the form you want to add to your website and click Embed. You can also create a new HubSpot form by clicking Create form.
  • Click WordPress short code, then click Copy to copy the embed code.
  • Navigate to a WordPress page or post, then paste the short code into the page editor.

After publishing your page, to view submissions to the form in WordPress:

  • From your WordPress account, in the left sidebar menu, navigate to HubSpot > Forms.
  • Hover over a form. Then click the Actions dropdown menu and select View submissions. Learn more about analyzing your form submissions.

Gutenberg Editor

If you’re using the latest version of Gutenberg, which removes inline JavaScript, use the Inline JS Block for Gutenberg plugin to embed HubSpot legacy forms and CTAs onto your page instead.

To embed a HubSpot legacy form to your WordPress pages and posts using the Gutenberg editor:

  • In your WordPress account, navigate to your page or post.

  • Click the plus icon in the toolbar. Search for the HubSpot Form block and click it to add it to your content.

  • In the block, you can select an existing form or create a new form:

    • To select an existing form, click the select an existing form dropdown menu and select a form.
    • To create a new form, navigate to HubSpot > Forms in the left sidebar menu and click Create form.

After publishing your page, to view submissions to the form in WordPress:

  • From your WordPress account, in the left sidebar menu, navigate to HubSpot > Forms.
  • Hover over a form. Then click the Actions dropdown menu and select View submissions. Learn more about analyzing your form submissions.

Add the HubSpot Embed window to your Salesforce page layouts

Please note: HubSpot’s legacy managed package in Salesforce containing HubSpot’s legacy Visualforce module is being deprecated. If you’re still using the legacy Visualforce module, it is recommended to uninstall the package in Salesforce and use HubSpot Embed moving forward instead.

HubSpot Embed is an iframe within Salesforce that displays a summary of the HubSpot interactions and activities a Salesforce record had. It lives within the Visualforce framework in Salesforce.

You can add the HubSpot Embed window to any Salesforce contact, lead, account, or opportunity records.

With HubSpot Embed, you can:

  • View the object record’s timeline and any associated objects in Salesforce.
  • Enroll the object in a workflow and view any previous workflow enrollments.
  • View property and property history for the object record.
  • Directly book meetings in HubSpot through Salesforce.
  • Enroll contacts in a sequence through Salesforce.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, please note the following:

Permissions required

  • To install and ensure automatic updates to the HubSpot Embed window, Salesforce users need the Customize Application profile permission.

  • To view the HubSpot Embed window on a Salesforce record, Salesforce users must also be a user in HubSpot and logged in to the latter system. Users will need the View records permissions in HubSpot.

  • The HubSpot-Salesforce integration must be installed.

  • To display information on a Salesforce account or opportunity record, the account or opportunity must be syncing to a HubSpot company or deal, and the latter must be associated to a syncing contact.

  • HubSpot Embed is not supported in mobile applications and in-app browsers in mobile applications.

Turn on HubSpot Embed

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Salesforce.
  • Click the Feature Discovery tab.
  • Click Install HubSpot Embed.

After installing HubSpot Embed, log in to your Salesforce account to continue the set up. Follow the steps below for the relevant Salesforce interface:

  • Salesforce Classic
  • Lightning Experience

Salesforce Classic

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account.

  • In the upper right, click Setup (or [Your Name] > Setup).

  • To add the HubSpot Embed window to your Salesforce record page layouts, in the Build section in the left sidebar menu, navigate to Customize > Leads/Contacts/Accounts/Opportunities > Page Layouts.

  • You’ll see a list of page layouts. Click Edit next to a page layout’s name.

Please note: if you have multiple page layouts, you must add the HubSpot Embed window to each page layout you want to display the window on.

  • Click the Section item in the toolbar and drag and drop it into the desired location on the page layout.

  • In the dialog box, enter a Section Name (e.g., HubSpot Information). Under Layout, select 1-Column. Click OK.

  • In the toolbar’s left sidebar menu, select Visualforce Pages.

  • Click the HubSpot_Embed_[object type]_V2 item in the toolbar and drag it into the newly-created section on the page layout.

  • Hover over the new HubSpot embed window and click the wrench icon in the top right.

  • In the dialog box, change the window Height to 500, then click OK.

  • In the top left of the toolbar, click Save to apply your layout changes.

  • Navigate to a Salesforce contact, lead, account, or opportunity record to view the HubSpot Embed window.

  • Repeat these steps for any other page layouts you want to add the HubSpot Embed window to.

Lightning Experience

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account.

  • In the upper right, click the settings gear icon and select settings Setup.

  • In the left sidebar menu, in the Platform Tools section, navigate to Objects and Fields > Object Manager.

  • In the list of objects, click Lead or Contact.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Page Layouts.

  • Click the name of a page layout.

Please note: if you have multiple page layouts, you must add the Visualforce window to each page layout you want to display the window on.

  • Click the Section item in the toolbar and drag and drop it into the desired location on the page layout.

  • In the dialog box, enter a Section Name (e.g., HubSpot Information).

  • Under Layout, select 1-Column. Click OK.

  • In the toolbar’s left sidebar menu, select Visualforce Pages.

  • Click the HubSpot_Embed_[object type]_V2 item in the toolbar and drag and drop it into the newly-created section on the page layout.

  • In the top right, hover over the newly-created section and click the wrench icon.

  • In the dialog box, change the window Height to 500, then click OK.

  • In the top left of the toolbar, click Save to apply your layout changes.

  • Navigate to a Salesforce lead or contact record and click the Details tab to view the HubSpot Embed window.

  • Repeat these steps for any other page layouts you want to add the HubSpot Embed window to.

To add the HubSpot Embed window to a Lightning Page or Lightning App:

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account.
  • In the upper right, click the settings gear icon and select settings Setup.
  • In the left sidebar, click Visualforce Pages.
  • For each HubSpot_Embed_object_V2 page, click Edit.
  • Select the Available for Lighting Experience, Experience Builder sites, and the mobile app checkbox.
  • Repeat these steps for each object type.
  • When adding to a Lightning Record page, add a standard Visualforce component to the page, then select the appropriate HubSpot Embed page.

Resolve HubSpot Embed errors

You may see the following error in your HubSpot Embed window:

No HubSpot info for this contact. This contact couldn’t be found. If you think this is an error, please contact your HubSpot account administrator.

To resolve this error:

  • Ensure that the Salesforce record viewed is currently syncing with the correct HubSpot contact.
  • Ensure that the user trying to view the HubSpot Embed window has the correct permissions in HubSpot to view that particular contact record.

Add the Website Grader widget to your website

The Website Grader widget is an embeddable version of HubSpot’s Website Grader that HubSpot solutions partners and providers can add to your HubSpot-hosted or external websites. The widget consists of a form and a module that you can add to your webpage.

Integration requirements

You must have the following permissions in HubSpot:

  • A Marketing Hub or Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription.

  • View and Edit access for contacts, companies, and deals.

  • Edit property settings permissions.

  • Marketing Access permissions.

  • Publish, Edit, and View access for Website tools (except HubDB).

  • App Marketplace Access, Global content settings, and Website settings permissions.

Add the Website Grader widget to your account

  • Navigate to widget.grader.com.
  • Click Add to portal.
  • Select the account you want to add the widget to, then click Choose Account.
  • You’ll be asked to grant permission for the Website Grader Widget to access your HubSpot account. Click Connect app.
  • You can add the Website Grader widget to a HubSpot-hosted page or an external website. On the Where will you be embedding the Website Grader widget? screen, select an option. Then follow the instructions to complete the widget set up in your account.
Embed the widget on a HubSpot-hosted page

If embedding the widget on your HubSpot-hosted website:

  • Select the A HubSpot-hosted page checkbox.
  • Click Next.
  • Add privacy disclaimer text to your form.
    • In the Company name field, enter your company’s name.
    • In the Privacy policy URL field, enter a link to your company’s privacy policy.
  • Click Next
  • To automatically add the Website Grader widget to your account, click Install module.
  • To view the module in your account, click Open portal. The module will be named HubSpot Website Grader widget.

Once the module has been added to your account, you can edit the module’s fields and style the form fields. You can then add it to a page template, or add it to a page using the drag-and-drop page editor.

Embed the widget on an external page

If embedding the Website Grader widget on an external page:

  • Select the An external website checkbox.

  • Click Next.

  • A form called “Website Grader Widget Form” will be created automatically in your account. To edit the form fields, click Edit this form. You can create a custom form as well.

  • Click Next.

  • Add privacy disclaimer text to your form.

    • In the Company name field, enter your company’s name.
    • In the Privacy policy URL field, enter a link to your company’s privacy policy.

  • Click Next.

  • In the Customize section, use the styling options to edit the logos and text that appear on the page. To review your changes, click Preview.

  • Click Next.

  • In the Add the widget to your website section, click Copy, then add the code to your website before the closing body tag.

After the widget has been added to your website page, visitors can scan a website URL after entering their email address and receive an overall grade for their website based on its performance. There will also be a marketing email titled Website Grader Result Email added to your HubSpot account. You can send this email to contacts who fill out the Website Grader on your website.

Segment contacts based on their website score

After adding the Website Grader widget to your account, the following contact properties will be created:

  • Grader Result: Performance Score (out of 30)
  • Grader Result: Mobile Score (out of 30)
  • Grader Result: SEO Score (out of 30)
  • Grader Result: Security Score (out of 10)
  • Grader Result: Overall Score (out of 100)
  • Grader Website

This is how you can interpret the scores and what’s being measured:

Score type

What’s being measured

Performance

The size of the network payload.

The number of requests the page makes.

The amount of time it takes for the page to become fully interactive.

The percentage of bytes used for caching website assets.

The number of redirects on the page.

The size of all unminified CSS and Javascript files.

The number of images that are appropriately sized.

Mobile

Whether the content is sized correctly for the viewport.

How mobile-friendly the font size is.

How mobile-friendly the tap targets on the page are.

SEO

Whether the page is blocked from indexing by search engine crawlers.

Whether the page has a meta description and descriptive text in the links.

Whether the page has plugin-based content.

Security

Whether the page loads over HTTPS or HTTP.

If the page includes front-end Javascript with known security vulnerabilities.

You can organize contacts into segments based on their scores in each category after they scan their website URL with the widget.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to CRM > Segments.
  • In the upper right, click Create segment.
  • In the left panel, select Contacts to create a segment of contacts. Then click Next.
  • To edit the segment’s name, click the edit icon and enter a name.
  • Click + Add filter and select Website Grader Widget: Ran Grader.
  • Click the name of the Website Grader properties, then refine the filter accordingly.

Add Zoom to your HubSpot meeting link

After you connect the Zoom app to your HubSpot account, add Zoom to your HubSpot meeting links. Using Zoom with HubSpot meeting links can help streamline meeting scheduling and reduce manual setup.

For example, when a prospect books a meeting through your scheduling page, a Zoom meeting is automatically created and added to the meeting invitation so both participants receive the joining information.

Before you get started

Before getting started, please do note the following:

  • Your HubSpot user email address must match your Zoom user email address to add a Zoom videoconference link to your meeting links. Verify the connected Zoom user in the integration settings. If the email addresses don’t match, remap the user in the Zoom meetings settings.
  • Your Zoom meeting link will be sent in the default language set in your HubSpot account.
  • If you turn on password protection in Zoom, users will be required to enter a password before viewing a recording.
  • Due to an API change from Zoom, meeting participants who join a meeting link directly may not be tracked in HubSpot meeting logs or created as contacts. Meeting participants need to be logged into their Zoom account and identifiable from their email address in order for HubSpot to track them as participants.
  • If you connect your individual Zoom account to HubSpot, the Zoom link included in the meeting will be your own link. This enables you to run Zoom conferences at the same time as other users in the HubSpot account. If you don’t connect your individual Zoom account, your meeting will use the Zoom link of the person who originally connected the Zoom integration. This can cause Zoom conflicts if multiple users try to run conferences at the same time.
  • Zoom removes email addresses for users identified as guests in Zoom unless they meet Zoom’s requirements. As a result, meeting registrants or participants without an email address won’t sync to HubSpot. To ensure all attendees sync to HubSpot, turn on the Only authenticated users can join setting for meetings in Zoom.

Add Zoom to your meeting link

You can add Zoom to your scheduling pages or when you schedule a meeting in the CRM.

Add Zoom to a meeting scheduling page

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Sales > Meetings Scheduler. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Sales > Meetings Scheduler directly.

  • If you’re creating a new scheduling page:

    • Click Create scheduling page.
    • In the dialog box, select a meeting option.
    • Click the Add videoconference link dropdown menu and select Zoom.

  • If you’re editing an existing link:

    • Hover over the scheduling page you want to add a Zoom videoconference to and click Edit.
    • In the Overview tab, click the Add videoconference link dropdown menu and select Zoom.

When a prospect books a meeting with you, a link to the Zoom videoconference will be automatically added to the calendar invite. Meeting links will be created in the default language set in your account.

Add Zoom when scheduling a meeting in the CRM

  • Navigate to your records:

    • Contacts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • Companies: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.
    • Deals: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.
    • Tickets: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Tickets. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Tickets directly.

  • Click the name of the record.

  • In the left panel, click meetings Meeting.

  • In the dialog box, set up your meeting.

  • Click the Location dropdown menu and select Zoom.

Manage individual Zoom meeting settings

To manage your meeting settings and data sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Zoom.

  • Click the Settings tab.

  • On the My settings tab, in the Meetings section:

    • Select whether your Zoom meeting recordings and transcripts should sync from Zoom to HubSpot. Recordings and transcripts for present and future meetings will sync if the setting is turned on.
    • You can also search by Zoom meeting ID to manually sync data from past Zoom meetings, including recordings, transcripts, and participant details.
    • You can find the meeting ID in Zoom. Participants from past Zoom meetings will be created as contacts in HubSpot.

Please note: if this section is greyed out, it means that the admin in your account has opted not to sync meeting data for Zoom within the app’s global settings

Exclude contacts from being created in HubSpot

If you use Zoom with members of your own organization and want to exclude your team members from becoming new contacts in HubSpot, add your company’s email address in the Contact exclusions section of your Zoom integration settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Zoom.
  • Click the Settings tab, then the Global Settings tab.
  • In the Contact exclusions section, enter the email address or email domain that you use for your organization.

If you’re using the Google Calendar integration with HubSpot, learn more about adding a videoconference link to a meeting scheduled from a record in the CRM.

View recorded meetings on contact timelines

If you use meeting cloud recordings in Zoom, you can view your meeting recordings on the associated contact’s timeline.

Please note: cloud recording must be switched on in your Zoom settings.

Contact record and timeline events won’t be created or updated if the participant’s email address:

  • Is a user email address in your account.
  • Is a secondary email address on the contact record.
  • Has a domain that is excluded in the Zoom integration settings

Association mapping with data sync

Association mappings sync record associations between HubSpot and your connected app so that associated records remain linked across both systems. For example, when a contact is associated with a company in one system, that relationship can sync to the other system.

Before you get started

For most data sync apps, association mappings are available by default, and you don’t need to configure multiple object syncs for associations to work. For example, when you set up a contact sync, the associated company field mapping will link the respective companies.

However, for some data sync apps (e.g., Airtable, Kintone), and when syncing custom objects, all syncs must be activated in order for associations to be recognized. Learn about how to set up associations with data sync below.

Setting up association mappings

For example, suppose your connected app stores contacts and companies in separate lists or databases. Each contact record includes a linked field, showing the company they’re associated with. To maintain this relationship when syncing to HubSpot, HubSpot must also replicate this association.

To set this up, first configure the company sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app you’d like to set up associations for.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Set up your sync.

  • Set up your sync for companies.

  • Make sure to choose a field to match on (e.g., name of company, domain of company). This matching key determines how the company records will sync with one another. It also helps the sync in associating contact records to the right company records.

  • Add any reference fields, if applicable.

  • Set up your mappings.

After completing the company sync configuration, you can now create association field mappings in another object sync (e.g., a contact sync):

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app you’d like to set up associations for.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Sync more data.

  • Set up your sync for contacts.

  • Make sure to choose a field to match on (e.g., email address).

  • Add any reference fields, if applicable.

  • When setting up your mappings, ensure that you map the contact field from the other app that contains the company information to a corresponding field in HubSpot. Select your other app’s field first to narrow down the available list of association fields in HubSpot. This will make sure that the associated company is mapped to the primary associated company in HubSpot, when a contact is synced from the other app.

Build apps with the HubSpot connector for Lovable

Please note: the information in this article is intended for participants in the HubSpot connector for Lovable private beta only.

Use the HubSpot connector for Lovable to build custom apps and user interfaces with HubSpot data. After an admin configures access, users can connect HubSpot to Lovable, describe an app using natural language, and share the app with other users.

Each user’s HubSpot data access is based on their existing HubSpot user permissions. When a user builds or accesses a Lovable app, they can only access HubSpot data that they have permission to access in HubSpot. Admins control who can build Lovable apps and who can access the HubSpot connector for Lovable.

Before you get started

Before users can build apps in Lovable using HubSpot data, review the following:

  • Super Admins: grant users the HubSpot connector for Lovable permission in HubSpot, and approve which users can install the connector and Lovable-built apps.
  • Lovable admins: turn on the HubSpot connector in the Lovable workspace.
  • Users who build apps: connect with their HubSpot account to Lovable, build the app, and share it with other users.
  • Users who access apps: access Lovable-built apps, but they don’t build the apps themselves.
  • HubSpot data is scoped to the individual user. Building or accessing an app does not give a user access to HubSpot data beyond their existing HubSpot permissions.
  • When connecting HubSpot to Lovable, it’s recommended that you select all available optional permissions. The optional permissions you select set the maximum HubSpot permissions available to apps you build with the connector. Selecting only some optional permissions can limit the apps and functionality you can build in Lovable.

Set up access for users (Admin required)

Complete the following steps before users can start using the HubSpot connector for Lovable.

1. Grant users permission to build apps in Lovable

A Super Admin must first grant the HubSpot connector for Lovable permission to users who will build Lovable apps.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record, then click the Access tab.
  • Under Permissions, click Edit permissions.
  • Click to expand the Choose permissions section.
  • Click AI features.
  • Toggle the HubSpot connector for Lovable switch on.
  • In the top right, click Save.

After granting the permission, approve the users who can install the connector.

2. Approve users to install the HubSpot connector for Lovable

A Super Admin must approve access for users to install the HubSpot connector for Lovable.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the Approved apps tab.

  • Click Approve apps.

  • Search for and select the HubSpot connector for Lovable.

  • In the Manage access banner, click Approve.

  • In the dialog box, select who can install the app and review the permissions, data, and APIs the connector can access.

  • Click Approve app.

Learn more about approving access to apps for your team.

3. Turn on optional permissions for the HubSpot connector for Lovable

Super Admins control which optional permissions are available in the HubSpot connector for Lovable, setting the permission ceiling for all app builders. Even if an optional permission is turned on, an app builder only has access if their own HubSpot permissions allow it.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the Approved apps tab.
  • For the HubSpot connector for Lovable, click Manage Access on the right.
  • In the right panel, click the Data Permissions tab.
  • In the Optional section, toggle some or all optional permissions on.
  • Click Save changes.
4. Turn on the HubSpot connector in your Lovable workspace

A Lovable admin must turn on the HubSpot connector in Lovable before approved users can connect HubSpot to Lovable.

  • In Lovable, in the left sidebar menu, navigate to Connectors.
  • Search for and select HubSpot.
  • In the Features section, click Enable for both the Chat connector and App user connector.

After the connector is turned on, users with the required HubSpot permissions and installation access can connect HubSpot to Lovable.

Set up the HubSpot connector for Lovable

After a Super Admin has granted the required HubSpot permission and connector access, and a Lovable admin has turned on the connector, users can connect HubSpot to Lovable and start building apps.

  • Navigate to lovable.dev and log in to your Lovable account.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Connectors.

  • Select HubSpot.

  • Click the + Add connection dropdown menu and select Chat Connector.

  • Click Connect.

  • Select the HubSpot account that a Super Admin has approved for you to access the connector.

  • Review the data and tools the connector can access in your HubSpot account. Optional permissions define the maximum permissions available to apps you build with the connector in Lovable, but aren’t all used automatically. An optional permission is only used when the app you’re building specifically requires it. To avoid reconfiguring permissions later, it’s recommended that you select all available optional permissions. Selecting only some optional permissions can limit the apps and functionality you can build in Lovable.

  • Review the terms and privacy policy. Then select the checkbox to accept the integration’s terms and conditions.

  • Click Connect app.

After connecting HubSpot to Lovable, you can use the connector to build an app in Lovable that uses HubSpot data.

If you encounter the error You don’t have the right permissions to install the HubSpot connector for Lovable during the installation process, ask a Super Admin to grant you the HubSpot connector for Lovable permission in HubSpot.

If you encounter the error You don’t have install access for this app, ask a Super Admin to approve your access to install the connector.

After installing the connector, choose how Lovable requests approval for tool calls. You can require approval for all tool calls, require approval only for specific tool calls, or always allow tool calls. The Always allow option can streamline the chat and help you reach results faster, but allows Lovable to make tool calls without further approval, giving you reduced visibility and control over connector activity.

Use the HubSpot connector for Lovable

After connecting HubSpot to Lovable, use natural language to describe the app or user interface you want Lovable to build:

  • In Lovable, enter a prompt describing the app or user interface you want to build and @mention HubSpot in your prompt. Then press Enter.

Please note:

  • The steps and questions that appear in Lovable may vary depending on the app you’re building and the information included in your prompt. The steps below represent a typical app creation flow.

  • It’s recommended to specify in the prompt that you want to build a user-level app to ensure user-level auth access.

  • Select who can access the app after you publish it:

    • Internally to my workspace: only signed-in users in your Lovable workspace can access the published app.
    • Publicly for external users: anyone with the app URL can access the published app.

  • Click Next. The selected audience will be applied once you publish the app.

  • On the Provisioning HubSpot app section, review the app’s required permissions in HubSpot. Then click Allow.

  • Lovable will start generating a preview of your app. The preview usually takes a few minutes to appear.

  • In the app preview, click Connect HubSpot.

  • In the dialog box, select your HubSpot account.

  • Review the HubSpot data that your Lovable-built app can access.

  • Select the checkbox, then click Connect app.

  • Your HubSpot data will appear in the app preview.

The app will only surface HubSpot data that you’re authorized to access based on your HubSpot user permissions. For example, if you can only view deals that you own, a Lovable app that displays HubSpot deals will only display the deals that you own.

Share a Lovable app with other users

Once you’ve built your app in Lovable, share it with other users in your workspace.

  • In the top right, click Publish.

  • Select who can view your app: your entire workspace or specific users.

  • To edit the app’s domain prefix, click the pencil icon next to the domain. Or click + Add domain to use a custom domain.

  • Click Publish.

  • After the app is published, click Copy link to copy the app’s URL and share it with colleagues in your workspace who’ll use the app.

When another user opens the app, they must connect their own HubSpot account. Their access to HubSpot data is base d on their HubSpot user permissions.

  • Open the URL for the Lovable app.

  • Click Connect to HubSpot.

  • When prompted for approval, click Request to install. A request will be sent to the Super Admin in HubSpot.

  • After the admin approves the request, complete the app connection steps.

Remix Lovable templates

Use a pre-built template as a starting point, then customize the remixed project for your team’s needs.

Before remixing a template, set up the HubSpot connector for Lovable and turn on the App User Connector option for your workspace.

  • Navigate to one of the following HubSpot’s pre-built Lovable templates:

    • Pipeline Pulse: displays deal value, follow-up suggestions, and likelihood of closing to help you identify and prioritize revenue opportunities.
    • Campaign Compass: tracks campaign and email performance over time, including their influence on scheduled meetings and closed revenue.
    • Optimal Ops: displays HubSpot ticket data, including open and resolved ticket counts, resolution times, backlog age, and issues that need attention.

  • Log in to your Lovable workspace.

  • After the template loads, click Remix in the top right.

  • Enter a name for the project. If you have access to multiple workspaces, select the workspace where you want to create the project. Then, provide consent to remix the template.

  • Follow the instructions in the remixed project:

    • Copy the user authentication prompt.
    • Paste the prompt into the Lovable agent chat window.
    • Select the option to turn on HubSpot login for individual users.

  • Click Connect HubSpot.

  • Follow the authentication prompts to connect HubSpot and load your HubSpot data into the app.

  • Customize the app as needed.

Configure HubSpot’s AI agent prompts with connected apps

After connecting an app to a HubSpot’s AI agent, configure prompt instructions to determine when and how the agent uses the connected apps.

Well-designed prompts help agents combine HubSpot data with information from external systems to complete specific business tasks consistently.

Permissions required Agent Builder permissions are required to create and customize agents and assistants in Agent Builder.

Permissions required Additional permissions may be required depending on the goal of the assistant or agent. For example, an assistant or agent that generates a landing page requires Edit and Publish permissions to edit and publish landing pages.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features Some agents may require HubSpot Credits. Learn more about features using HubSpot Credits

Add prompts for connected apps to HubSpot’s AI agents

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Hub. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub directly.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • Hover over the agent you want to edit and click Edit.
  • In the Instructions section, enter your prompts. For example, you can use the following prompt:
  • Example prompt:
  • “You are connected to the G2 MCP Server. For every deal analysis, always query the G2 MCP Server to retrieve buyer intent signals, competitor comparison activity, and intent scores for the companies associated with closed-lost deals. Combine G2 external market signals with HubSpot CRM data to provide a complete picture of loss reasons. When a competitor is identified in G2 data, cross-reference it against the deal’s loss reason in HubSpot. Surface patterns where G2 intent activity spiked or shifted toward a competitor before deal close.”

Use case: create automated account intelligence from sales conversations

The following example shows how to configure a HubSpot AI agent connected to the Gong and Notion apps. Use this example as a general framework and customize the instructions based on the connected apps and the agent’s goal.

Business objective

A sales organization aims to reduce the time account teams spend researching customer conversations, allowing them to focus more on engaging with prospects.

Historically, reps must manually review call recordings, search for mentions of competitors, and document key takeaways across multiple systems.

By connecting external apps to a HubSpot AI agent, the organization can use information from these apps when researching accounts and generating insights.

Example configuration

In this example, a sales team connects Gong and Notion to a HubSpot AI agent:

  • Connect the agent to Gong to analyze sales calls and identify recurring competitive objections.
  • Connect the agent to Notion to store account summaries in a shared workspace.
  • Configure prompts for the connected apps following the best practices below.
Best practices for prompts using connected apps
  • Identify the database: since Notion pages and databases don’t follow a fixed structure, you need to instruct the agent exactly on which database to use.
    • Best practice: you should mention the name of the database, its purpose, and include the database ID when possible.
    • Example prompt: Use the Notion database titled ‘Content Projects Tracker,’ which includes the project name, status, owner, and due date.
  • Describe the property or column structure: describe your database structure in detail to help the agent understand the data.
    • Best practice: when referencing a database, you should list the relevant column names, what they contain, and their property type. If some fields are optional or not consistently used, they should be included.
    • Example prompt: The database includes these columns: ‘Project Name’ (title), ‘Owner’ (person), ‘Status’ (select), and ‘Deadline’ (date).
  • Define the agent’s task: be clear about the specific information the agent should find or extract.
    • Best practice: when defining the agent’s task or requesting for data, use specific names and details.
    • Example prompt: Find all items where the Status is ‘In Progress’ and the Deadline is within the next 7 days.
  • Specify actions and tools: if your agent needs to perform a specific action, explicitly state which tools it should use and how. This is especially useful if the agent has to choose between multiple tools.
    • Best practice: define the exact tool to use and how any actions should be executed, such as query_database, list_databases, or retrieve_page.
  • Provide an example input and output: if your agent needs to add or edit entries, it’s recommended that you include an example of what the data should look like.
    • Best practice: provide a clear example of each input and desired output with examples. You can also add conditions for different outputs.
    • Example prompt: When creating a new entry, fill in ‘Status’ as ‘Not Started’ by default and leave ‘Deadline’ blank.
Result

After the configuration is complete:

  • HubSpot’s AI agents can access data from connected business systems.
  • Sales teams can analyze customer conversations without leaving HubSpot.
  • Account summaries, competitor insights, and follow-up actions are automatically generated.
  • Teams spend less time gathering information and more time taking action.

Configure Microsoft Teams transcript API access

Microsoft now requires certain manual admin settings to keep Microsoft Teams transcript sync working with HubSpot. If you have configured this previously, you will still need to complete the following steps to meet the new API requirements. This article covers how to turn on the required settings in your Microsoft Teams admin center so that meeting transcripts and speaker data sync correctly to HubSpot.

Understand requirements

To complete this setup, you must have admin access to the Microsoft Teams admin center.

Set up transcript API access

In your Microsoft Teams admin center, turn on two settings to allow HubSpot to access meeting transcripts and attribute them to the correct speakers. Both settings below are required for the syncs to resume.

Turn on Graph transcript access

This setting allows HubSpot to securely access meeting transcripts via the Microsoft API.

  • In your Microsoft Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings.
  • Under Transcript API access, toggle the Microsoft Graph access switch on.
Turn on speaker attribution

Speaker attribution allows HubSpot to map transcript text to the correct individuals in a meeting.

  • Under Transcript API access, click Configure.
  • Toggle the Include Speaker Attribution switch on.

Alternative: update settings via PowerShell

You can also turn on these settings using the Enable Graph Transcript Access command in PowerShell. Note that this requires the latest Microsoft library update.

What to expect after updating

Once these settings are updated, HubSpot’s background tasks will attempt to restore your transcript subscriptions. It may take several hours for the sync to fully resume.

Connect and use HubSpot data sync

Use HubSpot data sync to keep data consistent between HubSpot and your other apps. After connecting a supported app, you can configure a one-way or two-way sync to automatically update records across both systems, reducing manual data entry and helping teams work with the same information. Review which apps use data sync.

For example, you can sync contacts, companies, deals, and other supported objects between HubSpot and your connected app so updates made in one system are reflected in the other based on your sync settings.

This article explains how data sync works, how to connect an app, configure your sync, and manage your synced records.

How data sync works

When you turn on a sync, data sync creates an internal index of all records in an object. It then uses that index to compare and monitor record changes to see how their state (syncing, failing, or excluded) should change as the record properties are updated. This means that the internal data sync index continually compares its database (either HubSpot or the connected app) and can recover any dropped or errored API call or endpoint.

When a record is updated, the sync engine examines the entire record against the copy it has and updates its copy to match the real record. This allows it to recover any missed or failed updates. Data sync might take some time to index all records when initiated, but will ensure a smoother and healthier sync experience.

Data sync uses normalization for matching in supported data sync apps when records are matched on non-unique name fields (for example, company or product names). This means capitalization, special characters, and punctuation are ignored when those name values are compared between HubSpot and your other app.

Sync principles

A data sync will always be between two apps, one being HubSpot. Every sync has two main phases, independent of the object syncing:

  • The initial sync: starts when a sync is activated or when saved. All existing records in both apps are passed through the sync engine to index and, if applicable, sync them.
  • The incremental sync: when all records are indexed, they are scanned for updates and new records. Indexed records that have changed since the last time they were checked are passed through the sync engine.
Initial sync

For a two-way sync, the initial sync consists of:

  • Index HubSpot: the HubSpot records are scanned, and the ID of the record and its matching identifiers are stored (by default this is the email for contacts, and name or domain for companies). The index is kept up to date throughout the entire syncing process going forward. Read more on how matching works.
  • Index the other app, and sync: the records from the other app are scanned and synced. For every resource that is fetched, a check is made to see if there’s any matching identifier (e.g., email address for contacts) in the index table of HubSpot. If there is, the records are matched and both records are passed through the sync engine together. If there isn’t a match, the record will go through the sync engine on its own. When the sync engine matches records, it combines all the information it has (the records’ field values, the filters, field mappings, sync history, etc.) and based on that, it builds the next action (request changes to the resources, do nothing, log an error, etc.)

Please note: the first record returned by the app’s API will be syncable; the next one will be considered a duplicate.

  • Sync HubSpot: the HubSpot records are scanned again to check if they need to be synced. This step will result in the syncing of existing records in HubSpot, not in the other app.

Please note:

  • Initial syncs for large databases may take some time. This can vary between apps due to the speed of the connected app’s API. Syncs with millions of records may take several days to complete.
  • Saving the sync will restart the initial sync.
  • HubSpot will send an email when the initial sync completes.
Incremental sync

The incremental sync constantly scans for updates in HubSpot and the other app (based on the sync direction) and waits to be triggered. HubSpot checks if there are changes every five minutes. The other app, or its API, uses webhooks to alert of any changes.

Connect an app

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions to connect an app in HubSpot. Depending on the app, there may be other permissions required for the specific app you’re connecting.

You can search for and connect to an app in two ways: from the App Marketplace or the imports page.

To connect an app from the App Marketplace:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and click the app name.
  • Click Install.
  • In the dialog box, click Next, then log in to your app account.
  • Review the requested access permissions, then click Allow. You’ll be redirected back to the app page in your HubSpot settings.

If you’re setting up a sync from the imports page:

  • Click Import in the top right of any object home page, or access your import settings:

    • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
    • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Import & Export.
    • Click Go to import.

  • Click Connect an app.

  • In the dialog box, search for and select the app name.

  • Click Install.

  • You’ll be redirected to the app’s listing page to continue with the connection steps.

It’s possible to connect more than one instance of the same third-party app to HubSpot. For example, if you’re managing two Microsoft Dynamics accounts, you can connect and sync data from both accounts with one HubSpot account. To connect an additional account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the name of the app.
  • In the top right, click Account actions > Manage accounts.
  • In the right panel, click Connect another account.
  • Proceed with the steps to connect the app to HubSpot.

Turn on data sync

After connecting the app, you need to configure your app settings and turn the sync on to begin syncing data between the two systems.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app.

  • Click Set up your sync.

  • On the Select the data you want to sync page, select the object to sync in the app and the corresponding HubSpot object.

    • If you’re connecting a spreadsheet app, such as Airtable, Smartsheet, Kintone, Monday.com, or Notion, HubSpot automatically recommends a HubSpot object after you select your source table.

      • Review the recommended HubSpot object mapping.
      • If HubSpot recommends renaming or activating an object, review the recommendation and confirm the changes.
      • If needed, you can manually select a different HubSpot object.

  • Click the arrows dropdown menu, and select whether the sync is bi-directional or one way between the app and HubSpot, or vice versa.

Learn more about syncing contacts and leads to other apps.

Configure your sync direction

On the Configure page, choose the sync direction and map the third-party app’s fields to HubSpot properties.

In the Sync direction section, decide how you want data to sync from HubSpot to the third-party app, and vice versa. There are three options:

  • Data syncs between apps: all new and updated object information will be synced between the two apps. Properties will be merged for records that already exist in both systems.
  • Data syncs only to HubSpot: data will sync only from your third-party app to HubSpot.
  • Data syncs only to your third-party app: data will sync only from HubSpot to your third-party app.

If the third-party app you’re connecting supports event sync, you’ll have the ability to sync supported events, like email opens and clicks, from the third-party app to HubSpot.

Before turning event sync on, please note the following:

  • Event sync is one-way, from the third-party app to HubSpot.
  • Event sync only syncs events associated with contact records.
  • If a contact record fails to sync, any associated event can still sync to HubSpot.
  • Events will only sync if they are associated with contacts that are already in HubSpot.

To turn on event sync, select the checkbox One way sync [your third-party app] event to HubSpot.

In the Data conflict resolution section, click the dropdown menu and select the default app that’ll overwrite the other when there are data discrepancies. If there’s no field value in the default app, no data will be changed in the third-party app. This setting doesn’t overrule the sync direction selected in the Sync direction section.

Review your field mappings

Review and update how fields are mapped between HubSpot and your other app. Required fields will show in the field mappings table with an asterisk (*).

  • In the Mapped fields section, review how fields are currently mapped.

  • To generate suggested mappings for your fields, click Generate mappings. HubSpot analyzes the names and field types in both systems to suggest matches, including custom properties. Review the suggested mappings, then accept all or clear any mappings you don’t want to use.

  • To turn off a mapping, click to turn the toggle off.

Subscription required

  • If you have a Data Hub subscription, you can set up custom mappings for properties.
  • If you don’t have a paid Data Hub subscription, click Try out custom mappings to test the feature.

To set up a custom field mapping:

  • Click Add a mapping.

  • Use the dropdown menus to select the third-party app and the HubSpot property you want to map.

  • Click success Update.

  • To turn off custom mappings, click to toggle the switch off.

Learn more about specific rules and considerations for data sync field mappings.

Set up your sync rules

On the Limit page, configure how you want to sync records from HubSpot to your third-party app, and vice versa.

If you’re configuring a deal sync, you’ll be prompted to map your deal pipelines and stages between HubSpot and your third-party app. Only deals in the mapped deal stages will sync.

  • In the Map your deal pipelines and stages section, click the Choose a HubSpot pipeline dropdown menu to choose which HubSpot deal pipeline you want to sync with your third-party app.
  • Click Auto-map to automatically map HubSpot deal stages with your third-party app’s deal stages. The sync does a simple text search and attempts to map similar-sounding stages.
  • To map an additional pipeline, click Map another pipeline.

If you’re unable to view deal stages from your other app in HubSpot, it is because of the following reasons:

  • The connected user account doesn’t have the correct permissions to view the deal stages.
  • Data sync maps HubSpot deal stages with pipeline stages in your other app. If you have a non-standard sales process that doesn’t rely on deal/opportunity stages, you won’t be able to sync data using HubSpot data sync.

If you’re configuring a product sync and your third-party app has multiple product libraries, you must specify which product type items will be assigned to when they sync to HubSpot, and vice versa. HubSpot has one product library, while your third-party app may have several.

  • On the Limit page, click the Product type dropdown menu and select which product types will sync from HubSpot to your third-party app. Then click Next.
  • On the Organize page, select the product type the third-party app’s products will be assigned to when they first sync to HubSpot.

If you’re syncing data between HubSpot and a third-party app that has both contact and lead syncing available, you can specify which leads and contacts should sync based on their lifecycle stage.

  • If syncing leads, on the Limit page in the Contacts syncing from HubSpot to [your third-party app] section, click Edit and select which lifecycle stage contacts in HubSpot need to be in to sync to the third-party app as leads.
  • If syncing contacts, on the Limit page in the Contacts syncing from HubSpot to [your third-party app] section, click Edit and select which lifecycle stage contacts in HubSpot need to be in to sync to the third-party app as contacts.

Please note: if you’re setting up both a contact and lead sync for the same app, any lifecycle stages selected for one sync will not be available for the other.

If you’re configuring a contact sync, by default, HubSpot will only sync contacts that have a valid email address. To also sync contacts without an email address, in the Duplicate reduction section, clear the Only sync contacts with an email address checkbox.

Learn more about matching records.

Please note: when an app has both a company name and company domain field, HubSpot will match two records if they have the same company name but a different domain, and vice versa.

In the Filters section, choose criteria to limit which records will sync from HubSpot to your third-party app, and vice versa:

  • Click Edit.

  • In the right panel, in the Describe your filter box, describe your filter in plain language. For example, enter exclude contacts who have unsubscribed. Then, click Generate filters. Review the generated filters, then click Add these filters. Alternatively, you can manually select properties for your filter.

Please note: the Filters section only limits which records initially sync between HubSpot and the third-party app. Once records sync, they will continue to sync data back and forth based on the property mapping set up.

Associate records

HubSpot attempts to maintain the same associations between records (e.g., companies associated with contacts, or deals associated with companies) when syncing with the original app you connected, whenever possible. Learn more about association mapping with data sync.

Please note: in most cases, data sync can only automatically associate invoices to contacts. Invoices must be manually associated to company records in HubSpot.

Review rules and start the sync

On the Review page, review the rules you’ve configured, then click Save and sync. The initial sync will then begin to process.

After the initial sync is complete, records will sync within 10 minutes of a change.

Resync deleted records

If you’ve deleted records in either HubSpot or your third-party app, you can resync deleted records to recreate them in either app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the app.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • On the Object view tab, in the Failing column, click the number of records that are failing to sync.
  • In the right panel, click Actions.
  • Select either Resync deleted records in HubSpot or Resync deleted records in [third-party app].
  • Click Resync all.

You can also restore deleted records:

  • On the Record view tab, click More > Restore all deleted records.

  • In the side panel, click the Record type dropdown menu and select the record type and the Destination app dropdown menu to select which app to recreate the contacts in.

  • Click Review before restore.

  • Review all the records that’ll be restored, and click Restore all [number].

Turn off data sync

You can turn off data sync to prevent records from the app from syncing from HubSpot, and vice versa.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the app.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • Hover over the object sync, click the More dropdown menu, and select Turn off sync.
  • In the pop-up box, click Turn off sync.

Once the sync has been turned off, you can turn it on again by clicking Edit sync settings, or delete the sync.

Review your sync health

After connecting an app, view an overview of the records syncing between HubSpot and your third-party app.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Object view to view the sync status by objects.

    • Records that are being processed as part of an initial sync will have spinning circles next to them.
    • A record will have a status of In queue if another sync is in process, to prevent updates happening on the same data, at the same time.
    • Hover your mouse over each object’s sync status to find out more details about its sync progress. The sync status tracker shows the current sync stage for the integration, such as scanning, syncing, and synced and listening for changes.

  • In the In sync column, click the number of records to review all records syncing between HubSpot and the app.

  • In the Failing column, click the number of records to view all records failing to sync between HubSpot and the app.

    • In the Sync Activity column, click the RightIco right arrow next to an error to view more information about the reason for sync failure.
    • Click artificialIntelligenceIcon Troubleshoot to open Breeze Assistant and receive guidance and troubleshooting steps to resolve the sync error for a record.

  • In the Excluded column, click the number of records to view all records excluded from sync. This could be because they don’t match any of the filters in your sync settings, or they don’t have a unique identifier assigned to them, which may be due to a matching key being defined.

If the sync is failing for some records, you can trigger a resync only for those records.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the app.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab. Then click the Record view tab.
  • Click the checkbox next to the records you want to resync.
  • Then click Rerun sync on [count] record.

Export records from a data sync app

To export records from a data sync app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the app.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • In the In Sync, Failing, or Excluded columns, click the number next to the object you’d like to export records for.
  • In the top right, click More, then select Export.
  • Click the File format dropdown menu and select a format.
  • Click Export. Once the export is processed, you’ll receive a download link through email and in the notification center.

Connect apps to Breeze Assistant

Breeze Assistant lets you connect supported third-party apps so you can retrieve information and complete supported actions across those apps without leaving HubSpot. Connecting apps expands what Breeze Assistant can access, allowing you to get insights and complete tasks within Breeze Assistant.

For example, after connecting Asana, you can ask Breeze Assistant to check your open tasks or review the status of a project. After connecting Notion, you can ask Breeze Assistant to draft content using information from your HubSpot account.

Connected apps are also available in Breeze Assistant projects. Add connectors to a project to let Breeze Assistant retrieve information or complete supported actions in those apps as part of project conversations. Learn more about using projects in Breeze Assistant.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before you begin connecting apps to Breeze Assistant, review the following requirements and considerations.

  • Review the requirements to use Breeze Assistant.
  • You must have an account for each third-party app that you want to connect.
  • Only supported apps can be connected to Breeze Assistant.
  • Each app supports a different set of actions.
  • Apps that you’ve already connected through Agent Builder are available in Breeze Assistant and don’t need to be connected again.

Supported apps

Breeze Assistant currently supports connections for the following apps:

  • Amplitude
  • Atlassian
  • Asana
  • Box
  • Canva
  • Fathom
  • G2
  • Gmail
  • Gong
  • Google Calendar
  • Google Chat
  • Google Drive
  • Linear
  • NetSuite
  • Notion
  • Slack
  • Xero
  • Zoom

Connect an app to Breeze Assistant

To use apps with Breeze Assistant, first connect the apps that you want to access. After the connection is complete, you can ask Breeze Assistant to retrieve information or perform supported actions using those apps.

  • In the top navigation bar in your HubSpot account, click breezeSingleStarIcon Breeze Assistant.

  • Click +, then navigate to Connectors > + Add connector.

  • On the app that you want to connect, click Connect.

  • Sign in to your account for the app that you’re connecting.

  • Review the permissions required by the app. Then click Allow.

  • After the app is connected, click X in the top right to return to Breeze Assistant.

Use connectors in Breeze Assistant

After connecting an app, ask Breeze Assistant to retrieve information or complete actions in that app.

  • In the top navigation bar, click breezeSingleStarIcon Breeze Assistant.

  • Enter your prompt. For example, you can:

    • Check your open Asana tasks.
    • Summarize product usage data from Amplitude.
    • Create a Notion draft using information from a HubSpot record.
    • Find buyer intent information from G2.

  • Click the breezeSendIcon send icon in the bottom right.

  • The responses and actions available in Breeze Assistant depend on the connected app.

  • When you ask Breeze Assistant to create or edit data in a connected app, you’ll be prompted to grant the required access permissions.

If your prompt includes actions in an app that isn’t connected to your HubSpot account, Breeze Assistant lets you know that the app isn’t connected and provides instructions for connecting it.

Manage connectors in Breeze Assistant

To review the available actions for a connected app:

  • In the top navigation bar, click breezeSingleStarIcon Breeze Assistant.
  • Click +, then navigate to Connectors > Manage connectors.
  • On the connected app card, click Manage.
  • In the Overview section, review the available actions and example requests.

To disconnect an app that you no longer want Breeze Assistant to access:

  • In the top navigation bar, click breezeSingleStarIcon Breeze Assistant.
  • Click +, then navigate to Connectors > Manage connectors.
  • On the connected app card, click Manage.
  • In the top right, click Actions, then select Uninstall [app name].
  • In the dialog box, enter the required text in the text field.
  • Then click Uninstall.

Configure connector permissions

For each connected app, configure which tools Breeze Assistant can use. You can manage individual tool permissions or apply the same permissions to all tools.

To configure tool permissions:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app for which you want to manage tool permissions.

  • Click the Settings tab.

  • Review the available read-only and write tools the app has access to.

  • To view details about a specific tool, click the right arrow to expand the section and see more information about its permissions.

  • For each tool, select the permission that determines when Breeze Assistant can use it:

    • Always allow: the tool can be used without requiring confirmation.
    • Ask permission: you’ll be prompted to authorize access each time the tool is used.
    • Never allow: the tool won’t be available for use.

  • To update permissions for multiple tools at once, click the dropdown menu in the top right of the Read-only and Write sections and select a permission for all read tools or all write tools.

Connect apps to HubSpot’s AI agents

Connect HubSpot’s AI agents in Agent Builder to external systems through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This allows agents to access live business data and perform actions across supported applications without requiring custom integrations or code.

For example, a revenue operations team can connect an agent in HubSpot to Gong and Notion to analyze customer conversations and generate account planning summaries.

Permissions required Agent Builder permissions are required to create and customize agents and assistants in Agent Builder.

Permissions required Additional permissions may be required depending on the goal of the assistant or agent. For example, an assistant or agent that generates a landing page requires Edit and Publish permissions to edit and publish landing pages.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features Some agents may require HubSpot Credits. Learn more about features using HubSpot Credits

Supported apps

HubSpot’s AI agents currently supports connections for the following apps:

  • Amplitude
  • Asana
  • Atlassian
  • Box
  • Canva
  • Fathom
  • G2
  • Gmail
  • Gong
  • Google Calendar
  • Google Chat
  • Google Drive
  • Linear
  • Notion
  • Slack
  • Xero
  • Zapier
  • Zoom

Please note: each supported app has its own configuration requirements and capabilities. It’s recommended that you review the information on the website for each supported app above.

Connect an app to a HubSpot’s AI agent

The process for connecting an app may vary slightly depending on the app you want to connect. For example, some apps (such as Notion and Asana) use an OAuth-based connection, while others (such as Zapier) use a tokenized URL connection.

OAuth-based connection

OAuth is the standard way to connect HubSpot to an MCP Server. This process may vary slightly between MCP Servers but generally follows these steps:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Hub. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub directly.

  • Navigate to the Agents tab.

  • Hover over the agent you want to edit, click the menu icon and select Clone to clone the agent.

  • In the Actions section, click Add action.

  • In the right panel, click the Connectors tab.

  • Hover over the app you want to connect. Then click Connect and add.

  • Follow the on-screen prompts to authorize the connection.

Tokenized URL connection (Zapier)

Some MCP Servers, like Zapier, allow you to configure your own set of tools rather than a standard group. For these connections, you’ll need to supply a custom URL provided by the vendor.

  • Navigate to the Zapier MCP page.
  • In the top left, click + New MCP Server.
  • Click the MCP Client dropdown menu and select Other.
  • Enter a name for the MCP Server in the Name field.
  • Click Create MCP Server.
  • In the Tools section, select the tools you want the MCP Server to use.

Please note: while MCP connections offer a wide range of tools, it’s recommended that you select only the tools needed for your agent’s tasks.

  • At the top of the page, click the Connect tab.

  • In the Transport section, ensure that Streamable HTTP is selected.

  • In the Connect with server-specific URL section, click Copy URL next to the Server URL.

  • Back in your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.

  • Navigate to the Agents tab.

  • Hover over the agent you want to edit, click the menu icon and select Clone to clone the agent.

  • In the Actions section, click Add action.

  • In the right panel, click the Connectors tab.

  • Hover over Zapier MCP and click Connect and add.

  • In the pop-up window, in the Zapier MCP Server URL field, paste the Server URL you copied from Zapier.

  • Then click Connect to Zapier.

Manage connectors in Agent Builder

To disconnect an app from Agent Builder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Hub. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub directly.

  • Navigate to the Agents tab.

  • Hover over an agent and click Edit.

  • In the Actions section, click Add action.

  • In the right panel, click the Connectors tab.
