  • Hover over the connector you want to disconnect and click View details.

  • Then click Disconnect.

  • In the dialog box, click Disconnect.

Configure connector permissions

For each connected app, configure which tools HubSpot’s AI agents can use. You can manage individual tool permissions or apply the same permissions to all tools.

To configure tool permissions:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app for which you want to manage tool permissions.

  • Click the Settings tab.

  • Review the available read-only and write tools the app has access to.

  • To view details about a specific tool, click the right arrow to expand the section and see more information about its permissions.

  • For each tool, select the permission that determines when HubSpot’s AI agents can use it:

    • Always allow: the tool can be used without requiring confirmation.
    • Ask permission: you’ll be prompted to authorize access each time the tool is used.
    • Never allow: the tool won’t be available for use.

  • To update permissions for multiple tools at once, click the dropdown menu in the top right of the Read-only and Write sections and select a permission for all read tools or all write tools.

Next steps

After connecting an app, learn more about configuring prompts for your agent.

Connect Epic with HubSpot to sync sensitive data

Connect Epic to HubSpot to sync sensitive data from your electronic medical system into your CRM. The integration creates a one-way sync from Epic to HubSpot, allowing data to be stored in Sensitive Data properties on HubSpot records.

Syncing data from Epic lets you use medical and other sensitive information across HubSpot tools. For example, you can segment contacts using health-related properties, trigger automation in workflows, or build reports based on synced data.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements
  • Sensitive Data settings must be turned on in your HubSpot account.
  • You must have Super Admin permissions to turn on or edit Sensitive Data settings, connect the app, and configure sync settings.
  • You must have Epic administrator access to configure Group IDs in Epic.
  • If you want to sync appointments from Epic to HubSpot, you must activate the Appointments object in HubSpot first.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Data sync is one-way from Epic to HubSpot.
  • Sensitive data handling will be subject to HIPAA requirements.
  • The Epic integration is available only to HIPAA customers based in the U.S..
  • Syncing historical patient data from Epic to HubSpot requires customer-provided Epic Group IDs.

Supported sensitive data types

The Epic integration supports syncing the following category of sensitive data:

Health data (ePHI): electronic protected health information collected and managed by entities both covered and not covered by HIPAA.

Supported Epic objects

The following Epic objects sync to HubSpot:

Epic object

HubSpot object

Patients

Contacts

Appointments

Appointments

Connect the Epic app to HubSpot

Before configuring your sync settings, connect the Epic app to your HubSpot account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.

  • In the search bar, search for and select the Epic app.

    • If you have Sensitive Data already turned on:

      • Click Install.

    • If you have Sensitive Data turned off:

      • Click Enable sensitive data.
      • On the Enable sensitive data dialog box, click to toggle Sensitive data protection on.

  • Click Connect app.

  • In the Connect your Epic account dialog box, enter your FHIR URL.

  • Click Connect to Epic.

  • You’ll be redirected to the integration settings page in HubSpot, where you can set up your sync settings.

Set up a real-time sync from Epic

To set up a real-time sync from Epic to HubSpot, you must request access to Epic’s outgoing HL7 interfaces. With real-time sync, changes to records will flow automatically from Epic to HubSpot.

To set up a real-time sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Epic.

  • Navigate to the Settings tab.

  • In the Authentication URLs section, copy the Webhook URL and Authentication key values.

  • Share the Webhook URL and Authentication key with your Epic administrator, who will use this information to submit a support ticket to Epic and request access to Epic’s HL7 outgoing interfaces.

Sync past data from Epic

Add the Epic Group IDs to the integration settings to sync historical patient data from Epic to HubSpot.

To add the Epic Group IDs:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Epic.
  • Navigate to the Settings tab.
  • In the Add Group ID section, enter a Group ID. Then click + Add another Group ID to add more Group IDs.
  • Click Save.

Turn the sync on

After connecting the app, setting up the real-time sync through Epic, and adding your Epic Group IDs, configure how data syncs to HubSpot from Epic.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Epic.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Connect to CRM.

  • On the Select the data that you want to sync page, click the Epic dropdown menu and select the Epic object (e.g. patients) you want to sync to HubSpot. Then click the HubSpot dropdown menu and select the corresponding HubSpot object (e.g., contacts). It’s recommended to sync the Epic Patients object first, as appointments are tied to patients.

  • On the Configure page, select whether you want to match Epic records to HubSpot records, or if you don’t want to match records between the two apps. Matching records based on email address is recommended to avoid duplicates. Not matching is recommended if you’re syncing all records to HubSpot for the first time.

  • In the Mapped fields section, review the default property mappings, and how Epic information syncs from Epic to HubSpot.

Please note:

  • When selecting Epic properties for custom mapping, first select the HubSpot property. The Epic properties will then become available.

  • You can only sync an Epic sensitive property to a HubSpot sensitive property. If needed, recreate the HubSpot property as a sensitive property first.

    • If your account has a Data Hub Starter subscription, you can also create custom field mappings.

      • It’s recommended to click Generate mappings to generate suggested mappings for your fields. HubSpot analyzes field names and types in both systems to suggest matches, including custom properties. Review the suggested mappings, then accept all or clear any mappings you don’t want to use.

      • To manually create a custom mapping, click Add a mapping.

        • Click the HubSpot dropdown menu and select the HubSpot property you want to map.
        • Click the Epic dropdown menu and select the corresponding Epic property.
        • Click ✔️Update.

      • To turn off a custom mapping, toggle the switch off.

  • Click Next.

  • On the Limit page, configure how records should sync from Epic to HubSpot. Learn more about using sync filters in data sync apps.

  • Click Next.

  • On the Organize page, review the automatic association information.

  • Click Review.

  • On the Review page, review the rules you’ve configured. Then click Save and sync.

Once the sync is turned on, Epic records will automatically start syncing from Epic to HubSpot.

Use Epic data in HubSpot

Sensitive data from Epic appears on associated HubSpot records based on your configured mappings. Epic patient and appointment records sync to contact and appointment records in HubSpot.

To view synced Epic records in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly. Or In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Appointments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Appointments directly.
  • In the table, click a record’s name to access the contact or appointment record.
  • At the top of the left sidebar, click Actions, then select View all properties.
  • In the right panel, click therightright arrow to expand the Epic information section and view the Epic properties for the record.

Once data starts syncing from Epic to HubSpot, you can use it across the following tools:

  • Segments: create segments using synced Sensitive Data properties to segment records. For example, you can create segments based on appointment information or health-related attributes synced from Epic.
  • Workflows: use synced Epic properties in workflows to automate actions. For example, you can enroll contacts into workflows based on appointment activity or medical property values.
  • Reports: use synced data in reports to analyze patient engagement, appointment activity, or operational trends across your CRM data.

Connect Google Drive to HubSpot

Connect Google Drive to HubSpot to attach, organize, and access your Google Drive files across CRM records and HubSpot tools. After the app is connected, users can link Google Docs, Google Slides, PDFs, and folders to records, view file activity within HubSpot, and use Google Drive files in workflows and AI-powered tools.

The integration helps teams centralize customer-facing documents and reduce manual work when managing files across sales, marketing, service, and operations processes. For example, you can automatically create shared drives and folders for new deals, attach proposal documents to company records, or generate AI-powered overviews of Google Drive files directly in HubSpot.

You can also use Google Drive files with Content Remix and workflows to streamline content creation and document management across your account.

Before you get started

Permissions required You must have App Marketplace permissions or be a Super Admin in your HubSpot account to connect the Google Drive integration.

  • Google Drive is an account-level app in HubSpot. Each user must connect their HubSpot user account to their Google Workspace account in the Google Drive integration settings.
  • HubSpot users can only attach Google Drive files if their Google Workspace user has permission to access them.
  • You can attach a maximum of 25 Google Drive files per record.
  • You can attach any type of Google Drive file, but only relevant Google Docs, Google Slides, and PDFs will generate overviews.

Connect Google Drive to HubSpot

Connect Google Drive to HubSpot to access and manage Google Drive files from your CRM records. After connecting the Google Drive app, you can link Google files to HubSpot records.

Connect the Google Drive app
  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select Google Drive from the results.
  • On the Google Drive app page, click Install.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to connect your Google account.
Add Google Drive files to HubSpot records

After connecting the app, a Super Admin or a user with the Customize record page layout permission must add the Google Drive card to the right sidebar of your HubSpot records, as well as the Google Drive Document Overviews card to the Overview tab in the middle panel. This enables you to add new Google Drive files to CRM records, view existing files, and access AI-powered overviews. Learn more about adding cards to your record layout.

To add a new Google Drive file to a record in HubSpot:

  • Navigate to your records.

  • Click the name of a record to open it.

  • On the record page, navigate to the Google Drive card in the right sidebar.

  • On the card, click + Add.

  • Select the Google file you want to link to, then click Confirm.

The Google file will be added to the Google Drive card on the right sidebar of the HubSpot record.

Use the Google Drive integration

After connecting the Google Drive app, use Google Drive files across HubSpot tools. Generate AI-powered overviews of attached files, repurpose existing content with Content Remix, and automate Google Drive processes with workflow actions to create, organize, and link Google Drive files and folders.

View AI-powered overviews for Google Drive files

After adding Google Drive files to a record in HubSpot, you can view AI-powered overviews for them with HubSpot’s AI. The overviews consider both the file’s content and the record’s context in HubSpot.

To access overviews for Google Drive files:

  • Navigate to your records.
  • Click the name of a record.
  • On the Overview tab of the middle panel, navigate to the Google Drive Document Overviews card.
  • In the top right of the Google Drive Document Overviews card, click the regenerate icon to generate overviews for the attached Google Drive files.
  • Click the right arrow to expand the Google file you want to view overviews for.

If you later update the content of a Google Drive file that already had overviews generated, a yellow icon will appear next to the file name on the Google Drive Document Overviews card. This icon indicates that the overviews may be out of date and should be regenerated.

Repurpose Google Drive files with Content Remix

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use Content Remix.

After connecting the Google Drive integration, repurpose Google Drive files with Content Remix to create new content, like blog drafts, campaign plans, or pitch decks.

Learn more about repurposing existing content with Content Remix.

Use Google Drive workflow actions

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

After connecting the Google Drive app, use the following workflow actions to automatically create and organize Google Drive assets for your HubSpot records.

Workflow action

Description

Example use case

Create shared drive

Creates a new shared drive in Google Drive.

Create a shared drive when a new company record is created.

Create folder

Creates a folder in a selected shared drive.

Create a deal-specific folder inside a company’s shared drive.

Upload a file

Uploads a file from a CRM record file-type property.

Store signed agreements in Google Drive.

Link existing drive, folder, or file

Links to an existing drive, folder or file in Google Drive.

Link pre-existing Google Drive folders, drives, or files.

To use Google Drive workflow actions:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of your workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon.

  • In the left panel, select a Google Drive action:

    • To create a shared drive, select the Create shared drive action:
      • Click the Google account dropdown menu and select the Google account you want to use.
      • In the Drive name field, enter the name of the drive.
      • Then click Save.
    • To create a folder, select the Create folder action:
      • Click the Google account dropdown menu and select the Google account you want to use.
      • In the Parent ID or URL field, enter the location of the Google Drive where you want to create the folder.
      • In the Folder name field, enter the name of the folder.
      • Click the Attach to dropdown menu and select the record type you want to attach the folder to in HubSpot.
      • Then click Save.
    • To upload a file from HubSpot to Google Drive, select the Upload file action.
      • Click the Google account dropdown menu and select the Google account you want to use.
      • In the Parent ID or URL field, enter the location of the Google Drive or folder where you want to upload the file.
      • Click the CRM object dropdown menu and select the record type you want to attach the file to in HubSpot.
      • Then click Save.
    • To link to an existing drive, folder, or file, select the Link existing Drive, Folder, or File action.
      • Click the Google account dropdown menu and select the Google account you want to use.
      • In the Resource ID or URL field, enter the ID or URL of the drive, folder, or file you want to link to the HubSpot record.
      • Click the Link to dropdown menu and select the record type you want to link the drive, folder, or file to in HubSpot.
      • Then click Save.

Connect HubSpot and Adobe Acrobat Sign

Connect HubSpot and Adobe Acrobat Sign to create, send, and track agreements from contact, company, and deal records. This integration helps keep your agreement process connected to your CRM so you can manage agreements alongside customer records and view signing activity without switching between tools. You can also import existing Adobe Acrobat Sign agreements into HubSpot and use the integration card to access agreement details from your CRM records.

Please note: the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration lets you create, send, track, and import agreements in HubSpot. It doesn’t sync contact, company, deal, or document data between HubSpot and Adobe Acrobat Sign.

Before you get started

Before you begin using the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration, please note the following:

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account to install the integration.

  • You must be an admin in Adobe Acrobat Sign.
  • You must have an Adobe Acrobat Sign enterprise subscription plan.

Connect the app

Connect Adobe Acrobat Sign to HubSpot to create, send, and track agreements from your CRM records.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select the the Adobe Acrobat Sign app.
  • Click Install.
  • In the dialog box, enter your login credentials.
  • Click Install. You’ll be redirected to your Connected apps page.

Manage your Adobe Acrobat Sign settings

After connecting the app, manage connected users and discover available Adobe Acrobat Sign features from your integration settings.

Connected users

To view all connected users:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Adobe Acrobat Sign.
  • Click the Settings tab.
  • On the Connected users tab, the table shows all HubSpot users and Adobe Acrobat Sign user accounts, and the last modified date.

To link HubSpot user accounts to Adobe Acrobat Sign user accounts to grant only authorized users access to the integration:

  • On the Connected users tab, click Add new connection.
  • Click the Choose HubSpot user dropdown menu and select a user.
  • Click the Choose Acrobat Sign user dropdown menu and select a user.
  • Then click Save.

To edit or delete a connected user:

  • On the Connected users tab, next to the user you want to edit or delete, click Actions.

    • To edit a user, select Edit.
      • Click the Choose HubSpot user dropdown menu and select a user.
      • Click the Choose Acrobat Sign user dropdown menu and select a user.
      • Click Save.
    • To delete a user, select Delete.
    • Click Delete connection to confirm deletion.

Discover new features

To discover new features with the Adobe Acrobat Sign app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Adobe Acrobat Sign.

  • Click the Feature discovery tab.

  • You can review the following Adobe Acrobat Sign features:

    • Send agreements from HubSpot.
    • Import Adobe Acrobat Sign agreements.
    • Use the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration card with in-depth recipient tracking.

Add the Adobe Acrobat Sign card to your record views

Before you’re able to create, or add existing agreements to your records, you need to add the Adobe Acrobat Sign card.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to your contact, company, or deal record.

    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.

  • Click the name of a record.

  • Click Customize.

  • Click Default view. If you want to add a team view (Professional or Enterprise only), follow the steps here.

  • To add the Adobe Acrobat Sign card to an existing tab:

    • Hover over the middle column, then click + Add card.
    • Click the Card library tab.
    • Search for the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration card and click Add card.
    • Click the X to close the panel.
    • In the upper right, click Save and exit to save your changes and leave the editor.

  • To add the Adobe Acrobat Sign card to a new tab:

    • At the top right of the middle column, click the add icon, enter a name for your tab, then click Done.
    • Click Add card.
    • Click the Card library tab.
    • Search for the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration card and click Add card.
    • Click the X to close the panel.
    • In the upper right, click Save and exit to save your changes and leave the editor.

Create and send agreements

Create and send agreements from HubSpot.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to your contact, company, or deal record.

    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.

  • Click the name of a record.

  • To add an existing agreement:

    • In the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration middle card, click Add from Acrobat Sign to add an existing agreement.
    • In the right panel, select the agreement and click Add.

  • To create a new agreement:

    • In the Adobe Acrobat Sign integration middle card, click Create new.

    • In the right panel:

      • Click the Use a template dropdown menu and select an existing template, or select Without template to start from scratch.

      • Click the Recipients dropdown menu to add additional recipients.

      • Click Create agreement.

Please note: clicking Exit at any step in the creation process will save the agreement as a draft, which can be edited later.

- On the Documents tab, review the attached documents. You can also upload documents from your computer.
- Click Add document and select Browse files to add a file from the file manager, or Choose existing attachments to add attachments from the record.
- Click Save & Next.
- On the Recipients tab, choose recipients to receive the agreement.
- In the Basic information section, review the recipient's details such as their name, email, recipient type, and identity verification. Recipient details will be auto-populated when creating agreements from a contact or deal record. If there is more than one contact associated with the deal, the recipient details will be prefilled in the order that contact data is received from Adobe Acrobat Sign. This order is not necessarily in the same order as the contacts in the associated Contact card in the right sidebar.
    - Click Add new recipient and add any details for other recipients.
    - Click the arrows next to Order in which agreement is sent to change the order that the receipients will receive the agreement.

- Click Save & Next.

- On the Message tab, enter the Agreement name | Subject (required), and the Email message (optional).
- Click Save & Next. Proceeding at this stage will change the agreement status to Authoring, and you will not be able to change the agreement documents and recipients.
- On the Review tab, review the agreement.
- Click Send an agreement to send the document.

Edit a draft agreement

To edit a draft agreement:

  • Create your agreement and click Exit at any step before Review.
  • On the record, on the middle Adobe Sign integration card, hover over the draft agreement, click Actions, then select Edit.

Remove an agreement

To remove an agreement:

  • Create your agreement.
  • On the record, on the middle Adobe Sign integration card, hover over the draft agreement, click Actions, then select Remove from HubSpot.

Please note: removed agreements will no longer be available in HubSpot, but will still exist in Adobe Acrobat Sign.

Uninstall the Adobe Acrobat Sign app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Hover over the Adobe Acrobat Sign app, click Actions, then select Uninstall.
  • In the dialog box, type the required text and click Uninstall.

Connect HubSpot and Docusign

Connect HubSpot and Docusign to create, customize, send, and track Docusign envelopes from contact, company, and deal records. By managing envelopes from HubSpot, you can use CRM data when preparing documents and track envelopes alongside the associated records.

For example, map HubSpot properties to Docusign fields to populate an envelope with record data, such as a contact’s first and last name. This reduces the need to manually enter information from HubSpot when preparing an envelope.

Learn more about importing, creating, and managing Docusign envelopes in HubSpot.

Please note: while you can use HubSpot property values in Docusign envelopes, this integration is not a data sync app that syncs full record details to Docusign.

Before you get started

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account to connect HubSpot and Docusign.

  • You must have a paid Docusign plan to use this integration.
  • You must be a Docusign Admin in your Docusign account.

Connect the app

To connect Docusign to HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select the Docusign app.
  • Click Install.
  • In the dialog box, enter your login credentials.
  • Click Install. You’ll be redirected to your Connected apps page.

Please note: Docusign is a user-level app. This means each HubSpot user must connect their Docusign user. Learn more about connecting your user.

Manage your Docusign settings

In the Docusign integration settings, manage your connected users and account, add an HMAC security key from DocuSign and configure field mappings to use HubSpot contact, company, and deal properties in DocuSign envelopes.

To modify your Docusign settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Docusign.

    • To add a HMAC security key from Docusign:

      • In the top right, click Actions > HMAC settings.
      • In the dialog box, enter your HMAC key and click Save changes.

    • To change your Docusign account connected to HubSpot:

      • In the top right, click Actions > Change account.
      • In the dialog box, click the Choose an account dropdown menu to select a different connected account.
      • Click Change account.

    • To reconnect your admin user:

      • In the top right, click Actions > Reconnect user.
      • In the dialog box, enter your Docusign login credentials and click Log in.

Please note: if you are a user in multiple Docusign accounts, all accounts will be connected to HubSpot.

Manage connected users

View a table of your Docusign connected users and remove them if needed. HubSpot users who haven’t installed the Docusign app are still able to connect their Docusign user to HubSpot.

To view and manage connected users:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Docusign.
  • Navigate to the Settings tab.
  • Click Connected users.
  • The table shows all connected HubSpot and Docusign users, the connected status, and connection date.
  • To delete a user, click Actions > Delete in the table next to the user you want to delete.

To connect your user to the already installed Docusign app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Docusign.
  • In the top right, click Actions > Reconnect user.
  • In the dialog box, enter your Docusign login credentials, and click Log in.
Configure property mappings

Create a link between HubSpot properties and Docusign envelope fields using property mappings. For example, you want the contact’s first name to be automatically filled in on the Docusign envelope. You can configure the mapping so that Docusign’s HS Contact First Name field and HubSpot’s First name properties are connected. This means if you use the Docusign field HS Contact First Name in an envelope, Docusign will suggest the HubSpot contact’s First name value.

If a property isn’t mapped, its value won’t be suggested in the envelope. For example, if First name isn’t mapped, you’ll need to manually enter the desired value when you create the envelope.

Please note:

  • To map a custom Docusign field, it should have a unique tooltip and a text field type. Without a unique Tooltip value, the custom field will not be discoverable in the mapping settings.
  • Custom property mapping is only available for Docusign eSignature Business Pro or higher plans.

To review property mappings between Docusign and HubSpot records:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Docusign.

  • Navigate to the Settings tab. Then click Property Mappings.

  • To review mappings between HubSpot properties and Docusign fields, click the tab for the object you want to review.

  • To add a custom field mapping:

    • Click Add new mapping.

    • Click the dropdown menus and select the Docusign field and HubSpot property you want to map.

    • Click Save.

  • To delete a mapping, hover over a mapping and click Actions > Delete.

Uninstall the Docusign app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Hover over the Docusign app and click Actions > Uninstall Docusign.
  • In the dialog box, type the required text and click Uninstall.

Connect HubSpot and Google Chat

Connect the app for Google Chat to HubSpot to manage notifications from Google Chat, connect Google Chat to your inbox, connect Google Chat to your help desk workspace, and receive HubSpot notifications in Google Chat. Follow the steps below to connect HubSpot and Google Chat. Then learn more about using the integration for Google Chat.

Before you get started

There a number of different ways to connect Google Chat:

  • If you want to set up Google Chat for all users in your HubSpot account, you must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account. You must also be an administrator for the Google Space workspace you want to install the integration to.

  • A Super Admin, or user with App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account that isn’t an administrator for the Google Space workspace can install the integration for the account, but every user will have to map their respective user in HubSpot and complete an authentication flow.

  • An administrator of the Google Space workspace who isn’t a HubSpot user can install the HubSpot app for Google Chat from the Google Marketplace. Once installed, every user will have to map their respective user in HubSpot and complete an authentication flow.

Please note:

  • Only one Google Chat workspace can be connected to HubSpot through this integration.
  • Where the integration was installed by an admin from the Google Workspace Marketplace beforehand, users in the Google workspace whose emails match their HubSpot email address will be automatically mapped. If the email addresses don’t match, they will need to manually create a mapping.

Connect HubSpot and Google Chat

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for and select Google Chat.
  • Click Install. You’ll be redirected to Google in a new browser tab.
  • Review the requested permissions, then click Allow.

Once you’ve approved the requested permissions, you’ll be redirected back to HubSpot. You’ll also receive a Google Chat message confirming that you’ve installed the HubSpot app for your Google workspace.

Please note: in some cases, you may encounter a loop during setup, where the login dialog box closes, the settings page shows a loading spinner, and no account is connected. In these cases, ask your Google Workspace admin to enable chat apps for the entire organization, confirm the HubSpot chat app is allowlisted, then try connecting again.

Map HubSpot and Google Chat email addresses

If your HubSpot user email doesn’t match your Google user email, you’ll need to manually map your Google Workspace account with HubSpot, using your Google email.

To manually map a user account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Google Chat.
  • Click the General settings tab.
  • Click Connect account.
  • To connect using your Google Workspace email, click Using Google Workspace user email.

Please note: the app should be installed by an admin from the Google Workspace Marketplace to use this method. If it has not been installed, you can map using Google login instead.

- Enter your Google Workspace email in the Google account field, then click Update linked account.

- A pop-up window will confirm that a verification message has been sent to Google Chat.

- Navigate to your Google Chat app and click Verify on the message from HubSpot for Google Chat.
  • To connect via the Google login, click Using Google login.

    • Enter your Google credentials and click Continue.

    • Select the access you’d like to grant, then click Continue.

    • A pop-up window will confirm that a verification message has been sent to Google Chat.

    • Navigate to your Google Chat app and click Verify on the message from HubSpot for Google Chat.

Disconnect the integration for Google Chat

To uninstall the Google Chat app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Google Chat.
  • In the upper-right, click Uninstall.
  • In the dialog box, enter the required text and click Uninstall.

Next steps

After installing the integration for Google Chat, you can manage your HubSpot notifications and help desk tickets in Google Chat. You can also see a preview of HubSpot records when sharing a record URL in Google Chat.

To see previews of HubSpot records in Google Chat, please note the following:

  • You must first map your user between HubSpot and Google Chat.
  • You must add the HubSpot app to the Google Chat space you want to share the link of the HubSpot record to.
  • The link preview in Google Chat won’t appear if you’re sharing a link to a record in HubSpot that your HubSpot user doesn’t have permission to view. Learn more about user permissions in HubSpot’s user permissions guide.
  • You can only preview links in Google Chat for HubSpot contacts, companies, deals, tickets, emails, blog posts, dashboards, and reports.

Connect HubSpot and Google Contacts

Connect Google Contacts to HubSpot using data sync to keep contact information consistent between the two apps. Depending on your sync configuration, changes to contact information in HubSpot or Google Contacts can sync with the other app, reducing the need to update the same contact in both places.

For example, you can sync contacts from Google Contacts to HubSpot so your team can work with those contacts in HubSpot while maintaining their contact information in Google Contacts.

Before you get started

Before setting up your sync, review the following limitations and considerations:

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account to connect the app.

  • Only contacts in your main Google Contacts list can sync. Contacts in Other contacts do not sync. To include one of these contacts in the sync, add the contact to your main Google Contacts list.
  • Contacts stored locally on an Android device do not sync. The contacts must be stored in Google Contacts to be available for syncing.
  • Google Contacts labels can be used as filters to control which contacts sync, but cannot be mapped to HubSpot properties. Without filters, all contacts in the main Google Contacts list can sync, excluding contacts in the Trash and Other contacts folders.

Connect the app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for and select Google Contacts.
  • Click Install.
  • In the pop-up window, click Connect to Google Contacts.
  • In the dialog box, log into your Google account.
  • Review the requested access permissions, then click Allow. Then click Continue setup. You’ll be redirected to the Google Contacts integration sync settings in HubSpot.
  • Click Set up your sync to set up your sync rules.

Configure your sync settings

After connecting Google Contacts, you’ll need to configure your settings and turn the sync on to begin syncing data between the two integrations.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Google Contacts.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Set up your sync.

  • On the Select the data you want to sync page, decide how you want data to sync from HubSpot to Google Contacts, and vice versa. It’s only possible to sync contacts with this integration. Click the sync direction arrows and select a sync direction between HubSpot and Google Contacts. You can choose from the following options:

    • Data syncs between apps: data syncs bi-directionally between HubSpot and Google Contacts.
    • Data syncs only to Google Contacts: Google contacts will be created from HubSpot contacts based on criteria. Only Google Contacts properties will be created.
    • Data syncs only to HubSpot: HubSpot contacts will be created from Google contacts based on criteria. Only HubSpot contact properties will be updated.

  • In the upper right, click Next.

  • Click the Data conflict resolution dropdown menu and select which app will overwrite the other when it’s unclear which app has the most up-to-date information.

  • In the Mapped fields section set up your field mappings.

    • Default field mappings can’t be removed or edited. To turn off a field mapping, click to toggle the switch off.
    • To add a custom field mapping, click Add a mapping to set it up.

  • On the Limit page, in the Filters section, click Edit to add any filters to limit which contacts will sync from one app to the other. You can add multiple filters with AND or OR conditions. Then click Next.

  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.

Please note: the sync filters limit the scope of the sync but will not add contacts or companies to a segment with that filter.

Learn more about configuring your other sync settings.

Customize your field mappings

Subscription required A Data Hub subscription is required to customize field mappings.

The Google Contacts integration has 11 default mappings that cannot be edited. Learn how to add a new field mapping. Also, keep in mind the following limitations for the Google Contacts integration:

  • The phone number that is listed first in Google Contacts in the Phones property will map to the Phones property in HubSpot. Any additional phone numbers in Google Contacts won’t sync unless they are labeled as Mobile or Fax, in which case they will sync with the Mobile Phone Number and Fax Number in HubSpot respectively.
  • Existing custom text fields in Google Contacts cannot be synced to HubSpot.
  • Labels in Google Contacts cannot be synced with HubSpot properties.
  • It isn’t possible to sync the Owner property between HubSpot and Google Contacts.
  • If there are multiple values in a property in Google Contacts, the first property value will be synced to the HubSpot property.

Resolve sync errors

Google Contacts has a limit of 25,000 unique contacts, including contacts in the Other contacts and Trash folders. The maximum size of an individual contact is 128 KB. If you see the error Storage quota exceeded, follow these steps to resolve it:

  • Empty the Trash and Other contacts folder.
  • Delete any duplicate or unwanted contacts.
  • Amend individual contacts so that they are below the size restriction of 128 KB.

Learn more about other sync errors that you might encounter.

Connect HubSpot and Jira (Data Sync)

Connect HubSpot and Jira to sync your HubSpot tickets with Jira issues. This gives visibility to support teams in HubSpot and Jira to resolve customer issues more quickly. Learn how to connect your Jira workspace and configure the sync to fit your business needs.

Before you get started

Before you begin connecting to Jira, please note the following:

  • If you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the New Jira App Powered by Data Sync beta.
  • You must have a Jira Cloud account. The integration won’t sync with Jira instances running on customer-owned servers.
  • Ticket Status can only sync one-way from Jira to HubSpot.
  • Attachments sync between HubSpot tickets and Jira issues only if you add a custom mapping for them. Learn how to sync attachments.
  • Attachment sync is limited to the 100 most recent files for each Jira issue and HubSpot ticket.
  • Updates to and renames of HubSpot files aren’t synced to Jira.

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account to connect the app.

Subscription required You must have at least Data Hub Starter to create any custom field mappings.

Connect the app

To connect HubSpot and Jira:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for and select Jira (Data Sync).
  • Click Install. Then click Connect to Jira.
  • In the dialog box, enter your Atlassian credentials. Review the required permissions, and click Accept.

Configure your sync settings

There are two stages to setting up the sync:

  • Set up the HubSpot ticket to Jira issue sync (one-way or bi-directional).
  • Set up the HubSpot notes to Jira issue comment sync (one-way or bi-directional).
Set up HubSpot ticket to Jira issue sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Jira (Data Sync).

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Sync more data.

  • On the Select the data you want to sync page, click the Jira (Data Sync) dropdown menu and select Issues. Then select the Site, Project, and Issue Type. If you want to sync across multiple sites, projects, or issue types, you’ll need to configure an extra sync. You can configure an unlimited number of syncs.

  • Click the sync direction arrows and select a sync direction.

    • Data syncs between apps: data syncs bi-directionally between HubSpot and Jira. Any changes will be synced between HubSpot tickets and Jira issues and new records will be created in both apps.
    • Data syncs only to HubSpot: HubSpot tickets will be created from Jira issues based on criteria. Only HubSpot ticket properties will be updated.
    • Data syncs only to Jira (Data Sync): Jira issues will be created from HubSpot tickets based on criteria. Only Jira issue properties will be created.

  • Then click Next.

  • On the Configure page:

    • Click the Data conflict resolution dropdown menu and select which app will overwrite the other when it’s unclear which app has the most up-to-date information.
    • In the Mapped fields section set up your field mappings.
      • Default field mappings cannot be removed or edited. To turn off a field mapping, click to toggle the switch off.
      • To add a custom field mapping, click Add a mapping to set it up.

  • On the Limit page:

    • In the Map your ticket pipelines and stages section, select the ticket pipeline and map each HubSpot ticket stage to a Jira status.

Please note: Ticket Status can only sync one-way from Jira to HubSpot.

- In the Filters section, click Edit to add any filters to limit which tickets or issues will sync from one app to the other. You can add multiple filters with AND or OR conditions. By default, all records are included in the sync.
    - If you select a bidirectional sync between HubSpot and Jira, you must set up filters for when you want a HubSpot ticket to create a Jira issue, and when you want a Jira issue to create a ticket in HubSpot.
    - If you want to prevent Jira issues from creating HubSpot tickets, configure a restrictive filter. If you don't apply a filter, every new HubSpot ticket or Jira issue will create a corresponding record in the other system.
  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.
Set up HubSpot notes to Jira issue comments sync

Once your HubSpot ticket to Jira issue sync is set up, set up a second sync to sync HubSpot notes associated with tickets, with Jira issue comments:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Jira (Data Sync).

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Sync more data.

  • On the Select the data you want to sync page, click the HubSpot dropdown menu and select Notes. Under Jira (Data Sync), Issue Comments will automatically be selected in the first dropdown menu.

  • Under Jira (Data Sync), select the same Site, Project, and Issue Type that you selected for your HubSpot ticket dataSyncRight Jira issue sync, to make sure the relevant notes/issue comments are syncing between the associated tickets/issues.

  • Click the sync direction arrows and select a sync direction.

    • Data syncs between apps: data syncs bi-directionally between HubSpot and Jira. Any changes will be synced between HubSpot notes and Jira issue comments and new records will be created in both apps.
    • Data syncs only to HubSpot: HubSpot notes will be created from Jira issue comments based on criteria.
    • Data syncs only to Jira (Data Sync): Jira issue comments will be created from HubSpot notes based on criteria.

  • Then click Next.

  • On the Configure page:

    • Click the Data conflict resolution dropdown menu and select which app will overwrite the other when it’s unclear which app has the most up-to-date information.
    • In the Mapped fields section set up your field mappings.
      • Default field mappings can’t be removed or edited. To turn off a field mapping, click to toggle the switch off.
      • To add a custom field mapping, click Add a mapping to set it up.

  • On the Limit page:

    • In the Filters section, under Jira dataSyncRight HubSpot, a default filter will be set to sync all issue comments. You should match the logic of the HubSpot ticket dataSyncRight Jira issue sync.
    • In the Filters section, under HubSpot dataSyncRight Jira, a default filter will be set to make sure a HubSpot note’s associated ticket is known. This ensures that notes not associated with tickets aren’t synced to Jira.

      • Click Edit to edit this filter.

      • Add an AND filter to add any further filters that you added to your HubSpot ticket dataSyncRight Jira issue sync. For example, if your HubSpot tickets have a property called Support severity, which can have values from one to five (with five being the highest) and you only sync HubSpot tickets to Jira if their Support severity is three or higher, set the same filter in this section to match the ticket filter.

      • Click Edit to add any other filters to limit which comments or notes will sync from one app to the other. You can add multiple filters with AND or OR conditions. These should match the logic you set in your HubSpot ticket dataSyncRight Jira issue sync, and each additional filter you add should include the filter Ticket name is known, as per the above example, to make sure you’re only syncing notes that have an associated ticket.

  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.

  • The sync will review every note in HubSpot, but will only sync based on the above filters.

Sync attachments between HubSpot tickets and Jira issues

Sync files attached to HubSpot tickets and Jira issues so your support and development teams can see the same files in both apps. To sync attachments, add a custom mapping to your ticket sync.

Please note:

  • Attachment sync is limited to the 100 most recent files for each Jira issue and HubSpot ticket.
  • Updates to and renames of HubSpot files aren’t synced to Jira.

To add the attachments mapping to your ticket sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Jira (Data Sync).
  • Click the CRM syncs tab.
  • Hover over your Ticket sync, and click Edit.
  • On the Configure page, in the Mapped fields section, click + Add a mapping.
  • Click the Jira (Data Sync) dropdown menu, and select Attachments.
  • Click the HubSpot dropdown menu, and select Attachments.
  • Click Update.
  • Click Next until you reach the Review page. Then, review your sync configuration, and click Save and sync.
Add HubSpot ticket links to Jira issues

Once you have installed the Jira (Data Sync) app, you can display a link to the HubSpot ticket record directly within the corresponding Jira issue. This allows you to quickly navigate from a Jira issue to the relevant HubSpot ticket. This feature requires setting up a new field mapping in the Jira sync settings within HubSpot.

To set up HubSpot ticket links in Jira:

  • In Jira, navigate to the Jira project you’re working on.

  • In the bottom right, click Configure.

  • Create a new Jira field.

    • Enter a unique name for the field in Jira, such as HubSpot Ticket link.

    • For the field type, select URL.

    • Once you’re done, click Save changes in the bottom right.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Jira (Data Sync).

  • Click Edit on your ticket sync.

  • On the Configure page, in the Mapped fields section, click Add a mapping.

  • Click the Jira (Data Sync) dropdown menu and select the new Jira field you created in Jira.

  • Click the HubSpot dropdown menu and select the ticket property Ticket Link.

Please note: the ticket property Ticket Link in HubSpot is created automatically when you install the Jira (Data Sync) integration.

  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.
  • Once you’ve gone through the steps above, a link to the HubSpot ticket record will appear in the HubSpot Ticket link field when viewing issues in Jira. Clicking the link in Jira will redirect you to the ticket record in HubSpot.

Review your sync

To review your sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Jira (Data Sync).

  • Click the CRM syncs tab. This tab shows information about the number of records in sync, failing to sync, excluded from a sync, and the timestamp of when the sync was last edited.

    • To view the individual records, click the number in each column.
    • To run the sync immediately, click Sync now.
    • To create a new or additional sync, click Sync more data.
    • To edit an existing sync, hover over the sync and click Edit.
    • To turn off a sync, hover over the sync and click More > Turn off sync.
    • To delete a sync, hover over the sync and click More > Delete sync. In the dialog box, enter the required text and click Delete sync.

Use the Jira (Data Sync) sync card

After connecting the integration, you can view the Jira (Data Sync) sync card on ticket records that are in sync to Jira issues. This gives you a more accurate view of your record syncing status, including:

  • Which Jira record the HubSpot ticket record is syncing with.
  • The status of the sync.
  • The last time the record synced.
Add the sync card

If you didn’t customize the right sidebar of your records, the Jira (Data Sync) sync card will automatically be added to your records.

If you customized the right sidebar of your records, add the integration sync card to the right sidebar for the ticket object:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Objects, then select Tickets.

  • Click the Record Customization tab.

    • To edit the default view, click Default view. This view is displayed to all users who aren’t on an assigned team.
    • To create or edit a team view (Professional and Enterprise only), click Create team view, or click the name of an existing view. A team view is displayed only to users that are main team members on the selected team.

  • In the view editor, hover over the right sidebar and click Add card.

  • Click the Card library tab.

  • Search for and select the Integrations sync card.

  • Close the panel by clicking the X in the top right. Then, save your changes by clicking Save and exit in the top right.

View the sync card

After the sync card has been added to your ticket records, you can view the following information on it:

  • External record: which Jira issue the ticket is syncing with. Click the record name to open the record in Jira.

  • Status: the status of the sync between HubSpot and Jira (Data Sync). Sync statuses include:

    • Up to date: the record is syncing successfully.
    • Sync not found: the integration is active, but currently the HubSpot record isn’t syncing with Jira.
    • Sync off: the sync has been turned off in the integration settings page.
    • Record not syncing: the record isn’t syncing due to an error. For more information, hover over the sync status, or click the sync status to navigate to the sync health page.
    • Unknown sync: the record is syncing with Jira, but sync health information isn’t available.
    • Record excluded: the record is part of an excluded from the sync. For more information, hover over the Status.

  • Last updated: when the HubSpot and Jira data was last synced.

Connect HubSpot and LinkedIn Sales Navigator

Connect HubSpot with LinkedIn Sales Navigator to view LinkedIn insights and Sales Navigator activity directly on your HubSpot records. After connecting the app, users can access information such as profile details, shared connections, and account updates without leaving HubSpot.

This integration helps sales teams research prospects, personalize outreach, and maintain context during the sales process. For example, when reviewing a contact or company record in HubSpot, you can view relevant LinkedIn Sales Navigator information alongside your CRM data to identify engagement opportunities and prepare for conversations.

Review the video below to better understand how you can use HubSpot and LinkedIn Sales Navigator together.

Before you get started

Seats required You must have an assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat to use the LinkedIn Sales Navigator integration.

  • You must have a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus account to use this integration. When you connect to LinkedIn Sales Navigator, you’re only connecting the integration to your user account. To use the integration, each user will need to connect the LinkedIn Sales Navigator app from the HubSpot Marketplace while signed in to HubSpot with their unique login.
  • It is not possible to import contacts from LinkedIn using the integration.
  • If you have a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus account, you can also connect HubSpot and LinkedIn Sales Navigator and Business Manager via CRM Sync.

Connect HubSpot and LinkedIn Sales Navigator

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select the LinkedIn Sales Navigator app.
  • Click Install.

Necessary disclosure: as part of any LinkedIn integration, HubSpot will store your account name and profile picture.

View LinkedIn data in HubSpot

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to your contacts or companies:

    • Contacts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • Companies: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.

  • Click the name of a record.

  • In the right panel, locate the LinkedIn Sales Navigator card. It’ll contain LinkedIn information for the contact or company.

  • Please note: if you install the LinkedIn Sales Navigator app after Oct. 7, 2025, a Super Admin or a user with the Customize record page layout permission must add the integration card to the right sidebar of HubSpot records. Learn more about adding cards to a record page layout.

    • Contacts: view the contact’s LinkedIn job title, company, time in their current role, location, and industry. HubSpot uses the contact’s first name, last name, email, company, and job title to search for their profile.
    • Companies: view the company’s industry, size, and location. HubSpot uses the company’s name and domain to search for their company profile.

  • To save the contact information to a list in LinkedIn Sales Navigator, click Save in Sales Navigator.

  • To access a more detailed view, click View more.

  • To send an InMail to the contact on LinkedIn, click Send InMail.

  • For contacts, you’ll see the following tabs:

    • Icebreakers: view shared connections, experiences, and interests, plus a link to the contact’s recent activity stream.
    • Get introduced: ask a mutual connection for an introduction to your contact.
    • Related leads: quickly find other leads at the same company and add them to your Sales Navigator leads list.

  • For companies, you’ll see the following tabs:

    • Overview: view a summary of the company profile.

    • Find People: connect with other leads at the company that you share interests and experiences with.

    • Relationship Map: visualize and manage account information and connections.

    • Connections: view contacts at the company that you’re already connected with.

    • News: view company news to add context to your sales outreach.

Send InMails from contact and company records

You can compose and send InMails directly from a HubSpot contact or company record:

- In your HubSpot account, navigate to your contact or company records:
    - Contacts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to [CRM > Contacts](https://app.hubspot.com/l/contacts/objects/0-1). If More doesn't appear in your account, navigate to [CRM > Contacts](https://app.hubspot.com/l/contacts/objects/0-1) directly.
    - Companies: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to [CRM > Companies](https://app.hubspot.com/l/contacts/objects/0-2). If More doesn't appear in your account, navigate to [CRM > Companies](https://app.hubspot.com/l/contacts/objects/0-2) directly.
- Click the name of a record.
- In the right panel, locate the LinkedIn Sales Navigator card.

Please note: if you install the LinkedIn Sales Navigator app after Oct. 7, 2025, a Super Admin or a user with the Customize record page layout permission must add the integration card to the right sidebar of HubSpot records. Learn more about adding cards to a record page layout.

- Click Send InMail.
- In the LinkedIn InMail pop-up box, write your message, then click Send.

You can continue to send InMail messages in HubSpot and view the entire conversation in the LinkedIn InMail pop-up box, but the conversation will not automatically save to the record’s timeline. You can manually log a LinkedIn message to a contact timeline if needed.

If you have access to sequences, you can add task reminders to send InMails or connection requests. Learn how to use LinkedIn Sales Navigator tasks in a sequence.

Manage LinkedIn Sales Navigator tasks on mobile

If you have a paid LinkedIn Sales Navigator account integrated with HubSpot and have downloaded the HubSpot mobile app, you can manage your Sales Navigator tasks in the app.

  • Navigate to your tasks in the mobile app.
  • Tap on the Send InMail and Send connection request tasks.
  • You’ll be redirected to the LinkedIn app to complete your task. For the Send Connection request task, HubSpot will redirect you to the search screen in the LinkedIn app with the contact name prefilled.

Troubleshoot LinkedIn Sales Navigator

If you encounter issues with the LinkedIn Sales Navigator iframe in HubSpot not loading or displaying an error message, review the common issues below.

Please sign in to LinkedIn Sales Navigator

This message usually indicates that your LinkedIn Sales Navigator session has expired and needs to be re-authenticated.

To resolve this issue:

  • Log out of LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
  • Log back into LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
  • Return to HubSpot and verify whether the iframe loads correctly.

If the message continues to appear after you’ve successfully logged in, the issue may be related to your browser or local environment. It’s recommended to try the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Clear your browser cache and cookies.
  • Open HubSpot in an incognito or private browsing window.
  • Try a different supported browser.
  • Turn off browser extensions or ad blockers.
  • Confirm that you’re logged into the correct LinkedIn user account.
  • Confirm that you have a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus account.
  • Confirm that your HubSpot user has an assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat.
Subscription-related error messages

The following error messages are typically related to your LinkedIn Sales Navigator subscription:

  • You need a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Team contract to gain access to this integration.
  • Upgrade to LinkedIn Sales Navigator Team Edition.
  • LinkedIn Sales Navigator subscription not found.

If you receive one of these messages, verify the following:

  • You have a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus account.
  • Your HubSpot user has an assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat.
  • You’re logged in to the correct LinkedIn user account.

Connect HubSpot and LinkedIn Sales Navigator and Business Manager via CRM Sync

Connect HubSpot and LinkedIn Sales Navigator & Business Manager through CRM Sync. With this app, you’re able to:

  • Import and save HubSpot contacts and companies in a Sales Navigator list.
  • Automatically log Sales Navigator activities to HubSpot.
  • Create and update HubSpot contacts from Sales Navigator.
  • Include or exclude matched contacts and companies in Sales Navigator searches.
  • Run a Revenue Attribution Report in Business Manager.

Before you get started

Permissions required You must either be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace access permissions in your HubSpot account to install the app.

Seats required You must have an assigned Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise seat in HubSpot.

  • You must have a LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus plan.
  • If you want to see HubSpot data in Sales Navigator, you must be a Sales Navigator account admin.

Connect the app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Use the search bar to locate and select LinkedIn CRM Sync.
  • Click Install.
  • In the dialog box, click Connect to LinkedIn CRM Sync. You’ll be redirected to Sales Navigator to continue the process.
  • Select which environment you want to sync data with. You can only connect one HubSpot account with one Sales Navigator environment at a time.
  • In the dialog box, review the requirements and click Accept & Continue. You’ll be redirected back to HubSpot.
  • In the dialog box, click Set up sync to proceed with setting up the sync or Do this later to complete it at a later time.

Set up data sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click LinkedIn CRM Sync.
  • In the upper right, click Start all syncs. This will start the sync for contacts, companies, deals, and owners. Review the table below for how HubSpot objects match to LinkedIn terminology:

HubSpot object

LinkedIn terminology

Contacts

Leads

Companies

Accounts

Deals

Opportunities

Owners

N/A

  • To view information about a sync, hover over object sync and click View.

    • In the Configure section, review how data is syncing between HubSpot and LinkedIn objects.
    • In the Limit section, review which records will sync between HubSpot and LinkedIn.
    • In the Organize section, review whether automatic associations and deletions are possible with this object sync.

In addition to syncing HubSpot CRM data to LinkedIn, LinkedIn data also syncs to HubSpot in the form of CRM writebacks. To achieve this, each user must authenticate their Sales Navigator account with HubSpot:

  • Navigate to your CRM settings in LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
  • In the CRM Settings section, click Connect to CRM.
  • In the dialog box, click Establish Connection.

If you’re an Admin in Sales Navigator, you can control the writeback features from the Admin Settings page.

After connecting the two apps, review the following:

  • How syncing data to LinkedIn affects your use of Sales Navigator.
  • How data from LinkedIn Sales Navigator syncs to HubSpot.
  • How syncing data to Linkedin affects your use of Business Manager (Marketing).

Please note:

  • Only new and updated data will sync between HubSpot and Sales Navigator after the sync is turned on. If you want to reset the sync and sync all records regardless of whether they’ve been updated or not, uninstall and reinstall the app.
  • Editing the data sync is not possible. All mapped fields are either set to sync or not sync, so you cannot turn off individual mappings. To turn off the data sync, you must uninstall the app.

Uninstall the app

To disconnect HubSpot and LinkedIn CRM sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Hover over the LinkedIn CRM sync app, click Actions, then click Uninstall.
  • In the pop-up window, type the required text and click Uninstall.

Connect HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics 365

Connect the Microsoft Dynamics 365 app to HubSpot to sync data between Microsoft Dynamics 365 objects and HubSpot records. Keeping records in sync gives teams working in either app access to consistent, up-to-date customer information without manually updating the same data in both systems. You can configure one-way or two-way sync based on how you want data to move between the apps.

You can also create Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales orders from HubSpot deal records or through workflows. With a Data Hub subscription, you can create custom field mappings to control how data syncs between the two apps.

Before you get started

Before connecting Microsoft Dynamics 365 to HubSpot, review the following requirements:

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace Access permissions in your HubSpot account to install the integration.

  • Your Microsoft Dynamics 365 environment must be cloud-hosted on an official dynamics.com domain.
  • You must have Read permissions for records in Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • To set up a two-way sync, you must have Read and Write permissions for each record type in Microsoft Dynamics 365.

Install the Microsoft Dynamics 365 app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for Microsoft Dynamics 365, and select Microsoft Dynamics 365 in the results.
  • Click Install.
  • Enter your Microsoft Dynamics 365 subdomain and click Connect to Microsoft Dynamics 365.

You can connect two instances of Microsoft Dynamics 365 to HubSpot. Both instances will have the same syncing capabilities.

To connect another Microsoft Dynamics 365 instance:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • In the top right, click Account actions > Manage accounts.
  • In the right panel, click Connect another account.
  • Follow the steps to connect the other Microsoft Dynamics 365 account.

Turn on the sync

After connecting the app, you need to turn the sync on. You can configure a one-way or two-way sync for your data.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • Click Set up your sync.
  • On the Choose an object to sync page, select the object you want to sync between HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics 365. You can sync the following object types:

HubSpot object

Microsoft Dynamics 365 object

Company

Account

Contact

Contact and Lead

Deal

Opportunity

Custom objects

Entities

Product

Bundles and Products

Meetings

Appointments

Notes

Notes

Tasks

Tasks

Invoice

Invoice

Order

Sales orders

Emails

Emails

Calls

Phone calls

  • Click Next.

Please note: a task must be associated with another object record (e.g., lead or contact) to sync from HubSpot to Microsoft Dynamics. If the task is associated with a Dynamics Lead, it can only sync one-way from Microsoft Dynamics to HubSpot.

You can configure a one-way or two way sync for your data.

For any objects that match on a non-unique name field (for example, a company or product name, depending on your sync configuration), data sync uses normalization when matching records. This means capitalization, special characters, and punctuation in those name fields are ignored during matching.

Once the sync has been turned on, you can configure your sync settings. Learn more about configuring your sync settings and adding the HubSpot contact timeline to Microsoft Dynamics.

Sync custom Lookup properties with Microsoft Dynamics 365

Sync supported custom Lookup properties between HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics 365 to keep property values updated in both apps. For example, you can sync custom Lookup properties such as SDR Owner and CSM Owner, so changes made in either app are reflected in the other.

To configure two-way sync for custom Lookup properties:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • Click the sync you want to configure (e.g., Contact sync).
  • In the Mapped fields section, click + Add a mapping.

Subscription required A Data Hub subscription is required to create custom field mappings.

  • Click the dropdown menus and select the supported custom Lookup property in Microsoft Dynamics 365 and the corresponding HubSpot property.
  • Click the dropdown menu for the sync direction and select Data syncs between apps.
  • Click success Create.

To verify the sync, update a mapped property in HubSpot and confirm that the change syncs with Microsoft Dynamics 365. Repeat this process by updating the property in Microsoft Dynamics 365.

Turn off the sync

You can turn off data sync to prevent records from the app from syncing from HubSpot, and vice versa.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • Hover over the sync you want to turn off and click More > Turn off sync.
  • In the pop-up window, click Turn off sync.

After you turn off the sync, data will no longer sync between HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics.

Create a Microsoft Dynamics sales order from a deal record

Please note: make sure that you have configured the Microsoft Dynamics sales order to HubSpot order sync. If the sync isn’t configured, creating a Microsoft Dynamics sales order won’t create a corresponding HubSpot order.

You can manually create a Microsoft Dynamics sales order from a HubSpot deal record:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.
  • Click the name of the deal you want to create a Microsoft Dynamics sales order for.
  • On the right sidebar of the deal, on the Sales Orders card, click Add > Create a Microsoft Dynamics sales order.
  • On the Account page, select the Microsoft Dynamics account and the custom form to create a sales order.
  • Click Next.
  • On the Customer page, select the Microsoft Dynamics customer you want to create a sales order for.
  • Click Next.
  • On the Order page, add the order information to the sales order fields based on your chosen custom form type.
  • On the Review page, review the sales order and make any necessary edits.
  • Click Create sales order.

After you create a Microsoft Dynamics sales order, a corresponding HubSpot order will be created automatically. The HubSpot order will be associated with both the HubSpot deal and the Microsoft Dynamics sales order.

Please note: if the line item price is changed on a HubSpot deal record, this will not sync to the created Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales order.

Create a Microsoft Dynamics sales order using deal-based workflows

Please note: make sure that you have configured the Microsoft Dynamics sales order to HubSpot order sync. If the sync isn’t configured, creating a Microsoft Dynamics sales order won’t create a corresponding HubSpot order.

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

Use deal-based workflows to automatically create Microsoft Dynamics sales orders when the workflow is triggered.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Microsoft Dynamics 365.

  • Click the Feature Discovery tab.

  • In the Automate your Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales orders section, click Go to workflows.

  • To edit an existing workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or, learn how to create a new deal-based workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + add icon to add an action.

  • In the left panel, search for Microsoft Dynamics and select Create a Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales order.

  • Set up your Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales order action. The following fields are required:

    • Microsoft Dynamics 365 account: a list of connected Microsoft Dynamics 365 accounts will display. Select an account to create the sales order.

    • Subsidiary: a list of subsidiaries associated with the selected Microsoft Dynamics 365 account will display. Select a Subsidiary to create the sales order.

    • Customer: select either Use first associated HubSpot contact or Use first associated HubSpot company to set as the designated Customer for the sales order.

    • Items: set the deal’s associated line items as the Items for the sales order.

    • To add another field to the sales order, click the Add another field dropdown menu and select a field.

      • To populate the field with property values from the enrolled deal record, click Deal in this workflow. Then, select a property.
      • To populate the field based on other actions in the workflow, click the action name and select an option. You can populate fields based on an action’s outcome, or outputs from the action.
      • To remove a field from the sales order, click the delete icon next to the field.

After the workflow creates a Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales order, a corresponding HubSpot order will be created automatically. The HubSpot order will be associated with both the HubSpot deal and the Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales order.

Connect HubSpot and Microsoft Teams

Connect HubSpot and Microsoft Teams to bring HubSpot notifications, meetings, tasks, tickets, and workflow actions in one place without switching between applications. For example, you can receive HubSpot notifications in Microsoft Teams channels, add Microsoft Teams meeting links to scheduling pages, create tasks and tickets from Teams, and send workflow notifications to keep teams aligned on customer activity.

This article explains how to connect HubSpot and Microsoft Teams and configure the integration for your account.

Before you get started

Please note:

  • You can connect only one instance of Microsoft Teams to a HubSpot account.
  • A personal version of a Microsoft Teams account cannot be connected to HubSpot.
  • It’s not possible to install the same Microsoft Teams account across different HubSpot data centers.

Before connecting HubSpot and Microsoft Teams, make sure you’ve given your users in Microsoft Teams permission to install and use the HubSpot app.

  • Navigate to the Microsoft Teams admin center.

  • On the left sidebar, click Team apps > Manage apps and search for HubSpot.

  • Click the HubSpot app. Then click the Available to field.

  • In the Edit availability panel, click the Available to dropdown menu and select either Everyone or Specific users or groups, depending on whom you want to grant access to.

  • Back on the Manage apps page, in the top right click Actions > Org-wide app settings.

  • In the Org-wide app settings panel, check that the HubSpot app is allowed under your organization’s permissions policy. Then click Save.

App requirements
