  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Snowflake.

  • In the sunset banner, click Set up new sync.

  • You’ll be redirected to the Data Integration page.

  • In the right panel, your existing Snowflake account will auto-populate. Click Select.

  • Select the Snowflake table and warehouse that you want to sync.

  • On the How do you want to use your Snowflake data? dialog box, select one of the following options:

    • Connect this app directly to your CRM: sync the selected Snowflake data directly to HubSpot. This option is recommended if you don’t need to modify the source data before syncing.
      • You’ll be prompted to select the source columns and map them to the HubSpot object you want to sync to, as well as the sync frequency. Learn more about setting up the sync.
      • Click Sync to HubSpot CRM.
    • Connect this app to Data Hub: connect the source to Data Studio before syncing to HubSpot. This option is recommended if you want to manipulate your source data, create formulas, add conditional logic, or combine multiple data sources before syncing.
      • You’ll be prompted to select the source columns and the sync frequency.
      • Click Set up CRM sync.
      • You’ll be redirected to the Dataset builder where you can edit your source data with filters and formulas. Learn more about setting up the sync with Data Studio
3. Verify and monitor the new Snowflake sync

After setting up the sync, confirm that it’s importing data as expected.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Integration. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration directly.
  • Click the App syncs tab.
  • Verify that the sync is importing data correctly.
4. Turn off the legacy Snowflake sync

After you’ve verified that the new sync is working correctly, turn off or delete the legacy Snowflake sync.

Please note: only turn off the legacy sync after verifying that the new sync is working correctly and importing the expected data.

Connect HubSpot and Xero (Data Sync)

Connect HubSpot and Xero to sync contacts, products, invoices, and payments between the two platforms. Depending on the object, you can configure a one-way or two-way sync to keep customer and financial data consistent across your CRM and accounting software. This helps reduce manual data entry, minimize duplicate updates, and ensure your sales and finance teams are working with the same information. For example, when an invoice is created or updated in Xero, it can sync to HubSpot so your team can view billing information alongside customer records.

The Xero HubSpot integration allows you to:

  • Sync Xero and HubSpot contacts one-way, or bi-directionally.
  • Sync Xero items and HubSpot products one-way, or bi-directionally.
  • Sync Xero invoices to HubSpot, or sync invoices bi-directionally between Xero and HubSpot.
  • Sync payments applied to invoices from Xero to HubSpot, or bi-directionally between Xero and HubSpot.

Please note: it’s recommended to consult with your accounting and legal teams on the suitability of this functionality for your needs, before connecting the integration.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account.

Subscription required You must have at least Data Hub Starter to create any custom field mappings.

Understand limitations & considerations

The two-way invoice sync functionality is most useful for small businesses who are looking to run their billing from HubSpot, whether that’s creating invoices manually, using HubSpot’s subscription functionality, or converting their deals or quotes into payable invoices and subscriptions.

This integration is beneficial for small businesses looking to streamline their billing process, or streamline the handoff process from Sales to Accounting to start billing and collecting payments.

Some key features to consider:

  • Editing invoices: invoices created from HubSpot need to be edited from HubSpot (for example, adding or removing line item items, updating pricing, or removing a payment), otherwise the invoice will fail to sync. Invoices created in Xero can be edited inside Xero without any issues.
  • Syncing invoices with insufficient stock: invoices that include tracked inventory items with insufficient stock in Xero (items that would go on backorder) won’t sync. The error A validation exception occurred. Insufficient stock. Items are eligible for backorder will appear for these invoices in the sync settings in HubSpot.
  • Changing product SKUs: if you update a product’s SKU in HubSpot after it’s already been added as a line item on a synced invoice, that invoice can no longer sync to Xero. To fix this, remove and re-add the line item on the HubSpot invoice so it picks up the current SKU, then re-sync.
  • Charging tax: tax rates from your Xero account are imported into your HubSpot tax rates library when you configure outbound or bi-directional invoice sync. This allows for the imported tax rates from Xero to be applied to individual line items on your invoice. The tax information will then be synced to Xero along with your invoice.

Please note:

  • Invoices that use HubSpot’s automated sales tax won’t sync from HubSpot to Xero.

  • It’s recommended that you configure your tax rates in Xero before turning on outbound or bi-directional invoice sync.

  • Tax rates created in HubSpot won’t sync to Xero. If you update or add tax rates in Xero after the import, these changes won’t automatically sync to HubSpot. If your Xero tax rates don’t appear in your HubSpot account, re-save your bi-directional invoice sync configuration to trigger a new import, or contact HubSpot Support for assistance.

  • HubSpot does not support importing taxes for multi-tenant Xero accounts.

  • Syncing CurrencyRate: the Xero integration can sync Xero’s CurrencyRate to HubSpot’s exchange rate only if your HubSpot company currency matches your Xero tenant’s base currency. If the currencies don’t match, invoices won’t sync. To manage a cross-system base-currency mismatch, update your HubSpot company currency to match your Xero base currency, or turn off the mapping between Inverse Currency Rate and Exchange rate in your invoice sync settings.

  • Currencies: six currencies are supported: USD, CAD, EUR, GBP, AUD, and NZD.

Please note: if you turn on credit card fees in your payment settings, the fee won’t sync to invoices in Xero. This can require manual reconciliation. To avoid discrepancies, turn off the fee setting when using the Xero integration.

  • To prevent duplicate records, only payments created after you connect the app will sync to HubSpot.
  • Payment sync configuration uses required default settings that cannot be viewed or edited.

Connect the app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for and select Xero by HubSpot (Data Sync).
  • Click Install.
  • In the dialog box, enter your Xero credentials. Review the required permissions, and click Accept.

Configure your sync settings

It’s recommended to set up the sync in the order below as Xero requires the contact and products of an invoice to exist in Xero before an invoice is synced.

Set up the contact sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Xero.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Contact sync.

  • On the Configure page:

    • Click the sync direction arrows and select a sync direction between Xero Contacts and HubSpot Contacts. You can choose from the following options:

      • Data syncs between apps: data syncs bi-directionally between HubSpot and Xero.
      • Data syncs only to HubSpot: HubSpot contacts will be created from Xero contacts based on criteria. Only HubSpot contact properties will be updated.
      • Data syncs only to Xero: Xero contacts will be created from HubSpot contacts based on criteria. Only Xero contact properties will be created.

    • Click the Data conflict resolution dropdown menu and select which app will overwrite the other when it’s unclear which app has the most up-to-date information.

    • In the Mapped fields section set up your field mappings.

      • Default field mappings can’t be removed or edited. To turn off a field mapping, click to toggle the switch off.
      • To add a custom field mapping, click Add a mapping to set it up.

  • On the Limit page:

    • In the Filters section, click Edit to add any filters to limit which records will sync from one app to the other. You can add multiple filters with AND or OR conditions. By default, for the Xero dataSyncRight HubSpot sync, all records are included in the sync.
    • For the HubSpot dataSyncRight Xero sync, the following filters are recommended: At least one associated Invoice has Invoice status is none of Draft AND Create date is after [today’s date] OR Invoice status is none of Draft AND Object last modified date/time is after [today’s date].

  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.

Set up the product sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Xero.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • Click Product Sync.

  • On the Configure page:

    • Click the sync direction arrows and select a sync direction between Xero Items and HubSpot Products. You can choose from the following options:

      • Data syncs between apps: data syncs bi-directionally between HubSpot and Xero.
      • Data syncs only to HubSpot: HubSpot products will be created from Xero items based on criteria. Only HubSpot product properties will be updated.
      • Data syncs only to Xero: Xero items will be created from HubSpot products based on criteria. Only Xero item properties will be created.

    • Click the Data conflict resolution dropdown menu and select which app will overwrite the other when it’s unclear which app has the most up-to-date information.

    • In the Mapped fields section set up your field mappings.

      • Default field mappings can’t be removed or edited. To turn off a field mapping, click to toggle the switch off.
      • To add a custom field mapping, click Add a mapping to set it up.

  • On the Limit page:

    • In the Filters section, click Edit to add any filters to limit which records will sync from one app to the other. You can add multiple filters with AND or OR conditions. By default, for the Xero dataSyncRight HubSpot sync, all records are included in the sync.
    • For the HubSpot dataSyncRight Xero sync, the following filters are recommended: Object create date is after [today’s date] OR Last modified date is after [today’s date].

  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.

Set up the invoices sync
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Xero.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • Click Invoice sync.
  • On Configure page:
    • Click the sync direction arrows and select a sync direction between Xero Invoices and HubSpot Invoices. You can choose from the following options:
      • Data syncs between apps: data syncs bi-directionally between HubSpot and Xero.
      • Data syncs only to HubSpot: HubSpot invoices will be created from Xero invoices based on criteria. Only HubSpot invoice properties will be updated.
      • Data syncs only to Xero: Xero invoices will be created from HubSpot invoices based on criteria. Only Xero invoice properties will be created.
    • Click the Data conflict resolution dropdown menu and select which app will overwrite the other when it’s unclear which app has the most up-to-date information.
    • In the Mapped fields section set up your field mappings.
      • Default field mappings can’t be removed or edited. To turn off a field mapping, click to toggle the switch off.
      • To add a custom field mapping, click Add a mapping to set it up.
  • On the Limit page:
    • In the Filters section, click Edit to add any filters to limit which records will sync from one app to the other. You can add multiple filters with AND or OR conditions.

Please note: the following sync filters for the HubSpot dataSyncRight Xero sync are set automatically to prevent over-syncing and cannot be edited:

- Only HubSpot invoices will be synced from HubSpot to Xero (e.g., invoices where the Invoice source is any of HubSpot).
- Draft invoices will not be synced to Xero. Invoices must be in Open state in order to be synced to Xero.
- Only invoices created or modified after the time the sync was started will be synced to Xero.
  • On the Review page, review your sync configuration and click Save and sync.

Understand sync timing and frequency

Once the sync is turned on, data will automatically sync between HubSpot and Xero. After the first sync is complete, records will sync at regular intervals:

  • Changes from HubSpot to Xero are detected within a few minutes.
  • Changes from Xero to HubSpot are detected every 30 minutes.

Data can also be synced on demand by clicking the Sync now button on the CRM syncs tab to get the most recent updates.

Review your sync

To review your sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Xero.
  • Click the CRM syncs tab. This tab shows information about the number of records in sync, failing to sync, excluded from a sync, and the timestamp of when the sync was last edited.
  • To view the individual records, click the number in each column.
  • To run the sync immediately, click Sync now.
  • To edit an existing sync, hover over the sync and click Edit.
  • To turn off a sync, hover over the sync and click More > Turn off sync.

Frequently asked questions

What are the most common sync errors, and how do I resolve them?

Below, you’ll find some of the most common sync errors and a suggested resolution:

An invoice should have an associated customer. Make sure the associated customer is

present in both HubSpot & Xero to sync this invoice.

This error occurs because the contact on the invoice couldn’t be found in Xero. Most often, this is because the contact on the invoice doesn’t share the email address of the customer in Xero. To resolve, change the contact on the invoice that matches the email of the customer in Xero.

Line item or invoice amount modifications in HubSpot native invoices cannot be made through external applications. Please make any necessary changes directly in HubSpot.

This error occurs because an invoice that was created in HubSpot was modified in Xero. Reverse the changes to the invoice in Xero, and the same adjustments to the invoice in HubSpot to continue syncing.

A validation exception occurred. The contact name is already assigned to another contact.

This error occurs when a HubSpot contact has the same name as an existing contact in Xero. Contact names must be unique in Xero. To resolve the error, update the contact’s name in HubSpot so that it’s unique in Xero. The contact will automatically be included in the sync again.

A validation exception occurred. Insufficient stock. Items are eligible for backorder.

This error occurs when an invoice contains a tracked inventory item with insufficient stock in Xero, and Xero would place the item on backorder. The integration doesn’t support syncing invoices with items eligible for backorder.

How do I sync PO Number, or other invoice fields to/from Xero?

PO Number isn’t a default field on Xero invoices and must be added as a custom

field in Xero. For this reason, the HubSpot Xero integration cannot define an out of the box field mapping for it, and a custom field mapping must be set up (requires Data Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise).

Connect HubSpot and Zoho

Zoho is a suite of online productivity tools that includes a CRM, applicant tracking system, invoicing software, accounting software, and inventory management software. Learn more about how to connect Zoho to HubSpot using data sync.

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account to connect the app.

Connect HubSpot and Zoho

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.

  • Search for one of the following Zoho integrations:

    • Zoho CRM
    • Zoho Recruit
    • Zoho Inventory
    • Zoho Books
    • Zoho Invoice

  • Click Install.

  • In the dialog box, click Next.

  • Select the domain from the dropdown menu and click Next. You’ll be redirected to Zoho in a new window.

  • Review the requested permissions, then click Accept. Once you’ve approved the requested permissions, you’ll be redirected back to HubSpot.

  • Click Set up sync to set up your sync settings, or Do this later to finish the process.

Please note: if you’re connecting Zoho CRM, you need to add the Modified By field to the Zoho CRM objects you want to sync to HubSpot.

After connecting the integration, learn more about configuring your sync settings and mapping your properties.

Connect HubSpot and Zoom

Connect Zoom to HubSpot to manage meetings and webinar activity alongside your CRM data. With the Zoom integration, you can sync webinar registrations and attendance information to HubSpot, add registrants to your Zoom webinars using a workflow, and view Zoom cloud recordings on contact timelines.

Using the integration helps you track engagement across Zoom webinars and meetings without manually updating records. For example, you can identify contacts who registered for or attended a webinar, segment them for follow-up campaigns, and automate post-event actions such as sending emails, assigning tasks, or updating contact properties.

Please note: starting Aug. 31, 2026, Microsoft Teams meeting recordings and transcripts are stored on the meeting record instead of the call record. Learn more about this change.

Before you get started

Permissions required

  • You must have App Marketplace permissions or be a Super Admin in your HubSpot account to install the Zoom app.

  • You must have admin permissions in the Zoom account.

  • If your Zoom account was associated with a Business Unit before the migration to Brands, you’ll continue using that same brand. Any new Zoom accounts connected to HubSpot will also use this brand. You cannot associate new brands or reassign brands to the Zoom integration.

  • If you intend to use HubSpot and Zoom webinars, your Zoom account must have the Zoom webinar add-on.

  • To sync Zoom meeting or webinar participants to HubSpot, participants must have a valid email address. The integration uses email to match participants to existing HubSpot contacts, and creates new contacts for those who don’t exist in HubSpot yet.

  • To sync cloud recordings and transcripts from Zoom to HubSpot, ensure that your Zoom account supports cloud recording and audio transcripts, and that both settings are turned on in Zoom.

  • Each user must connect their individual Zoom user account to HubSpot, and the cloud recording must remain available in Zoom for it to sync.

Please note:

  • It is not recommended to connect your Zoom account to multiple HubSpot accounts if there is sensitive or private information that shouldn’t be accessible to all connected accounts.
  • You can only connect one Zoom account (one Zoom tenant) to a single HubSpot account.
  • If your HubSpot account previously used Business Units, you may have been able to connect multiple Zoom accounts before migrating to Brands. After migrating to Brands, if you disconnect a Zoom account, you won’t be able to reconnect additional Zoom accounts.
  • The Zoom integration doesn’t support Personal Meeting IDs (PMIs).

Install the Zoom app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.

  • In the search bar, search for and select the Zoom app.

  • Click Install.

  • In the dialog box, enter your Zoom login credentials, then click Sign in.

  • You’ll be prompted to grant permission for Zoom for HubSpot to access your Zoom account. Click Allow.

  • You’ll be redirected back to HubSpot, where you’ll see Zoom appear under Connected Apps. Click Zoom to link an individual Zoom user account and configure new contact exclusions.

Manage individual Zoom settings

To view or edit your connected user:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Zoom.

  • Navigate to the Settings tab.

  • Click the User management tab.

  • On the My settings tab, in the Connected HubSpot to Zoom User section, see which Zoom user is connected to your HubSpot user.

    • To change the connected user, click Change connected user.

    • In the right panel, click the Zoom user dropdown menu and select the Zoom user you want to connect to your HubSpot user account. If you don’t see your user in the dropdown menu, ensure that you have been added as a user to the connected Zoom account.

To view your individual settings for Zoom meetings:

  • Click the Meetings tab.

  • On the My settings tab, in the Meetings section, select whether your Zoom meeting recording and transcripts should sync from Zoom to HubSpot. If the options are grayed out, this means your account admin has turned off the setting on a global level.

    • Don’t sync meeting recordings and transcripts: this option won’t sync any meeting recordings or transcripts to HubSpot. However, meetings will still log as activities on the HubSpot contact records of the participants.
    • Sync meeting recordings and transcripts: this option will automatically log meetings and sync meeting recordings and transcripts to HubSpot.
    • In the Manage individual meetings section, you can search meetings by Meeting ID that you’re the organizer of. You can find the Zoom Meeting ID in the meeting invite. Then click Sync now to sync the meeting data to HubSpot.

Please note: recordings and transcripts from meetings that use a Personal Meeting ID (PMI) won’t sync to HubSpot. To sync them, use a scheduled meeting with a unique meeting ID instead of your PMI.

  • In the Auto-recording section, click the Enable auto-recording of meetings in Zoom toggle on to record all your Zoom meetings automatically. When you turn this setting on, you give HubSpot permission to activate the auto-recording setting in your Zoom account on your behalf. In order for the recordings to sync to HubSpot, you need to turn on the sync for meeting recordings and transcripts.

To view your individual settings for Zoom webinars:

  • Click the Webinars tab.

  • On the My settings tab, in the Webinars section, select which webinars you want to sync from Zoom to HubSpot.

    • To automatically sync any new webinars you create in Zoom to HubSpot, select the Sync data from newly scheduled webinars by default checkbox.

    • Don’t sync webinar recordings and transcripts: this option won’t sync any webinar recordings or transcripts to HubSpot.

    • Sync webinar recordings and transcripts: this option will automatically sync webinar recordings and transcripts to HubSpot.

    • In the Manage individual webinars section, you can search for webinars by Webinar name or ID that you’re the organizer of. Then click Sync now to sync the webinar data to HubSpot.

Please note: if your HubSpot and Zoom user accounts have the same email address, your Zoom user account will automatically be linked to HubSpot and cannot be unlinked. You can only switch to a different Zoom user account.

Manage global Zoom settings

To view and manage account-wide settings for Zoom meetings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Zoom.

  • Navigate to the Settings tab.

  • Click the Global settings tab.

    • In the Meetings section, click the Sync meeting data toggle on to sync all present and future Zoom meetings for all users in the HubSpot account. You can select whether to sync meeting recordings and transcripts for none of, all, or selected Zoom users in the HubSpot account.
    • To sync past meetings, you’ll need to manually sync the specific meeting you’re interested in.
    • In the Exclusions section, you can add domains to prevent meetings from being synced to HubSpot by users with a specific domain in their email address.

To view and manage account-wide settings for Zoom webinars:

  • Click the Webinars tab.

  • Then click the Global settings tab.

    • In the Webinars section, click the Sync webinar data toggle on to sync webinar data from Zoom to HubSpot. You can select whether to sync webinar data for none of, all, or selected Zoom users in the HubSpot account. Webinars will sync to marketing events.
    • In the Exclusions section, you can add domains to prevent webinars from being synced to HubSpot by users with a specific domain in their email address.

To manage individual user settings:

  • Click the User management tab.

  • Then click the Global settings tab.

  • In the Manage individual user settings section, view and manage the settings of individual Zoom users.

    • Click User settings next to the user whose settings you want to edit.
    • In the right panel, check the Sync this user’s meeting recordings and transcripts box to sync all meetings created by this user from Zoom to HubSpot.
    • Check the Sync data from newly scheduled webinars by default box to automatically sync data from any new webinar created by the user to HubSpot.
    • Check the Sync this user’s webinar recordings and transcripts box to sync all recordings and transcripts from webinars created by this user from Zoom to HubSpot.

Review Zoom features

To review all features available with the Zoom app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Zoom.

  • Click the Feature discovery tab.

  • Review the features available with the Zoom app:

    • Add Zoom links to your meetings.
    • Review Zoom cloud recordings and transcripts.
    • Segment contacts using Zoom webinar properties.
    • Promote your webinar using a workflow.

Connect HubSpot to Google BigQuery

Sync data from Google BigQuery with HubSpot CRM objects, such as contacts, companies, deals, associations, and other data from your account.

The sections below walk you through how to authorize the Google BigQuery app, then configure syncing settings between your Google Cloud account and HubSpot.

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin in your HubSpot account to install the integration.

Connect and configure the Google BigQuery integration

To connect your Google BigQuery account to HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Click the search bar and enter Google BigQuery.
  • Click Google BigQuery from the listing page.
  • Click Install.
  • Click Continue setup.

You’ll be redirected to the Data integration tool, where a side pane will guide you through syncing data between your HubSpot and BigQuery accounts, based on the directions you want to sync:

  • Google BigQuery → HubSpot: configure syncing from BigQuery to HubSpot.
  • HubSpot → Google BigQuery: configure syncing from HubSpot to BigQuery.
Sync Google BigQuery data to your HubSpot account

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

To send Google BigQuery data to HubSpot, add and configure a new user with the required roles in your BigQuery account:

  • In the right pane, select Google BigQuery → HubSpot.

  • Copy the Google service account email that HubSpot generates.

  • In your Google Cloud account, navigate to your project IAM settings, create a new user with the service account email you copied from HubSpot, then add the BigQuery Data Viewer and BigQuery Job User roles for the newly created user.

  • Copy the Project ID from your Google Cloud account.

  • Back in HubSpot, paste in the Project ID, then click Test connection.

  • Once the connection is verified, click Next to complete the setup.

Sync HubSpot data to your Google BigQuery account

To send HubSpot data to Google BigQuery, you’ll configure a user with the required permissions in your Google Cloud account, along with specifying the associated GCP project and GCS bucket URI.

Please note: you’ll need Google Cloud admin access to the GCP project where the BigQuery dataset will live, and a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket where HubSpot will stage Parquet files.

  • In the right pane, select HubSpot → Google BigQuery.

  • Copy the Google service account email that HubSpot generates.

  • In your Google Cloud account, navigate to your project IAM settings, create a new user with the service account email you copied from HubSpot, then add the BigQuery Data Viewer, BigQuery Job User, and Storage object owner roles for the newly created user.

  • Copy the Project ID from your Google Cloud account.

  • Back in HubSpot, paste in the Project ID.

  • Add your Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket URI:

    • The URI for the GCS bucket should follow the structure: gs://{bucket}/hubspot-dataout/{portalId}/{runId}/{tableName}/
    • BigQuery external tables are created in a dedicated dataset in the GCP project and follow the format: hubspot_data_set_{hubId}
    • Data will be written to the GCS bucket, and the associated tables will reference parquet files in GCS.
    • Learn more about creating GCS buckets in Google’s documentation.

  • Click Test connection.

  • Once the connection is verified, click Next.

  • Select the checkboxes next to the data sources you’d like to sync (e.g., Contacts, Associations, Events, etc).

  • Configure the sync frequency and schedule.

  • Click Start sync.

Monitor syncing

After you’ve configured syncing between your accounts, you can review syncing status and history from the sync details page:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Integration. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration directly.
  • Under Monitor your imports & syncs, click the App syncs tab.
  • Click the search bar and search for Google BigQuery.
  • Click Google BigQuery. Note that multiple entries may appear if you’ve configured syncing in both directions.
  • On the sync details page, you can manage and review your sync settings and history:
    • To archive or edit syncing details, in the top right, click Actions then select the corresponding option.
    • To immediately trigger a sync, in the top right, click Sync now.
    • Synced records, associations, and errors are summarized at the top of the page.
    • Recent sync activity will appear in the table. Click the Sync history tab to review specific sync attempts and completions. You can filter by specific date ranges or a sync status.

Sync statuses and error handling

The table below outlines possible syncing statuses:

Status

Description

Syncing

A sync attempt is currently in progress.

Synced

The last sync completed successfully.

Failed

The last sync encountered an error.

Archived

The sync configuration was manually removed, but can be reviewed for posterity.

If a sync fails:

  • A Failed status will appear on the sync details page, along with information about which tables succeeded or failed to sync.
  • No data is partially written on failure: BigQuery tables only update on successful completion of a sync.
  • The next scheduled sync will automatically re-attempt a full sync.
  • You can trigger a re-sync manually at any time from the sync details page.

Network allowlisting

Syncing HubSpot data to third-party providers like BigQuery is routed through HubSpot’s proxy IPs. These IP ranges are used by other HubSpot integrations, such as data sync and webhooks.

If your organization restricts inbound access to your GCP resources, you should allowlist the following CIDR ranges based on your HubSpot hublet:

Hublet

CIDR

NA1

54.174.62.128/26

NA2

216.157.40.32/27

NA3

216.157.41.32/27

EU1

143.244.87.0/25

AP1

216.157.42.32/27

Learn how to find out where your HubSpot account data is hosted.

Beta limitations

Keep the following limitations in mind during this beta:

  • Sync frequency: the available sync frequencies depend on the sync direction. You can manually trigger a re-sync from the sync details page in HubSpot at any time.
    • HubSpot to Google BigQuery: once, every 6 hours, every 12 hours, daily, weekly, or monthly.
    • Google BigQuery to HubSpot: every 15 minutes, every 30 minutes, every hour, every 2 hours, every 3 hours, every 6 hours, every 12 hours, daily, weekly, or monthly.
  • One export per data type: each object type, event type, or association pair can only be exported in one sync configuration per HubSpot account.
    • For example, if contacts are already being exported to one BigQuery destination, they cannot be added to a second configuration until the original destination is archived.
    • This prevents duplicate data pipelines and ensures a single source of truth per data type in your data warehouse.
  • Limited sensitive data support: you can store and sync sensitive data to your HubSpot account, but you cannot sync sensitive data to your BigQuery account.
  • No support for object_x_views: the object_x_views object isn’t currently supported for syncing with BigQuery. Use object_with_object_properties, or join objects with object_properties to get equivalent per-record views.

Next steps

After you’ve connected the BigQuery integration and set up your sync settings, learn about the schema for synced tables in BigQuery.

Connect NetSuite to Breeze Assistant

Connect NetSuite to Breeze Assistant to access and work with NetSuite records without leaving HubSpot. After connecting NetSuite, you can ask Breeze Assistant to retrieve information from NetSuite and complete supported actions on NetSuite records.

For example, you can ask Breeze Assistant to summarize an account’s NetSuite history, generate summaries and reports using NetSuite data, and get financial information from NetSuite, such as payment history and open invoices.

Before you get started

Before you connect NetSuite to Breeze Assistant, review the following requirements and considerations.

Understand requirements
  • Before connecting NetSuite to Breeze Assistant, a NetSuite admin must complete these steps in NetSuite.
  • Review the requirements to use Breeze Assistant.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • NetSuite is a third-party service. When using the connector, Oracle’s data and privacy policies apply. Review Oracle’s Associated Risks, Controls, and Mitigation Strategies for more information.
  • The NetSuite AI Connector Service hasn’t been assessed for HIPAA compliance and shouldn’t be used to store, process, or transmit electronic protected health information (ePHI). If you have Sensitive Data turned on in your HubSpot account, it’s recommended not to use the connector. Learn more about NetSuite and HIPAA.
  • Before confirming changes, review the changes suggested by Breeze Assistant.
  • You can’t delete NetSuite data through the connector.
  • By default, authentication tokens are valid for 48 hours. In NetSuite, you can extend this validity period to a maximum of 30 days. When the token expires, you must authenticate the connection again.

Admin steps in NetSuite

Before connecting NetSuite to Breeze Assistant, a NetSuite admin must complete the following steps in NetSuite.

1. Turn on the required NetSuite features

Before using the NetSuite connector in Breeze Assistant, a NetSuite admin must turn on the required SuiteCloud features.

  • In NetSuite, navigate to Setup > Company > Enable Features.

  • Click the SuiteCloud subtab.

  • In the SuiteScript section:

    • Select the Client SuiteScript checkbox. If prompted, click I Agree to accept the SuiteCloud Terms of Service.
    • Select the Server SuiteScript checkbox. If prompted, click I Agree to accept the SuiteCloud Terms of Service.

  • In the Manage Authentication section, select the OAuth 2.0 checkbox. If prompted, click I Agree to accept the SuiteCloud Terms of Service.

  • In the SuiteTalk (Web Services) section, select the REST Web Services checkbox.

  • Click Save.

2. Configure a NetSuite role for the connector

Each user who needs access to the connector must have a NetSuite role with the required permissions. Consider creating a dedicated role for the connector rather than adding these permissions to an existing role with broader access.

Configure the role permissions
  • In NetSuite, navigate to Setup > Users/Roles > Manage Roles.
  • To configure an existing role, click Edit next to the role. To create a role, click New.
  • Click the Permissions subtab, then click Setup.
  • Add the following permissions:
    • MCP Server Connection: select Full access. This permission allows users to connect to the AI Connector Service.
    • Log in using OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens: select Full access. This permission allows OAuth 2.0 authentication.
    • REST Web Services: select Full access if users will create, retrieve, or update records through the MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp.
  • Click Save.

Please note: after creating a NetSuite role, it may take some time for the role to become available. Wait until the role is available before continuing with the setup.

Add record permissions to the role

Add record permissions for the NetSuite objects you want Breeze Assistant to retrieve, such as sales orders, invoices, and customer payments.

  • In NetSuite, switch to the Administrator role.
  • Navigate to Setup > Users/Roles > Manage Roles.
  • Open the role you created for the NetSuite connector.
  • Navigate to Permissions > Transactions.
  • Add permissions for the NetSuite objects you want Breeze Assistant to retrieve, then set the access level for each permission to Full. For example, you can add permissions for sales orders, invoices, customer payments, or other NetSuite objects.
  • Click Save.
Assign the role to users
  • In NetSuite, navigate to Lists > Employees > Employees.
  • Click Edit next to the user you want to assign the role to.
  • Navigate to the Access tab.
  • Under Role, search for and select the role you configured in the previous steps.
  • Click Add.
  • Then click Save.

Please note: the NetSuite AI Connector Service cannot run under the Administrator role or any role with full access to NetSuite features. This security safeguard helps prevent unintended results if the external AI client’s security is compromised.

3. Install the MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp

To use the NetSuite connector with Breeze Assistant, install the MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp. The SuiteApp lets you query NetSuite data in Breeze Assistant using natural language.

The SuiteApp uses the user’s existing NetSuite role and permissions to determine which data and actions they can access.

  • Log in to NetSuite as a NetSuite admin.
  • Click the SuiteApps tab.
  • In the Search SuiteApps field, enter MCP Standard Tools.
  • Click the MCP Standard Tools icon.
  • On the top right of the SuiteApp page, click Install.
  • Wait for the installation to complete.
4. Create an OAuth 2.0 integration record

Create an integration record in NetSuite to configure OAuth 2.0 authentication between NetSuite and HubSpot. Learn more in the NetSuite documentation.

  • In NetSuite, navigate to Setup > Integration > Manage Integrations > New.

  • Enter a name for the integration.

  • Set the State field to Enabled.

  • In the OAuth 2.0 Scopes section:

    • Select the Authorization Code Grant checkbox.

    • Clear the Public Client checkbox. A Client Secret is required to connect NetSuite to HubSpot.

    • In the Redirect URI field, enter the HubSpot redirect URI. The URI must use oauth-redirect.hubspot.com.

    • Select the NetSuite AI Connector Service checkbox.

    • Clear the other OAuth scope checkboxes, including RESTlets, REST Web Services, and SuiteAnalytics Connect.

  • Clear all checkboxes in the Token-based Authentication and Client Credentials sections, including the Client Credentials (Machine to Machine) Grant checkbox.

  • Click Save.

  • Copy and securely store the generated Client ID and Client Secret.

Please note: the Client ID and Client Secret appear only after you save the integration record for the first time. If you don’t save these values, you’ll need to reset them in the integration record to generate new credentials.

The REST Web Services OAuth scope in this section is separate from the REST Web Services role permission configured earlier. The role permission determines the user’s access to REST APIs, while the OAuth scope restricts the OAuth token to the NetSuite AI Connector Service.

5. Find the NetSuite MCP server URL

The MCP server URL is specific to your NetSuite account and determines which tools are available through the connection.

Find your account ID
  • In NetSuite, navigate to Setup > Company > Company Information.
  • Locate the account ID at the top of the page.
  • Click the Company URLs tab to review the account-specific SuiteTalk URL.
Set up the appropriate MCP server URL
  • To use the MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp, use:
  • https://<accountid>.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/mcp/v1/suiteapp/com.netsuite.mcpstandardtools
  • To expose all available SuiteApps and account customization projects, use:
  • https://<accountid>.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/mcp/v1/all
  • To expose a specific SuiteApp, use:
  • https://<accountid>.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/mcp/v1/suiteapp/<publisherid>.<projectid>
  • Replace <accountid> with your NetSuite account ID.

Connect NetSuite to Breeze Assistant

After a NetSuite admin has configured the connector in NetSuite, connect NetSuite to Breeze Assistant. Have the NetSuite MCP server URL, Client ID, and Client Secret available before starting.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.

  • Search for and select the NetSuite Connector.

  • Click Install.

  • In the dialog box:

    • In the NetSuite MCP Server URL field, enter the NetSuite MCP server URL for your NetSuite account.
    • In the Client ID field, enter the Client ID generated from the NetSuite integration record.
    • In the Client Secret field, enter the Client Secret generated from the NetSuite integration record.

  • Click Connect to netsuite_mcp.

  • You’ll be redirected to NetSuite. Log in using a non-administrator role with the required MCP permissions, then authorize HubSpot to access NetSuite.

  • After authorization, you’ll be redirected to HubSpot and the connection will be established.

Use the connector in Breeze Assistant

After connecting, ask Breeze Assistant to retrieve information or complete actions in NetSuite.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.

  • Click +, then navigate to Connectors.

  • Click to toggle the NetSuite connector switch on.

  • Then enter your prompt.

  • For example, you can:

    • Ask Breeze Assistant to show you the last 5 sales orders for a specific company in NetSuite, including line items, amounts, and current status.
    • Ask Breeze Assistant to show you all open invoices more than 60 days overdue across all subsidiaries in NetSuite, sorted by amount.
    • Ask Breeze Assistant to show you all sales orders created this week in NetSuite that are still in pending fulfillment status.
    • Ask Breeze Assistant to compare the total revenue by subsidiary in NetSuite for Q1 this year vs Q2 this year.
    • Ask Breeze Assistant to show you all customers in a specific subsidiary in NetSuite who placed their first NetSuite order in the last 6 months.
    • Ask Breeze Assistant to give you a full account summary for a specific company in NetSuite, including all orders, invoices, payments, and open issues.

  • Click the Send icon in the bottom right.

  • Breeze Assistant will generate a response using your NetSuite data.

Connect your Salesforce sandbox to HubSpot

With the HubSpot-Salesforce integration, you can connect either a Salesforce production organization or a Salesforce sandbox to HubSpot.

Connecting a sandbox allows you to test the integration, review sync behavior, and validate configuration changes in a non-production environment before applying them to your live Salesforce data.

The process for connecting a Salesforce sandbox account to HubSpot will depend on whether you have already installed the HubSpot-Salesforce integration.

HubSpot-Salesforce integration is not currently installed

Follow the steps to install the HubSpot-Salesforce integration. To connect your Salesforce sandbox to HubSpot, ensure you select the Yes, this will connect to a sandbox checkbox, and install the integration package in your Salesforce sandbox.

HubSpot-Salesforce integration is currently installed

If the integration is already installed and your Salesforce production organization is connected to HubSpot, connect your Salesforce sandbox to HubSpot following the steps below:

  • Install the integration package in your Salesforce sandbox.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Salesforce.

  • Click the Actions dropdown menu and click Connect a different sandbox user.

  • Enter your Salesforce sandbox credentials and click Log In to Sandbox.

  • Review the integration permissions, then click Allow.

Create a NetSuite sales order in HubSpot

After connecting HubSpot and NetSuite, create NetSuite sales orders directly from HubSpot to keep deal and order data in sync across both platforms. You can trigger sales order creation automatically using deal-based workflows, or create orders manually from a deal record. When a sales order is created, a corresponding HubSpot order is generated and associated with the deal automatically.

When creating NetSuite sales orders, you can also set unit costs for line items manually or sync unit costs from associated HubSpot deal line items using workflows.

Before you get started

  • Products in your HubSpot product library must match the corresponding items in NetSuite. This can be achieved either by turning on product sync or by manually mapping the NetSuite Item Name/Number to the HubSpot product SKU.
  • The company currency in your HubSpot account must match the base currency set in your NetSuite account.
  • When creating a sales order in HubSpot, include all required fields from a NetSuite sales order. To identify these fields, create a sales order in NetSuite and take note of the required fields.
  • Configure the NetSuite sales order to HubSpot order sync before creating orders in HubSpot. If the sync isn’t configured, creating a NetSuite sales order won’t create a corresponding HubSpot order.
  • If your NetSuite account uses legacy tax and your sales order form requires a tax code, set the Tax Code field in the workflow action. Tax codes are pulled from NetSuite for the selected subsidiary, so the subsidiary must have a tax agency configured.

Set up the product sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click NetSuite.
  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.
  • Click Sync more data.
  • On the Select the data that you want to sync page, click the Select an object dropdown menu for NetSuite, and select the object to sync to HubSpot products. You can sync Assembly Items, Inventory Items, Kit Items, Non Inventory Resale Items, Non Inventory Sale Items, Service Resale Items, and Service Sale Items.
  • Click the Select an object dropdown menu for HubSpot and select Products.
  • Click the arrows dropdown menu, and select whether the sync is bi-directional or one way between the app and HubSpot, or vice versa.
  • Finish setting up the sync and turn the sync on. Learn more about customizing your sync settings.

Map the NetSuite item to HubSpot product

To sync NetSuite items such as Gift Certificates or Drop Ship Items to HubSpot products, add the NetSuite Item Name/Number to the HubSpot product SKU field.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Products. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Products directly.
  • Click the product you want to map to the NetSuite item.
  • In the SKU field, enter the NetSuite ItemID (Item Name/Number). The NetSuite item must be active in NetSuite. Inactive items cannot be added to sales orders.
  • Click Save.

Create NetSuite sales orders using deal-based workflows

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

Please note: a NetSuite customer sync is required for this feature. When configuring the integration’s sync settings, Company customers or Individual customers must be selected.

Use deal-based workflows to automatically create NetSuite sales orders when the workflow is triggered.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click NetSuite.

  • Click the Feature discovery tab.

  • On the Automate your NetSuite sales orders card, click Go to workflows.

  • To edit an existing workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or, learn how to create a new deal-based workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add an action.

  • In the left panel, search for NetSuite and select Create a NetSuite sales order.

  • Set up your NetSuite sales order action. The following fields are required unless indicated:

    • NetSuite account: a list of connected NetSuite accounts will display, select an account to create the sales order.

    • Items: set the deal’s associated line items as the Items for the sales order. Tax codes for line items are automatically mapped to the corresponding NetSuite tax codes during sync.

    • Item Price: select Use HubSpot item line price or Use NetSuite list price.

    • Subsidiary: a list of subsidiaries associated with the selected NetSuite account will display. Select a Subsidiary to create the sales order.

    • Customer: select either Use first associated HubSpot contact or Use first associated HubSpot company to set as the designated Customer for the sales order.

    • Include Attachments (optional): select the checkbox to include all files from the Attachment section of a HubSpot deal record in the corresponding NetSuite order.

    • NetSuite Folder: select which folder the attachments will be created in.

Permissions required To access attachments in NetSuite, the integration user role must have Documents and Files permissions under the Lists subtab in NetSuite.

- Tax Code (optional): select a tax code to apply to the sales order's line items. The list shows the tax codes configured in NetSuite for the selected Subsidiary.
    - A tax code is used by NetSuite accounts on legacy tax, where a tax code is required on every sales order line. On SuiteTax accounts, leave this field empty and NetSuite's tax engine calculates tax automatically.

Please note:

  • The unit costs set on the deal’s associated line items in HubSpot will automatically sync to NetSuite when the sales order is created.

  • If your NetSuite sales order form requires a tax code, you must set this field or the sales order won’t be created. If no options appear in the dropdown, confirm the account uses legacy tax and that the selected subsidiary has a tax agency configured in NetSuite

    • To add another field to the sales order, click the Add another field dropdown menu and select a field. Only standard NetSuite fields will be displayed; reference fields won’t appear.
      • To populate the field with property values from the enrolled deal record, click Deal in this workflow. Then, select a property.
      • To populate the field based on other actions in the workflow, click the action name and select an option. You can populate fields based on an action’s outcome, or outputs from the action.
      • To remove a field from the sales order, click the deletedelete icon next to the field.

After the workflow creates a NetSuite sales order, a corresponding HubSpot order will be created automatically. The HubSpot order will be associated with both the HubSpot deal and the NetSuite sales order.

Please note:

  • Make sure that you have configured the NetSuite sales order to HubSpot order sync. If the sync isn’t configured, creating a NetSuite sales order won’t create a corresponding HubSpot order.
  • The HubSpot order will be associated with the deal only if the order sync is turned on. If the sync is paused or hasn’t been started, the HubSpot order will be created but won’t be associated with the deal. To create missing associations:
    • Turn on or resume the order sync.
    • Re-run the workflow for any orders created while the sync was off.

Create NetSuite sales order from a deal record

To manually create a NetSuite sales order from a HubSpot deal record:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.

  • Click the name of the deal you want to create a NetSuite sales order for.

  • On the right sidebar of the deal, on the Sales Orders card, click Add > Create a NetSuite sales order.

  • On the Account page, select the NetSuite account and the custom form to create a sales order.

  • Click Next.

  • On the Customer page, select the NetSuite customer and the Subsidiary account you want to create a sales order for.

  • Click Next.

  • On the Attachments page, click the Include attachment dropdown menu and select whether to include attachments.

  • Click Next.

  • On the Order page, add the order information to the sales order fields based on your chosen custom form type.

    • For line items already associated with the deal, select or update the unit cost.
    • To add new line items from NetSuite, select the line items, then use the unit cost from NetSuite or enter a custom unit cost.

  • On the Review page, review the sales order and make any necessary edits.

  • Click Create sales order.

After you create a NetSuite sales order, a corresponding HubSpot order will be created automatically. The HubSpot order will be associated with both the HubSpot deal and the NetSuite sales order.

Please note: make sure that you have configured the NetSuite sales order to HubSpot order sync. If the sync isn’t configured, creating a NetSuite sales order won’t create a corresponding HubSpot order.

Create and use custom LLM workflow actions

Connect HubSpot with a supported large language model (LLM) provider to use the Use a custom LLM action in your workflows. This action lets you select from multiple supported LLM providers and models to generate outputs directly within a workflow.

For example, you can summarize information from a record, classify incoming data, or generate personalized content, then use the response to automate the next steps in your workflow.

After connecting an LLM provider, you can select a model and configure prompts directly within the workflow action.

Supported LLM providers

You can use the following LLM providers with the Use a custom LLM workflow action:

  • OpenAI
  • Anthropic (Claude)
  • Cohere
  • xAI (Grok)
  • Google (Gemini)

Retrieve your LLM API key

To connect HubSpot to an LLM provider, you’ll first need the API key from the LLM provider you want to use.

Please note: you must keep the API key secure, as it provides access to your LLM instance.

OpenAI API key

To connect your OpenAI account and HubSpot, a user with the role of owner in your OpenAI account must first retrieve your OpenAI API key:

  • Navigate to OpenAI. Then, sign up or log into your account.

  • Retrieve your API key.

    • For existing projects, ensure you have the necessary permissions to use the API.
    • Only organization owners can create new projects and generate the corresponding API keys. Learn more about the different roles and permissions in your OpenAI account.
    • Check that your API key is still valid and not expired.
Anthropic API key

Before you can connect your Anthropic account to HubSpot, a user with the role of admin or developer in your Anthropic account must first retrieve your Anthropic API key:

  • Navigate to console.anthropic.com to sign up or log into your Anthropic account.
  • Access your Anthropic API key.
Cohere API key

Before you can connect your Cohere account to HubSpot, a user with the role of owner in your Cohere account must first retrieve your Cohere API key:

  • Navigate to dashboard.cohere.com to sign up or log into your Cohere account.
  • Access your Cohere API key.
xAI API key

Before you can connect your xAI account to HubSpot, a user with API write permissions in your xAI account must first retrieve your xAI API key:

  • Navigate to https://accounts.x.ai/sign-in to sign up or log into your xAI account.
  • Access your xAI API key.
Google (Gemini) API key

Before you can connect your Gemini account to HubSpot, you’ll need to retrieve your Gemini API key first:

  • Navigate to ai.google.dev to sign up or log into your Gemini account.
  • Access your Gemini API key.

Add the Use a custom LLM action to a workflow

After retrieving the API key for your LLM provider, you can add the Use a custom LLM action to workflows in HubSpot.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.

  • Set your enrollment triggers.

  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.

  • In the left panel, search for and select the Use a custom LLM workflow action.

  • From the AI provider dropdown menu, click Connect for the AI provider you want to connect to.

  • In the dialog box, enter the API key for the LLM provider.

  • Click Connect to [LLM provider].

  • From the AI model dropdown menu, select the AI model you want to use for the API call.

  • In the Prompt message field, enter your prompt.

  • Click to expand the Advanced settings section. Then, configure the following:

    • Temperature: the randomness of the generated text. Lower values will result in more predictable responses, while higher values will result in more creative responses.

    • Reasoning effort: the effort on reasoning. You can select from High, Medium, or Low. Higher values will result in more detailed responses but may take longer to generate.

  • At the top, click Save.

Manage your connected LLM account

To uninstall an LLM app:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and click the app for the desired LLM provider.
  • In the top right, click Actions > Uninstall.

To reconnect your LLM account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and click the app for the desired LLM provider.
  • In the top right, click Actions > Reconnect app.

Create HubSpot tasks and tickets in Microsoft Teams

After connecting HubSpot and Microsoft Teams, create HubSpot tasks and tickets directly from Microsoft Teams. This allows you to capture follow-up work and support requests while working in Microsoft Teams. Tasks and tickets created in Microsoft Teams are also added to HubSpot and can be associated with contact, company, or deal records.

Create a task

Create HubSpot tasks from Microsoft Teams to track follow-up actions without navigating to HubSpot. When creating a task, you can add task details and associate it with a contact, company, or deal record.

To create a task in Microsoft Teams:

  • Start a new conversation in Microsoft Teams.

  • Click … > click the HubSpot app.

  • Click Create a task.

  • In the dialog box, fill out the relevant fields. You can also associate the task to a HubSpot company, contact, or deal record.

  • Click Save.

  • Once the task is created, you’ll see a completion message in Microsoft Teams.

From the task created in Microsoft Teams, you can complete the following actions:

  • Associate: associate the task to any contact, company, or deal record in HubSpot.
  • Update notes: update the task details.
  • Mark as completed: mark the task as completed.
  • Post to channel: post the task details to a Microsoft Teams channel.

Create a ticket

Create HubSpot tickets from Microsoft Teams to track customer requests or issues in HubSpot. When creating a ticket, you can specify its pipeline, status, owner, and priority, and associate it with a contact, company, or deal record.

To create a ticket in Microsoft Teams:

  • Start a new conversation in Microsoft Teams with the Hubspot bot.

  • Click … > click the HubSpot app.

  • Click Create a ticket.

  • In the dialog box, fill out the relevant fields including the ticket name, description, pipeline and status, owner, and priority. You can also associate the ticket to any HubSpot contact, company, or deal record.

  • Click Save.

  • Once the ticket is created, you’ll see a completion message in Microsoft Teams.

From the ticket created in Microsoft Teams, you can complete the following actions:

  • Associate: associate the ticket to any HubSpot contact, company, or deal record.
  • Add note: add a note to the ticket.
  • Update ticket status: update the ticket’s status.
  • Post to channel: post the completion message to a Microsoft Teams channel.

Embed HubSpot data into a Microsoft Dynamics 365 app

After you’ve connected HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics 365, you can embed HubSpot in your Microsoft Dynamics 365 app. This allows you to view information for a HubSpot contact, company, or deal record directly in the Microsoft Dynamics 365 interface.

The HubSpot Embed window in Microsoft Dynamics 365 displays HubSpot timeline activities, such as logged emails, workflows the record is enrolled in, and record properties. It also includes a link to the corresponding record in HubSpot.

Before you get started

Before getting started, do note the following:

Permissions required To view the HubSpot Embed window in Microsoft Dynamics 365, you must be logged into HubSpot and have View records permissions in HubSpot.

  • To view the HubSpot Embed window on a Microsoft Dynamics 365 record, you must be a user in both Microsoft Dynamics 365 and HubSpot.
  • HubSpot Embed must be turned on in both HubSpot and Microsoft Dynamics 365 to complete the installation process.

Turn on HubSpot Embed

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Click the Feature discovery tab.
  • On the Bring the power of HubSpot to Microsoft Dynamics 365 card, click Install HubSpot Embed.
  • In the dialog box, click Install.
  • Review the necessary permissions, then click Accept. You’ll be redirected back to HubSpot.
  • Once HubSpot Embed has been installed, click Close.
  • After installing HubSpot Embed in HubSpot, log in to your Microsoft Dynamics 365 account.

Embed HubSpot into a Microsoft Dynamics 365 app

  • In Microsoft Dynamics 365, navigate to the My Apps page.

  • In the search bar, search for the app you want to embed HubSpot into.

  • On the app card, click the three horizontal dots icon and select Open in App Designer.

  • Once the app is open, click the three horizontal dots icon in the upper left and click Switch to classic.

  • In the Contact/Company/Opportunity section, click Forms.

  • In the right panel, select the form you want to embed HubSpot into.

  • Click the pencil icon to open the form editor.

  • In the Components section, under the Layout tab, select 1-column tab.

  • In the right panel, enter a Label and Name for the tab.

  • Under the Display tab, click HTML web resource.

  • In the dialog box, search for and select hubspot_HubSpotEmbed. Then click Add.

  • On the right side, enter a unique name and label for the web resource.

  • Click Save to save the changes or click Publish when you’re ready to take the changes live.

  • Once the changes are saved, navigate to a contact, company, or deal record in Microsoft Dynamics 365 and click the HubSpot tab to view the HubSpot information.

Explore HubSpot Embed features

With HubSpot Embed, you can:

  • View the record’s timeline and any associated objects in Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Enroll the record in a workflow and view any previous workflow enrollments.
  • View the record’s properties and property history.
  • Directly book meetings in HubSpot through Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • Enroll contacts in a sequence through Microsoft Dynamics 365.

Embed HubSpot data into a NetSuite layout

After connecting HubSpot and NetSuite, you can embed HubSpot data into a NetSuite layout. This allows you to view information for a HubSpot contact, company or deal record directly in a NetSuite layout.

The HubSpot Embed window in NetSuite displays HubSpot timeline activities, such as logged emails, workflows the record is enrolled in, and record properties. It also includes a link to the corresponding record in HubSpot.

Turn on HubSpot Embed

  • Click NetSuite.
  • Click the Feature discovery tab.
  • In the Enable extra features banner, click Enable.
  • On the Bring the power of HubSpot to NetSuite card, click Install HubSpot Embed.
  • In the dialog box, click Install.

Embed HubSpot into a NetSuite layout

To install the HubSpot Sync Bundle:

Explore HubSpot Embed features

With HubSpot Embed, you can:

Embed HubSpot data into a Zoho CRM record

After connecting HubSpot and Zoho CRM, you can embed HubSpot data into a Zoho record. This allows you to view information from a HubSpot contact, company, or deal record directly in Zoho.

The HubSpot Embed window displays timeline activities such as logged emails, workflows that the record is enrolled in, and record properties. It also includes a link to the corresponding HubSpot record.

Turn on HubSpot Embed for Zoho

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Zoho CRM.
  • Navigate to the Feature discovery tab.
  • On the Bring the power of HubSpot to Zoho CRM card, click Install HubSpot Embed. A banner stating Your HubSpot embed was installed in Zoho CRM will appear. This means the embed has been installed in HubSpot; however, you still need to complete the installation process for Zoho CRM.
  • To complete the installation process, click Learn more. This will open Zoho CRM in a new tab.

View the HubSpot Embed window in Zoho

Export to BigQuery (Legacy)

Learn how to connect HubSpot and Google BigQuery to sync HubSpot data to your Google BigQuery instance.

Please note: HubSpot does not share HIPAA data to Google BigQuery.

Connect HubSpot and BigQuery

To connect HubSpot and Google BigQuery, you must run through these steps in order:

  • Install Google BigQuery from the HubSpot App Marketplace.
  • Create a custom IAM role in Google Cloud Platform.
  • Assign the custom role to the Google Service Account.
  • Grant the HubSpot-generated Google BigQuery account permissions to modify BigQuery tables.
  • Complete set up in HubSpot.
1. Install Google BigQuery from the HubSpot App Marketplace

It’s recommended that you have your HubSpot account and Google BigQuery account open in separate tabs when connecting the two apps.

  • Make sure your HubSpot account is opted into the beta: Access HubSpot data in Google BigQuery.
  • Navigate to this link and select your HubSpot account.
  • Click Install.
  • Enter your Bucket URI and Project ID.
  • Click Next.
  • Review and take note of the Google Service and BigQuery accounts as you’ll need them in the next step. Then, navigate to your Google Cloud console to complete the next step.
2. Create a custom IAM role in Google Cloud Platform

  • Log into your Google Cloud console.

  • Click the left navigation menu and select IAM & Admin > Roles.

  • At the top, click Create Role.

  • Enter a title, optional description, and ID for the role.

  • Click Add permissions.

  • In the table, select the following permissions and click Add:

bigquery.datasets.create

bigquery.datasets.get

bigquery.datasets.getIamPolicy

bigquery.jobs.create

bigquery.tables.create

bigquery.tables.createIndex

bigquery.tables.createSnapshot

bigquery.tables.createTagBinding

bigquery.tables.delete

bigquery.tables.deleteIndex

bigquery.tables.deleteSnapshot

bigquery.tables.update

bigquery.tables.get

storage.buckets.get

storage.objects.create

storage.objects.delete

storage.objects.get

storage.objects.list

  • Click Create.
3. Grant Google Service Account permissions to access Cloud Storage Buckets

  • Click the left navigation menu and select Cloud Storage > Buckets.

  • Select a bucket to configure.

  • Click the Permissions tab.

  • On the View by principals tab, click Grant access.

  • In the right panel, in the New principals field, enter the Google Service Account name from Step 1.

Please note: make sure to assign the Google Service Account, not the BigQuery account.

  • In the Assign roles section, click the dropdown menu and select Custom > <role> where <role> is the custom IAM role created in Step 2.
  • Click Save. The Google Service account will be added to the Storage Object Viewer role.
4. Grant the HubSpot-generated Google BigQuery Account permissions to modify BigQuery tables
  • Click the left navigation menu and select IAM & Admin > IAM.
  • Click Grant Access.
  • In the right panel, in the New principals field, enter the HubSpot-generated Google BigQuery Account from Step 1.
  • In the Assign roles section, click the dropdown menu and select Custom > <role> where <role> is the custom IAM role created in Step 2.
5. Complete set up in HubSpot
  • Back in your HubSpot account, click Continue to Connected Apps.
  • In the dialog box, select the checkboxes, then click Allow and install.

Data format for syncing between HubSpot and Google BigQuery

Available data for syncing

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to Google BigQuery:

  • Objects: standard and custom objects, such as contacts, companies, tickets, or products.
  • Records: individual object records.
  • Associations: all association types and associated records.
  • Events: event data for both standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events.
  • Segments: HubSpot contact and company segments.
  • Owners: record owners.
  • Pipelines: deal and ticket pipelines and pipeline stages.
  • Properties: properties and their values on the object records, including the property history.

Object data of different types are organized and available in two ways:

  • Individual: each object type is stored in its own table and has only records of the same object type. For example, objects_contacts contains only contact records.
  • Combined: all records for all object types are combined into one database object. Thus, when querying, you need to specify a filter like “WHERE objectTypeId=’0-1’

Custom objects will be assigned an ID at the time of creation, and will be identified as 2-unique_ID. For example, 2-12345.

objects_x tables

Each available object type, including custom objects, has its own specific table. These tables are named following the format OBJECTS_&lt;object type name> where &lt;object type name> is the plural form label of the objecttype.(Note that if the object type has no plural form, then &lt;object type name> will be the singular form label of the object type name concatenated with “S”).

Below is a complete list of available HubSpot object types, a short description of the data they represent, and their corresponding tables.
