When using HubSpot’s MCP server, HubSpot may collect summaries of tool calls, including the intent of the request and whether it succeeded. We take steps to anonymize names of people, companies or deals. This data is used to monitor connector performance and to help us improve your experience.

Set up enterprise-managed authentication in Claude

Enterprise-managed authentication (EMA) lets admins set up the HubSpot connector for their Claude organization. Eligible members then see HubSpot already connected in Claude, without installing the connector or approving a separate connection themselves.

With Claude-issued managed authorization, admins choose who receives automatic access in Claude and manage the connector’s access in HubSpot. Each member connects as their own HubSpot user, with their existing HubSpot permissions.

Before you get started

Before you set up authentication, confirm the following roles and prerequisite steps:

  • A Claude Team or Enterprise organization with Claude-issued managed authorization available for the HubSpot connector.
  • An admin who can manage connectors in Claude and a HubSpot Super Admin who can manage approved apps. One person can perform both these roles if needed.
  • The HubSpot connector is available in your Claude organization’s Connector settings.
  • The HubSpot connector has been installed by an admin in the HubSpot account you want to connect. You can start with this existing connection before configuring EMA for other team members.
  • An active HubSpot user account for each team member who will use the connector. Each member’s Claude email address must match their verified HubSpot email address.

If an admin hasn’t installed the connector in the target HubSpot account, follow these instructions to set up the HubSpot connector for Claude to complete the initial connection. Then, review the app’s approval and access settings before proceeding.

Verify that each team member has the correct permission set in HubSpot. For currently supported tools, team members use the same HubSpot permissions and entitlements in Claude, subject to the connector’s allowed scopes and data permissions.

Learn more about Claude’s managed authorization settings and role controls.

Access settings in Claude and HubSpot

The table below outlines the different access settings in Claude and HubSpot:

Setting

What it controls

Claude Roles with access

Which team members can find and setup the connector.

Claude Applied roles

Which roles connect through managed authorization.

Claude scopes

Which permissions Claude can request for the connection.

HubSpot install permissions

Which HubSpot users and teams are allowed to connect to the app.

HubSpot data permissions

Which data and APIs the app is allowed to access.

HubSpot user permissions

Which records and actions the specific team member can access in HubSpot.

Giving someone access to the connector in Claude doesn’t create a HubSpot user or expand their HubSpot permissions. Review access in both services before enabling the connection for your team.

Claude confirms that admins and users of the connector are current members of your Claude organization with email address they’ve configured. It doesn’t confirm a separate identity-provider sign-in or check that provider’s multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirements or HubSpot’s sign-in rules. Anthropic recommends enforcing single sign-on (SSO) in Claude.

Set up managed authentication

The steps below walk you through how to confirm your current connector permissions, find your organization’s issuer URL in your Claude settings, enable EMA, then test out the resulting connection.

1. Review the connector’s access in HubSpot

First, confirm the current permissions for the HubSpot connector for Claude:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click the Approved apps tab.
  • Find the HubSpot Connector for Claude, then click Manage access.
  • Click the Installed Permissions tab, review who can connect to the app. Include the HubSpot users who should receive automatic access in Claude. Members must also have access to the connector in Claude and belong to a role selected for managed authorization.
  • Click the Data permissions tab, review the data and APIs the connector can access. Add the permissions that your team needs, then save your changes.

HubSpot’s app data permissions apply to all users, including admins. Required permissions can’t be turned off. Learn more about managing access to apps.

Keep this HubSpot page open while you access your Claude account in a separate tab.

2. Get your Claude organization’s issuer URL

Next, you’ll find and copy the issuer URL from your Claude settings, which identifies the Claude organization that HubSpot will trust when connecting members.

  • In Claude, navigate to Organization settings > Connectors and select HubSpot.
  • In the connector’s settings, find Managed authorization and open its setup.
  • Under Identity source, select Claude-issued.
  • Copy the full Issuer URL shown in the setup screen. If Claude shows Set up manually, expand it to view the URL.

Keep this setup page open in a separate browser window or tab. You’ll return to it after enabling EMA in HubSpot.

3. Enable EMA in HubSpot

Use the issuer URL you copied to configure EMA in HubSpot:

  • Return to the connector’s Manage access panel in HubSpot.
  • Click the Advanced tab.
  • Click the Enterprise managed authentication (EMA) switch to open setup.
  • Copy the Account ID shown in the panel. This is the HubSpot account you are connecting, and you’ll use it as the tenant ID in Claude.
  • Paste the full URL from Claude into Issuer URL field.
  • Click Turn on EMA.
  • Confirm that the status is On and that the saved issuer URL is correct.

If the EMA setting is missing, check out the troubleshooting section below.

4. Test and enable the connection in Claude

Now that EMA is configured, test out the connection in Claude:

  • Return to the managed authorization setup in Claude.
  • For the Tenant ID field, enter the HubSpot Account ID you copied. Although Claude labels this field optional, you should still enter it for the HubSpot connection.
  • Click Run test and check that every stage succeeds.
  • Click Continue to open the Roles setup. Select which roles should connect through managed authorization. Review the selection before enabling it for your organization.
  • Click Enable.
  • On the Connector details panel, confirm that Managed authorization is on and Applied roles lists the roles you selected.
  • Under Managed authorization, click Edit next to Scopes to review and update the permissions Claude can request.
  • Review Roles with access to confirm that the intended members can find and connect the connector. Click Edit if you need to change this access.

Both Claude role settings matter: members need access to the connector, and their role must be included in managed authorization to connect automatically. Members must also meet the HubSpot account, email, and install-permission requirements described above. For more about Claude’s role settings, check out this Claude Support article.

Check the member experience

Before announcing the change to your organization, ask a few team members to check the connection:

  • Open Claude in the organization where managed authorization is enabled.
  • Confirm that HubSpot appears connected. Enable the connector for the conversation if needed.
  • Start with a request that doesn’t change data, such as: Which HubSpot account and user am I connected as? Don’t change any data.
  • Confirm that the response identifies the expected HubSpot account and, if available, the team member’s user details.
  • Try a request to read a record the team member can access in HubSpot.

Some user details require additional permissions. If those details aren’t available, you can still check the connected account and a permitted record read. Missing optional details alone don’t mean authentication failed; don’t grant extra access just to complete this check.

Team members who meet the access requirements don’t need to complete an individual HubSpot sign-in or connection consent screen. EMA doesn’t remove approval prompts you configure for individual tool actions, such as updates to CRM records.

Manage access after setup

To update a team member’s access after setup:

  • In your Claude account, open the Claude Connector details panel.
  • Under Managed authentication, click Edit next to Applied roles to change which roles use managed authorization.
  • To change who can find and connect the connector, click Edit next to Roles with access.
  • Click Edit next to Scopes to manage which permissions Claude can request.

In HubSpot, review the Install Permissions tab to change who is allowed to connect to the app and Data Permissions tab to manage the data and APIs it can access. Each member continues to use their own HubSpot permissions.

Learn more about general connector capabilities and usage guidance in this article.

Remove a member’s access

Follow your organization’s offboarding process in both Claude and HubSpot. Removing a person from the Claude organization stops Claude from issuing new identity assertions for them. An access token that was already issued can remain usable until it expires or is revoked, so don’t rely on a membership change alone for immediate removal of access.

Before assigning a former member’s email address to someone else, remove the former member as a HubSpot user through your organization’s offboarding process. Removing only their connector access doesn’t remove the old HubSpot user associated with that email address.

Turn off EMA

To turn off EMA:

  • In Claude, open the HubSpot connector’s Managed authorization settings and click Disable.
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected apps > Approved apps.
  • Find the connector, click Manage access, then select Advanced.
  • Click to toggle the Enterprise managed authentication (EMA) switch off, then click Turn off to confirm.

Disabling managed authorization ends automatic connection. Members who still need the connector must connect individually, subject to your organization’s settings and HubSpot install permissions. Existing access tokens may remain valid until they expire or are revoked.

Troubleshooting

The sections below provide guidance on common errors you may encounter during the setup process.

The EMA setting isn’t available

Confirm that you’re a HubSpot Super Admin, you’re in the correct HubSpot account, and you’re managing the approved HubSpot connector for Claude. If Enterprise managed authentication (EMA) still doesn’t appear under Advanced, contact HubSpot support to check availability for your account and connector.

Claude’s connection test fails

Consult the table below for details on what to check based on the stage when the connection failed:

Failed stage

What to check

Check eligibility

Confirm that your Claude organization and the connector have access to Claude-issued managed authorization. Contact Claude support if the option isn’t available.

Also check Claude organization membership and that an email is on file.

Discover authorization server

Confirm that you selected the intended HubSpot connector. If discovery still fails, contact HubSpot support with the connector name and the time of the test.

Create the identity assertion

Confirm that the person running the test is a current member of the Claude organization and has an email address on their account.

Exchange for access token

Check that EMA is on in the intended HubSpot account, the saved issuer URL exactly matches Claude’s URL, and the tenant ID is the correct HubSpot account ID. Confirm that the testing user has a matching verified HubSpot email and is allowed by the app’s install permissions.

Probe connector

HubSpot issued a token, but the connector didn’t accept the request. Contact HubSpot support with the connector name, failed stage, and time of the test.

An invalid_grant error alone doesn’t identify the root cause. Check the account, issuer URL, email match, and access settings before repeating the test.

A team member can’t find HubSpot or still sees a Connect prompt

First, check that the member is in the intended Claude organization. In your Claude settings, on Connector details page, review Roles with access if they can’t find the connector and Applied roles if they aren’t connecting through managed authorization.

In HubSpot, confirm that they have an active user account, their verified email matches their Claude email, and install permissions allow them to connect.

A team member connects but can’t access expected data

Review the connector’s scopes in your Claude account, the app’s Data Permissions in HubSpot, and the team member’s HubSpot permissions. Automatic connection doesn’t grant access to records or actions the member can’t use in HubSpot.

If the issue continues, contact support with the operation that failed and the time it occurred. Don’t include access tokens or signed identity assertions in a support request.

When using HubSpot Smart Transfer, the apps listed below are supported. Each supported app has its own set of objects and engagements that can be transferred to HubSpot using HubSpot Smart Transfer’s Data Sync. Each app also has specific data types that can’t be transferred via Data Sync, such as Attachments from Pipedrive or Lists and Tags from ActiveCampaign. Please note: the data transferred through one-time post-sync transfers will not be part of an ongoing sync and therefore will not automatically stay up to date.

Sync activities and tasks between HubSpot and Salesforce

After installing the HubSpot-Salesforce integration, you can sync HubSpot marketing and sales activities with Salesforce tasks. Syncing HubSpot activities like email opens, clicks, and form submissions with Salesforce tasks gives your team a complete view of the customer journey, interactions, and activities in a single, unified system, improving collaboration and efficiency. You can also report on HubSpot activities within Salesforce.

Before you get started

Before you begin setting up the sync, please note the following:

  • Turning on the sync will not automatically import all task data from Salesforce to HubSpot. Individual records will sync when they are created or updated in Salesforce. To import all data into HubSpot, use an import.
  • Once you select a HubSpot activity to sync to Salesforce, all HubSpot activities of that type will sync.
  • Emails created in Salesforce using the Einstein Activity Capture tool don’t sync to HubSpot, as they aren’t created as task (email) activities in Salesforce.
  • Salesforce doesn’t allow records, including tasks, to be assigned to inactive users/owners. If a HubSpot engagement is assigned to an inactive owner, the engagement won’t sync to Salesforce and a sync error will occur. To resolve the error, temporarily reactivate the owner or reassign the engagement owner in HubSpot.

Types of syncs between HubSpot and Salesforce

Depending on how your Salesforce activities are set up, whether you want the sync to be one-way or two-way, and which activities you want to sync, there are two types of sync you can choose from:

  • Timeline sync
  • Activity sync

Timeline sync

It’s a one-way sync from HubSpot to Salesforce that syncs HubSpot timeline events to Salesforce as tasks.

HubSpot events supported by the Timeline sync

The following HubSpot events are supported by the Timeline sync:

  • Form submissions
  • Marketing email sends, opens, and clicks
  • Sales email sends, opens, and clicks
  • Meetings scheduled
  • Calls made
  • Notes created
  • Sales content viewed
  • Tasks created
  • Events from installed integrations
Sync timeframes for HubSpot timeline events to Salesforce tasks

Please keep in mind the following timeframes, after the sync is turned on:

  • Sales emails, tasks, meetings, notes, and sales content views: these activities will only sync after the contact has been triggered to sync. Any activities from prior to the contact sync will not be synced retroactively.
  • Marketing email events: only marketing email events that occurred within 30 days of the contact being synced will sync to Salesforce.
  • Form submissions: only form submissions that occurred within one year of the contact being synced will sync to Salesforce.

Please note:

  • Every time a contact opens or clicks a marketing email sent from your HubSpot account, HubSpot deduplicates each type of activity on the object record timeline. If you have set up these email activities to sync to Salesforce, the corresponding Salesforce tasks are created via HubSpot’s Email Events API, which does not deduplicate activities.
  • If a contact opens or clicks a marketing email multiple times, multiple Salesforce tasks will be created.
  • If a contact forwards a marketing email to another recipient, any subsequent email opens and clicks will be attributed to the original contact, and more Salesforce tasks will be created.
How to set up the Timeline sync
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Navigate to the Data sync tab.
  • Click Activities > Timeline.
  • Next to the respective HubSpot event, click to toggle the switch on to sync that event to a Salesforce task.
  • To specify the Salesforce task type for the activity, click the Salesforce Task Type dropdown menu and select a task type. If you don’t select a specific task type (i.e., – No task type – is selected), the activity will sync to Salesforce as a task without a type.

Activity sync

It’s a two-way sync between HubSpot and Salesforce. This type of sync allows for bidirectional syncing, giving more granular control over what syncs and in what direction.

To turn on the Activity sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Feature discovery tab.
On the Enable new Activity Sync card, click Install.

Please note: if you turn on both the Activity sync and the Timeline sync for the same event type, ‌the Activity sync will override the corresponding Timeline sync setting to prevent duplicate records from being created in Salesforce.

HubSpot events supported by the Activity sync

The following HubSpot events are supported by ‌Activity sync:

  • Tasks
  • Sales emails
  • Calls
  • Meetings
How to setup the Activity sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Search for and select Salesforce.

  • Navigate to the Data sync tab.

  • Click Activities. Then click Tasks, Emails, Calls, or Meetings to sync the respective HubSpot activity.

  • For the event type that you want to sync, click to toggle the sync switch on.

  • In the Creating and Updating [Activity] section, review what happens when an activity event is created or updated in HubSpot and Salesforce.

  • In the Deleting [Activity] section, select what happens in HubSpot and Salesforce when ‌an activity event is deleted.

  • In the Deduplication by Field Mapping section, click the dropdown menu and select the field mapping that you want to use to deduplicate the activity events.

  • In the Resolve Sync Conflict Rule section, click the dropdown menu and select the app that should be preferred to resolve any conflict of data.

  • In the Selective Sync section, control which Salesforce activity events sync to HubSpot.

    • Click Add filter.
    • In the right panel, click the Field dropdown menu and select a filter.
    • Then, click Save and apply filter. Add more filters as needed. Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.
    • Toggle the switch for selective sync on.

  • In the Property Mappings section, review how Salesforce fields sync to HubSpot activity properties.

    • Hover over a property and click Actions.
    • Then select Edit to edit the mapping or Delete to delete the mapping.
    • Click Add new mapping to add a new field mapping.

  • In the Associations section, if you want to sync the contact association and the account association, click to toggle the Sync Account association and Sync Contact association switches on.

    • For each association, click the Primary association field dropdown menu and select the field you want HubSpot to use to associate the two objects.
    • Click the Association label dropdown menu and select the association label you want to use.
    • Click the Sync direction dropdown menu and select how you want the association to sync between HubSpot and Salesforce (Two-way sync, Salesforce to HubSpot only, or HubSpot to Salesforce only).

Report on HubSpot activities in Salesforce

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account.

  • Click the Reports tab.

  • In the top right, click New Report.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Activities to see a list of all activity-based reports.

  • Click Activities with Contacts or Activities with Leads (separate reports must be created for contacts and leads).

  • In the top right, click Start report.

  • To filter by a specific activity type or activity date, click the Filters tab in the top left. Then click the existing default filters to edit them, or click Add filter to search for other filters you wish to apply.

  • In the top right, click Run Report to run the report or click Save to save the report.

Troubleshoot activity sync errors

You may encounter the following error message when syncing HubSpot marketing and sales activities to Salesforce tasks:

Problem getting task info from Salesforce. We’re having trouble getting task type data from Salesforce. This could be because the Salesforce user doesn’t have permission to read the Type field.

To resolve this error, follow the two steps below.

1. Ensure that the Type field is visible to all profiles in Salesforce

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account:

    • Salesforce Classic:
      • In the upper right, click Setup (or [Your Name] > Setup).
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Build > Customize > Activities > Task Fields.
      • In the list of fields, click Type.
    • Lightning Experience:
      • In the upper right, click the settings gear icon and select settings Setup.
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Platform Tools > Objects and Fields > Object Manager.
      • In the list of objects, click Task.
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Fields & Relationships.
      • In the list of fields, click Type.

  • Click Set Field-Level Security.

  • In the header row of the Field-Level Security for Profile table, select the Visible checkbox.

  • At the top, click Save. This will make the task type field visible to all profiles.

2. Ensure that the Type field is visible on the Task Page Layout in Salesforce

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account:

    • Salesforce Classic:
      • In the upper right, click Setup (or [Your Name] > Setup).
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Build > Customize > Activities > Task Page Layouts.
      • On the left of Task Layout, click Edit.
    • Lightning Experience:
      • In the upper right, click the gear icon settings and select settings Setup.
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Platform Tools > Objects and Fields > Object Manager.
      • In the list of objects, click Task.
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Page Layouts.
      • Click Task Layout.

  • Click the Type item in the toolbar and drag and drop it into the desired location on the page layout.

  • In the top left of the toolbar, click Save to apply your layout changes.

After you’ve made the Type field visible to all profiles and added it to your task layout in Salesforce, check if the error is resolved in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Salesforce.
  • Navigate to the Data sync tab.
  • Click Activities > Timeline.
  • If the error has been resolved, the error message will no longer appear in this section.

Sync companies between HubSpot and Salesforce

Turn on additional company sync functionality to sync companies without associated contacts and configure company deduplication, association sync, company merges, and selective sync.

For example, if two company records represent the same organization but have no associated contacts, they can be matched and synced between HubSpot and Salesforce. This helps maintain consistent company data across both platforms.

Before you get started

Before using company sync, please note the following:

  • The Salesforce integration must be connected to your HubSpot account.
  • If you’re using the standard company sync, once you turn on the additional company sync functionality, you cannot revert to the previous company sync experience. It’s recommended to test the company sync in a developer test account or sandbox account before turning it on in a production account.
  • When you turn on the company sync, this may temporarily increase Salesforce API usage as the new sync indexes records. Once indexing is complete, API usage will return to normal.
  • Company merges in HubSpot do not merge records in Salesforce.

Turn on the company sync

To turn on the company sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Feature discovery tab.
  • On the New Company Sync card, click Enable.

After turning the sync on, company records will start syncing.

Understand how the company sync works

Company sync includes the same core syncing behavior as the standard company sync. It also supports additional functionality for syncing companies without associated contacts, company deduplication, association sync, sync conflict rules, company merges, and selective sync.

Associated contacts

Company records can sync even when they aren’t associated with any contacts.

Association sync

Sync company associations based on Salesforce lookup fields. You can also sync association labels and choose your preferred sync direction (Two-way sync, Salesforce to HubSpot only, or HubSpot to Salesforce only).

Company deduplication

Companies are deduplicated based on mapped field values. For records to match, the mapped field values must be identical in both HubSpot and Salesforce.

For example, if the Company domain name property is mapped between HubSpot and Salesforce, company records with the same domain value can be matched and synced.

Existing matched records will not be affected by the deduplication logic. The deduplication logic will only apply to new companies and accounts moving forward, after the company sync is turned on.

Learn more about setting up deduplication using field mapping.

Company sync rules

Control what happens to companies and accounts when records are created, updated, or deleted in HubSpot and Salesforce.

To manage these settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Search for and select Salesforce.

  • Click the Data sync tab.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Companies > Sync rules.

    • For creating and updating records, configure the sync direction between HubSpot and Salesforce:
      • Salesforce to HubSpot: select what happens in HubSpot when a Salesforce account is created or updated.
      • HubSpot to Salesforce: select what happens in Salesforce when a HubSpot company is created or updated.
    • For deleted records, configure what happens in HubSpot when a Salesforce account is deleted:
      • Salesforce to HubSpot: select whether the corresponding HubSpot company is deleted when a Salesforce account is deleted.
      • HubSpot to Salesforce: when a HubSpot company is deleted, the corresponding Salesforce account is not deleted. This setting cannot be edited.
Sync conflict rule

When records match between HubSpot and Salesforce, you can set which data source will be used when it’s unclear which has the most up-to-date information. This rule only affects records when they first sync.

Company field mapping sync rules

Existing sync rules from the standard company sync remain available. An additional field mapping sync rule, Always use HubSpot, lets you sync data from HubSpot to Salesforce for a field mapping.

Please note: the sync rule feature only applies when using a two-way object-level sync rule. If a one-way object-level sync rule is selected, the value is overridden in the one-way direction.

Company merges

Company merges are supported in HubSpot.

When two HubSpot company records are merged:

  • The resulting HubSpot record continues syncing with its associated Salesforce record.
  • Salesforce records are not merged automatically.
Selective sync

Use selective sync to control which Salesforce accounts sync from Salesforce to HubSpot. Only Salesforce accounts that match the filter criteria will sync to HubSpot.

To set up selective sync for company records:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Data Sync tab.
  • Click Companies > Sync rules.
  • In the Selective Sync section, control which Salesforce accounts sync to HubSpot.
  • Click Add filter.
  • In the right panel, click the Field dropdown menu and select a filter.
  • Then, click Save and apply filter. Add more filters as needed. Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.
  • Toggle the switch for selective sync on.
  • Click Save.

Sync custom objects between HubSpot and data sync apps

Use data sync to sync custom objects between HubSpot and supported data sync apps. Syncing custom objects helps keep the same object data available across both systems, reducing manual updates and supporting consistent records for your business processes.

For example, if you use a custom object to track subscriptions, assets, or locations in HubSpot, you can sync those records with a connected app so updates are reflected in both systems. After connecting the app, configure the sync direction, map fields, and define sync rules for your custom object.

Before you get started

  • You must create the custom object in your HubSpot account before setting up the custom object sync.

  • Currently, it’s possible to sync custom objects with the following data sync apps:

    • Airtable (tables)
    • Kintone (tables)
    • Microsoft Dynamics 365 (entities)
    • Smartsheet (sheets)
    • Snowflake
    • Zoho CRM (modules)

Turn on the sync

To turn on your custom object sync:

  • Connect the app to your account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click the app.

  • Navigate to the CRM syncs tab.

  • If this is the first time you’re syncing an object, click Set up your sync. If you have other objects already synced, click Sync more data.

  • On the Select the data you want to sync page, select the object to sync to or from in the other app.

  • Select the custom object you want to sync to or from in HubSpot. Custom objects are located under Additional objects in the dropdown menu.

  • Click the arrows dropdown menu, and select whether the sync is bi-directional or one way between the app and HubSpot, or vice versa.

  • Click Next.

Configure your sync direction and mapped fields

  • On the Configure page, choose how you want data to sync from HubSpot to the other app, and vice versa. There are three options:

    • Data syncs between apps: all new and updated object information will be synced between the two apps. Properties will be merged for records that already exist in both platforms.
    • Data syncs only to HubSpot: data will be synced from your other app to HubSpot.
    • Data syncs only to [your other app]: data will be synced from HubSpot to your other app.

  • In the Data conflict resolution section, click the dropdown menu and select the default app that’ll overwrite the other when there are data discrepancies. If there’s no field value in the default app, no data will be changed in the other app. This setting doesn’t overrule the sync direction selected in the Sync direction section.

  • In the Mapped fields section, review the default property mappings and how information syncs between HubSpot and your other app. If you have a paid Data Hub subscription, you can set up custom mappings for properties. Required fields will show in the field mappings table with an asterisk (*).

    • To turn off a mapping, click to turn the toggle off.
    • To set up a custom field mapping:
      • Click Add a mapping.
      • Use the dropdown menus and select the other app property and the HubSpot property you want to map.
      • Click success Update.
      • To turn off custom mappings, click to toggle the switch off.

Set up your sync rules

  • On the Limit page, configure how you want to sync records from HubSpot to your other app, and vice versa.

  • In the Filters section, choose criteria to limit which records will sync from HubSpot to your other app, and vice versa:

    • Click Edit.
    • In the right panel, select the property to limit records syncing from HubSpot to your other app, and vice versa.
    • Click Done. Then click Next.

Please note: the Filters section only limits which records initially sync between HubSpot and the other app. Once records sync, they will continue to sync data back and forth based on the property mapping set up.

Associate records

When syncing with a custom object, associations won’t be maintained. It is recommended to map them manually.

Review rules and start the sync

On the Review page, review the rules you’ve configured, then click Save and sync. The initial sync will then begin to process.

After the initial sync is complete, records will sync within 10 minutes of a change.

Sync custom objects between HubSpot and Salesforce

After connecting Salesforce to HubSpot, you can sync Salesforce custom objects with HubSpot. Syncing custom objects keeps object data consistent across both platforms. For example, if your Salesforce account uses a custom object to track subscriptions, you can sync that object with HubSpot so your teams can access and use the same data for segmentation, automation, and reporting.

Before you get started

  • You must create the custom object in your HubSpot account before setting up the custom sync within your Salesforce integration settings.
  • It’s not possible to create field mappings involving Salesforce lookup fields on custom objects. You can sync this data through the association setting.

Set up your custom object sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Salesforce.

  • Navigate to the Data sync tab.

  • In the top left, click + Sync custom object.

  • In the popup box, click Get started.

  • On the Map objects page, click the dropdown menus to select your Salesforce object and the associated HubSpot custom object to sync. Then click Next.

  • On the Sync rules page, review your sync rules and decide what happens in either app when you update or delete a custom object. Click the Resolve sync conflict rule dropdown menu and select the app that should be used to resolve any conflicts. Then click Next.

Please note: a sync will not be triggered when a Salesforce record is removed from a Campaign. The related contact or custom object record in HubSpot must be triggered to sync for the custom object record to be deleted.

Associations

The associations fields shown on the Associations page represent what is set up in Salesforce for that custom object. If you don’t see the correct field, please reach out to your Salesforce administrator. It isn’t possible to sync a custom object to both Salesforce contacts and leads.

  • Click to toggle the associations you want to sync between Salesforce and HubSpot.
  • Click the Primary association field dropdown menu and select the field you want HubSpot to use to associate the two objects.
  • Click the Association label dropdown menu and select the association label you want to use.
  • Click the Sync direction dropdown menu and select how you want the association to sync between HubSpot and Salesforce (Two-way sync, Salesforce to HubSpot only, or HubSpot to Salesforce only).
  • Click Next.

Please note: associations can only be passed between objects that are already syncing with HubSpot. For example, if you have company sync turned on then you will be able to sync associations between accounts and your custom objects.

Field mappings
  • On the Field mappings page, select the Salesforce field you want to sync to the HubSpot required field. Custom objects in HubSpot must have at least one required field. Click the Sync Rule dropdown menu and select the sync direction for the field (Two-way, Always use Salesforce or Always use HubSpot).
  • Click Next.
  • Review your property mappings. Click the HubSpot field dropdown menu to edit a mapping.
  • Click the Sync Rule dropdown menu and select the sync direction for each field mapping (Two-way, Always use Salesforce or Always use HubSpot).
  • Click Next.
Preview

  • On the Preview page, preview and review your custom object setup. You can click Edit or Back to change your settings.

  • Click Next.

Turn on sync

  • On the Turn sync on page, select Start continual sync to sync records when they’re created or updated in Salesforce. Or Select Save for later if you want to turn on the sync at a later time.

  • In the bottom right, click Turn sync on or click Save for later.

Import custom objects from Salesforce

After setting up a custom object sync, you can import custom objects from Salesforce to pull in existing data for custom objects.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • In the top right, click Add contacts > Import.

  • On the Data integration page, click Import data.

  • Click Objects from an app.

  • Select Salesforce records, then click Next.

  • Select Custom Objects, then click Next.

  • Choose the custom object you want to import.

  • Click Review to review the number of records in the import.

  • Click Begin import.

  • You’ll be redirected back to the Data integration page. When your import is complete, it’ll appear in the import table.

Review the sync settings

After turning the sync on for a custom object, a new tab will appear in your Salesforce sync settings with the name of your custom object. From this tab, you can review the custom object sync rules, field mappings, and associations.

To review the sync settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Salesforce.

  • Navigate to the Data sync tab.

    • Click [custom object] > Sync rules.

      • In the Selective Sync section, control which Salesforce records sync to HubSpot.

        • Click Add filter.

        • In the right panel, click the Field dropdown menu and select a filter.

        • Then, click Save and apply filter. Add more filters as needed. Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.

        • Toggle the switch for selective sync on.

      • In the Limiting what syncs section, you can control which HubSpot records are eligible to sync to Salesforce.
        • Click the dropdown menu and select an existing active segment.
        • To create a new active segment, click + Create Inclusion List.

    • On the left sidebar, under [custom object]:

      • Click Field mappings to view all custom object properties mapped between HubSpot and Salesforce.

        • To add a new mapping, click Add new mapping. Then select the properties from the respective dropdown menus and click Save.
        • To edit an existing mapping, click Actions next to the mapping, then select Edit.
        • To delete a mapping, click Actions, then select Delete.

      • Click Associations to manage the association settings for the custom object sync.

    • To turn off or delete the custom object sync:

      • In the top right, click to toggle the sync switch off to turn off the custom object sync.

      • To delete the custom object sync, in the top right click Delete custom object sync.

Sync data to AWS S3 (legacy)

Connect HubSpot and AWS S3 to sync HubSpot data to an S3 bucket. After connecting the app, HubSpot can sync CRM data, including objects, records, associations, events, and segments to AWS S3 for storage, reporting, and analytics.

For example, you can sync contact and company data to an S3 bucket and use it in your organization’s data warehouse, business intelligence tools, or data processing workflows.

Please note: HubSpot does not share HIPAA data to AWS S3.

Before you get started

Prior to setting up the integration, you’ll need to opt your HubSpot account into the Access HubSpot data in AWS S3 beta.

Connect HubSpot and AWS S3

To connect HubSpot and AWS S3, you must follow the steps below in order:

  • Configure access permissions for the AWS S3 bucket.
  • Create an IAM policy.
  • Create the IAM role in AWS.
  • Connect HubSpot and AWS S3.
  • Grant the IAM user permissions to access S3 bucket objects.
1. Configure access permissions for the S3 bucket

HubSpot needs the following permissions on an AWS S3 bucket and folder to access files in the folder and sub-folders:

  • s3:GetBucketLocation
  • s3:GetObject
  • s3:GetObjectVersion
  • s3:ListBucket
  • s3:PutObject
  • s3:DeleteObject
2. Create an IAM policy
  • Log into the AWS Management Console.
  • On the home dashboard, click Services > Security, Identity, & Compliance > IAM.
  • On the left sidebar, click Account settings.
  • In the Security Token Service (STS) section, look for the AWS region that corresponds to the region your AWS account is located in. Click to toggle the switch on to activate the region.
  • On the left side panel, click Policies.
  • Click Create policy.
  • On the JSON tab, click Add new statement.
  • Add the policy document below that will give HubSpot the permissions it needs to load or unload data using a single bucket and folder path. You can also purge data files using the PURGE copy option.

Please note:

  • Make sure to replace &lt;bucket> and &lt;prefix> with your actual bucket name and folder path prefix. The Amazon Resource Names (ARN) for buckets in government regions have an arn:aws-us-gov:s3::: prefix.

  • Setting the s3:prefix condition to either [“*”] or [“<path> /*”] grants access to all prefixes in the specified bucket or path in the bucket respectively.

    {  “Version”: “2012-10-17”,  “Statement”: [  {  “Effect”: “Allow”,  “Action”: [  “s3:PutObject”,  “s3:GetObject”,  “s3:GetObjectVersion”,  “s3:DeleteObject”,  “s3:DeleteObjectVersion”  ],  “Resource”: “arn:aws:s3::://*”  },  {  “Effect”: “Allow”,  “Action”: [  “s3:ListBucket”,  “s3:GetBucketLocation”  ],  “Resource”: “arn:aws:s3:::”,  “Condition”: {  “StringLike”: {  “s3:prefix”: [  “/*”  ]  }  }  }  ]}

  • Click Next.

  • In the Review and create section, add the Policy name and an optional description.

  • Click Create policy.

3. Create the IAM role in AWS

To configure access permissions for HubSpot in the AWS Management Console:

  • Log into the AWS Management Console.

  • On the home dashboard, click Services > Security, Identity, & Compliance > IAM.

  • On the left sidebar, click Roles.

  • Click Create role.

  • In the Trusted entity type section, select AWS account.

  • In the An AWS account section, select Another AWS account and enter your own AWS account ID. You’ll later change the trust relationship to give access to HubSpot.

  • Select Require external ID and input a placeholder ID like 0000. You’ll later change the trust relationship for your IAM role and specify the external ID for your storage integration. An external ID is used to grant access to your AWS resources to a third-party app like HubSpot.

  • Click Next.

  • Select the policy created in Step 1 and click Next.

  • In the Role details section, enter a Role name and Description to identify the role.

  • Click Create role.

  • On the Role summary page, copy the ARN value. You will use this value in the next step.

4. Connect HubSpot and AWS S3

Prior to installing the integration, make sure your HubSpot account is opted into the Access HubSpot data in AWS S3 beta.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for and select AWS S3.
  • Click Install.
  • Enter the IAM Role Name configured in Step 3 and the S3 URL Path for the bucket you want the data to be stored in.
  • Click Next.
  • Review and copy the AWS IAM User and AWS External ID values as you’ll need them in the next step. Then, click Continue to Connected Apps.
5. Grant the IAM user permissions to access bucket objects
  • Log into the AWS Management Console.
  • On the home dashboard, click Services > Security, Identity, & Compliance > IAM.
  • In the left sidebar, click Roles.
  • Select the role you created in Step 3.
  • Select the Trust relationships tab and click Edit trust policy.
  • Modify the policy documents with the values you recorded in Step 3.

{

"Version": "2012-10-17",

"Statement": [

{

"Sid": "",

"Effect": "Allow",

"Principal": {

"AWS": "&lt;hubspot_user_arn>"

},

"Action": "sts:AssumeRole",

"Condition": {

"StringEquals": {

"sts:ExternalId": "&lt;hubspot_external_id>"

}

}

}

]

}

  • In the above policy, change the following two fields to the values you recorded from Step 4:

    • hubspot_user_arn to the STORAGE_AWS_IAM_USER_ARN value
    • hubspot_external_id to the STORAGE_AWS_EXTERNAL_ID value

After completing the above steps, HubSpot can sync data into AWS S3.

Data format for syncing between HubSpot and AWS S3

Available data for syncing

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to AWS S3:

  • Objects: standard and custom objects, such as contacts, companies, tickets, or products.
  • Records: individual object records.
  • Associations: all association types and associated records.
  • Events: event data for both standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events.
  • Segments: HubSpot contact and company segments.
  • Owners: record owners.
  • Pipelines: deal and ticket pipelines and pipeline stages.
  • Properties: properties and their values on the object records, including the property history.

Object data of different types are organized and available in two ways:

  • Individual: each object type is stored in its own table and has only records of the same object type. For example, objects_contacts contains only contact records.
  • Combined: all records for all object types are combined into one database object. Thus, when querying, you need to specify a filter like “WHERE objectTypeId=’0-1’

Custom objects will be assigned an ID at the time of creation, and will be identified as 2-unique_ID. For example, 2-12345.

objects_x tables

Each available object type, including custom objects, has its own specific table. These tables are named following the format OBJECTS_&lt;object type name> where &lt;object type name> is the plural form label of the objecttype. Note that if the object type has no plural form, then &lt;object type name> will be the singular form label of the object type name concatenated with “S”.

Below is a complete list of available HubSpot object types, a short description of the data they represent, and their corresponding tables.

object_with_object_properties

This table contains data from your HubSpot records. You can get one row for each record within an objecttype (e.g., all contact records in the contacts objecttype).

object_properties_history

This table contains historical property values. For contacts, it contains the most recent 45 values. For all other objects, it contains the most recent 20 values. The table has a row for each historical property value. The current value of a property is determined by the most recent UPDATEDAT timestamp in the property’s history.

Association queries

Like objects data, associations data is organized in two ways:

  • Individual: each association type is stored in its own table and contains only records of that type. For example, associations_contacts_to_deals contains only association records between contact and deal objects. T
  • Combined: all records for all association types are combined into one table.
associations_x_to_y

Each association type has its own view, labeled as associations_&lt;association type name> e.g. associations_contacts_to_deals.

association_definitions

This table contains information about all of the available association types between HubSpot objects, with one row per association type.

property_definitions

This table contains information about object properties and event properties in your HubSpot account. Event properties include standard events, such as email opens and clicks, and custom behavioral event properties. This information can be helpful for defining values found in object_properties and events data.

Events

Events include standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events. Each event has its own table, labeled as events_eventname.

object_and_event_type_definitions

This table contains definitions for all objects and events available in your HubSpot account.

Sync frequency and data organization

Data syncs daily between HubSpot and AWS S3. A folder will be created for each day that the data is synced. Each of the following tables will be available as a folder with gzipped CSV files:

ASSOCIATIONS

OBJECT_PROPERTIES_HISTORY

OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES

OWNERS

OWNER_TEAM

PIPELINES

PIPELINE_STAGES

PROPERTY_DEFINITIONS

TEAMS

There will be several subfolders for each table. If the size of the table exceeds 15 MB, there will be multiple gzipped CSV files under each table folder.

Sync deals between HubSpot and Salesforce

Use the updated deal object sync to connect HubSpot deals with Salesforce opportunities and control how records, pipelines, properties, and associations sync between both platforms.

For example, you can map a Salesforce opportunity record type to an existing HubSpot deal pipeline, then control which opportunities are eligible to sync and how matching records are identified.

The updated deal sync also supports configurable pipeline mappings, deal deduplication, deal merges, association sync, sync conflict rules, and selective sync.

Before you get started

Before using the updated deal sync, please note the following:

  • The Salesforce integration must be connected to your HubSpot account.
  • Once you switch to the updated deal sync, you cannot revert to the standard deal sync experience. It’s recommended to test the updated deal sync in a developer test account or sandbox account before turning it on in a production account.
  • When you turn on the updated deal sync, this may temporarily increase Salesforce API usage as the new sync indexes records. Once indexing is complete, API usage will return to normal.
  • Existing pipeline mappings will be migrated to the updated deal sync automatically. You don’t need to recreate existing mappings after turning on the updated sync.
  • Only deals in HubSpot pipelines mapped to Salesforce opportunity record types are eligible to sync between HubSpot and Salesforce.
  • Deal merges in HubSpot do not merge records in Salesforce.

Turn on the updated deal sync

To turn on the updated deal sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Search for and select Salesforce.

  • Click the Feature discovery tab.

  • On the New Deal Sync card, click Enable.

  • In the dialog box, click Enable.

After you turn on the updated deal sync, existing deal sync settings and pipeline mappings will be migrated automatically. Deal and opportunity records will continue syncing based on your configured sync settings.

Understand how the updated deal sync works

The updated deal sync includes the core syncing behavior of the standard deal sync. It also provides additional controls for pipeline mappings, deal deduplication, deal merges, association sync, sync rules, selective sync, and inclusion segments.

Pipeline mappings

With the updated deal sync, you can manage your pipeline settings, by mapping the record types in Salesforce to the corresponding deals pipelines in Hubspot. This lets you control which pipeline an opportunity syncs to in HubSpot and which Salesforce record type a HubSpot deal syncs to.

Existing mappings from the standard deal sync are migrated automatically when you turn on the updated deal sync. After migration, you can review and edit these mappings in your Salesforce integration settings.

To manage pipeline mappings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Data sync tab.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Deals > Pipeline mappings.
  • For each HubSpot object pipeline, click the Salesforce record type dropdown menu, then select the Salesforce record type to map to that HubSpot pipeline.
  • Click Save.
Association sync

Control which associations sync between HubSpot deals and Salesforce opportunities. You can configure which associations sync between HubSpot and Salesforce, which association labels to use, and the sync direction (Two-way sync, Salesforce to HubSpot only, or HubSpot to Salesforce only).

To configure the association sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Data sync tab.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Deals > Associations.
  • Click to toggle the associations you want to sync between Salesforce and HubSpot.
  • Click the Primary association field dropdown menu and select the field you want HubSpot to use to associate the two objects.
  • Click the Association label dropdown menu and select the association label you want to use.
  • Click the Sync direction dropdown menu and select how you want the association to sync between HubSpot and Salesforce (Two-way sync, Salesforce to HubSpot only, or HubSpot to Salesforce only).
Deal deduplication

Deals can be deduplicated based on mapped field values. For records to match, the mapped field values must be identical in both HubSpot and Salesforce.

For example, if the Order Number property is mapped between HubSpot and Salesforce, deal records with the same order number will be mapped and synced.

Existing matched records aren’t affected when you configure the deal deduplication logic. The deduplication settings apply when new deal and opportunity records are matched moving forward, after the updated deal sync is turned on.

Learn more about setting up deduplication using field mapping.

Deal sync rules

Control what happens to deals and opportunities when records are created, updated, or deleted in HubSpot and Salesforce.

To manage these settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Search for and select Salesforce.

  • Click the Data sync tab.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Deals > Sync rules.

    • For creating and updating records, configure the sync direction between HubSpot and Salesforce:
      • Salesforce to HubSpot: select what happens in HubSpot when a Salesforce opportunity is created or updated.
      • HubSpot to Salesforce: select what happens in Salesforce when a HubSpot deal is created or updated.
    • For deleted records, configure what happens in HubSpot when a Salesforce opportunity is deleted:
      • Salesforce to HubSpot: select whether the corresponding HubSpot deal is deleted when a Salesforce opportunity is deleted.
      • HubSpot to Salesforce: when a HubSpot deal is deleted, the corresponding Salesforce opportunity is not deleted. This setting cannot be edited.
Sync conflict rule

When a HubSpot deal matches a Salesforce opportunity for the first time, you can select which data source should be used if it’s unclear which record contains the most up-to-date information.

The sync conflict rule only applies when records first sync.

To set up a sync conflict rule:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Data sync tab.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Deals > Sync rules.
  • Click the Resolve sync conflict rule dropdown menu and select the app that should be used to resolve any conflicts.
  • Click Save.
Deal field mapping sync rules

Existing sync rules from the standard deal sync remain available. Additional field mapping sync rules, Always use HubSpot and Use HubSpot unless blank, lets you sync data from HubSpot to Salesforce for a field mapping.

Please note: the sync rule feature only applies when using a two-way object-level sync rule. If a one-way object-level sync rule is selected, the value is overridden in the one-way direction.

Deal merges

Deal merges are supported in HubSpot.

When two HubSpot deal records are merged:

  • After merging the HubSpot records, the resulting record continues syncing with the Salesforce record that matches the selected salesforceobjectid value. To control which Salesforce record continues syncing with the resulting HubSpot record, select the corresponding salesforceobjectid value as the winning value during the merge.
  • Salesforce records are not merged automatically.
Selective sync

Use selective sync to control which Salesforce opportunities are eligible to sync from Salesforce to HubSpot. Only opportunities that meet your configured filter criteria will sync to HubSpot.

To set up selective sync for deals:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Search for and select Salesforce.
  • Click the Data sync tab.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Deals > Sync rules.
  • In the Selective Sync section, click Add filter.
  • In the right panel, click the Field dropdown menu and select a field.
  • Configure the filter criteria, then click Save and apply filter.
  • Add additional filters as needed. Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.
  • Toggle the selective sync switch on.
  • Click Save.
Limit which HubSpot deals sync to Salesforce

Use an inclusion segment to control which HubSpot deals are eligible to sync to Salesforce.

When an inclusion segment is selected, only HubSpot deals that meet the segment criteria are eligible to sync to Salesforce.

Learn how to set up an inclusion segment.

Sync HubSpot data to Amazon S3

Use the Amazon S3 integration to sync HubSpot CRM data to an Amazon S3 bucket that you own. You can choose which objects, associations, and events to sync, configure a recurring sync schedule, and monitor sync status from within HubSpot.

Each sync exports a full snapshot of the selected data in Parquet format to your Amazon S3 bucket. You can then use the synced data with analytics and data processing tools, such as AWS Glue, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, Spark, Databricks, or Python notebooks.

Please note: the Amazon S3 integration is available to new Amazon S3 users who are not using the legacy Amazon S3 integration. If you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the new Amazon S3 integration beta.

Before you get started

Before you begin syncing data to Amazon S3, review the following requirements and limitations.

Understand requirements
  • If you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Amazon S3 integration beta.
  • You must create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role associated with your HubSpot account.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • During beta, data is synced only in Parquet format.
  • Each sync creates a complete snapshot of the selected data.
  • HubSpot creates a new folder for each sync and doesn’t delete previous syncs from your S3 bucket.
  • Sensitive Data isn’t supported to sync.

Create the IAM role in AWS

To configure access permissions for HubSpot in the AWS Management Console:

  • Log into the AWS Management Console.

  • On the home dashboard, click Services > Security, Identity, & Compliance > IAM.

  • On the left sidebar, click Roles.

  • Click Create role.

  • In the Trusted entity type section, select your AWS account.

  • In the AWS account section, select Another AWS account and enter your own AWS account ID. You’ll later change the trust relationship to give access to HubSpot.

  • Select Require external ID and input a placeholder ID like 0000. You’ll later change the trust relationship for your IAM role and specify the external ID for your storage integration. An external ID is used to grant access to your AWS resources to a third-party app like HubSpot.

  • Click Next.

  • In the Role details section, enter a Role name and Description to identify the role.

  • Click Create role.

  • On the Summary page, copy the ARN value. You will use this value in the next step.

Connect HubSpot and AWS S3

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select Amazon S3.
  • Click Install.
  • Select your AWS IAM role, then click Install.
  • Click Next.
  • Enter the ARN value from the AWS IAM role in the Role ARN field.
  • Click Connect to Amazon S3.

Configure bucket permissions

HubSpot needs the following permissions on an AWS S3 bucket and folder to access files in the folder and sub-folders:

  • s3:GetBucketLocation
  • s3:GetObject
  • s3:GetObjectVersion
  • s3:ListBucket
  • s3:PutObject
  • s3:DeleteObject

After connecting the app, grant HubSpot permission to sync data to your S3 bucket.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Amazon S3.

  • In the right panel, click Select for the Amazon S3 account you want to sync data to.

  • On the Permissions page, click Copy to copy the example permission policy and attach it to the AWS IAM role you created earlier. Please note to update the permission policy with your bucket names.

  • Log into the AWS Management Console.

  • On the home dashboard, click Services > Security, Identity, & Compliance > IAM.

  • On the left sidebar, click Account settings.

  • In the Security Token Service (STS) section, look for the AWS region that corresponds to the region your AWS account is located in. Click to toggle the switch on to activate the region.

  • On the left side panel, click Policies.

  • Click Create policy.

  • On the JSON tab, click Add new statement.

  • Add the policy you copied in Step 4 that will give HubSpot the permissions it needs to load or unload data using a single bucket and folder path.

Please note:

  • Make sure to replace <bucket> and <prefix> with your actual bucket name and folder path prefix. The Amazon Resource Names (ARN) for buckets in government regions have an arn:aws-us-gov:s3::: prefix.

  • Setting the s3:prefix condition to either [“*”] or [“<path> /*”] grants access to all prefixes in the specified bucket or path in the bucket respectively.

  • Click Next.

  • In the Review and create section, add the Policy name and an optional description.

  • Click Create policy.

Configure the destination bucket

  • Back on the Permissions page in HubSpot, in the Bucket field, enter the bucket name.

  • Click Test connection.

  • If the connection test is successful, click Next.

Configure the sync

  • On the Data source page, select the data that you want to sync.

  • Select the checkboxes for the objects, associations, and events you want to sync from HubSpot to Amazon S3.

  • Click Next.

  • On the Details page, click the Sync frequency dropdown menu and select the frequency that you want data to sync from HubSpot to Amazon S3.

  • Click Start sync.

Manage the sync

After setting up a sync and data starts syncing from HubSpot to Amazon S3, you can review its status, identify errors, update settings, or archive the sync.

To review and manage the sync:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Integration. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration directly.

  • Navigate to the App syncs tab and locate your Amazon S3 sync in the table.

  • Review the sync status:

    • Syncing: a sync run is in progress.
    • Synced: the last sync completed successfully.
    • Failed: the last sync encountered an error.
    • Archived: the sync configuration was removed.

  • Click the sync name to view more details, including successfully synced and failed records.

To edit or remove a sync:

  • In the table, click the Amazon S3 sync.

  • In the top right, click the Actions dropdown menu, then select one of the following:

    • Edit sync: update the sync settings.
    • Archive sync: delete the sync configuration.

Data format for syncing between HubSpot and Amazon S3

Available data for syncing

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to AWS S3:

  • Objects: standard and custom objects, such as contacts, companies, tickets, or products.
  • Records: individual object records.
  • Properties: properties and their values on the object records, including the property history.
  • Associations: all association types and associated records.
  • Events: selected standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events, including selected event properties.

Object data of different types are organized and available in two ways:

  • Individual: each object type is stored in its own table and has only records of the same object type. For example, objects_contacts contains only contact records.
  • Combined: all records for all object types are combined into one database object. Thus, when querying, you need to specify a filter like “WHERE objectTypeId=’0-1’

Custom objects will be assigned an ID at the time of creation, and will be identified as 2-unique_ID. For example, 2-12345.

S3 folder structure

HubSpot writes each successful sync to a HubSpot-managed prefix in your Amazon S3 bucket using the following structure:

s3://&lt;bucket-name>/hubspot-dataout/&lt;account-id>/&lt;run-id>/&lt;table-name>/&lt;file-name>

For example:

s3://my-company-hubspot-data/hubspot-dataout/12345678/98765/OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES/part-000.parquet

s3://my-company-hubspot-data/hubspot-dataout/12345678/98765/EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE/part-000.parquet

s3://my-company-hubspot-data/hubspot-dataout/12345678/98765/ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES/part-000.parquet

Each sync creates a new run-id folder. HubSpot doesn’t delete data from previous sync runs.

If you want to automatically remove older sync, configure an Amazon S3 lifecycle policy for the bucket or prefix.

HubSpot generates file names for each sync run, and file names may differ between sync runs. Don’t configure downstream processes to depend on specific file names. Instead, read all files in the appropriate table-name folder for the export run that you want to process.

Sync Microsoft Teams Meeting Recordings and Transcripts to HubSpot

After connecting the Microsoft Teams app to your HubSpot account, you can automatically sync Microsoft Teams data to HubSpot, including:

  • Automatically sync Microsoft Teams-generated meeting video recordings and transcripts to HubSpot.
  • Sync participant data to existing contact records in HubSpot.
  • Create new contact records for meeting attendees who aren’t already in the CRM.
  • Access Microsoft Teams meeting transcripts, recordings, and summaries on meeting records.
  • Quickly preview Microsoft Teams meeting recordings and transcripts on associated records.
  • Use Conversation Intelligence (CI) to further analyze your Microsoft Teams meeting transcripts (Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise only).

Please note: starting Aug. 31, 2026, Microsoft Teams meeting recordings and transcripts are stored on the meeting record instead of the call record. Learn more about this change.

Before you get started

Make sure you have connected the admin-level install version of Microsoft Teams to your HubSpot account. If you’ve connected the user-level install option, uninstall the app, and install the admin-level install option.

Please note: for meeting recordings and transcripts to sync to HubSpot, the meeting must have a corresponding calendar event in Microsoft Teams or Microsoft Outlook. If there’s no calendar event, HubSpot cannot retrieve the recording and transcript data.

To sync Microsoft Teams meeting recordings and transcripts to HubSpot, follow the steps below to set up PowerShell, grant permissions to users, and configure Transcript API access.

Set up PowerShell and connect to Microsoft Teams

If you have already set up an application access policy via PowerShell for Microsoft Teams webinar sync to HubSpot, you can skip this step.

  • Follow the instructions in this article to install PowerShell in your operating system.

  • Open PowerShell in your system:

    • Mac: open Terminal and run pwsh to launch PowerShell.
    • Windows: search for “PowerShell” in the Start menu, then click Run as administrator.

  • Run Connect-MicrosoftTeams in PowerShell and click Enter. If you haven’t installed the Teams PowerShell module, learn how to install the module.

Grant permissions to users

Follow the instructions in this article to grant permissions to a set of users:

  • Run the following command in PowerShell to create an access policy: New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity MY-APP-POLICY -AppIds "0493df14-0cd5-4c89-b413-e0b9b90bbb17" -Description "MY APP POLICY DESCRIPTION".

  • To grant permissions to selected users , run the following command: Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName MY-APP-POLICY -Identity "USER_ID”.

    • To get a user ID, click a specific user in the Microsoft admin center. The user ID will be in the page URL.
    • You must run this command for each individual user.

  • To grant permissions to all existing users, run the following command: Get-CsOnlineUser | Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName MY-APP-POLICY.

  • To grant permissions to all existing and future users at once, run the following command: Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName MY-APP-POLICY-2 -Global.

Please note:

  • If you already have an existing application-level policy and want the same permission structure to be applied to HubSpot, add the HubSpot App ID to the policy.
  • You can assign only one application access policy at a time to a particular user. Assigning a new application access policy to a user will override any existing application access policy.
Configure Transcript API access

Before syncing Microsoft Teams transcripts to HubSpot, a Microsoft Teams admin must turn on Microsoft Graph access and Include Speaker Attribution in the Microsoft Teams admin center. Both settings are required for transcript sync to work. If either setting is turned off, transcripts won’t sync to HubSpot even if the other Microsoft Teams sync settings are configured. Learn how to configure Microsoft Teams transcript API access.

Manage Microsoft Teams meeting sync settings

Configure your HubSpot account’s meeting sync settings and decide how meeting recordings and transcripts sync from Microsoft Teams to HubSpot.

Manage global Microsoft Teams meeting settings

To view and manage account-wide Microsoft Teams meeting settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Microsoft Teams. Then click the Settings tab.

  • Click the Meetings tab and then click the Global Settings tab.

  • In the Meetings section, toggle the Sync meeting data switch on to sync meeting data for all future meetings from Microsoft Teams to HubSpot.

  • In the Sync meeting recordings and transcripts section, choose from the following options:

    • Don’t sync meeting recordings and transcripts for Microsoft Teams users on this account: meeting recordings and transcripts will not be synced to HubSpot. However, meetings will still log as activities on the HubSpot contact records of the participants.

    • Sync meeting recordings and transcripts for ALL Microsoft Teams users on this account: meetings will be automatically logged, meeting recordings and transcripts will be synced to HubSpot for all users on the Microsoft tenant.

    • Sync meeting recordings and transcripts for SELECTED Microsoft Teams users on this account: admins can choose the specific users for whom meeting recordings and transcripts should be synced to HubSpot.

  • In the Exclusions section, add domains to prevent meetings from being synced to HubSpot by users in the meeting invitee list who have a particular email address domain. You can also prevent new contact records from being created for internal employees.

    • In the Recording exclusions section, click Enter domain or choose from list.
    • In the Contact exclusions section, enter your company’s domain name to prevent internal employees from being created as new contacts in HubSpot.
Manage personal Microsoft Teams meeting settings

If you’re a Microsoft Teams user, you can also manage your individual Meetings settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Microsoft Teams. Then click the Settings tab.

  • Click the Meetings tab.

  • On the My settings tab, in the Meetings section, choose whether you want to sync meeting recordings and transcripts:

    • Don’t sync meeting recordings and transcripts: this option won’t sync any meeting recordings or transcripts to HubSpot. However, meetings will still log as activities on the HubSpot contact records of the participants.
    • Sync meeting recordings and transcripts: this option will automatically log meetings and sync meeting recordings and transcripts to HubSpot.

  • In the Manage individual meetings section, you can search meetings by Meeting ID that you’re the organizer of. You can find the Microsoft Teams Meeting ID in the meeting invite. Then click Sync meeting to sync the meeting data to HubSpot.

Troubleshoot Microsoft Teams meetings not syncing

If your Microsoft Teams meetings aren’t syncing after turning on the sync, the likely cause is that they aren’t generating attendance reports in your Microsoft Teams tenant. To sync to HubSpot, Microsoft Teams meetings must generate an attendance report.

A Microsoft Teams admin must update the meeting policy in the Microsoft Teams Admin Center:

  • Navigate to the Microsoft Teams Admin Center.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Meetings > Meeting policies.
  • Select the policy you’d like to update, such as the global organization-wide policy or a custom policy assigned to meeting organizers.
  • Navigate to the Meeting scheduling section.
  • Locate the setting Attendance and engagement report or Allow attendance report, and set the value to On.
  • Click Save to apply the changes.

View Microsoft Teams meeting recordings and transcripts

Once a Microsoft Teams meeting has ended, a meeting record will be created in your HubSpot account. The meeting record will contain both the meeting video recording and transcript.

To view the meeting transcript and video recording:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to CRM > Meetings.
  • Click the title of the meeting.
  • Review the Microsoft Teams-generated meeting transcript and video recording.

If you’re a user with an assigned Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat, you can use Conversation Intelligence (CI) to analyze your Microsoft Teams meeting transcripts.

The meeting record will be logged on the contact record of meeting attendees. The logged meeting will show the meeting date, the participants, and a link to the recording. To review the meeting recording and transcript, click Review recording.

If a contact record for a meeting attendee doesn’t exist in HubSpot yet, a new contact record will be created.

Contact record and timeline events will not be created or updated if the participant’s email address:

  • Is a user email address in your account.
  • Has a domain that is excluded in the Microsoft Teams integration settings.

Sync records between HubSpot and Salesforce

With the Salesforce integration, you can create and use inclusion segments to control which records sync from HubSpot to Salesforce.

Inclusion segments define which records are eligible to sync from HubSpot to Salesforce based on specific criteria. Records that aren’t in your segment won’t sync between HubSpot and Salesforce.

For example, you can create an inclusion segment to sync only companies in a specific lifecycle stage, or only tickets with a defined status.

To limit what records sync from Salesforce to HubSpot, learn more about using selective sync.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with inclusion segments, make sure you understand how they affect your Salesforce sync behavior.

  • You can use inclusion segments when syncing contacts, companies (after upgrading to the new company sync), deals (after upgrading to the new deal sync), tickets, and custom objects.
  • Only active segments can be set as your Salesforce inclusion segment, as they will update dynamically as records meet or don’t meet your segment criteria.
  • Selecting a segment as your inclusion segment will not automatically sync the segment with Salesforce. Members of the segment will only sync with Salesforce when a sync is triggered. Learn how to manually resync a segment with Salesforce.
  • If new or existing Salesforce leads or contacts are set to automatically create HubSpot contacts in your integration settings, a new contact will be created or an existing contact will be synced in HubSpot when a Salesforce lead or contact is created, even if the HubSpot contact is not in your inclusion segment. Further updates to the contact or lead from either HubSpot or Salesforce will not sync to the other platform until they meet the segment criteria.
  • In rare cases, when a property update changes a record’s inclusion segment membership, a record update may sync before the inclusion segment is re-evaluated.
