      • HubSpot workflow actions that relate to Salesforce will remain in your workflow, but won’t execute.

  • In the text field, type uninstall. Then click Uninstall.

Reassign contacts, companies, and deals to HubSpot owners

If you have any contacts, companies, and deals in HubSpot that were previously assigned to Salesforce-only users, they must be reassigned to HubSpot owners. You’ll receive an email from HubSpot with the subject: Reassign your contacts, companies, and deals to HubSpot owners.

  • In the email, follow the instructions to identify contacts, companies, and deals currently owned by Salesforce-only users and reassign them to a HubSpot owner.

  • After reassigning your records, click Go to Owner cleanup page.

  • You’ll be redirected to the Salesforce integration owner cleanup page in HubSpot. In the upper right, click Remove Salesforce owners.

  • In the dialog box, click Got it.

Uninstall the HubSpot integration package in Salesforce

  • Navigate to your Salesforce account.

    • Salesforce Classic:
      • In the upper right, click Setup (or [Your Name] > Setup).
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Build > Lightning Bolt > Installed Packages.
    • Lightning Experience:
      • In the upper right, click the settings gear icon and select settings Setup.
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Platform Tools > Apps > Packaging > Installed Packages.

  • Locate the HubSpot Integration package. In the Action column, click Uninstall.

  • On the next screen, you’ll see a list of all the package components and custom objects that’ll be deleted when you uninstall. You’ll also see any customizations, data, reports, and relationships associated with them.

  • Select Save a copy of this package’s data for 48 hours after uninstall or Do not save a copy of this package’s data after uninstall.

Please note: if you choose not to save a copy of the package data during this step, you will not be able to access or retrieve it later.

  • Select the Yes, I want to uninstall this package and permanently delete all associated components checkbox.
  • Then click Uninstall.

Use app objects from your connected apps

Some apps on the HubSpot App Marketplace provide support for using objects from a third-party service directly within the various tools in your HubSpot account. These objects include custom schemas with app-specific fields like identifiers and timestamps, making integration data available and actionable throughout your account.

After you connect an app that supports app objects to your HubSpot account, the corresponding app objects will be available to use in your account. Learn more about the supported tools for app objects and how to access them in your account in the sections below.

Please note: if you’re a developer who’s interested in using app objects in your app, you can learn more in HubSpot’s developer documentation.

Supported tools

The following HubSpot tools currently support app objects:

  • App cards
  • Custom properties
  • Exports
  • Imports
  • Segments
  • Pipelines
  • Workflows

Some apps may offer support for syncing app object data based on events that occur in your HubSpot account (e.g., changing an app object property, creating a new app object record, or deleting an app object record).

Review records on the app objects index page

You can create new app object records and review any existing records on the index page:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • In the top left, click Contacts, then select [App object name].

  • Any existing app object records will appear in the list.

    • You can click the name of a record to navigate to the record page.
    • To create a new app object record, click Create [App object name] in the top right. Follow the prompts to provide the corresponding details for the new record.

Manage app object settings

To manage app object properties, existing associations, and pipelines, or customize the appearance of your app object record:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Objects > App Objects.

  • Click the Select an object dropdown menu, then select the app object.

  • On the Setup tab, manage the settings for record creation and app object properties:

    • Click Manage [App object name] properties to review the default properties for the app object, or create custom properties.
    • You can also click Customize the [App object name] form to make changes to the default record creation form used to create a new app object record from the index page.

  • Click the Associations tab to review existing associations for the app object. You cannot currently create new associations, configure labels, or set association limits.

  • Click the Pipelines tab to create and manage app object pipelines.

  • Click the Record customization tab to configure the app object record layout and content:

    • To change the default view for all users who aren’t on an assigned team:
      • Click Default view.
      • Create or update the cards or tabs that appear on the record.
      • Click Save in the top right to save your progress at any time, or click Save and exit to save your changes and leave the editor.
    • To create or edit a team view (Professional and Enterprise only):

      • Click Create team view or click the name of an existing team view.

      • At the top of the editor, enter a name for the view.

      • In the top right, click Assign teams to select the teams who will have access to the view. In the dialog box, select the checkboxes of the teams, then click Done.

      • Create or update the cards and tabs displayed on the record.

      • Click Save in the top right to save your progress, or click Save and exit to save your changes and leave the editor.

  • Click the Preview Customization tab to configure the sidebar preview that appears when previewing an app object record.

  • Click the Index Customization tab to configure the index page for existing app objects.

Create a segment of app object records

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • In the top right, click Create segment.
  • Under Create a segment of…, click to expand the Other objects section, then select [App object name].

Continue customizing your segment settings by following the steps in this article.

Create a workflow based on an app object

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the top right, click Create workflow, then select From scratch.
  • In the left panel, click Trigger manually.
  • Search for and select [App object name], then click Save and continue.

Continue to build your workflow by adding actions and configuring its corresponding settings.

Use Breeze Assistant in Slack

Use Breeze Assistant in Slack to search and summarize CRM records, analyze pipeline data, prepare for meetings, and create content using natural language. Breeze Assistant can display responses as formatted tables, CRM record and meeting cards, reports, and generated files, including presentations and CSVs.

For example, ask Breeze Assistant to identify deals without a scheduled next step, then review the results in a table directly in Slack. This helps you access and work with your HubSpot data directly in Slack without switching between tools.

To get started, mention Breeze Assistant in a Slack channel or thread, or send it a direct message from the Messages tab of the HubSpot app in Slack.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements
  • You must connect the Slack app to your HubSpot account and log in to Slack with your HubSpot user.
  • You must turn on Breeze Assistant in your HubSpot account.
  • To use Breeze Assistant from the Messages tab of the HubSpot app in Slack, a Slack workspace admin must reconnect the Slack app to HubSpot to grant the required permissions.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • In Slack channels and threads, Breeze Assistant only responds when it is explicitly @mentioned. You must @mention Breeze Assistant for each request.
  • Breeze Assistant does not monitor channels or threads automatically.
  • In direct conversations with Breeze Assistant from the Messages tab, you don’t need to @mention Breeze Assistant to start or continue a conversation.

Set your active HubSpot account

If your Slack workspace is connected to multiple HubSpot accounts, you must select which HubSpot account Breeze Assistant should use in Slack. If you only have one HubSpot account connected to Slack, you can skip this step.

  • In Slack, type the command /hs-breeze-select-portal and press Enter.
  • In the generated prompt, select the HubSpot account you want to use.

Breeze will use the selected HubSpot account for all future requests in this Slack workspace. If you need to switch HubSpot accounts in the future, you can run the same command again.

Use Breeze Assistant in the Messages tab

Use the Messages tab of the HubSpot app in Slack to start and continue a direct conversation with Breeze Assistant. Suggested prompts are also available to help you start common tasks.

  • In the left sidebar menu in Slack, navigate to the Agents and apps section.

  • Click HubSpot (Breeze).

  • On the Messages tab, select a suggested prompt or enter a message for Breeze Assistant.

  • Breeze Assistant will respond directly in the conversation.

  • To continue the conversation, enter another message. You don’t need to @mention Breeze Assistant in each message.

Use Breeze Assistant in Slack channels and threads

To use Breeze Assistant in a Slack channel or thread, explicitly @mention it each time you want it to respond.

  • In Slack, navigate to a channel or thread.

  • Type @HubSpot(Breeze) followed by your request.

  • Press Enter to send your message.

  • Breeze Assistant will display a thinking indicator. Then it’ll respond directly in the channel or thread.

For follow-up questions, @mention Breeze Assistant again and include your request. Breeze Assistant can use context from the surrounding channel or thread to help answer your question, but it doesn’t automatically monitor conversations.

Best practices for Breeze Assistant in Slack

  • Be specific: include record names, ticket numbers, or company names to help Breeze Assistant find the relevant record.
  • Use natural language: describe what you want in plain language. You don’t need to use exact field names or API syntax.
  • Ask follow-up questions: @mention Breeze Assistant for each follow-up request and include enough context for Breeze Assistant to understand the request.
  • Combine actions: you can include multiple actions in a single request. For example, Summarize the Acme Corp deal and create a task to follow up by Friday.

What Breeze Assistant can do in Slack

Breeze Assistant works with standard CRM objects, including contacts, companies, deals, and tickets, as well as custom objects, tasks, notes, meetings, and emails. Use Breeze Assistant in Slack to search, summarize, create, and update records, analyze data, search HubSpot documentation, and complete other HubSpot tasks without leaving Slack.

When you ask Breeze Assistant questions or request content in Slack, responses can include formatted tables, CRM record cards, meeting cards, reports, and generated files. The response format depends on your request.

Below are example prompts that you can use with Breeze Assistant in Slack.

Summarize CRM records

Summarize contact, company, deal, or ticket records. Breeze Assistant will retrieve the latest data and return a concise overview.

  • Summarize a deal:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Summarize the deal with Acme Corp
  • Check ticket status:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s the latest on ticket #4521?
  • Review a company record:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Give me an overview of the Delta Airlines company record
  • Get context on a contact:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What should I know before my call with Lexie Wingham?
Analyze CRM data

Ask Breeze Assistant to identify records that meet specific criteria or summarize data from your HubSpot account.

For example, use the following prompts:

  • Identify deals requiring follow-up:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Which of my deals have no next step scheduled?
  • Review pipeline data:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) How many open deals over $50,000 do we have in EMEA?
  • Find inactive accounts:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Build me a list of accounts with no activity in 90 days.

Breeze Assistant can display matching records and summarized results in formatted tables, with CRM record cards when relevant.

Create and update CRM records

Create new records or update existing ones, including properties, owners, and associations, for all CRM objects. You can also request bulk changes to multiple records.

  • Create a new contact:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Create a new contact: John Smith, john@acme.com, CEO at Acme
  • Update a deal stage:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Update the Acme Corp deal stage to “Closed Won”
  • Update a record owner:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Assign the Delta Airlines deal to Sarah Chen
  • Create a custom object record:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Create a new Project record for “Phoenix” with status “In Progress” and link it to the Acme Corp company
  • Reassign records in bulk:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Reassign all of Sarah’s accounts to Mike

When you request a CRM update, Breeze Assistant displays a confirmation card with the proposed changes. For bulk updates, the card lists all affected records so you can review the changes before they’re applied.

Enroll records into workflows

Enroll records into existing workflows by asking Breeze Assistant in Slack. Include the record and workflow name in your request.

For example, use the following prompts:

  • Enroll a contact:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Enroll John Smith into the sales-to-CS handoff workflow
  • Enroll a company:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Enroll Acme Corp into the customer onboarding workflow
Create and update tickets

Create tickets, update ticket properties, change statuses, and assign owners.

  • Create a ticket:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Create a ticket for Acme Corp: “Billing discrepancy on Q3 invoice”, priority high
  • Change ticket status:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Change ticket #4521 status to “Waiting on Customer”
  • Assign a ticket:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Assign ticket #4521 to Sarah Chen
  • Link a ticket to another record:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Associate ticket #4521 with the Acme Corp deal
Create tasks and log notes

Create tasks or log notes on CRM records from Slack.

  • Create a follow-up task:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Create a task to follow up with Sandy by Friday
  • Log a note on a deal:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Log a note on the Roku deal: discussed expanding to Asia
  • Summarize a thread and save it:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Summarize this thread and add a note to Delta Airlines’ record
Analyze your pipeline

Ask Breeze Assistant to run counts, totals, comparisons, and trends across your CRM data.

  • Count records by stage:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) How many open deals do I have in the “Proposal” stage?
  • Summarize deal volume by rep:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Show me all deals closed last month by rep, grouped by stage
  • Calculate pipeline value:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s the total pipeline value for deals closing this quarter?
  • Compare time periods:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Compare deal volume this quarter vs last quarter
Analyze revenue and pipeline health

Ask Breeze Assistant for forecasts, win/loss trends, rep performance, deal velocity, and at-risk pipeline.

  • Forecast against quota:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) How are we tracking against our Q4 revenue target?
  • Win/loss analysis:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What were our top 3 win reasons and top 3 loss reasons last quarter
  • Deal velocity and sales cycle:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s our average sales cycle length for deals closed this quarter vs last quarter?
  • Identify at-risk pipeline:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Show me all deals in the “Proposal” stage that haven’t been updated in 14 days
  • Rep performance comparison:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Rank my reps by closed-won revenue this quarter
  • Pipeline coverage:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Do we have enough pipeline coverage to hit next quarter’s target
  • Stalled deals:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Which deals have been in the same stage for more than 30 days?
Analyze marketing performance

Ask Breeze Assistant about campaign effectiveness, lead generation, funnel conversion, and marketing attribution.

  • Campaign ROI:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s the ROI on our “Spring Webinar” campaign?
  • Lead source effectiveness:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Which lead sources produced the most closed-won deals this quarter?
  • Funnel conversion rates:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s our lead-to-customer conversion rate this month?
  • Top-performing campaigns:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Rank our active campaigns by deals influenced
  • MQL to SQL conversion:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What percentage of MQLs converted to SQLs last quarter?
  • Channel comparison:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Compare deal volume from organic vs paid channels this quarter
Monitor customer health and churn risk

Identify at-risk accounts, track customer engagement, and surface expansion opportunities.

  • At-risk customers:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Which customers have open high-priority tickets with no activity in 7 days?
  • Expansion opportunities:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Show me customers whose deal value increased by more than 20% this year
  • Churn signals:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) List customers whose last engagement was more than 60 days ago
  • NPS and satisfaction:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s our average NPS score this quarter, and which accounts have the lowest scores?
  • Renewal pipeline:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Show me all contracts renewing in the next 90 days with no active engagement
Search across records

Search across objects, associations, and build filtered lists.

  • Find associated records:

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Show me all contacts associated with the Acme Corp company

  • Find records by association:

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Which deals are associated with ticket #4521?

  • Filter across objects:

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) List all open tickets for companies in the “Enterprise” tier

  • Search communications:

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What was the last email sent to Acme Corp?

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Show me recent communications with Delta Airlines

Create meetings and prepare for meetings

Ask Breeze Assistant to create meetings or gather context before a scheduled meeting. When preparing for meetings, Breeze Assistant summarizes relevant CRM data and recent activities.

  • Create a meeting:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Create a meeting with the Acme Corp prospect tomorrow at 9:00 AM for a demo
  • Prepare for a scheduled meeting:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Prep me for my 2pm with Uniqlo
  • Get context on a contact:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What should I know before my call with Lexie Wingham?
Log calls

Log calls on CRM records by describing the call to Breeze Assistant in Slack. Include the relevant record and call details in your request.

For example, use the following prompts:

  • Log a call:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Log a call with John Smith about the Acme Corp renewal
  • Log call notes:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Log a call with John Smith and note that we discussed renewal pricing.
Generate content

Ask Breeze Assistant to create presentation content based on CRM information.

  • For example, enter the following prompt:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Create a proposal deck for the Acme opportunity

Review the generated presentation in the Slack response.

Search HubSpot documentation

Ask Breeze Assistant to search HubSpot Knowledge Base articles, Academy content, Marketplace listings, and pricing documentation.

  • Find a HubSpot Knowledge Base article:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) How do I set up a custom report in HubSpot?
  • Check plan details:
  • @HubSpot(Breeze) What’s included in the Sales Hub Professional plan?
Summarize Slack threads

Summarize conversations in Slack threads where Breeze Assistant is present.

  • Summarize a thread

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Summarize this thread

  • Summarize and save to CRM

  • @HubSpot(Breeze) Summarize this thread and log it as a note on the Acme deal

Please note: you must @mention Breeze Assistant each time you want it to summarize or take action on a conversation. Breeze Assistant can use the available channel or thread context, but it does not automatically monitor conversations.

Use Google Meet with HubSpot meetings

Automatically add a Google Meet link to meetings scheduled in your HubSpot account. With the Google Meet app, you can include a conferencing link for every meeting booked through your HubSpot Smart CRM, making it easy to connect with your contacts.

Use HubSpot’s integration with Google Meet to add Google Meet links to meetings scheduled from HubSpot and keep meeting activity connected to your CRM. After connecting the Google Meet app, you can add meeting links to scheduling pages or manually scheduled meetings and log meetings to the associated HubSpot records.

This helps you manage customer conversations and meeting information in one place without manually updating records after each meeting.

Please note: starting Aug. 31, 2026, Microsoft Teams meeting recordings and transcripts are stored on the meeting record instead of the call record. Learn more about this change.

Before you get started

Permissions required You must have App Marketplace permissions or be a Super Admin in your HubSpot account to install the Google Meet app.

  • Google Meet is a user-level app and must be installed individually by each user. Each user must have App Marketplace permissions to install and connect the Google Meet app. If a user cannot connect the app, an admin must grant the required permissions before the user can try again.
  • Meeting links are generated only for meetings booked with a connected Google Calendar.
  • HubSpot creates a private, secondary (shadow) calendar in your Google account to manage meeting links and events. You won’t see this in your primary Google Calendar, and it doesn’t affect existing meetings or calendar syncing.

Connect the Google Meet app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select the Google Meet app.
  • Click Install.
  • In the dialog box, sign in to your Google account.
  • Click Continue. Then review the requested permissions and click Allow.
  • You’ll be redirected back to HubSpot.

Add a Google Meet link to HubSpot meetings

You can use the Google Meet app to send meeting links to your contacts and log the meetings in your HubSpot account.

Add Google Meet to a meeting scheduling page

  • Connect your calendar to HubSpot.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Sales > Meetings Scheduler. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Sales > Meetings Scheduler directly.

  • Hover over the scheduling page you want to update, then click Edit.

  • Under Location, click Add videoconference link, then select Google Meet.

  • In the bottom left, click Save. Meeting links will be created in the default language set in your HubSpot account.

Please note: the above steps will add a Google Meet URL to the Location field of your Google meeting, but it won’t include the Join with Google Meet button.

Schedule a meeting with a Google Meet link manually

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to your contacts, companies, deals, or tickets.

  • Click the name of the record.

  • In the left sidebar, click meetings Schedule a meeting. In the Schedule pop-up window, set up your meeting.

  • To input a Google Meet link, click the Select location dropdown menu.

  • Click Google Meet.

  • A Google Meet link will be generated for the meeting.

Update HubSpot records from a Google Meet meeting

During a Google Meet meeting, you can:

  • Retrieve existing HubSpot contact records for meeting participants.
  • Create new contact records.
  • Associate the meeting with relevant HubSpot records.
  • Add notes to HubSpot contact records.
  • Use HubSpot Playbooks.

To set up the HubSpot app for Google Meet:

  • Install the Google Meet app.

  • To add the HubSpot app to Google Meet meetings:

    • Click the Meeting tools button at the bottom of the meeting screen.

    • Click the HubSpot for Google Meet icon. Then log in with your Google credentials and accept the Google terms.

  • Once the app has been added:

    • In the Participants tab, view all participants in the meeting. Participants are automatically mapped to their HubSpot contact record, if both their First Name and Last Name match the corresponding properties in HubSpot. If any participants aren’t automatically mapped, click Map next to their name to associate them to an existing HubSpot contact record or create a new one.

    • In the Associations tab, view and map any HubSpot records to this meeting from your records (e.g., contact, company, deal, ticket, etc).

    • In the Comments tab, take notes and make comments during the meeting. The note will be saved to the relevant associated records in HubSpot.

    • In the Playbooks tab, access any relevant HubSpot playbooks to guide your conversation during the call. You can also add information to the playbook to be automatically synced into HubSpot (Sales Hub and Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only).

Once the Google Meet meeting has ended, a meeting record will be created on the meetings index page in your HubSpot account. The meeting record will contain the recording and any notes taken during the meeting. The meeting record will also be logged on the contact record of meeting attendees.

Sync Google Meet recordings

If you have a Google Meet Business or Enterprise account, you can sync your Google Meet recordings to review to HubSpot. Learn more about syncing Google Meet recordings.

Use HubSpot and Microsoft Teams webinars

After connecting HubSpot and Microsoft Teams, you can sync webinar registration and attendance data from Microsoft Teams webinars to HubSpot. This lets you track webinar engagement alongside your CRM data and use registration and attendance information to segment contacts and automate follow-up actions. For example, you can enroll webinar registrants in workflows or create lists based on who registered for or attended a webinar.

Before you get started

Make sure you have connected the admin-level install version of Microsoft Teams to your HubSpot account. If you connected the user-level install version, learn more about how to switch to the admin-level install.

To sync Microsoft Teams webinar information to HubSpot marketing events, follow the steps below to set up PowerShell, connect to Microsoft Teams, and grant permissions to users.

Set up PowerShell and connect to Microsoft Teams

  • Follow the instructions in this article to install PowerShell in your operating system. If you already have PowerShell installed, you can skip this step.

  • Open PowerShell in your system:

    • Mac: open Terminal and run pwsh to launch PowerShell.
    • Windows: search for “PowerShell” in the Start menu, then click Run as administrator.

  • Run Connect-MicrosoftTeams in PowerShell and click Enter. If you haven’t installed the Teams PowerShell module, learn how to install the module.

Grant permissions to users

Follow the instructions in this article to grant permissions to a set of users:

  • Run the following command in PowerShell to create an access policy: New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity MY-APP-POLICY -AppIds "0493df14-0cd5-4c89-b413-e0b9b90bbb17" -Description "MY APP POLICY DESCRIPTION".

  • To grant permissions to selected users , run the following command: Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName MY-APP-POLICY -Identity "USER_ID”.

    • To get a user ID, click a specific user in the Microsoft admin center. The user ID will be in the page URL.
    • You must run this command for each individual user.

  • To grant permissions to all existing users, run the following command: Get-CsOnlineUser | Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName MY-APP-POLICY.

  • To grant permissions to all existing and future users at once, run the following command: Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName MY-APP-POLICY-2 -Global.

Please note:

  • If you already have an existing application-level policy and want the same permissioning structure to be applied to HubSpot, add the HubSpot App ID (0493df14-0cd5-4c89-b413-e0b9b90bbb17) to the policy.
  • You can assign only one application access policy at a time to a particular user. Assigning a new application access policy to a user will override any existing application access policy.

Review webinar settings

Configure your HubSpot account’s webinar sync settings and decide how contacts are created in HubSpot from Microsoft Teams.

Manage global Microsoft Teams settings
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Teams.
  • Click the Settings tab. Then click Webinars.
  • Navigate to the Global Settings tab.
  • In the Webinars section, toggle the Sync webinar data switch on to sync webinar data from Microsoft Teams to HubSpot. This will sync webinar data for all webinars created by all Microsoft Teams users on the HubSpot account.
  • In the Exclusions section, you can add domains to prevent webinars from being synced to HubSpot by users with a specific domain in their email address. You can enter your company’s domain name to prevent internal employees from being created as new contacts in HubSpot.

You can also manage webinar settings for individual users:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Microsoft Teams.

  • Click the Settings tab. Then click Global Settings.

  • At the bottom of the page in the Manage Individual User Settings section, search for the user and click User settings next to it.

  • In the right panel, in the Webinar Settings section:

    • Select the Sync data from newly scheduled webinars by default checkbox to automatically sync any data from a new webinar created by that user.

    • Click Manage individual webinars for this user to manage sync settings for an individual webinar.

Manage personal Microsoft Teams settings
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Microsoft Teams.
  • Click the Settings tab. Then click Webinars.
  • On the My settings tab, review all webinars that you’re the organizer of.
  • Select the checkboxes in the Sync column next to the webinars you want to sync to HubSpot marketing events. This ensures any new webinar updates are synced to HubSpot.
  • To sync data for a past webinar, hover over the webinar and click Sync now to retrieve all historical webinar data.
  • To automatically sync any new webinars you create in Microsoft Teams to HubSpot, select the Sync data from newly scheduled webinars by default checkbox.

Please note:

  • Newly created contacts will be created with only the First Name, Last Name, and Email contact properties.
  • The Microsoft Teams app will not automatically recreate a contact record if it was previously deleted.
  • Webinar registration forms must be configured and managed in Microsoft Teams.

Use forms on HubSpot pages for webinar registration

Use a HubSpot form to collect registrations for your Microsoft Teams webinars. Once a visitor submits the registration form, a registration event appears on the contact’s activity timeline in HubSpot. Registration data is also added to the webinar details in Microsoft Teams.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Create a form.
  • Set up your form fields. The form must have First Name, Last Name, and Email to accept registrations.

Please note: HubSpot’s integration with Microsoft Teams webinars only supports three required fields for webinar registration: First name, Last name, and Email. If you make any other field required for registration, the webinar registration will fail.

  • After completing the form setup and publishing it, add your form to a HubSpot page.
  • In the left sidebar editor of the HubSpot page, navigate to Contents. Then click the Form module.
  • Navigate to the Form automation section.
  • In the Webinar form section, click the Select integration dropdown menu. Select Microsoft Teams and the webinar for which the form will collect registrations.
  • Continue setting up your HubSpot page.

Automatically enroll contacts to Microsoft Teams webinars

Subscription required A Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, Data Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create workflows.

Set up a workflow to automatically enroll contacts to your Microsoft Teams webinars. Before going through the steps below, make sure to set up the Microsoft Teams integration, and configure the webinar sync settings.

  • Create a new workflow.
  • Set your contact enrollment triggers.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, scroll to the Integrated apps section.
  • Click the arrow next to Microsoft Teams and select Add Contact to Microsoft Teams webinar.
  • Click the Webinar dropdown menu and select the webinar.

The first name, last name, and email address of the contact will always be included to register the contact.

Please note: HubSpot’s integration with Microsoft Teams webinars only supports three required fields for webinar registration: First name, Last name, and Email. If you make any other field required for registration, the webinar registration will fail.

When the workflow is on, registered contacts will display under the Attendance tab in the webinar settings of Microsoft Teams.

If the webinar is synced to HubSpot, the contact will appear on the marketing event record in HubSpot, and a registration timeline event will appear on the contact’s record.

View webinar registration and attendance details

Please note:

  • If your webinar needs a manual registration approval in Microsoft Teams, registrations and attendees will not automatically sync to HubSpot. You can manually sync webinar information from the My Settings tab in Webinars settings and click Sync now next to the webinar you want to sync.
  • Only participants configured with the attendee role in Microsoft Teams will be synced as registrants in HubSpot. Participants configured with the presenter role won’t sync to HubSpot. Before the webinar, ensure that all participants you want synced as registrants are configured with the attendee role in Microsoft Teams.

Once you’ve configured your webinar settings, any webinars you choose to sync from Microsoft Teams to HubSpot will create a marketing event in HubSpot with the following information:

  • Number of registrants, attendees, and cancellations.
  • Event name
  • Date
  • Start and end time
  • Organizer
  • Status
  • Description

These marketing event properties can be used as criteria in segments and reports.

Please note: if the webinar organizer is also a webinar participant, they will not be counted in the number of registrants or attendees.

You can also view webinar events on the HubSpot contact record with the following information:

  • Webinar date
  • When a contact joined the webinar
  • When the contact left the webinar
  • Duration attended

Use HubSpot and Zoom webinars

After connecting Zoom to HubSpot, sync webinar registration and attendance data from Zoom to HubSpot. This helps you track how contacts engage with your webinars and use that information across your marketing and sales processes.

For example, you can segment contacts based on webinar registrations, attendance, or engagement, then use those audiences for follow-up campaigns and reporting. Webinar activity also syncs to marketing events and contact records, giving teams a centralized view of webinar engagement in HubSpot.

You can also automate webinar registration by adding contacts to Zoom webinars using workflows.

If you’re experiencing sync errors for Zoom webinars, learn how to troubleshoot common sync errors.

Before you get started

Before getting started, please note the following:

  • Your Zoom account must have the Zoom webinar add-on.
  • The Zoom integration does not support Zoom Events or webinars created as part of a Zoom Event.
  • Zoom removes email addresses for users identified as guests in Zoom unless they meet Zoom’s requirements. As a result, webinar registrants or participants without an email address won’t sync to HubSpot. To ensure all attendees sync to HubSpot, turn on webinar registration in Zoom.
  • The Zoom integration only accepts and syncs with three required fields in the Zoom registration link: First name, Last name, and Email. If the registration link has any other required fields, the registration will fail.
  • Users in the account won’t be created as contact records in HubSpot if they register for or attend a Zoom webinar. If a contact record has already been created for them in HubSpot, Zoom activities won’t sync to their contact record.
  • Timeline events won’t be created for contacts who registered for a webinar using their secondary email address. Only the primary email address is used to create and update contact records.
  • Contact records that were previously deleted won’t be automatically recreated by the Zoom integration.

Sync Zoom webinars to HubSpot

Once you’ve connected the Zoom integration, set up your HubSpot account’s webinar sync settings and choose how new contacts are created in HubSpot.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click Zoom.

  • Navigate to the Settings tab.

  • Click Webinars, then click the Global settings tab.

  • In the Webinars section, click the Sync webinar data toggle on to sync webinar data from Zoom to HubSpot. This will sync Zoom webinar registrants and attendees, and will also sync data to marketing events.

  • In the Sync webinar recordings and transcripts section, select whether you want to sync webinar recordings and transcripts for none of, selected, or all Zoom users in your HubSpot account.

  • In the Exclusions section, add domains to prevent webinars from being synced to HubSpot by users with a specific domain in their email address.

    • In the Recording exclusions section, click Enter domain or choose from list.
    • In the Contact exclusions section, enter your company’s domain name to prevent internal employees from being created as new contacts in HubSpot.

Add contacts to a Zoom webinar using a workflow

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

Please note:

  • To add contacts to a Zoom webinar using a workflow, the Zoom user that owns the webinar must be connected in HubSpot’s Zoom integration.
  • You’ll receive the error Webinar host cannot register for the webinar if you try to enroll the webinar host or connected user into a Zoom webinar using a workflow.

Use the Add Contact to Zoom Webinar workflow action to automate webinar registration. If you have separate Zoom accounts connected to multiple brands, this action can only register contacts for webinars that are associated with the Zoom account connected to the primary Account brand in HubSpot. Using the action to add contacts to a Zoom webinar that isn’t associated with the primary Account brand will result in the contact not being registered for the webinar.

To set up a workflow to automate Zoom webinar registration:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Create a new workflow, or hover over an existing workflow and click Edit.
  • In the workflows editor, after setting up your enrollment criteria, click the + icon to add an action.
  • In the right panel, under Zoom, select the Add Contact to Zoom webinar action.
  • Click the Webinar dropdown menu and select the webinar for which you want to register the contact.
  • Click Save.

The contact will be registered for the webinar using their first name, last name, and email contact properties. Learn more about the Add Contact to a Zoom webinar action.

Segment Zoom webinar contacts

Segment using Zoom properties

Please note: starting Jan. 8, 2025, Zoom contact-based properties cannot be used to segment contacts anymore. You can still use these properties for contacts with Zoom activity from before this date. To segment contacts after Jan.8, 2025, use marketing event filters.

You can filter contact records using the following properties, which are automatically created in your HubSpot account after connecting the Zoom integration:

  • Average Zoom webinar attendance duration: the average percentage of each webinar that the contact attends. A 100% value for this property, for example, would mean that the contact attended the full duration of each webinar.
  • Last registered Zoom webinar: the URL of the webinar the contact most recently registered for. This is populated if the contact was added as a registrant to the Zoom webinar manually or through a HubSpot workflow.
  • Total number of Zoom webinar registrations: the total number of webinars the contact has registered for.
  • Total number of Zoom webinars attended: the total number of webinars the contact attended.

Please note: the Total number of Zoom Webinars attended property will not be updated for contacts who attend the same recurring webinar.

Segment using marketing event filters

You can also segment your contacts using marketing event filters:

  • Attendance duration: how long the contact attended the webinar for.
  • Registered for marketing event: if they registered, or didn’t register for a webinar.
  • Canceled marketing event registration: if they canceled their webinar registration.
  • Attended marketing event: if they attended, or didn’t attend a webinar.

You can also segment your contacts based on the attributes of a specific Zoom event using the following filters:

  • Zoom: Recording Available Event: if you recorded one of your Zoom events, you can choose this filter, then refine by the Event Topic, Event Start Time, or Recording URL.
  • Zoom: Webinar Attendance Event: to filter based on attendance, choose this filter to segment your contacts based on the Attendance Duration, Attendance Duration Percent, Webinar id, or Webinar name.
  • Zoom: Webinar Registration Event: to filter based on registration, choose this filter to segment your contacts based on the Webinar id, or Webinar Name.

View Zoom webinar registrations

When a contact registers, attends or cancels a registration for a Zoom event, the contact will automatically be created or updated in HubSpot’s marketing events object.

Zoom webinar events also appear on HubSpot contact record timelines, showing you the webinar date, when a contact joined and left the webinar.

Use HubSpot’s calendar sync with Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar

Use HubSpot’s Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar integration to sync meetings between your calendar and HubSpot, create calendar events for meetings, and send invites to meeting guests.

The calendar sync keeps meeting activity in one place and maintains a record of customer interactions across HubSpot and your calendar. For example, if you schedule a meeting with a contact in HubSpot, the event is automatically added to your connected calendar and logged on the contact record.

To use your calendar with the HubSpot meetings tool, refer to this article instead.

Before you get started

Before getting started, do note the following:

  • Calendar sync will only sync with a user’s primary calendar. If a user has multiple calendars in Outlook or Google, HubSpot will only sync with the primary or default calendar.
  • You can connect either the Google Calendar sync or the Outlook Calendar sync to HubSpot. You can’t use both at the same time.
  • Events created before you connect your calendar won’t sync to HubSpot. This applies also if the guests for those events are contacts in your HubSpot account and have the same email address in the Email property. Only events created in Google or Office 365 while the integration is active will sync to the contact’s timeline. You can manually log older meetings on relevant CRM records.

Connect Google Calendar to HubSpot

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for the Google Calendar integration, and select Google Calendar in the results.
  • Click Install.
  • In the Install pop-up window, review what to expect when connecting Google Calendar to HubSpot. Then click Install.
  • In the Connect your calendar pop-up window, select Google/Gmail. Then click Connect your calendar.
  • In the Connect your Google account pop-up window, click Accept and connect to Google.
  • You’ll be redirected to Google to sign in or choose a Google account if you have multiple accounts.
  • Review the requested permissions and click Allow.

You’ll be redirected back to HubSpot with a dialog box confirming that Google Calendar for HubSpot has been installed.

Connect Outlook Calendar to HubSpot

Before connecting your Outlook calendar to HubSpot, make sure you’re logged into the right email account in Outlook.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Search for the Outlook Calendar integration, and select Outlook Calendar in the results.
  • Click Install.
  • In the Connect your calendar pop-up window, select Microsoft Outlook. Then click Connect your calendar.
  • In the Connect Your Outlook 365 Inbox pop-up window, click Accept and connect to Outlook 365.
  • You’ll be redirected to Office 365, where you can log into your account.
  • Review the requested permissions and click Accept.

After entering your login credentials, you’ll be redirected back to HubSpot with a dialog box confirming that Outlook Calendar has been installed.

Once the integration is installed, other users in the HubSpot account can connect their Outlook Calendar to HubSpot.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to General.
  • Click the Calendar tab.
  • Click Connect your calendar.

Schedule a meeting in HubSpot

  • After you’ve connected your Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar, navigate to any contact, company, deal, or ticket in your HubSpot account.
  • In the left sidebar, click date Schedule a meeting to create a meeting event.
  • In the Schedule pop-up window, enter your meeting details.
  • Click Save to add the meeting to your calendar and send the contact a meeting invitation.

Learn more about scheduling a meeting on a contact, company, deal, or ticket record.

Please note: deleting a meeting in HubSpot will not remove the event from Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar.

Schedule a meeting in Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar

When you create a meeting in Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar and invite a contact who exists in your HubSpot account, the meeting will appear on their contact timeline in HubSpot. Similarly, if a contact in HubSpot invites you to a meeting, the meeting will also appear on their timeline in HubSpot.

Calendar sync considerations for meetings

Meeting sync behavior
  • If you edit or delete an event in your calendar, the updates will automatically appear in the meeting on the contact timeline in HubSpot.
  • For recurring meetings, HubSpot will sync the next five upcoming events in the series up to a year in advance.
  • When you cancel a meeting in Outlook, the meeting is deleted from the contact timeline in HubSpot.
  • Outlook meetings with an event body larger than 65,536 characters won’t sync to HubSpot through calendar sync.
Attendees and contact creation
  • Once a meeting has been created, adding attendees to the meeting engagement in HubSpot won’t add them to the calendar event. To avoid this issue, you can make a small change to the meeting’s description at the same time you’re adding attendees, then click Save and send update.
  • When a meeting is created from your connected calendar, the meeting will only log on the timeline of contacts that already exist in your HubSpot account. HubSpot won’t automatically create contact records if the guests don’t already exist in your HubSpot account.
  • For the meeting to appear in your contact’s timeline, the guest must be using the same email address in their contact record’s Email property.
  • Group emails that are added as attendees to the meeting event invite won’t be synced to HubSpot. Instead, invite each group member individually to the meeting event.
Internal, private, and out-of-office event sync
  • HubSpot automatically prevents any events from being added for members of your organization based on email domain (your HubSpot account’s target and connected domains), and existing users. Events will also not be created from any @hubspot.com email addresses.
  • HubSpot’s calendar sync doesn’t sync private calendar events to your HubSpot account. If a public event is later changed to private, the engagement will remain in your HubSpot account, but changes to the event will no longer sync.
  • You can sync out of office events between HubSpot and your Google or Outlook Calendar. Learn more about managing user out of office hours.

Use HubSpot’s integration with Eventbrite

Connect the Eventbrite app to HubSpot to sync event registration and attendance activity to your HubSpot contacts. When someone registers for a synced Eventbrite event, their activity is added to their contact record in HubSpot, and a new contact record is created if one doesn’t already exist.

Use Eventbrite activity in HubSpot to identify event registrants and attendees, segment contacts, automate event follow-up, and track Eventbrite events as marketing events. For example, create a segment of contacts who attended an event, then use the segment to send a follow-up email.

Permissions required You must be either a Super Admin or have App Marketplace Access permissions to connect Eventbrite to HubSpot.

Install the Eventbrite app

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Use the search bar to locate and select the Eventbrite app.
  • Click Install.
  • On the next screen, enter your Eventbrite email address and click Get started. You’ll be prompted to create an account or log into your existing account.

Please note: only events created by the integration user (the user who logs in when connecting Eventbrite and HubSpot) will sync to HubSpot. The email address used to log in must be the account administrator in the connected Eventbrite account.

  • Click Allow to grant HubSpot access to your Eventbrite account.

  • You’ll be redirected to the Eventbrite settings screen, where you’ll see your existing Eventbrite events.

    • If your Eventbrite account has access to multiple organizations, you can switch between them to view events created for a different organization. Click the dropdown menu under Choose an organization to see their events, then select a different organization.
    • By default, sync will be disabled for your events. To enable syncing for an event, click to toggle the Sync switch on.
What to expect after you connect the Eventbrite app

Once you’ve turned on the integration:

  • A new contact properties group named Eventbrite will be automatically created, which will include two new properties: Last Registered Event Name and Last Registered Event Date. When a contact registers for a new event, these fields will be updated automatically.
  • When someone registers for an event you’ve synced to HubSpot, you’ll see an Eventbrite registration event on that contact’s timeline. If the person registering for the event isn’t a contact in HubSpot, a new contact record will be automatically created. All standard Eventbrite registration properties (Cell phone, Company, First Name, Last Name, Home Address, Job Title, and Website) will be included in the timeline event.

Please note: if a contact was previously deleted in HubSpot, the Eventbrite integration won’t recreate the contact when they register for or attend an event. To sync Eventbrite data for the contact, restore the deleted contact or manually create a new contact, then sync the event again.

  • If an attendee answers custom questions on the Eventbrite registration form, each question response will also sync to the contact timeline as a separate activity. Text, dropdown, multiple choice, and checkbox questions are supported.
  • If someone updates their order form for an event, an Eventbrite Updated order information event will appear on their contact’s timeline.
  • When a contact cancels their registration, an Eventbrite cancellation/refund event will appear on their timeline.
  • Every time someone attends an event for which they’ve registered, you’ll see an Eventbrite attendance event on that contact’s timeline (this requires that you check-in attending users via Eventbrite).

Any new events you create in Eventbrite will sync automatically. You can turn off this option by unchecking the Automatically sync new events checkbox on the Eventbrite settings page in HubSpot. You can also turn off syncing for any event at any time by toggling the Sync switch off for a certain event.

Please note: only standard Eventbrite registration properties (Cell Phone, Company, First Name, Last Name, Home Address, Job Title, and Website) will be synced to HubSpot. Custom properties will not be synced.

Segment Eventbrite registrants and attendees

After turning on the Eventbrite integration with HubSpot, you’ll have access to Eventbrite segmentation options in your segments and workflows in HubSpot. This includes the ability to segment based on the following HubSpot contact properties:

  • Last registered event
  • Last registered event date

You’ll also see the following options for filtering in your segments based on events synced from Eventbrite:

  • Eventbrite: registration properties
  • Eventbrite: attendance properties
  • Eventbrite: refund properties
  • Eventbrite: order information update properties

Please note: the above segmentation options are not available in Marketing Hub Starter accounts.

Some example segments you can create are:

  • Event registrants: Registration property | Event Name | is equal to | [enter your event name].

  • Event attendees: Attendance property | Event Name | is equal to | [enter your event name].

  • Contacts who have registered for an event in the past month: Contact property | Last Registered Event Date | is less than | 4 weeks ago.

Once you’ve created your segments, you can use them to send one-off emails or as enrollment triggers in a workflow to send automated emails to your different segments to remind them of the event or follow up afterward. You can also use workflows to send follow-up emails after the event.

You can also set rules based on Eventbrite properties in manual lead scoring.

Use marketing events with Eventbrite

Once you add the marketing events object to HubSpot, and have installed the Eventbrite integration, Eventbrite events will sync to marketing events in HubSpot. Learn how to view, analyze, and report on marketing events.

Use HubSpot’s integration with GoToWebinar

Manage webinar registration and engagement data between HubSpot and GoToWebinar. When you connect your GoToWebinar account to HubSpot, webinar registration and attendance information syncs with contact records, allowing you to track webinar activity in HubSpot.

Use the integration to automate webinar registration with workflows, segment contacts based on webinar engagement, and report on webinar performance. For example, you can automatically register contacts for a webinar, then use registration or attendance data to trigger follow-up actions in HubSpot.

Before you get started

Before installing the GoToWebinar integration, please note the following:

Permissions required To connect GoToWebinar to HubSpot, you must be either a Super Admin or have App Marketplace Access permissions.

  • The GoToWebinar integration can only be connected to one GoToWebinar account. You can use the Zapier integration to set up a simple integration with a second GoToWebinar account.
  • To register contacts for a webinar through a HubSpot form submission, your connected GoToWebinar account must be on GoTo’s Complete plan. Contacts won’t be registered for the webinar if your GoToWebinar account is on a different plan. For the latest GoTo’s pricing information, refer to GoTo’s pricing page.

Install the GoToWebinar integration

To install the GoToWebinar integration:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select the GoToWebinar app.
  • Click Install.
  • Enter your GoToWebinar credentials and click Sign in. After logging in to GoToWebinar, your accounts will automatically be connected and you will be redirected back to the Connected apps page in HubSpot.

Turn on your webinar

From your GoToWebinar integration page, you can manually sync past webinars and turn on auto-syncing for all new webinars. Please note the following:

  • The connecting user must be the co-organizer for a webinar to be available for syncing.
  • After turning on a sync, it can take between 1 minute and 2 hours or more for a webinar to sync. This depends on the amount of information queued to sync. The Sync status column will display the current status of the sync for each webinar.

To turn on a webinar:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click GoToWebinar.

  • Navigate to the Event sync settings tab.

  • On the Upcoming webinars and Past webinars tabs, view all upcoming and past webinars from the GoToWebinar connected account.

    • To manually sync a webinar, select the checkbox in the Sync column. HubSpot will then start importing data from GoToWebinar.
    • By default, syncing will be turned off for all webinars created before the integration was set up. To turn on auto-syncing for new webinars, select the Auto-sync data from future webinars checkbox.

Set up a form for your webinar

Please note: to register contacts for a webinar through a HubSpot form submission, your connected GoToWebinar account must be on GoTo’s Complete plan. Contacts won’t be registered for the webinar if your GoToWebinar account is on a different plan. For the latest GoTo’s pricing information, refer to GoTo’s pricing page.

When you’re ready to begin collecting registrations for your upcoming webinar, you can do so using the following methods:

  • Register contacts via a GoToWebinar registration page.
  • Register contacts via a HubSpot form (using a default form module) embedded on a HubSpot page.
  • Register contacts via a HubSpot form embedded on an external page.
  • Register contacts via a HubSpot form (using a custom module linked to a webinar) embedded on a HubSpot page.

If you’re using a HubSpot form, please note the following:

  • The GoToWebinar registration page and your HubSpot landing page aren’t linked. Using a HubSpot landing page with a HubSpot form means that you don’t need to use the GoToWebinar registration page.
  • When linking a form on a HubSpot page or a form embed code to GoToWebinar, the integration will not automatically include any fields from the GoToWebinar registration page. To collect this information, it is recommended to add the same questions from your GoToWebinar registration page to your HubSpot form.
  • When setting up your form, take note of which form fields can be used to pass information between HubSpot and GoToWebinar.
  • To make sure the GoToWebinar integration with HubSpot registers a contact for a webinar in your GoToWebinar account, the following fields must be set as required and must be the only required fields in the form:
    • First name
    • Last name
    • Email
Use a form on a HubSpot landing page

You can create forms in HubSpot that automatically register contacts for a webinar created in GoToWebinar upon submission. When visitors submit the form, they will be sent to GoToWebinar and appear as a registrant in your registrant list.

  • Registrant data will be added to HubSpot in real time.
  • Attendee data will be added to HubSpot 15 minutes after your webinar is over.

To register contacts to a GoToWebinar webinar:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Create a form.
  • Set up your form fields. The form must have First Name, Last Name, and Email to accept registrations.
  • After completing the form setup and publishing it, add your form to a HubSpot page.
  • In the left sidebar editor of the HubSpot page, navigate to Contents. Then click the Form module.
  • Navigate to the Form automation section.
  • In the Webinar form section, click the Select integration dropdown menu and select GoToWebinar.
  • Click the Select a webinar dropdown menu and select the webinar for which the form will collect registrations.

Please note: only upcoming webinars will be listed as an option in the dropdown menu. Webinars that have already taken place will not be listed.

  • Continue setting up your HubSpot page.
Embed a HubSpot form on an external page

You can also embed a HubSpot form on an external page to register visitors for a webinar by changing the form’s embed code to include the GoToWebinar webinar key.

The steps to add the GoToWebinar webinar key to your HubSpot form embed code differ depending on whether you’re using a HubSpot form built with the legacy editor or the updated form editor.

To retrieve your GoToWebinar webinar key:

  • From your GoToWebinar account, navigate to your webinar event details page.
  • From the URL of the page, copy the webinar key.

To add the GoToWebinar webinar key to your HubSpot form:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.

  • Hover over an existing form and click Actions, then select Share.

  • Click the Embed code tab. Then click Copy to copy the embed code from your form.

    • If you’re using a HubSpot form built in the legacy editor:
      • When adding the embed code to your external page, edit the form embed code.
      • After formID, add a comma.
      • Add a goToWebinarWebinarKey identifier with the webinar key for your webinar.
    • If you’re using a HubSpot form built in the updated form editor:
      • When adding the embed code to your external page, paste the following script immediately before the form embed code.
      • &lt;script> window.addEventListener("hs-form-event:on-ready", function(event) { HubSpotFormsV4.getFormFromEvent(event).setExtraSubmissionMetadata({ goToWebinarWebinarKey: 'insert key here' }); }); &lt;/script>
      • Replace 'insert key here' with your GoToWebinar webinar key.
Create a custom form module

You can create a custom module to use with the GoToWebinar integration. To use the GoToWebinar integration in your custom form module you’ll need to add gotowebinar_webinar_key=’ to your custom module.

Learn more about creating a custom form module.

Segment and follow up with registrants and attendees

When contacts start registering for your webinars, you can segment them based on their webinar activity using the GoToWebinar integration filter in segments.

Please note: the above segmentation options are not available in Marketing Hub Starter accounts.

You can also add webinar data to your HubSpot score criteria to make sure that the HubSpot score for your contacts is accurate and up to date.

Once you’ve segmented your contacts, send emails to your contacts based on their engagement with your webinar. In addition to any promotional email you create to encourage registration, below are a few suggestions:

  • Reminder emails in advance of the webinar.
  • Thank you emails for those who attended.
  • Sorry we missed you emails for those who registered but didn’t attend.
  • Request to schedule a demo emails for those who attended and have a high lead score.

Please note: the integration doesn’t have an automated system to add personalized links from GoToWebinar within HubSpot emails.

Sync webinar data to Salesforce

If you have the HubSpot-Salesforce integration installed, webinar activity will automatically pass to Salesforce in the HubSpot Embed window.

To send more targeted messages to your sales reps, you can pass data to Salesforce as a task with a workflow. For example, if you want to alert a sales rep every time one of their leads attends a webinar, you can create a workflow that sends a task to Salesforce. The task will appear on the Salesforce lead or contact record in the Activity History section.

If you’re using the Salesforce integration, it’s important to change the field mapping between the email field in HubSpot and Salesforce to Use most recent value. This is relevant because data is pulled from GoToWebinar into HubSpot based on the email address. Therefore if the email address in HubSpot changes between the time a contact registers and when they attend the webinar, HubSpot won’t be able to match the attendance data with the new email address.

Add contacts to a GoToWebinar using workflows

Subscription required A HubSpot Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

Please note: to enroll contacts in your GoToWebinar event, the sync for the event must be switched on in your integration settings.

You can enroll and register contacts automatically for your GoToWebinar webinars using workflows.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Select an existing Contact-based workflow or create a new Contact-based workflow.

  • Edit your enrollment triggers.

  • Click the + plus icon to add a workflow action.

  • In the left panel, in the Integrated apps section, click to expand the GoToWebinar section.

  • Click the Add Contact to Webinar action.

  • Click the Webinar dropdown menu to select your GoToWebinar event. Then, click Save.

  • Turn on your workflow.

When a contact is enrolled in the workflow, a confirmation email including the webinar link will be sent to their primary email address.

Use marketing events with GoToWebinar

HubSpot can aggregate marketing events from the GoToWebinar integration to provide you with a consistent overview of your marketing events.

Uninstall the integration

To disconnect your HubSpot and GoToWebinar accounts:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • To the right of GoToWebinar, click the Actions dropdown menu. Then select Uninstall.

Use HubSpot’s integration with SurveyMonkey

Connect SurveyMonkey to HubSpot to send surveys to contacts and sync survey responses to HubSpot. Use survey response data to understand contacts’ feedback and activity, then segment contacts or use their responses as criteria in workflows. For example, you can automatically send a survey after a support ticket is closed, then use the response data to follow up with contacts based on their feedback.

Before you get started

Permissions required You must be a Super Admin or have App Marketplace permissions in your HubSpot account to connect the app.

If you have a SurveyMonkey Basic account, it is not possible to sync surveys collected by a web link collector or email collector. If you’ve synced surveys in the past using an email collector, you’re still able to view any past responses in your HubSpot account. However, you will not be able to use the email collector method moving forward.

Please note: HubSpot’s integration with SurveyMonkey can only be connected to a SurveyMonkey account with a license in the U.S.

Install the SurveyMonkey integration

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.
  • In the search bar, search for and select SurveyMonkey.
  • Click Install.
  • Enter your SurveyMonkey credentials and click Log In.

Review sync settings

Configure the sync settings for HubSpot’s integration with SurveyMonkey and decide how surveys will sync from SurveyMonkey to HubSpot.

Manage global sync settings for SurveyMonkey surveys

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click SurveyMonkey.

  • Click the Settings tab.

  • Toggle the Sync data from new surveys switch on to sync all future SurveyMonkey surveys to HubSpot automatically.

  • To sync incomplete survey responses from SurveyMonkey to HubSpot, select the Include partial survey responses checkbox.

Manage sync settings for individual SurveyMonkey surveys

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click SurveyMonkey.

  • Click the Settings tab.

  • Use the search bar to search surveys by survey name.

  • To sync data for a past survey, hover over the survey and click Sync now to sync all historical survey data to HubSpot.

To customize the sync settings for a single survey:

  • Click the name of the survey.
  • In the right panel, toggle the Auto sync survey responses switch on to automatically sync future survey responses for the individual survey. Then, select the Include partial survey responses checkbox to sync partial responses for that survey.
Syncing email addresses and names from survey respondents

HubSpot collects a survey respondent’s email address differently based on the survey type:

- Email invitation collector surveys: the recipient's email address is collected automatically when they click the survey link. You don't need to include an email address field in the survey. Email invitation collector surveys can be sent:
    - From the CRM card on a contact record.
    - From the contacts index page.
    - Through workflows using the Send SurveyMonkey Survey workflow action.
    - Directly from SurveyMonkey.
- Web link collector surveys: you must ask your respondents for their email addresses unless you send the survey through a HubSpot marketing email with a custom variable. There are various methods to collect their email addresses that will work with HubSpot:
    - Add a custom variable email to the survey link (e.g., [surveymonkey.com](https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/XXXXX?email=)). HubSpot will use this email address to sync the response to the matching contact, and it takes priority over any email questions in the survey. If the email address in the custom variable is invalid, HubSpot will fall back to the email questions in the response.

    - Include a Contact Information question with the Email address field. The question can be added anywhere in your survey and the Email address field label can be in any language.
    - Include a Single Textbox question that asks your respondents for an email.
        - If you include both types of questions in one survey, HubSpot will sync the email address submitted to the Contact Information question. If your survey has multiple questions that ask for an email address, HubSpot will use the first email address to create a contact.
        - If there's no email address in the Contact Information question, HubSpot will search the other single text answer fields for one. If there's an email address with the normal email format name@company.com, HubSpot will associate this email address with the respondent.

HubSpot will also sync a survey respondent’s name from a Contact Information question. If the respondent is a contact whose name already exists, the contact’s name will not be updated.

Send a survey through a marketing email

Send a SurveyMonkey survey using a marketing email to collect responses from contacts. By adding a custom variable to the survey link embedded in the email, responses can be attributed to contact records when the survey data syncs to HubSpot.

To generate a web collector link for a survey:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.

  • Click SurveyMonkey.

  • Navigate to the Settings tab.

  • Next to the survey, click the link icon.

  • In the dialog box, choose how to create the personalized link.

    • Automatically generate the link:
      • Click Authorize.
      • Complete the authentication process to give HubSpot additional permissions in SurveyMonkey.
    • Manually set up the link:

      • Click Manual setup.

      • In SurveyMonkey:

        • Open your survey in the survey editor.
        • Click Logic, then select Custom variables.
        • In the Variable name field, enter hs_cid, then click Save.
        • Confirm that hs_cid appears in the variables list.
        • Return to HubSpot and click I’ve added the custom variable.

  • Click the Select a collector dropdown menu. Then select an existing collector, or click Create new collector.

  • Click Copy to copy the personalized link.

  • Add the link to your marketing email.

When contacts click the survey link in the email and complete the survey, their responses will be attributed to their contact record in HubSpot.

Send a survey from the contact index page

To send a survey from the contact index page:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • Select the checkbox next to the contacts you want to send a survey to.

  • In the top menu, click More > Send SurveyMonkey survey.

  • In the right panel, select the survey you want to send to the contact.

  • Click Send.

Send a survey from a contact record

To send a survey from a contact record:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of the contact.
  • In the right panel, in the SurveyMonkey card, click Send existing survey.
  • In the right panel, select the survey you want to send to the contact.
  • Click Send.
  • When the survey has been sent you’ll see the status and details in the SurveyMonkey card on the contact record.

Please note: it is not possible to send custom surveys from HubSpot.

Use SurveyMonkey surveys in workflows

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

Use SurveyMonkey data in workflows to enroll contacts based on their survey activity. You can also use the Send Survey workflow action to automatically send a SurveyMonkey survey to enrolled contacts.

Enroll contacts based on SurveyMonkey activity

Use SurveyMonkey surveys or questions as enrollment triggers to automate actions based on whether contacts responded to a survey or how they answered a specific question.

For example, enroll contacts who responded to a SurveyMonkey survey, then send them different follow-up communications based on their responses.

To set SurveyMonkey enrollment triggers:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Automation > Workflows.

  • To edit an existing contact-based workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or, create a new workflow.

  • In the left panel, click When filter criteria is met.

  • Click Events.

  • Select SurveyMonkey, then select an enrollment trigger:

    • SurveyMonkey surveys: select a survey, then set the criteria based on whether HubSpot got a response from the contact.
    • SurveyMonkey questions: select a question, then set the criteria based on the contact’s response.

  • Add additional enrollment criteria as needed, then click Save to save your enrollment triggers.

Please note: SurveyMonkey criteria cannot be used as re-enrollment triggers.

Send a SurveyMonkey survey with a workflow

Use the Send Survey workflow action to automatically send a SurveyMonkey survey to enrolled contacts. For example, send a customer satisfaction survey when a contact’s associated support ticket is closed.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Automation > Workflows.

  • To edit an existing contact-based workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or, create a new workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add an action.

  • In the left panel, under SurveyMonkey, select Send Survey.

  • To select the survey you want to send, click the Select a Survey dropdown menu.

  • Click Save. Continue setting up your workflow.

View SurveyMonkey data in HubSpot

When syncing is turned on for a survey, HubSpot will sync all existing data, along with any new respondent data. Any new email addresses will be created as new contacts in HubSpot. Existing contacts will have the survey data added to their contact record.

Responses will not update contact properties, but they will appear on the contact timeline. You can also view and segment the response data on individual contact records and in segments.

View SurveyMonkey data on an individual contact record

Once you’ve synced your SurveyMonkey surveys, survey responses will appear as activities on your contacts’ timelines. Quiz scores for quiz-type surveys will also appear on contact records alongside responses and you’ll be able to use them as criteria in contact-based workflows and segments. If you have a SurveyMonkey Basic plan, the timeline event will show that the contact responded to the survey. If you have an annual paid SurveyMonkey plan, the timeline event will show a breakdown of your contacts’ responses to specific questions.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of a contact.
  • At the top of the contact’s timeline, click Filter activity, then select the SurveyMonkey checkbox.
Segment contacts based on SurveyMonkey activity in segments

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
