    • Record not syncing: the record isn’t syncing due to an error. For more information, hover over the sync status, or click the sync status to navigate to the sync health page.

    • Unknown sync: the record is syncing with the integration, but sync health information isn’t available.

    • Record excluded: the record is part of an excluded bucket. For more information, hover over Sync status.

  • Last updated: when data was last synced between HubSpot and the integration.

Account & Setup: Privacy & Consent

Analyze cookie consent banner interactions

When a contact visits your website and interacts with a cookie consent banner, the interaction is logged in HubSpot as analytics activity on a contact record. You can use interaction data to segment contacts into segments or analyze consent banner interactions in reports.

View individual contact interaction with a consent banner

Permissions required View contacts permissions are required to view contact data.

To view a single contact’s interaction with a cookie consent banner:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of the contact.
  • Navigate to the Activities tab.
  • Filter activities to include Analytics activity.
  • Cookie tracking events will be displayed on the timeline.

Create a segment of contacts based on their interaction with the cookie consent banner

Permissions required Edit Segment permissions are required to create segments.

Please note: notify consent banner view interactions are only included in segments if you are using the new consent banner editor. Click interactions are not included.

To create a segment of contacts who’ve had a certain interaction with the cookie consent banner:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • Create a segment.
  • Select Contact properties as the filter category.
  • Select Privacy Consent.
  • Select to include contacts that completed or did not complete a privacy consent event. For example, select Contact has completed with value > Approved to include contacts that accepted cookies.
  • Select the event:
    • Approved: cookies were accepted. If you have the display cookies by category toggle turned on for your consent banner, the contact’s approval only applies to analytics cookies. If you do not have the display cookies by category toggle turned on, the contact’s approval applies to all cookies.
    • Declined: cookies were declined. if you have the display cookies by category toggle turned on for your consent banner, the contact’s decline only applies to analytics cookies. If you do not have the display cookies by category toggle turned on, the decline applies to all cookies.
    • Revoked: cookies were removed. Learn more about the Remove cookies API.
  • Save and process the segment.

Create a custom cookie consent banner custom report

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create a custom report.

Permissions required Dashboard, reports, and analytics Create/Own and Edit permissions are required to create custom reports.

Please note: notify consent banner interactions are only included in reports if you are using the new consent banner editor.

Use the custom report builder to analyze cookie banner clicks and views:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Reporting > Reports. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Reporting > Reports directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create report.
  • Select Custom report.
  • Click Choose my own data sources.
  • To use cookie banner interactions as the primary data source, click the Primary data source dropdown menu, then select Cookie banner.
  • In the upper right, click Next.
  • In the left sidebar, select whether you want to report on cookie banner clicks or views by selecting either Cookie banner clicks or Cookie banner views.
  • Continue building your report.

Cookies set in your visitor’s browser by HubSpot

If you host your website by HubSpot or have installed the HubSpot tracking code, the cookies below may be set on your visitors’ browsers, depending on your site’s setup. You can learn more about the cookies set by HubSpot by reading below.

Please note: if you’re visiting your own site to test your HubSpot tracking cookies, you may see a console error on the SameSite attribute for cookies related to hubspot.com or app.hubspot.com. These cookies are your HubSpot app cookies (e.g., they let you log into HubSpot) and are unrelated to the tracking cookies for your visitors. Check the Community thread for more information.

Necessary cookies

These are essential cookies that do not require consent.

__cfruid

This cookie is set by HubSpot’s CDN provider because of their rate limiting policies. It expires at the end of the session. Learn more about Cloudflare cookies.

__cfuvid

This cookie is set by HubSpot’s CDN provider because of their rate limiting policies. It expires at the end of the session. Learn more about Cloudflare cookies.

__cf_bm

This cookie is set by HubSpot’s CDN provider and is a necessary cookie for bot protection. It expires in 30 minutes. Learn more about Cloudflare cookies.

__hs_opt_out
  • This cookie is used by the opt-in privacy policy to remember not to ask the visitor to accept cookies again.
  • This cookie is set when you give visitors the choice to opt out of cookies.
  • It contains the string “yes” or “no”.
  • It expires in six months.
__hs_do_not_track
  • This cookie can be set to prevent the tracking code from sending any information to HubSpot.
  • It contains the string “yes”.
  • It expires in six months.
__hs_initial_opt_in
  • This cookie is used to prevent the banner from always displaying when visitors are browsing in strict mode.
  • It contains the string “yes” or “no”.
  • It expires in seven days.
__hs_cookie_cat_pref
  • This cookie is used to record the categories a visitor consented to.
  • It contains data on the consented categories.
  • It expires in six months.
__hs_gpc_banner_dismiss
  • This cookie is used when the Global Privacy Control banner is dismissed.
  • It contains the string “yes” or “no”.
  • It expires in 180 days.
__hs_notify_banner_dismiss
  • This cookie is used when the website uses a Notify consent banner type.
  • It contains a boolean value of True.
  • It expires in 180 days.
hs_ab_test
  • This cookie is used to consistently serve visitors the same version of an A/B test page they’ve seen before.
  • It contains the id of the A/B test page and the id of the variation that was chosen for the visitor.
  • It expires at the end of the session.
hs-messages-is-open
  • This cookie is used to determine and save whether the chat widget is open for future visits.
  • It is set in your visitor’s browser when they start a new chat, and resets to re-close the widget after 30 minutes of inactivity.
  • If your visitor manually closes the chat widget, it will prevent the widget from re-opening on subsequent page loads in that browser session for 30 minutes.
  • It contains a boolean value of True if present.
  • It expires in 30 minutes.
hs-messages-hide-welcome-message
  • This cookie is used to prevent the chat widget welcome message from appearing again for one day after it is dismissed.
  • It contains a boolean value of True or False.
  • It expires in one day.
__hsmem
  • This cookie is set when visitors log in to a HubSpot-hosted site.
  • It contains encrypted data that identifies the membership user when they are currently logged in.
  • It expires in seven days.
__Host-hs-membership-csrf
  • This cookie is used to ensure that content membership logins can’t be forged.
  • It contains a random string of letters and numbers used to verify that a membership login is authentic.
  • It expires at the end of the session.
hs-membership-logout-referer
  • This cookie is set when visitors log out of HubSpot-hosted sites.
  • It contains the value of the Referer header in the visitor’s browser at the time of logout. This is the URL of the page the visitor was previously on before they logged out.
  • It expires in one hour or when the visitor logs in to a HubSpot-hosted site.
hs.superstore.laboratory.<id>
  • It contains an offline cache of cohorts that a user got assigned for HubSpot Product experiments.
  • It doesn’t contain personal identifiable information or information that can identify your device or hardware
  • HubSpot experiments are anonymous and aren’t attached to user sessions. However, if tracking consent is given, specific experiments might be tied to identifiable user sessions.
  • The individual contents of this storage entry expire automatically upon specific dates determined by HubSpot Product. Often, these are 48 hours.
  • It can’t be manually removed and is automatically created whenever conditions are met.
<id>_key
  • When visiting a password-protected page, this cookie is set so future visits to the page from the same browser do not require login again.
  • The cookie name is unique for each password-protected page.
  • It contains an encrypted version of the password so future visits to the page will not require the password again.
  • It expires in 14 days.

Analytics cookies

These are non-essential cookies controlled by the cookie banner. If you’re a visitor to a site supported by HubSpot, you can opt out of these cookies by not giving consent.

__hmpl
  • It contains metadata regarding tracking events that HubSpot collects throughout the user’s journey at HubSpot.
  • It’s stored either on the Browser’s Session Storage or Local Storage based on the presence or lack of tracking consent.
  • It doesn’t contain personal identifiable information or information that can identify your device or hardware.
  • It can’t be manually removed and is automatically created whenever conditions are met.
hublytics_events_53
  • This browser storage entry is used by HubSpot Product to temporarily store tracking events created by HubSpot Product until they get dispatched over the network.
  • It’s stored either on the Browser’s Session Storage or Local Storage based on the presence or lack of tracking consent.
  • It doesn’t contain personal identifiable information or information that can identify your device or hardware.
  • It can’t be manually removed and is automatically created whenever conditions are met.
__hstc
  • The main cookie for tracking visitors.
  • It contains the domain, hubspotutk, initial timestamp (first visit), last timestamp (last visit), current timestamp (this visit), and session number (increments for each subsequent session).
  • It expires in six months.
hubspotutk
  • This cookie keeps track of a visitor’s identity. It is passed to HubSpot on form submission and used when deduplicating contacts.
  • It contains an opaque GUID to represent the current visitor.
  • It expires in six months.
__hssc
  • This cookie keeps track of sessions.
  • This is used to determine if HubSpot should increment the session number and timestamps in the __hstc cookie.
  • It contains the domain, viewCount (increments each pageView in a session), and session start timestamp.
  • It expires in 30 minutes.
__hssrc
  • Whenever HubSpot changes the session cookie, this cookie is also set to determine if the visitor has restarted their browser.
  • If this cookie does not exist when HubSpot manages cookies, it is considered a new session.
  • It contains the value “1” when present.
  • It expires at the end of the session.

If you are logged in to HubSpot, HubSpot will set additional authentication cookies. Learn more about cookies set in the HubSpot product. You can also see whether a contact accepted these cookies in their timeline.

Functionality cookies

Chatflow cookie

This is the cookie used for the chatflows tool. If you’re a visitor, this allows you to chat with a representative on the site.

messagesUtk
  • This cookie is used to recognize visitors who chat with you through the chatflows tool. If the visitor leaves your site before they’re added as a contact, they will have this cookie associated with their browser.
  • With the Consent to collect chat cookies setting turned on:
    • If you chat with a visitor who later returns to your site in the same cookied browser, the chatflows tool will load their conversation history.
    • The messagesUtk cookie will be treated as a necessary cookie.
  • When the Consent to collect chat cookies setting is turned off, the messagesUtk cookie is controlled by the Consent to process setting in your chatflow.
  • HubSpot will not drop the messagesUtk cookie for visitors who have been identified through the Visitor Identification API. The analytics cookie banner will not be impacted.
  • This cookie will be specific to a subdomain and will not carry over to other subdomains. For example, the cookie dropped for info.example.com will not apply to the visitor when they visit www.example.com, and vice versa.
  • It contains an opaque GUID to represent the current chat user.
  • It expires after six months.
Chatflow cookie consent text

With the Consent to collect chat cookies setting enabled, HubSpot will prompt visitors for consent to drop a cookie in their browser before the start a chat or when they attempt to the leave the page during a chat conversation. This cookie is used to interact with website visitors and provide a visitor’s chat history.

If you choose to display the banner before the visitor starts a chat and the visitor does not give consent, they will not be able to start the chat.

If you choose to display the banner upon exit intent, however, the visitor can start the chat, but if they don’t consent to cookies before navigating away from the page, the chat widget will reset and the conversation will end.

With this setting turned off, a visitor can start a chat and give consent to process their information via the Consent to process setting.

Visitors can also accept or decline cookies on the HubSpot cookie banner if it is turned on on your pages.

  • If a visitor accepts the cookie when they start a chat, but then clicks Decline on the HubSpot cookie banner, the cookie will be removed.
  • If a visitor clicks Decline on the HubSpot cookie banner before starting a chat, HubSpot will not drop a cookie or prompt them to consent to cookies in the chat widget.

Advertisement cookies

Advertisement cookies are ad pixel cookies (such as Facebook, LinkedIn and Google) that you can opt to install using the HubSpot ads tool.

If you have the Facebook pixel code installed on your website, Facebook may set a cookie in a visitor’s browser.

If you use the HubSpot ads tool to select and install your Facebook pixel on pages with the HubSpot tracking code, HubSpot will link the placing of that pixel code to the cookie notification banner. If you require opt-in consent through this banner, the Facebook pixel will not be able to set any cookies until the visitor has opted in.

If you manually placed the pixel code on pages (e.g., by editing your site header HTML), HubSpot will not be able to control the visitors Facebook is able to set cookies on.

For additional information, refer to Facebook’s business tools terms and Facebook’s cookie consent guide.

Cookies from third-party systems

HubSpot cannot control cookies placed by third-party scripts on your website. When a visitor accepts cookies through the HubSpot consent banner, they consent to HubSpot’s cookies only.

However, you can put code in place to know when a visitor has accepted or declined HubSpot cookie tracking, then send that information to your third-party system. Learn more about using HubSpot’s consent banner for third-party scripts.

External scripts

If you’re placing external scripts on your site, refer to HubSpot’s developer documentation to learn more about associating these scripts to the cookie banner.

Other information

Learn about removing the cookies created by the HubSpot tracking code that are included in the consent banner under data privacy. When a visitor’s cookies are removed, the visitor will be considered “new” and will see the cookie policy banner the next time they visit your site.

Visitors who visited your website before your cookie policy banner was set up will already have the cookies created by the HubSpot tracking code in their browser. They will, therefore, not see the cookie policy banner until their cookies are removed or expired.

If you use the HubSpot tracking code, your visitors’ data is collected and used to monitor your website traffic. HubSpot also uses certain data collected from the HubSpot tracking code to improve HubSpot’s products and services, including the Breeze Intelligence commercial dataset. You can turn off data sharing with HubSpot for your account by navigating to your account settings. Learn more about the data that’s collected by the HubSpot tracking code.

Cookies set on HubSpot’s websites

HubSpot is committed to privacy and protecting individual rights on the internet. When you visit HubSpot’s websites, sign up for a HubSpot account, attend a HubSpot virtual event, or request more information about HubSpot, HubSpot automatically collects information using tracking technologies, such as cookies and tracking pixels.

HubSpot may use cookies or similar technologies (such as web beacons and JavaScript) to analyze trends, administer the website, monitor how visitors navigate through websites, and gather demographic information about HubSpot’s user base. Learn more about how HubSpot uses cookies on its websites and how to manage your cookie preferences.

Learn about cookies

HubSpot websites use different types of cookies. Some cookies are necessary for the websites and services to function properly. Others are optional and help HubSpot to perform analytics, provide different functionality, or engage in targeted advertising.

Please note: tracking pixels (e.g., ptq.gifs) are used to record anonymous data, such as page views and clicks. These don’t store any personal information and aren’t considered cookies.

Below is a list of the types of cookies that may be set on your browser when you visit a HubSpot website.

Necessary cookies

Necessary cookies are cookies that are required for HubSpot’s sites to function properly. The table below includes examples of necessary cookies.

Cookie name

Vendor

Purpose

__cfduid

Detection of malicious actors.

__cf_bm

Cloudflare

Cookie placed on end-user devices that access customer sites protected by Bot Management or Bot Fight Mode. This cookie is necessary for these bot solutions to function properly.

__cfuvid

Cloudflare

First-party cookie used by Cloudflare, a content delivery network, to identify individual clients behind a shared IP address. It helps Cloudflare optimize application performance, identify trusted web traffic, and mitigate malicious attacks. This cookie doesn’t store personally identifiable information and doesn’t correspond to any user ID within the web application

HubSpot

Used by the cookie banner to remember not to ask the visitor to accept cookies again.

_hs_cookie_cat_pref

Saves the preferences chosen by the visitor from the cookie banner.

HubSpot

Session-based cookie platform to show and group individual user sessions in an anonymous and non-identifiable way, to allow HubSpot.com to work properly. It’s discarded at the end of a session.

Verifies the user’s email for log-in purposes to the HubSpot product.

Necessary for login to the HubSpot product

Allows the user to access the app with the correct permissions.

Test cookie HubSpot uses to identify if the user’s browser accepts SameSite Lax cookies. It helps determine if HubSpot can make the Hubspotapi cookie SameSite Lax in the future, which is currently set as SameSite None.

HubSpot

Used with the Hubspotapi cookie to remember whether the user checked the remember me box (controls the expiration of the main cookie’s authentication).

Hubspotapi-strict

HubSpot

Similar to Hubspotapi-lax, a test cookie that HubSpot uses to identify if the user’s browser accepts SameSite Strict cookies. This determines if HubSpot can make the Hubspotapi cookie SameSite Strict in the future, which is currently set as SameSite None.

hs_langswitcher_choice

HubSpot

Sets browser language for users.

Hubspotutk

HubSpot

Tracks a visitor’s identity. It’s passed to HubSpot on form submission and used when deduplicating contacts. It contains an opaque GUID to represent the current visitor.

gbu9uvfhph6a0mdatwbzomssrlboczvs

E-Hawk Talon

Used to prevent fraudulent signups on sign-up pages. Expires at the end of the session.

AWSALB

Amazon Web Services (AWS)

Load-balancing cookie used by Amazon Web Services (AWS) to manage traffic distribution across multiple instances of an application.

It’s generated and managed by the Application Load Balancer and helps route traffic to the most appropriate server to ensure a smooth user experience, especially during periods of high traffic.

AWSALBCORS

Amazon Web Services (AWS)

Used by websites to ensure a smooth and efficient user experience. It was created by Amazon as part of its web services unit for applications that use load balancers. This particular cookie acts like a traffic controller, performing the function of load balancing.

LiSESSIONID

Khoros

Session management cookie, often set by sites using the Khoros platform or similar. It is used to identify a user’s session on a particular community or website, ensuring that the user remains logged in across multiple pages.

This cookie is typically associated with the user’s session and expires when the session ends.

LithiumVisitor

Khoros

Used by Khoros to compute billing visits, registered billing visits, visits, registered visits, and unique visitors metrics. The cookie is encrypted and stores when it was first issued, when it was last seen by Khoros, and a unique visitor ID (unique per visitor’s browser).

cg_uuid

CHEQ

This server-side cookie hosted by cheqzone.com detects when the same device is used in a separate browser session, ensuring consistent blocking of fraudulent or malicious sessions. This cookie lasts for up to 365 days.

Functionality cookies

Functionality cookies are used to enhance the performance of a website. They’re non-essential cookies controlled by the cookie banner. Without them, certain website functions may not be available.

If you’re a visitor to a HubSpot site, you can opt out of funtionality cookies or manage your cookie preferences using the options provided in the cookie banner or the Manage cookies link in your browser.

Analytics cookies

Analytics cookies are non-essential cookies controlled by the cookie banner. They’re used to track how users navigate and interact with the website. The information collected is used to help us improve the website.

If you’re a visitor to a HubSpot site, you can opt out of analytics cookies or manage your cookie preferences using the option provided in the cookie banner or the Manage cookies link in your browser.

Cookie name

Vendor

Purpose

The main cookie used by Google Analytics. Enables the service to distinguish one visitor from another.

Tracks sessions. This is used to determine if HubSpot should increment the session number and timestamps in the __hstc cookie. It contains the domain, viewCount (increments each pageView in a session), and session start timestamp. It expires in 30 minutes.

__hssrc

HubSpot

Whenever HubSpot changes the session cookie, this cookie is also set to determine if the visitor has restarted their browser. If this cookie doesn’t exist when HubSpot manages cookies, it’s considered a new session. It contains the value “1” when present. Expires at the end of the session.

HubSpot

The main cookie used for tracking visitors. Contains the domain, HubSpotutk, initial timestamp (first visit), last timestamp (last visit), current timestamp (this visit), and session number (increments for each subsequent session). Expires in six months.

Used to determine and save whether the chat widget is open for future visits.

It’s set in your visitor’s browser when they start a new chat, and resets to re-close the widget after 30 minutes of inactivity.

Stores referral data for the current visitor. This data includes the source of the referral (e.g., domain name), the medium used (e.g., email, social media), and any search terms associated with the referral. The cookie is overwritten each time a visitor comes from a new referrer.

Advertisement cookies

Advertisement cookies are ad-pixel cookies (such as Facebook, LinkedIn, and Google). They’re used to track user behavior and gather insight to deliver tailored ads.

If you’re a visitor to a HubSpot site, you can opt out of advertisement cookies or manage your cookie preferences using the options provided in the cookie banner or the Manage cookies link in your browser.

You may have certain rights regarding the collection and use of your data under applicable data protections laws including, but not limited to, the California Consumer Privacy Act. Create data privacy request pages for specific brands

If you manage multiple brands within your HubSpot account, you can create distinct data privacy request pages for each brand. This feature helps you deliver consistent, on-brand experiences to your customers and streamlines how your team tracks data privacy requests across brands. When a brand’s data privacy request form is submitted, you can filter requests by brand, all from your data privacy request page.

Please note: while these features live in HubSpot, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific situation.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to configure and manage data privacy request settings.

Create data privacy request pages for specific brands

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.

  • Click Data privacy request page.

  • Hover over a brand, click Actions, then select Configure.

  • In the data privacy request page editor, you can select the data request options that you’d like to offer your contacts:

    • To allow contacts to request the permanent deletion of their personal data, toggle the Delete contact data switch on.
    • To allow contacts to request a copy of their data, toggle the Export contact data switch on.
    • To add a field for contacts to select their location, toggle the Country switch on.
    • To turn on CAPTCHA for your request page, toggle the ReCAPTCHA switch on. CAPTCHA adds a step to verify that a visitor isn’t a robot, before they can submit the request. HubSpot uses reCAPTCHA v2 for spam prevention.
    • In the Business email field, enter an email address. The email address will be used in the verification email sent to users, to ask questions about data privacy.
    • In the Email sending domain field, select the domain that will be shown in the From field of verification emails.

  • After setting up your page, in the top right, click Publish page. Learn more about managing data privacy request pages.

Filter data privacy requests by brand

Once you’ve created distinct data privacy request pages for specific brands, you can view and filter data requests by brand.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.
  • At the top, click the Data request manager tab.
  • To add a brand quick filter, click More at the top of the table and select Brand.
  • To filter requests by brand, click the Brand dropdown menu and select a brand.
  • Continue to manage your data privacy requests.

Customize cookie banner styling

Once you’ve set up your consent banner, you can customize how your cookie banner will appear on your website. Customize style options include the banner’s position, shape, colors, and button style.

Permissions required Website settings permissions are required to customize cookie banner styling.

To customize your cookie banner:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Privacy & Consent.
  • Navigate to the Cookies tab.
  • Click the domain name of the domain’s banner you’d like to customize.
  • In the Consent Banner Options section, click Customize.
  • To preview your changes on a specific banner, in the left panel, select a banner in the Preview on a specific banner dropdown menu. You can only preview one banner at a time, but any changes made will apply to all banners under a domain.
  • To customize the position where your banner will be displayed, click Banner Position. Select one of Center, Bottom, Bottom Left, Bottom Right, or Top.
  • To customize the background style of your banner, click Background Style.
    • Select the Shape of your banner, the Background color, and the Padding and Width.
    • To add a dismissal button to the banner, click to toggle the Dismissal button switch on.
  • To customize the font style for your banner, click Font Style. Click the font color to choose a custom color or select from your brand colors.
  • To customize the style of the buttons on your banner, click Button Style.
    • Select the Shape of your buttons and customize the colors for your buttons and the font on the buttons.
    • Click the background, font, or border color to choose a custom color or select from your brand colors.
  • If your banners allow opt-in/opt-out by category, you can also customize your cookies by category pop-up. To do this, navigate to the Cookies by Category tab.
  • To customize the background style of your cookies by category pop-up, click Background Style. Select the Shape of your banner, the Background color, Font color, and the Padding and Width.
  • To customize the style of the buttons on your cookies by category pop-up, click Button Style.
    • Select the Shape of your buttons and customize the colors for your buttons and the font on the buttons.
    • Click the background, font, or border color to choose a custom color or select from your brand colors.
  • To customize the style of the categories on your cookies by category pop-up, click Categories style.
    • Select the Shape of your categories and customize the colors for your background, font, and toggle.
    • Click the background, font, or toggle color to choose a custom color or select from your brand colors.
  • To reset the styling of any category, click Reset next to that category.
  • In the top right, click Save and Exit.

If you don’t opt in, your HubSpot account will be migrated automatically through a phased rollout. This automatic migration began on May 11, 2026, and is rolling out to a percentage of accounts at a time until all are migrated. Learn more about this change on HubSpot’s changelog.

A cookie consent banner allows visitors to opt in or opt out of being tracked in your HubSpot account with cookies. This feature works for all HubSpot pages as well as any external pages with your HubSpot tracking code installed.

Super Admins and users with permission to edit website settings can customize visitor cookie tracking and consent banners to comply with global data protection laws and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).

Please note: while HubSpot has cookie tracking and consent banner settings, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific business circumstances.

Add a cookie policy

The following instructions apply to the v1 cookie consent banner editor. If you’ve opted in to the new consent banner, learn how to set up and edit cookie consent banners.

Please note: if you’re using a cookie-blocking extension, you may see a blank page on the Cookies tab. To resolve this, turn off the extension or use an incognito window.

To add a cookie policy in the v1 cookie consent editor:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Privacy & Consent.
  • Click the Cookies tab.
  • Click Add policy.
  • Set up the following configuration details:
    • Enter the Policy label, which is the name that’ll display in your HubSpot account.
    • Enter the domain to which the policy will be assigned.
    • To set a subdirectory for a more targeted banner, enter a URL path. For example, if the French version of your website is hosted on the /fr subdirectory, enter fr.
    • Select the countries in which the banner will be displayed to visitors. The visitor’s browser IP address determines which country they’re in. If you don’t select any countries, the banner will be displayed to all visitors.
    • To never allow cookie tracking for the pages or countries specified, select the Decativate cookies checkbox. If you select this, you don’t need to set up the notification settings. Click Publish to finish creating the policy.
  • Set up the notification settings:
    • To inform visitors that your site uses cookies, toggle the Notify visitors that your site uses cookies switch on. Customize the notification fields.
    • To require users to opt in to cookie tracking, toggle the Require opt-in switch. Customize the opt-in fields.
    • To show visitors the cookies that will be placed on their browser by category, toggle the Display cookies by category switch on. Customize the category fields. Learn more about the cookies and their categories.
  • Click Publish.

Edit default privacy and consent text

When you include data privacy and consent information on forms, scheduling pages, and documents, visitors can consent to receiving communications and to the storage and processing of their data. Customize the default privacy and consent text displayed to visitors and manage the text for different languages.

Please note: while these features live in HubSpot, your legal team is the best resource for compliance advice for your specific situation.

Permissions required Edit account defaults permissions are required to edit default privacy and consent text.

Before you get started

  • Edits made to the default consent text will apply to all new data privacy-enabled forms and scheduling pages created moving forward. Customizations made to individual forms and scheduling pages will override these default settings.
  • If the default text is edited, existing forms won’t be automatically updated. To update an existing form, delete the current data privacy options field from the form, and re-add it to include the updated wording.
  • For legacy forms, edit the consent text directly on each form.

Customize default privacy and consent text

Customize the default privacy and consent text displayed on forms, scheduling pages, and documents.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Privacy & Consent.
  • Click the Consent options tab.
  • To view and edit consent text for a specific language, click the Current language dropdown menu and select a language.
  • Next to the consent text you want to customize, click Edit.
  • In the right panel, update the consent text in the text box.
  • If you’re editing the Consent to communicate text, click the Subscription type dropdown menu and select a subscription type.
  • Click Save.

Review privacy and consent options

  • Legitimate interest: let your visitors know that they can unsubscribe from your communications at any point if they’re no longer interested in hearing from you, and link to information about unsubscribing and your privacy practices if applicable.
  • Privacy policy: give your visitors information about your privacy policies and practices, and offer a link to more information if applicable.
  • Consent to communicate: give your visitors information about how and why you’d like to contact them, and let them know that you’re offering them the option to consent to that communication.
  • Consent to process data: depending on the settings chosen on your individual forms or scheduling pages, visitors will see the explicit or implicit consent to process data language.
    • Explicit consent: let visitors know that they need to check the box to consent to the storing and processing of their personal data.
    • Implicit consent: let visitors know that by submitting their information, they are consenting to the storing and processing of their personal data.

HubSpot consent banner | Frequently asked questions

Find answers to the most commonly asked questions about website consent management tools in HubSpot.

General

How does HubSpot track website visitor activity?

HubSpot uses cookies to track your website visitors and contacts. A cookie is a small text file that is left behind on a visitor’s browser when they come to your site. When the HubSpot software runs on your website, it leaves behind a cookie on your visitors’ browsers that helps HubSpot identify them on future visits.

Should I adjust my privacy policy?

If your business has a presence in Europe, or if you store any data on contacts in the European Union (EU), you must adjust your privacy policy to comply with EU laws. The EU has mandated that member countries create laws that require websites to gain consent from end users prior to storing data on a website visitor’s computer. These regulations are designed to help your website visitors protect their privacy and determine how their behaviors online are used by others.

Under the GDPR, if a contact of yours is an EU citizen, they must be given notice that you’re using cookies to track them (in a language they can understand), and they need to consent to being tracked by cookies. You can set this privacy policy in HubSpot, show it to your visitors, and prompt them to consent to allow cookies to comply with EU regulations.

Please note: while HubSpot provides cookie tracking and consent banner tools, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific business circumstances. In addition, while these features help to enable compliance, there’s no one solution that fits every situation. Learn more in the HubSpot GDPR Playbook.

What’s the difference between first-party and third-party cookies?

First-party cookies are set and stored by a website’s domain. Often times, these cookies are used to collect analytics data, remember language settings, or store shopping cart contents. Information collected by first-party cookies doesn’t leave the website.

Third-party cookies are set by a server outside of the website’s domain and are commonly associated with website functionality and ad targeting. Information collected by third-party can be used by companies outside of the website you’re visiting.

Are HubSpot’s cookies first-party or third-party?

The HubSpot tracking code script drops first-party cookies. Though the HubSpot tracking code collects data to personalize the site visitor’s experience, the data is not shared across websites and it belongs only to your HubSpot account.

Learn more about which cookies HubSpot sets in a visitor’s browser.

Implementation

Why is my consent banner not appearing?

The consent banner may not be displayed for the following reasons. For each reason, review the steps to fix the issue:

  • Visitors are using browser settings or extensions that automatically clear cookies, which can remove the consent banner preference cookies. You cannot bypass this, but can verify your settings are configured correctly to display the banner to other visitors.
  • Your external page doesn’t have the HubSpot tracking code installed. To fix this, you must install the HubSpot tracking code. If your account was created after November 2022, you’ll need to add your external domain to your consent management settings.
  • Your external page URL doesn’t match the path rules configured in your cookie policy. To fix this, ensure that the external page URL matches the domain and URL path rules in your cookie policy.
  • You’ve targeted specific countries and visitors are using location-altering tools like a VPN. If you want to continue targeting specific countries, you can’t bypass this. If you want to show the consent banner to all visitors regardless of location, remove the targeted countries.
  • The Deactivate cookies or Allow all cookies setting is turned on in the consent banner’s advanced settings. When either of those settings are on, the banner won’t appear. If turned on, turn the setting off.
  • Your site has conflicting code that’s hiding the banner. For example, display: none or visibility: hidden. Remove or fix conflicting code.
  • You’ve already clicked Accept on the consent banner. If you’ve accepted cookies, the banner may not appear again on the page because it has already received and remembered your consent. To allow visitors to reopen the banner, add a Cookie Settings button to the consent banner.
Why is my consent banner appearing in an iframe?

A consent banner that is configured to target all URLs will load on all pages that contain your HubSpot tracking code. Because an iframe embeds a page within another page, an iframe embedded page with the tracking code is expected to load the consent banner too.

You can resolve this by configuring your consent banner to only appear on specific domains and URLs. Alternatively, you can remove the HubSpot tracking code from the page being loaded in the iframe. Be aware that removing the tracking code will remove tracking capabilities from that page if it’s being used elsewhere outside of the iframe.

Why is my consent banner reappearing after accepting/declining?

This issue may occur for a couple reasons:

  • The visitor may be using a browser setting or extension to automatically clears cookies, which may be removing the consent banner preference cookies.
  • If you’re embedding a page with an iframe, the SameSite flag restricts the iframe page from being able to read or set cookies on its domain when it differs from the parent page’s domain. As a result, HubSpot will be unable to store the banner preference selected in the iframe.
How can I manage HubSpot cookies with a third-party consent banner?

Unless you’re using the Cookiebot integration, managing HubSpot cookies with a third-party banner requires a custom developed setup, such as:

  • Using the consent banner API to manage HubSpot cookies through the third-party banner.
  • Using a combination of CSS and JavaScript to hide HubSpot’s banner from the visitor, then configuring the third-party banner’s button clicks to correspond with HubSpot banner button clicks. This would enable you to automatically set HubSpot consent banner preferences through your third-party banner without displaying both to visitors.
Why are HubSpot cookies loading without accepting cookie consent?

If HubSpot cookies are loading before consent has been collected, it’s likely that your consent banner policy type is set to Notification. Instead, ensure that your banner is set up to either require opt-in and/or Allow opt-in by category. You can update this setting any time within each banner’s settings.

Learn more about setting up your consent banner.

Manage consent for email open and click tracking

Use consent-based email tracking to collect and manage recipients’ consent for email open and click tracking. You can record and update tracking consent in HubSpot and allow contacts to manage their consent from their subscription preferences page.

When consent-based email tracking is turned on, HubSpot checks the email tracking consent status associated with each recipient email address before tracking opens and clicks. Recipients who have given consent are tracked, while recipients who have declined consent or don’t have a recorded consent status aren’t tracked. Consent-based email tracking applies to supported emails sent through HubSpot and connected email accounts.

For example, if you’re required to collect prior consent before tracking email opens and clicks, contacts can provide consent through their subscription preferences page. HubSpot records their email tracking consent status and applies it to future email tracking.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the Consent Email Tracking Capabilities beta.

Please note: this article provides guidance about requiring consent to track emails in HubSpot and is not intended as legal or compliance advice. Learn more about email tracking guidelines for obtaining prior consent and consult your legal team to determine the requirements that apply to your specific situation.

Permissions required Super Admin or Partner Admin permissions are required to turn on consent-based email tracking and set email tracking consent statuses.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, review the following requirements, limitations, and considerations that apply to this beta.

Requirements

If you’re sending one-to-one emails using the HubSpot Sales Chrome extension, refresh Gmail to ensure you’re using the latest version of the extension (3.3.4.44739).

Limitations & considerations
  • Email tracking consent applies across brands. You cannot set a separate email tracking consent status for each brand. When a recipient’s status changes, the new status applies to emails sent through HubSpot regardless of the associated brand.
  • HubSpot forms do not support the collection of email tracking consent through the data privacy fields or through the Email tracking consent property. Instead, you can add a custom property to your form, then use a workflow to update the email tracking consent status when the form is submitted.
  • Email tracking consent statuses cannot be imported directly. If you’re importing contacts with email tracking consent information from another platform, you can import that information into a custom property. After importing, update the contacts’ email tracking consent status in bulk from the contacts index page, segments, or workflows.
  • Email tracking consent statuses cannot be updated through the HubSpot API.
  • Email tracking consent settings don’t currently apply to CTAs embedded in marketing emails. CTA views and clicks are recorded through a separate CTA tracking system. To respect a recipient’s email tracking consent, use a button with a URL or add hyperlinks directly to the email body instead of embedding a CTA.

How consent-based email tracking works

When consent-based email tracking is turned on, HubSpot uses each recipient’s email tracking consent status and your tracking settings to determine whether to track email opens and clicks:

  • Email tracking turned on: HubSpot tracks opens and clicks only for recipients whose email tracking consent status permits tracking.
  • Email tracking turned off: HubSpot doesn’t track opens or clicks, regardless of the recipient’s email tracking consent status.
Email tracking consent status

The email tracking consent status is associated with an email address rather than a contact. If a contact has multiple email addresses, HubSpot checks the consent status of the email address receiving the email to determine whether to track opens and clicks.

The email tracking consent status contains the following data:

  • Consent status: whether the recipient has consented to tracking.
  • Consent timestamp: the date and time consent was collected.
  • Consent source: where consent was collected.
  • Consent collection method: how the recipient provided consent.

The following consent statuses determine whether tracking is permitted when email tracking is turned on:

Email tracking consent status

Definition

Tracking

Not specified (default)

There’s no record of tracking consent for the recipient. This is the default value when the consent status hasn’t been set and is displayed as -- when viewing the Email tracking consent contact property on the contacts index page, in segments, and on the contact record.

Not tracked

Consent declined

The recipient has explicitly denied email open and click tracking.

Not tracked

Consent given

The recipient has explicitly agreed to email open and click tracking.

Tracked

Consent not applicable

Prior consent isn’t required for email open and click tracking based on the recipient’s location or other applicable circumstances.

Tracked

Please note: when an email address has an email tracking consent status of Not applicable and data privacy settings are turned on, HubSpot uses the contact’s Legal basis for processing contact’s data property to determine whether to track email opens and clicks:

  • Known legal basis: email opens and clicks are tracked.
  • No known legal basis: email opens and clicks are not tracked.

When a recipient’s email tracking consent status is Not specified or Consent declined, HubSpot doesn’t collect open or click events for their emails. This may affect other HubSpot features that rely on email engagement data, such as graymail suppression, workflows, and segments. Learn more about how turning off email tracking affects other HubSpot features.

Supported email types

Consent-based email tracking applies to emails sent through HubSpot or through a connected email account. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Marketing emails, including regular marketing emails, automated emails sent through workflows, and blog/RSS emails.
  • One-to-one emails sent from the CRM or through the HubSpot Sales extension or add-in.
  • Sequence emails.
  • Emails sent through the help desk or the conversations inbox.
  • Transactional emails, including those sent using the single-send API.

Please note: consent-based email tracking is not currently supported for transactional emails sent through the SMTP API.

Set up consent-based email tracking

Turn on consent-based email tracking to manage email open and click tracking based on recipients’ email tracking consent statuses. This setting applies to all email recipients in your CRM. It cannot be limited to recipients in specific countries or regions.

1. Set email tracking consent statuses for existing recipients

Before you turn on consent-based email tracking, it’s recommended to review and update existing recipients’ email tracking consent statuses to ensure the appropriate tracking is applied to future emails.

  • By default, recipients’ email tracking consent status is set to Not specified. When a recipient’s consent status hasn’t been set, this value is displayed as -- when viewing the Email tracking consent contact property. Recipients with this status are not tracked.
  • If you’ve collected tracking consent through a custom property, learn how to update email tracking consent statuses in bulk.
  • If you have recipients who aren’t required to provide prior consent, you can set their status to Consent not applicable. Recipients with this status are tracked based on your email tracking settings.
2. Turn on consent-based email tracking

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, select Privacy & Consent.

  • Toggle the Require consent to track emails switch on.

  • In the dialog box, click I understand.

  • Turn on marketing email tracking and one-to-one email tracking.

After you turn on consent-based email tracking, each recipient’s email tracking consent status is checked when an email is sent. If a recipient’s consent status does not allow tracking, the email is sent without applying open or click tracking.

3. Add the Email tracking consent card to the contact view

After you turn on Require consent to track emails, add the Email tracking consent card to your contact view to manage email tracking consent statuses for individual contacts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, in the Data Management section, click Objects.

  • On the Objects page, click the Select an object dropdown menu and select Contacts.

  • Click the Record Customization tab.

  • Click the contact view.

  • Click the About tab.

  • Hover over the Enrollments section and click + Add card.

  • In the right panel, click the Card library tab.

  • Navigate to the Email tracking consent card and click Add card.

  • In the upper right, click Save and exit.

Learn more about managing cards on the record.

Set email tracking consent statuses in bulk

If you’ve previously collected email tracking consent using a custom contact property, you can use that property to identify contacts who’ve provided consent. For example, create a segment of contacts whose custom property indicates they’ve agreed to email tracking. Then, follow the steps below to update their email tracking consent statuses in bulk.

If you’re collecting email tracking consent using a custom contact property on a HubSpot form, you can use a workflow to automatically update recipients’ email tracking consent statuses when they submit the form.

Please note: the Email tracking consent contact property is automatically set by HubSpot and can’t be edited directly.

Update email tracking consent on the contacts index page
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the contacts you want to update.
  • Click the More dropdown menu, then select Edit email tracking consent.
  • In the right panel, click the Email tracking consent status dropdown menu and select the consent status.
  • Click the Email property values to update dropdown menu and select the email addresses to be updated (e.g., primary email address only or primary and additional email addresses).
  • Click Update.

Learn more about bulk editing records.

Update email tracking consent in a segment

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.

  • Click the name of an existing segment or create a contact segment.

  • Select the checkboxes next to the contacts you want to update.

  • Click the More dropdown menu, then select Edit email tracking consent.

  • In the right panel, click the Email tracking consent status dropdown menu and select the consent status.

  • Click the Email property values to update dropdown menu and select the email addresses to be updated (e.g., primary email address only or primary and additional email addresses).

  • Click Update.

Update email tracking consent using a workflow

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

When you’re updating email tracking consent statuses in a workflow, use the Manage email tracking consent action. The Email tracking consent contact property is automatically set by HubSpot and can’t be updated with the Edit record action.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Select an existing workflow or create a contact-based workflow.

  • Set up your enrollment triggers to decide which contacts are enrolled.

  • Click the add icon to add your workflow actions.

  • In the left panel, click CRM to expand the section, then select Manage email tracking consent.

  • Click the Contact dropdown menu and select the contact whose email tracking consent you want to update (e.g., Enrolled contact or All associated contacts).

  • Click the Set consent to track status to dropdown menu and select the email tracking consent status.

  • Click the Email property values to update dropdown menu and select the email addresses to be updated (e.g., primary email address only or primary and additional email addresses).

  • Click Save.

  • Add any additional actions to your workflow, and edit the workflow settings.

  • In the upper, right click Review and turn on.

Manage email tracking consent for an individual contact

Update email tracking consent statuses and view ‌the status history for individual contacts using the Email tracking consent card. The Email tracking consent contact property is automatically set by HubSpot and cannot be edited directly.

Please note: if the Email tracking consent card isn’t displayed on your contacts, learn how to add the card to your contact view.

Edit email tracking consent

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • Click the name of the contact.

  • In the middle column, click the About tab.

  • In the Enrollments section, navigate to the Email tracking consent card and click View and manage statuses.

  • In the right panel, review the contact’s email tracking consent status for the contact’s primary and additional email addresses.

  • To update a status, hover over the email address and click Update status.

  • In the dialog box, click the Email tracking consent status dropdown menu and select a consent status.

  • Click Update.

View email tracking consent history
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of the contact.
  • In the middle column, click the About tab.
  • In the Enrollments section, navigate to the Email tracking consent card and click View and manage statuses.
  • In the right panel, click the History tab.
  • Review the email tracking consent status and the following details:
    • Updated by: the user who updated the consent status.
    • Update source: how the consent status was updated (e.g., through a workflow or the subscription preferences page).
    • Date: the date and time the consent status was recorded.

Email tracking consent source data is automatically populated by HubSpot and cannot be edited.

Allow contacts to opt in or out of email tracking

After you turn on Require consent to track emails, an email tracking consent checkbox is automatically added to the subscription preferences page. Contacts can use this checkbox to opt in or out of email tracking.

By default, the checkbox is displayed on the subscription preferences page for recipients whose email tracking consent status is Consent given, Consent declined, or Not specified. It’s hidden for recipients whose status is Consent not applicable.

To opt in or out of email tracking, your contacts can take the following steps:

  • Click Manage preferences in the footer of a marketing email to open their subscription preferences page.
  • Select or clear the Can we track opens and clicks on future emails sent to this email address checkbox.
  • Click Update email preferences.

When a contact updates their tracking preference, HubSpot automatically updates the email tracking consent status associated with their email address.

Please note: the email tracking consent status won’t be updated if the recipient accesses the subscription preferences page through a test marketing email.

To manage the email tracking consent checkbox’s language and text:

  • Translation: when using HubSpot’s default email subscription preferences module, the checkbox is automatically translated based on the language of the subscription preferences page. Learn more about creating marketing emails in multiple languages and setting the language of subscription preference links.
  • Customization: to edit the checkbox text, learn how to edit subscription page templates.

Please note:

  • The email tracking consent checkbox is not available for the default unsubscribe settings for one-to-one emails.
  • The email tracking consent checkbox is added to HubSpot’s default email subscription preferences module. If you’re using a custom subscription preference page, you’ll need to include the email subscription preferences module for the email tracking consent checkbox to appear.

Report on email tracking consent activity

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create custom reports

Use the custom report builder to review historical changes to email tracking consent statuses across your CRM. Each time a recipient’s email tracking consent status is updated, HubSpot records a unique event that includes the consent status, timestamp, source, and user who made the update. When creating a custom report, you can track these events using the Communication Subscriptions data source.

For example, if you’re running a historical audit of email tracking consent, you can create a report to review how many consent status updates occurred over a specific period, broken down by consent status or source.

  • Tracking consent updated: an event recorded each time a recipient’s email tracking consent status is updated.
  • Brand: the brand associated with the email tracking consent status. Email tracking consent applies across brands, so this value displays your account’s default brand.
  • Consent status: the recipient’s email tracking consent status at the time of the update.
  • Email: the email address associated with the consent status.
  • Email name: the marketing email associated with the subscription preferences page used to update tracking consent. This field is only populated when the update source is the subscription preferences page.
  • Object_id: the unique ID of the email tracking consent update event.
  • Source: the source of the email tracking consent status update (e.g., workflow, bulk update, or subscription preferences page).
  • Timestamp: the date and time when the consent status was updated.
  • User: the HubSpot user who updated the consent status, if applicable.
  • Workflow: the workflow that triggered the consent status update, if applicable.

Please note: the form and import fields do not contain data based on tracking consent update events.

To create a custom report on email tracking consent activity:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Reporting > Reports. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Reporting > Reports directly.

  • In the upper right, click Create and select Create report.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Custom report. Click Next.

  • Click Create report on your own.

  • Under Primary data source, click the dropdown menu and select Communication Subscriptions.

  • Toggle the Add more data sources switch on if you want to add more data sources. Learn more about selecting data sources.

  • In the upper right, click Next.

  • In the left sidebar, under Communication Subscriptions events, select Tracking consent updated.

  • Click and drag fields from the left sidebar into the Configure tab to build your report. Below is an example configuration for reviewing historical email tracking consent updates over time:

    • Data source: Communication Subscription events
    • Chart type: Vertical bar
    • X-axis: timestamp
    • Y-axis: (Count) tracking consent updated
    • Break down by: Consent status

  • On the Filter tab, click the Event timestamp filter to set the date range you want to audit.

  • In the upper right, click Save report.

The resulting report shows the number of email tracking consent update events over time, broken down by consent status. Learn more about creating custom reports.

Frequently Asked Questions

Find answers to commonly asked questions about managing consent for email open and click tracking.

If a contact opts out of email tracking, will their existing tracking data be deleted?

No. When a contact opts out of email tracking, opens and clicks will no longer be tracked for future emails sent to the contact. Previously collected open and click data remains unchanged.

What happens to email tracking if a recipient’s email tracking consent changes after an email is sent?

If a recipient’s email tracking consent status changes after an email is sent, HubSpot uses the recipient’s current email tracking consent status and the account’s email tracking settings at the time the email is opened or clicked to determine whether to record the email engagement.

For example, if an email was sent when the recipient’s consent status allowed tracking, but their status later changes to Consent declined, an open or click that occurs after the status changes will not be recorded. Similarly, if email tracking is turned off after the email is sent, subsequent opens or clicks will not be recorded.

How is email performance data calculated when some recipients have not given consent to tracking?

When consent-based email tracking is turned on, marketing email open and click rates are calculated using only emails that were both delivered and tracked. Delivered emails that were not tracked because of the recipient’s consent status are excluded from these calculations.

For example, if a marketing email is delivered to recipients with different email tracking consent statuses, only recipients whose emails were delivered and tracked are included when calculating the open and click rates on the marketing email Performance tab.

On the marketing email Recipients tab, you can view the number of tracked and untracked emails to understand how consent-based email tracking affects the email’s recipient data.

Please note: sequence performance data calculations remain unchanged when consent-based email tracking is turned on.

Can email tracking data be collected anonymously when a recipient has not consented to tracking?

No. Anonymous email tracking is not supported in this beta. If a recipient’s email tracking consent status doesn’t allow tracking, email opens and clicks are not tracked for that recipient.

How does email tracking consent affect tracking settings for individual emails?

When Require consent to track emails is turned on, HubSpot tracks email opens and clicks only when email tracking is turned on and the recipient’s email tracking consent status permits tracking. This applies to both account-wide and individual email tracking settings.

For example, if you’ve turned off tracking for an individual marketing email, recipients with a Consent given or Consent not applicable status will not be tracked.

What happens if I turn off the Require consent to track emails setting?

When Require consent to track emails is turned off, HubSpot does not check a recipient’s email tracking consent status. If email tracking is turned on, opens and clicks are tracked regardless of the recipient’s email tracking consent status.

How can I audit changes to the Require consent to track emails setting?

To review when the Require consent to track emails setting was turned on or off, check your account’s audit logs:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left panel, under Account Management, click Audit Logs.
  • Click the Category dropdown menu and select Security Activity.
  • Click the Subcategory dropdown menu and select Email tracking [enabled/disabled].

Learn more about viewing and exporting account activity history.

Can I translate the email tracking consent checkbox on the subscription preferences page?

Yes. If you’re using HubSpot’s default email subscription preferences module, the email tracking consent checkbox is automatically translated based on the language of the subscription preferences page.

Learn more about creating marketing emails in multiple languages and setting the language of subscription preference links.

Can I manage email tracking consent by subscription type?

No. In HubSpot, a recipient’s email tracking consent applies across all subscription types in your account. Email tracking consent is tied to the purpose of tracking (e.g., measuring email engagement), rather than to individual subscriptions.

This approach is based on the following consent principles:

  • Purpose-based consent: consent is given for a specific tracking purpose. This purpose defines how tracking data is used, regardless of the tracking technology or the type of email being sent.
  • Consent withdrawal: withdrawing email tracking consent must be as straightforward as giving it. Consent is managed across subscription types to avoid requiring recipients to withdraw consent separately for each type.
  • Separate consent: consent to receive emails and consent to track emails are separate. For example, recipients should be able to withdraw their tracking consent without unsubscribing from emails.

Learn more about email tracking consent guidelines.

Manage data privacy requests

Set up your data privacy request page where contacts can submit requests related to the management of their personal data. For example, allow contacts to request copies of the data you’re storing or to have their data permanently deleted. For any requests made outside of the page, you can manually create data privacy requests for contacts.

Contact can also request their enriched data to be deleted. By default, all requests from contacts with enriched data must be received.

Please note: while HubSpot provides this feature, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific situation.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to configure and manage data privacy request settings.

Set up a data privacy request page

Configure and publish a data privacy request page for contacts who visit your website to request actions related to their personal data. If you manage multiple brands, learn how to configure a data privacy request page for each brand.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.

  • In the Data privacy request page section, click Configure.

  • In the page editor, set up your data privacy request page:

    • To allow contacts to request the permanent deletion of their personal data, toggle the Delete contact data switch on.
    • To allow contacts to request a copy of their data, toggle the Export contact data switch on.
    • To add a field for contacts to select their location, toggle the Country switch on.
    • To turn on CAPTCHA for your request page, toggle the ReCAPTCHA switch on. CAPTCHA adds a step to verify that a visitor isn’t a robot, before they can submit the request. HubSpot uses reCAPTCHA v2 for spam prevention.
    • In the Business email field, enter an email address. The email address will be used in the verification email sent to users, to ask questions about data privacy.
    • In the Email sending domain field, select the domain that will be shown in the From field of verification emails.
    • Click Publish page.

Share, update, or unpublish a data privacy request page

After creating your data privacy request page, you can share the page. You can also update your data request options or unpublish the page.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.
  • To update an existing data privacy request page, click Edit.
  • To share the data privacy request page, click Copy next to the page URL.
  • To unpublish an existing data privacy request page, click Unpublish page. In the dialog box, click Unpublish to confirm.

Manually create data privacy requests

Manually create data privacy requests for contacts who made requests without using the form, such as in-person or on a call.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.

  • At the top, click the Data request manager tab.

  • Click Create new request.

  • In the right panel, set up your data request:

    • Select the contact that you’d like to create the request for.
    • Select the data request type. You can select from Data deletion, Data export, and Enriched data deletion.
    • Select the request date. This is the date that the data request should be completed by.
    • Select the owner. This is the user assigned to action the data privacy request.
    • Click Create new request.

Assign and action data privacy requests

After publishing your data privacy request page, review and manage data privacy requests from the data request manager. Complete requests by exporting contact data, permanently deleting a contact, or deleting enriched contact data. For enriched data delete requests, you can action them manually or automatically delete the data.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.
  • At the top, click the Data request manager tab.
  • On the Data privacy request manager page, you can navigate to different views or create a custom view. Learn how to create and manage saved views.
  • In each view, you can use the dropdown menus at the top to filter your data requests.
  • To assign or reassign an owner to a request:
    • Hover over the owner column in the request. Then, click Assign or Reassign.
    • In the dialog box, click the Owner dropdown menu and select a HubSpot user. Then, click Assign or Reassign. Data privacy requests can only be assigned to Super Admins.
  • To take action on a request, click the request. In the right panel, follow the instructions to complete the request, then confirm the action in the dialog box.
  • To take action on multiple requests of the same type, select the checkboxes of the requests. Click the action at the top of the table, then follow the instructions in the dialog box. This will only be available if all selected requests have the same recommended action. For example, select all Data deletion requests, then click Delete contact data at the top of the table.
  • To mark multiple requests as completed, select the checkboxes of the requests, then click Mark as completed at the top of the table. In the dialog box, click Mark as completed to confirm.

Automatically action enriched data delete requests

To automatically delete the enriched data whenever a contact requests you delete their enriched data, the Delete enriched data when request is received setting should be turned on. When turned on, these requests will be automatically actioned to delete the enriched data, and you’ll receive an email when a request is processed.

To turn on the setting:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.
  • Toggle the Delete enriched data when request is received switch on.

To turn off the setting:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under Account Management, select Privacy & Consent.
  • Toggle the Delete enriched data when request is received switch off.

Manage data privacy settings in your HubSpot account

Data privacy laws, such as General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), exist to enhance the protection of individuals’ data. These laws also increase the obligations of organizations that collect or process personal data.

Data privacy settings provide a central location for turning on features that support compliance efforts throughout your account.

Please note: while these features live in HubSpot, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific situation.

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit account defaults permissions are required to turn data privacy settings on or off.

Turn on data privacy settings

To turn data privacy settings on for your account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Privacy & Consent.
  • Toggle the Data privacy settings switch on.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes, turn on data privacy settings.
Review and edit data privacy compliance settings

To limit marketing emails to contacts with consent to communicate:

  • In the Data privacy settings section, click Recommended next steps to stay compliant.
  • Toggle the Limit emails to contacts with a subscription switch on. This setting is recommended to comply with GDPR and other privacy laws.

To change the default legal basis to communicate for customer support surveys:

  • In the Record your reason for sending your contacts customer support surveys section, click Change reason.
  • In the dialog box, click the Default legal basis for surveys dropdown menu and select an option.
  • In the Explanation for permission or consent field, enter an explanation.
  • Click Save.

The following occurs in your account when data privacy settings are turned on. In certain cases, you’ll need to make manual edits to existing content.

  • The cookie consent banner is turned on. Click Edit consent banner to make changes.
  • Scheduling pages will include data privacy messaging. Scheduling pages created before data privacy settings are turned on will not be updated automatically. Click View meeting pages to manually add data privacy messaging.
  • Newly created forms will include a data privacy section in the footer of the forms. For existing forms, add notice and consent information for each form.
  • Unsubscribe links are turned on for one-to-one and sequences emails for users that don’t yet have them turned on.
  • You can add communication consent and legal basis for processing to contacts through a record import, bulk edit, or manual contact creation.
  • One-to-one email opens and clicks will not be tracked for contacts without a value for legal basis for processing contact’s data.
    • If you’re using the HubSpot Sales extension or add-in, banners on contact records will be displayed notifying you if a contact doesn’t have a legal basis for processing.

Turn off data privacy settings

For EU accounts (i.e., data storage is based in the EU), data privacy settings are turned on by default. It’s recommended to keep the settings on to help your account remain compliant with GDPR, but you can turn them off if needed.

To turn data privacy settings off in your account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Privacy & Consent.
  • Toggle the Data privacy settings switch off.
  • In the dialog box, review the changes that’ll occur in your account, then click Turn off data privacy settings to confirm.

Please note: if you turn off data privacy settings, the cookie consent banner will not be automatically turned off.

Delete contacts

Under data privacy laws such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), contacts in your account have the right to request that you delete all of their personal data.

Permanent delete functionality is available to all accounts, even if data privacy settings are turned off. When deleting a contact you’ll have two options:

  • Restorable delete a contact to keep the option to restore within 90 days.
  • Permanent delete the contact to comply with GDPR and other data privacy laws.

Manage data retention policy settings for inactive contacts

Data privacy laws, such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), include principles like data minimization and storage limitations, which advocate for not retaining personal data longer than necessary.
