HubSpot user permissions guide

Permissions define how users can work within HubSpot tools they have access to through their seat. Super Admins can set user permissions to control what users can view, create, edit, or delete in an account. For example, you can give a sales rep permission to communicate only with contacts they own, while allowing a sales manager to communicate with all contacts.

You can also limit edit access to properties and assign content access for specific users.

Learn more about user permissions by joining a small group coaching session

Permissions required Super Admin or users with Add and edit users permissions are required to customize permissions.

CRM

On the CRM tab, set permissions for CRM objects and tools.

To manage user permissions for your conversations inbox, review the documentation on how to create a conversations inbox.

CRM objects

The following CRM objects and activities have customizable permissions:

  • Contacts
  • Companies
  • Deals
  • Leads
  • Orders
  • Carts
  • Tickets
  • Tasks
  • CRM emails
  • Meetings
  • Calls
  • Notes
  • Custom objects

To customize which objects or activities the user can create, view, edit, and delete, click the object (e.g. Contacts, Companies, etc.) to expand the section.

Depending on the object, you can select from the following permissions:

  • View: click the dropdown menu to control the set of objects or activities the user can view.
    • The options are All [objects], Their team’s [Objects], and Their [Objects].
    • When selecting Their team’s [Objects] or Their [Objects], you can select the Unassigned checkbox to allow the user to view unassigned records or activities.
    • Users with Their [Objects] permissions will only see their assigned records on index pages, in the segments tool, and in reports.
  • Edit: click the dropdown menu to control the set of objects or activities the user can edit. Users with Edit access can also merge records (BETA).

    • The options are All [objects], Their team’s [Objects], Their [Objects], and None.

    • When selecting Their team’s [Objects] or Their [Objects], you can select the Unassigned checkbox to allow the user to edit unassigned records or activities.

  • Create: toggle the create switch on to control the set of objects the user can create (including importing).

Please note: the Create permission specifically controls the user’s ability to create new records. It does not apply to records that are created through other HubSpot tools or integrations, such as via workflows, form submissions, inbox conversations, email tracking or logging, and Salesforce imports.

  • Delete: click the dropdown menu to control the set of objects or activities the user can delete.

    • The options are All [objects], Their team’s [Objects], Their [Objects], and None.
    • When selecting Their team’s [Objects] or Their [Objects], you can select the Unassigned checkbox to allow the user to delete unassigned records or activities.

  • Merge (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and custom objects): click the dropdown menu to control the set of objects the user can merge.

    • The options are All [objects], Their team’s [Objects], Their [Objects], and None.
    • When selecting Their team’s [Objects] or Their [Objects], you can select the Unassigned checkbox to allow the user to merge unassigned records.

Please note:

  • To delete a single record or multiple records in bulk from an object’s index page, users will need bulk delete permissions.
  • View permissions are not the same as a View-only Seat. Learn more about the different seat types and what they give a user access to.
  • Users with Edit permissions can delete activities on a record. You must remove their Edit permissions if you don’t want them to have this ability.
  • Users with View permissions can still create notes or tasks on records of that object. Users must have Communicate permissions to edit notes or tasks on those records, associate activities with other records, or create other activities, such as emails, calls, and meetings.
  • Ownership permissions are based on the default owner properties and custom HubSpot user field type properties. Users who are set as the owner with either type of property have owner access to the record. Users with [Objects] their team owns permissions can access records owned by any members of their assigned teams.
CRM Tools

Customize access to bulk actions, property settings, and the workflows tool.

  • Communicate: click the dropdown menu to control the contacts, companies, deals, tickets, tasks, and individual custom objects a user can log an email, call, or meeting to, as well as associate these activities with other records.
    • The options are All records, Records their team owns, Records they own, and None.
    • When selecting Records their team owns or Records they own, select the Unassigned checkbox to allow the user to communicate with unassigned contacts and companies.
    • This permission setting only applies to CRM emails, not marketing emails. Learn more about setting permissions for marketing emails.
  • Bulk delete: toggle the Bulk delete switch on to let the user bulk delete contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and tasks. This would allow the user to delete contacts from within a segment or in a board view, for example. Users without this permission can still delete contacts, company, deals, tickets, and tasks from individual records if they have the Edit permission for that CRM object. Users with this permission can also delete leads in the prospecting workspace.
  • Import: toggle the Import switch on to let the user import CRM records in bulk or one at a time in your HubSpot account.
  • Export: toggle the Export switch on to let the user export CRM records and reports from your HubSpot account.
  • Export without approval: toggle the Export without approval switch on to let the user s export CRM records from your account without approval.
  • Approve exports: toggle the Approve exports switch on to let the user approve exports by other users.
  • Edit customer tasks: toggle the Edit customer tasks switch on to let the user view, edit, and delete tasks assigned to contacts.
  • Edit associations: toggle the Edit associations switch on to let the user add, edit, and delete associations and association labels on existing records. To change associations when working in a record, the user will also need Edit access for records.

Please note: users without this permission can still add associations when they manually create a record using the create form (e.g., when creating contacts).

  • Enrich records: toggle the Enrich records switch on to let the user update record properties and add companies from buyer intent with enrichment data from HubSpot.
  • Custom views (Professional and Enterprise only): toggle the Custom views switch on to let users create, edit, and delete custom views in the inbox.
  • Create CRM views: toggle the Create CRM views switch on to allow the user to create new views on CRM index pages for contacts, companies, deals, and other CRM objects. By default, all users have permission to create views. Toggle the switch off to prevent the user from creating or cloning views while still allowing them to use existing views.
  • Customize record page layout: toggle the Customize record page layout switch on to let the user update the content and appearance of the record layout.

Marketing

On the Marketing tab, set permissions for marketing publishing tools.

  • Brand settings: toggle the Brand settings switch on to give the user access to view or edit brand identity (including brand kits) and brand voice.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view brand settings, but not create or edit them.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create and edit brand kits and brand voice.
  • Segments (previously Lists): toggle the Segments switch on to give the user access to the segments tool.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view segments, but not create or edit them.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create and edit segments. To add records to a static segment, a user also needs Edit access for contacts and companies.
  • Forms: toggle the Forms switch on to let the user access the forms tool.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view forms and form submission data.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, publish, and delete forms.

Please note:

  • To create and connect a support form to a channel, a user must have the Account Access permission.

  • To edit a form’s follow-up email, a user must have the Marketing Email Publish permission.

  • Delete form submissions: toggle this switch on to let the user delete submissions on individual forms. To turn this permission on, the user needs access to edit forms first.

  • Files: toggle the Files switch on to let the user view, edit, and delete files in the files tool. Within the files tool, you can also limit access to individual files, folders, or subfolders to specific users and teams.

    • View: the user will be able to review existing files. The user will not be able to edit existing file details.
    • Edit: the user will be able to upload new files, review existing files, and edit file details. However, the user will not be able to delete files. Learn more about [managing your file details](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/files/organize-edit-and-delete-files?hubs_content=knowledge.hubspot.com/files/manage-your-users-file-access&hubs_content-cta=managing%20your%20file%27s%20details).
    • Delete: the user will be able to upload new files, review existing files, edit file details, and delete files. Learn more about [deleting and restoring files](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/files/archive-delete-restore-files?hubs_content=knowledge.hubspot.com/files/manage-your-users-file-access&hubs_content-cta=deleting%20and%20restoring%20files).
    • No access: if none of the options are turned on, the user will not have access to the files tool, and will not be able to review, edit, or delete existing files. However, users will still see the Files option in the navigation bar and have access to the file picker in other editors.

  • Marketing Access: toggle the Marketing Access switch on to let the user access marketing tools, such as the email tool or opting contacts out of marketing emails. This also lets the user access Website activity on contact records. With Marketing Access switched on, you can turn on more specific marketing tool permissions.

Marketing tools
  • Ads: toggle the Ads switch on to give the user access to the ads tool.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view ad account activity.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user connect accounts from supported ad networks.
  • Campaigns: toggle the Campaigns switch on to give the user access to campaigns.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view campaigns.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user manage campaigns and assets.
  • Marketing email: toggle the Marketing email switch on to give the user access to marketing emails.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view marketing emails, but not edit or publish them.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create emails, delete emails, edit the default values for email personalization, and send test emails. However, they cannot send marketing emails to contacts or save emails for automation to use in workflows.

    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish, send marketing emails, and save emails to use in workflows.

Please note:

  • A user must have at least View access to unbounce a contact.

  • A user must have at least View access and Website settings permission to configure email footer and styling settings.

  • To publish resubscription emails, a user must have the Website settings permission.

  • CTA: toggle the CTA switch on to give the user access to CTAs.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view CTAs.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete CTAs.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish CTAs.

Please note: to create CTAs (legacy) a user must have Edit or Publish access for Blog, Email, Landing pages, or Website pages.

  • SMS: toggle the SMS switch on to give the user access to SMS.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view SMS messages in your account.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete SMS messages in your account.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and send SMS messages in your account.
  • Lead Scoring: toggle the Lead Scoring switch on to let the user view and create scores for your marketing leads.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view lead scores in your account.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete lead scores in your account.
  • Buyer Intent: toggle the Buyer Intent switch on to give the user access to configure settings in buyer intent such as target markets, intent criteria, intent recommendations, auto-add, and email digests. Users will also need this permission to create and edit saved views in buyer intent.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view buyer intent content in your account.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user edit buyer intent content in your account.
  • Social: toggle the Social switch on to give the user access to social posts.

    • Publish: click the dropdown menu to control the social accounts the user can publish to. Users with All accessible accounts, Their connected accounts, or Draft only social permissions can see all shared social accounts in social monitoring, publishing, and reports, as well as any social accounts they connected.

      • All accessible accounts: the user can publish to social accounts they connected, or to any shared social accounts. The user can also configure social settings.
      • Their connected accounts: the user can only publish to social accounts they connected.
      • Draft only (Marketing Hub Enterprise only): the user cannot publish to any social accounts, but can create draft social posts in social accounts they connected or any shared social accounts.
      • None: the user has no access to the social tool, which will not appear in the navigation menu when they are logged in.

    • Approve: toggle the Approve switch on to let the user approve requests to publish social posts.

Website tools
  • Blog: toggle the Blog switch on to give the user access to blog content.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view blog content.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete blog content, as well as create and edit blog authors. However, they cannot publish new posts or update live posts.

    • Manage private content: toggle the Manage private content switch on to let the user publish private blog posts.

    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update blog content.

Please note: to view the SEO tool, a user must have at least View access to Email, Blog, Landing pages, or Website pages. To make updates to the SEO tool, a user must have at least Edit access to Email, Blog, Landing Pages, or Website pages, or have access to Website settings.

  • Podcasts: toggle the Podcasts switch on to give the user access to podcasts.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view podcast content.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete podcast content. However, they cannot create new podcast episodes or update live podcast episodes.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update podcast content.
  • Case Studies: toggle the Case Studies switch on to give the user access to case studies.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view case studies.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete case studies
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update podcast content.
  • Landing pages: toggle the Landing pages switch on to give the user access to landing pages.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view landing page content.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete landing page content. However, they cannot create new pages or update live pages.

    • Manage private content: toggle the Manage private content switch on to let the user publish private landing pages.

    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update landing page content.

  • Website pages: toggle the Website pages switch on to give the user access to website pages.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view landing website page content.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete website page content. However, they cannot create new pages or update live pages.

    • Manage private content: toggle the Manage private content switch on to let the user publish private website pages.

    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update website page content.

  • Content Remix: toggle the Content Remix switch on to give the user access to the content remix tools.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user review existing content remixes.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete content remixes and remixed content.
  • HubDB (Content Hub only): toggle the HubDB switch on to give the user access to HubDB table customization settings. You must turn on HubDB table settings to create, clone, and delete tables.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user see data within the table rows and export data. However, they cannot add additional data.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user add rows to a table, clone locked rows, import data, and export data.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user add new rows, edit existing rows, and delete rows from a table.
  • Content embed: toggle the Content embed switch on to give the user access to create and manage content embeds.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view content embeds.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete content embeds.
    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update content embeds.
  • URL Redirects: toggle the URL Redirects switch on to give the user access to URL redirects.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view redirected URLs.
    • Publish: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete URL redirects
  • Design tools: toggle the Design tools switch on to let the user edit templates and modules. Users with this permission can also access the template marketplace and save marketing emails as templates.
  • Content staging: toggle the Content staging switch on to let the user access the [content staging tool](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/website-pages/redesign-and-relaunch-your-site-with-content-staging?hubs_content=knowledge.hubspot.com/user-management/hubspot-user-permissions-guide&hubs_content-cta=content%20staging%20tool).

Please note: it’s recommended to also give a user Global content settings and Website Settings permissions if they’ll need to edit global web assets and blog/website settings.

Approvals

Customize permissions to approve content publishing. Approvals must be turned on for each tool.

  • Approve marketing emails: toggle the switch on to let the user approve requests to publish marketing emails.
  • Approve blog posts: toggle the switch on to let users approve requests to publish blog posts.
  • Approve landing pages: toggle the switch on to let users approve requests to publish landing pages.
  • Approve website pages: toggle the switch on to let users approve request to publish website pages.

Sales

On the Sales tab, set more granular permissions and restrictions for sales tools such as the prospecting agent, sales templates, and meeting scheduling pages. You can also assign sales seats.

Prospecting agent
  • Prospecting agent assignment: toggle the switch on to let users assign contacts and companies to the prospecting agent for monitoring and outreach.
  • Prospecting agent admin: toggle the switch on to let users configure the prospecting agent, including creation, modification, and deletion of selling profiles.
Sales access
  • Sales Access: toggle the Sales Access switch on to let the user access sales templates, snippets, documents, calling, and the meetings tool. With the switch on, more granular permissions will appear for HubSpot’s sales tools.
    • Templates: toggle the Templates switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete templates. Users with assigned Sales Hub and Service Hub paid seats that do not have permission to create and edit templates will still be able to view and send templates.
    • Documents: toggle the Documents switch on to let the user upload and manage sales documents.
    • Meeting scheduling pages: toggle the Meeting scheduling pages switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete scheduling pages for other users. A user must also have Personal email access toggled on.

Please note:

  • Once you toggle on Sales Access, the permissions listed below will be dependent on the subscription tier of your seat.

  • If you’ve assigned all of your paid seats, you can click Purchase another user to upgrade a user. Learn more about managing paid Sales Hub users.

    • Forecast: customize View and Edit access to the sales forecast tool. Updating forecast permissions in Sales will also update permissions in Service.
      • Users with Forecast they own permissions can only view their own forecasts.
      • Users with Forecast their team owns permissions can see their own forecasts as well as their teammates within that team.
    • Playbooks: customize View, Edit, and Publish access to the sales playbook tool. Updating forecast permissions in Sales will also update permissions in Service.
    • Sequences: toggle the Sequences switch on to give users access to sequences.
      • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view sequences.
      • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create and edit sequences.
      • Delete: toggle the Delete switch on to let the user delete sequences.
      • Manage private content: toggle the Manage private content switch on to let the user view, edit, and delete private sequences.
    • Bulk enroll sequences: toggle the Bulk enroll sequences switch on to let users bulk enroll multiple contacts at the same time into a sequence.
    • View connected record data: toggle the View connected record data to give users access to view data from connected account(s) when using multi-account management.

Revenue

On the Revenue tab, set permissions for products, line items, quotes, quote templates, payments, contracts, credit memos, invoices, payment links, and subscriptions.

Product and pricing information
  • Create custom line items: toggle the switch on to let the user create line items from a deal record or quote when using the line item editor. If using the API to create custom line items, this doesn’t apply.
  • Products: toggle the Products switch on to give the user access to the product library.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view products in the product library.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user edit products in the product library.

    • Delete: toggle the Delete switch on to let the user delete products in the product library.

Quoting

  • Quotes:

    • Approve quotes: toggle the switch on to let users approve quotes.
    • Manage quote templates: toggle the switch on to let users manage quote templates for quotes or legacy quotes.
Payments
  • Manage payments and subscriptions: toggle the switch on to let the user view transaction history, download reports, send receipts, issue refunds for payments, and cancel subscriptions.
  • Manage payment links: toggle the switch on to let the user manage one-time and recurring payment links.
Billing and adjustments
  • Contracts: toggle the Contracts switch on to give the user access to contracts.
    • View: click the dropdown menu to select which contracts the user can view. The options are All contracts, Their team’s contracts, and Their contracts.
    • Create: toggle the Create switch on to allow the user to create contracts.
    • Edit: click the dropdown menu to control the set of contracts the user can edit. The options are All contracts, Their team’s contracts, and Their contracts.
    • Delete: click the dropdown menu to control the set of contracts the user can delete. The options are All contracts, Their team’s contracts, and Their contracts.
  • Credit memos: toggle the Credit memos switch on to give the user access to credit memos.
    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view credit memos.
    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user edit credit memos.
  • Invoices: toggle the Invoices switch on to give the user access to the invoices.
    • View: click the dropdown menu to select which invoices the user can view. The options are All invoices, Their team’s invoices, and Their invoices. Select the unassigned checkbox to allow the user to also view unassigned invoices.
    • Edit: click the dropdown menu to control the set of invoices the user can edit. The options are All invoices, Their team’s invoices, Their invoices, and None. Select the unassigned checkbox to allow the user to also edit unassigned invoices.
    • Delete: click the dropdown menu to control the set of invoices the user can delete. The options are All invoices, Their team’s invoices, Their invoices, and None. Select the unassigned checkbox to allow the user to also delete unassigned invoices.
  • Subscriptions: toggle the Subscriptions switch on to give the user access to the subscriptions.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view subscriptions.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user edit subscriptions.

    • Delete: toggle the Delete switch on to let the user delete subscriptions.

Service

On the Service tab, set more granular permissions and restrictions for service tools such as feedback surveys and knowledge base articles, as well as assign [paid Service Hub seats](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/account-management/manage-seats?hubs_content=knowledge.hubspot.com/user-management/hubspot-user-permissions-guide&hubs_content-cta=paid%20Sales%20Hub%20seats).

  • Service Access: toggle the Service Access switch on to let the user access feedback surveys, knowledge base articles, templates, and the meeting tool. With the switch on, more granular permissions will appear for HubSpot’s service tools.

    • Feedback surveys: toggle the Feedback surveys switch on to give the user access to feedback surveys.

      • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view feedback surveys.
      • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete feedback surveys.

    • Knowledge base settings: toggle the Knowledge base settings switch on to give the user Publish access to the knowledge base tool. When this switch is toggled on, the Knowledge base articles switch and the associated switches are automatically turned on.

      • Knowledge base articles: toggle the Knowledge base articles switch on to give the user edit access to knowledge base articles. Users will need knowledge base settings access to create knowledge base articles.

        • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user edit knowledge base articles.

        • Manage private content: toggle the Manage private content switch on to let the user publish private knowledge base articles.

        • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish and update knowledge base articles.

        • Approve: toggle the Approve switch on to let the user approve knowledge base articles.

    • Templates: toggle the Templates switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete templates. Users with assigned Sales Hub and Service Hub paid seats that do not have permission to create and edit templates will still be able to view and send templates.

    • Meeting scheduling pages: toggle the Meeting scheduling pages switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete scheduling pages for other users. A user must also have Personal email access toggled on.

    • Customer agent editor: toggle the Customer agent editor switch on to let the user create, edit, and manage customer agent configurations.

Please note:

  • The permissions listed below will be dependent on the subscription tier of your seat.

  • If you’ve assigned all of your paid seats, you can click Purchase another user to upgrade a user. Learn more about managing paid Service Hub users.

    • Forecast: customize View and Edit access to the forecast tool. Updating forecast permissions in Service will also update permissions in Sales.
      • Users with Forecasts they own permissions can only view their own forecasts.
      • Users with Forecasts their team owns permissions can see their own forecasts as well as their teammates within that team.
    • Playbooks: customize View, Edit, and Publish access to the service playbook tool. Updating forecast permissions in Service will also update permissions in Sales.
    • Sequences: toggle the Sequences switch on to let users create sequences.

      • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view sequences.

      • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create and edit sequences.

      • Delete: toggle the Delete switch on to let the user delete sequences.

      • Manage private content: toggle the Manage private content switch on to let the user view, edit, and delete private sequences.

      • Bulk enroll sequences: toggle the Bulk enroll sequences switch on to let users bulk enroll multiple contacts at the same time into a sequence.

    • View connected record data: toggle the View connected record data to give users access to view data from connected accounts when using multi-account management.
    • Manage Customer Success Settings: toggle the Manage Customer Success Settings switch on to create shared views, pin reports for all users, and create or edit customer health scores.
    • Edit workforce management: toggle the Edit workforce management switch on allow users to edit the availability status, working hours, out of office hours, and capacity limits of other users from the workforce management tool in help desk.

Data Management

  • Data Studio: toggle the Data Studio switch on to give the user access to the data studio tool.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let user view the datasets without making changes. They can also activate datasets for reporting.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user edit datasets and activate them for only reporting.

    • Use: Toggle the Edit switch on to let the user use datasets for activations that use HubSpot Credits - (i.e, workflows, list, sync to CRM, and trade).

  • Data quality tool access: toggle the Data quality tool access switch on to give the user access to the data quality tools.
  • Data enrichment access: toggle the Data enrichment access switch on to give the user access to enriching records and add companies from buyer intent.
  • Data Agent access: toggle the Data Agent switch on to give the user access to the data agent tools and smart properties.

Automation

  • Workflows: toggle the Workflows switch on to give the user access to workflows.

    • View: toggle the View switch on to let the user view workflows.

    • Edit: toggle the Edit switch on to let the user create, edit, and delete workflows. To toggle on this setting, the user must have the View permissions turned on as well.

    • Publish: toggle the Publish switch on to let the user publish workflows. To toggle on this setting, the user must have the View and Edit permission turned on as well.

    • Enroll: toggle the Enroll switch on to let the user manually enroll records.

      • Users with Enroll permission only can enroll records into workflows from CRM cards or any record index pages.
      • Users with both View and Enroll permissions can enroll records directly from workflows. Learn more about manually enrolling records in workflows.
      • If a user has Edit but no Enroll permission, they will not be able to enroll records, even when editing the workflow. The option to enroll records that currently meet the enrollment criteria after editing a trigger on a workflow, or when turning on a workflow will not appear.

    • Delete: toggle the Delete switch on to let the user delete workflows. The user must have the Edit permission turned on as well.

  • Chatflows: toggle the Chatflows switch on to let the user create, edit, and publish chatflows in your HubSpot account.

Reporting

On the Reporting tab, you can give the user the permissions to create, edit, and view dashboards, reports, and analytics tools. If turned off, the user won’t see Reports in the navigation menu when they are logged in.

  • Goals: toggle the Goals switch on to let users view, create, and edit goals. Click the View and Edit dropdown menus to control the level of access users have to view, create, and edit goals. Users must have an assigned seat to be assigned goals.
  • Data quality tools access: toggle the Data quality tools access switch on to let non-Super Admin users access the data quality command center to monitor and clean data quality issues.
  • Reports Access: toggle the Reports Access switch on to let the user access reporting tools, including dashboards, reports, and analytics tools. With the switch on, more granular permissions will appear for HubSpot’s reporting tools.

    • Dashboard, reports, and analytics: toggle the Dashboard, reports, and analytics switch on to let the user access reporting tools

      • View: lets the user view dashboards, reports, and analytics tools. This is selected by default when the Reports access switch is toggled on.

      • Edit: lets the user edit dashboards, reports, and analytics tools that they have access to. This will be selected if you grant permission to the user to create and own.

      • Create/own: lets the user create and own dashboards and reports.

      • Admin: toggle the Admin switch on to let the user create any report or dashboard. This permission also gives access to all analytics tools and will override any settings in the Reports permission tab.

    • Marketing reports: toggle the Marketing reports switch on to let users access marketing reports in HubSpot’s analytics tools. This includes traffic analytics, page performance, competitors, tracking URL builder, events (Marketing Hub Enterprise only), and reports settings.

    • Multi-Account reports access: toggle the Multi-Account reports switch on to let users view reports containing data from multiple HubSpot accounts. This includes access to the data that’s surfaced in these reports. Learn more about multi-account reports.

      • If the user doesn’t exist in the other accounts, they’ll have view-only access to data that’s surfaced in the report.
      • If the user exists in the other accounts in the report, the data they can view in the report is determined by their permissions within each of those accounts.

    • Custom events: toggle the Custom Events switch on to let users view, edit, and delete custom events data.

AI features

On the AI features tab, give users permissions to use Breeze Assistant and create and activate agents and assistants.

  • Breeze Assistant: toggle the Breeze Assistant switch on to allow users to chat with Breeze Assistant.
  • Breeze Assistant Admin: toggle the Breeze Assistant Admin switch on to allow users to view and delete saved prompts for all Breeze Assistant users.
  • Agent Builder: toggle the Agent Builder switch on to allow users to create, edit, and activate agents and assistants, as well as tools and knowledge vaults.
  • Customer agent editor: toggle the Customer agent editor switch on to allow users to create, edit, and manage customer agent configurations.

Account

On the Account tab, you can set more granular permissions for account administration.

Settings access
  • Modify billing and change name on contract: toggle the Modify billing and change name on contract switch on to let the user view the account information, company information, transactions, and important documents. The user will also need this permission to buy new paid seats and assign paid seats in the account. The user will also need this permission to pause the prospecting agent.
  • Marketing contacts access: toggle the Marketing contacts access switch on to let the user set contacts as marketing contacts or non-marketing contacts.
  • Personal email access: toggle the Personal email access switch on to let the user connect their individual work email to send and track 1:1 emails from the CRM, to access Meeting scheduling pages, and to connect their calendar to HubSpot. Once they connect their inbox, they’ll also be able to use the HubSpot Sales extension.
  • App Marketplace access: toggle the App Marketplace access switch on to let the user install apps from the HubSpot Marketplace and third-party websites. Certain integrations will still require specific permissions.
  • App Marketplace Uninstall access: toggle the App Marketplace Uninstall access switch on to let the user uninstall apps.
  • Template Marketplace access: toggle the Template Marketplace access switch on to let the user install modules and templates from the HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Permanently delete contacts: toggle the Permanently delete contacts switch on to let the user permanently delete contact records. To delete contacts, the user will also need the contact delete permission on the CRM tab.
  • Edit property settings: toggle the Edit property settings switch on to let the user create, edit, and manage access to object properties. This permission will also give the user access to create and edit pipelines or stages.
  • Custom data translations: toggle the Custom data translations switch on to let the user turn on custom translations, export a file with translations keys, and import translations.
  • Subscription Type settings: toggle the Subscription Type settings switch on to let the user create, edit, and manage subscription types.
  • HubDB table settings: toggle the HubDB table settings switch on to let the user configure table settings and create, clone, unpublish, or delete HubDB tables.
  • Global content and theme settings: toggle the Global content and theme settings switch on to let the user edit global content and themes for website content.
  • Website settings: toggle the Website settings switch on to let the user edit website settings. This will also give the user the ability to update the SEO tool and manage the email account settings.
  • Knowledge base settings: toggle the Knowledge base settings switch on to let the user edit the knowledge base settings. This permission will also give the user Publish access to the knowledge base tool by default.
  • Customer Portal settings: toggle the Customer Portal settings switch on to let the user edit the customer portal settings. This permission will also give the user Publish access to the customer portal tool by default.
  • Domain settings: toggle the Domain settings switch on to let the user connect and edit domains.
  • Developer tools access: toggle the Developer tools access switch on to let the user access and manage developer features, including: app management, developer projects, [development sandboxes](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/crm), standard sandboxes, personal access keys for CLI authentication, and developer test accounts.

Please note:

  • While the Developer tools access permission enables access to these tools, a developer will still require additional permissions depending on what they’re building. For example, a developer would need Create custom line items permission if they’re building a private app that will create line items for invoicing.

  • If you had previously set a developer as a Super Admin and want to migrate them to the new developer permissions, it’s recommended to start with the Developer permission template. The template will include a set of permissions that are commonly needed when developing on HubSpot beyond access to the developer tools.

  • User table access: toggle the User table access switch on to let the user view the user table in their HubSpot account settings.

Please note: if the User table access switch is off, users will still be able to view users elsewhere in their HubSpot account (e.g., when reassigning a contact to another owner).

  • Audit log access: toggle the Audit log access switch on to let the user access audit logs.
  • Availability Management: toggle the Availability Management switch on to let the user edit team member availability.
  • Security Center access: toggle the Security Center access switch on to allow users to manage security health.

Please note:

  • Even if access to specific assets has been restricted to certain teams or users, Super Admins still have the ability to view them.
  • Assets, such as templates, sequences, documents, and playbooks, can only be viewed by Super Admins, and the teams and users who have access. Super Admins also need a a paid Sales or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat to view sequences and playbooks.
  • A CMS Hub or Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription is required to limit access to blog posts and pages by teams.
User & account access
  • Account Access: toggle the Account Access switch on to let users access the ability to manage user settings for your account. Users with this permission can view any conversations inbox in the account, but can’t take actions in the inbox, such as replying to a thread, unless they are added as a team member. They can, however, reply to inbox emails directly from the record.
    • Add and edit users: toggle the Add and edit users switch on to let a user add new users, deactivate, or remove existing users from your account. You need Modify billing permissions to assign paid seats. You won’t be able to assign permissions you don’t have.
    • Add and edit teams: toggle the Add and edit teams switch on to let users organize users into different groups that you can use to control access, filter reports, and more.
    • Limit access by teams: toggle the Limit access by teams switch on to let users share assets with other users. Users with this permission have access to all assets no matter what team they’re on.
    • Presets: toggle the Presets switch on to let users configure users and teams within your account to choose defaults like home screen, dashboard, and language.
    • Edit account defaults: toggle the Edit account defaults switch on to let users set your account’s name, branding, new user defaults, language, time zone, data privacy settings, and default date and number format. If you’re in a Professional or Enterprise account and are using multiple currencies, you have to be a Super Admin to edit the account’s default currency.

Please note: you must be a Super Admin to access private apps.

If you have a Marketing Hub subscription, an in-app banner will appear when you’ve reached 98% of your Marketing Contacts tier limit. To remove this banner, you must turn off Modify billing and change name on contract permissions.

Super Admin

Super Admin permissions give access to all the account tools and settings detailed in this article, except for paid Sales Hub or Service Hub features, which require a Sales or Service seat.

  • If you have a paid subscription, Super Admins must have a Core, Sales, or Service seat.
  • Super Admins can also [create and manage scheduling pages](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/meetings-tool/create-and-edit-scheduling-pages?&_ga=2.99965022.1172001715.1636377977-1688256857.1636377977#create-meetings-links) for the other users in the account. Super Admin permission sets aren’t modifiable.
  • If you remove a user as a Super Admin, their level of access will be altered depending on what new permissions they are assigned.
  • Only a Super Admin can set another user as a super admin.
  • Only a Super Admin can access the [Communications index page](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/view-and-filter-records#:~:text=Communications%3A%20In%20your%20HubSpot%20account%2C%20navigate%20to%C2%A0CRM%C2%A0%3E%C2%A0Contacts%2C%20then%20click%20the%C2%A0Contacts%C2%A0dropdown%20menu%20and%20select%C2%A0Communications.%20This%20index%20page%20is%20only%20accessible%20to%C2%A0Super%20Admins%C2%A0and%20it%20displays%20LinkedIn%2C%20SMS%2C%20and%20WhatsApp%20messages.).

Please note: the key difference between a Super Admin and a user with all permissions assigned is that Super Admin can do virtually anything in the account; users with all permissions but not Super Admin status may not be able to control features that are outside of the scope of the permissions panel.

If a Super Admin is required to complete a task or process, it’s recommended to have an existing Super Admin complete the task instead of updating an individual user’s permissions. To set a user as a Super Admin:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, hover over the user record. Then click the Actions dropdown menu for the user, and select Make Super Admin.

Partner Admin

Partner Admin permissions can only be granted to HubSpot Solutions Partner employees working in your account. Partner admins have similar access to Super Admins. Review the differences in the table below:

  • Targeted admin permissions needed for HubSpot Solutions Partners to serve customers.

  • Ability to add and remove other super admins
  • Management of account billing and financial transactions

  • Partner Admins do not need to be assigned a paid Sales Hub or Service Hub seat to access the features.

In addition, Partner Admins do not have access to the following features:

  • [SCIM user provisioning through Okta.](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/user-management/provision-hubspot-users-with-scim-through-okta#:~:text=Set%20up%20SCIM%20provisioning,application%20in%20your%20Okta%20account.)
  • Authorization for apps that can create, update, or delete users
  • Migration to other data centers

Learn how to set a HubSpot Solutions Partner employee as a Partner Admin.

Partner account

On the Partner Program tab, you can give a user access to partner tools in your HubSpot account and designate them as a Partner employee in client portals. By default, all new users in a partner account won’t be given access to partner tools until the Partner tools switch is toggled on.

  • Partner Admin: toggle the Partner Admin switch on to let verified Partner employees manage your account and add or edit other Partner employees. This permission requires a Partner Seat which is only available to external Partner employees who are managing your account.
  • Partner Client object: toggle the Partner Client object switch on to let the user access your HubSpot clients data and collaborate with HubSpot.
    • View: let the user view your HubSpot clients data.
    • Edit: let he user edit your HubSpot clients data.
  • Partner Services Object: toggle the Partner Services Object switch on to let the user access your HubSpot client service data and collaborate with HubSpot.
    • View: let the user view your HubSpot client service data.
    • Edit: let the user edit your HubSpot client service data.
  • Partner tools: toggle the Partner tools switch on to give the user access to partner tools.
    • Partner dashboard: toggle the Partner dashboard switch on to give the user access to view and manage the partner dashboard.
    • Partner commission access: toggle the Partner commission access switch on to let the user access payment information in the Partner Commission App.
    • Client access manager: toggle the Client access manager switch on to let the user manage your employees’ client account access from one place.
    • Solutions directory: toggle the Solutions Directory switch on to give the user Edit access to the directory.
    • Partner Portability: if you’re opted into the Partner Portability beta, toggle the Partner Portability switch on to give the user the ability to copy assets to client accounts.

Log in as another HubSpot user

Super Admins in accounts with two-factor authentication or a passkey set up on their HubSpot account can log in as another user in their HubSpot account to troubleshoot issues, verify access to tools, or update basic profile information. When you log in as a user, you’ll see the account from their perspective, which helps you confirm permissions, settings, and visibility.

For example, you can log in as a team member to confirm they have access to a specific tool, assist with troubleshooting, or a user’s name or profile picture. All logins are recorded in the security activity history export, and the user is notified when a Super Admin accesses their account.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to login as another HubSpot user.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements
  • Signing in through single sign-on (SSO) doesn’t replace the Super Admin’s requirement to set up two-factor authentication or a passkey in HubSpot.
  • It’s not possible to log in as another user who has Super Admin or Modify billing & change name on contract permissions.
  • While logged in as another user, it’s not possible to edit user permissions, manage a user’s profile and preferences or recover the account on behalf of the user.
  • It’s not possible to log in as a user who has not accepted their invite sent when a new user is created.
  • It’s not possible to change a user’s name or profile image if the user is on one HubSpot account.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • When logged in as another user, the session will only remain active for 30 minutes.
  • It’s not possible to bypass two-factor authentication for a user.
  • This feature isn’t available for accounts on a trial subscription.

Log in as another user

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • Hover over the user you want to impersonate, then click the Actions dropdown menu and select Log in as user.

  • Click Log in.

  • An email will be sent to the user to notify them that a Super Admin logged into their profile.

  • While logged in as another user, any actions taken are recorded in the user’s activity log.

  • To switch back to your user account, sign out and log in with your username and password.

Manage notifications from the HubSpot mobile app

Stay informed about your sales, marketing, and service activities on the go with HubSpot mobile notifications. You can turn on and troubleshoot push notifications on your iOS or Android device, so you never miss important updates from the HubSpot mobile app.

Turn on mobile notifications (iOS)

Before you can receive mobile notifications on your iOs device, you must turn on notifications in the settings.

  • When getting started with the HubSpot app, a “HubSpot” Would Like to Send You Notifications prompt will appear. Tap Allow.
  • You can also turn on notifications at any time by opening the Settings app, then tapping Notifications > HubSpot.
  • Tap to toggle the Allow Notifications switch on, then customize your notifications for sounds and alerts.

Learn more about managing notifications on your iOs device.

If you’ve allowed notifications in your iOS settings, but are still not receiving notifications, turn on notifications within the app itself.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • Tap Menu, then tap the settings settings icon in the left sidebar.
  • Tap Notifications. Then tap the activities you’d like to receive notifications for, and tap to toggle on each specific notification.

Turn on mobile notifications (Android)

  • Open Settings on your device.
  • Tap Apps > HubSpot > App notifications or Notifications.
  • Ensure the On or Allow notifications switch is toggled on, or the Block switch is toggled off.

Learn more about managing notifications on your Android device.

If you’ve allowed notifications in your Android device settings, but are still not receiving notifications, turn on notifications within the app itself.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • Tap Menu, then tap the settings settings icon in the left sidebar.
  • Tap Notifications, then turn on notifications accordingly.

Delete and mark notifications as read or unread (iOS and Android)

Please note: marking a notification as unread is only available on Android.

You can mark notifications as read on your device.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • In the top right, tap the notificationIcon Nnnotification icon.
  • In the top right tap the verticalMenuIconmenu icon.
  • Tap Select notifications. You can also select a notification by tapping and holding the notification.
  • Tap the checkbox at the top to select all or tap the checkboxes next to the notifications you want to delete or mark as read.
  • To mark notifications as read, in the top right, tap the emailOpen mark as read icon.
  • To mark notifications as unread, in the top right tap the emailClosed mark as unread icon.
  • To delete notifications, tap the deleteIcon delete icon.

Mute notifications (iOS and Android)

You can mute notifications on your device.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • In the top right, tap the notificationIcon Nnnotification icon.
  • In the top right tap the verticalMenuIconmenu icon.
  • Tap Mute all notifications.
  • Tap the amount of time you want to mute your notifications for.
  • To resume notifications, tap Resume notifications.

Troubleshoot mobile notifications (iOS and Android)

If you’re experiencing issues with HubSpot mobile notifications, check if notification settings are turned off for the HubSpot app on your device.

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.

  • Tap Menu, then tap the settings settings icon in the left sidebar.

  • Tap Notifications.

  • If your notifications are switched off in your settings, tap Open Settings App to turn on notifications for the HubSpot app.

  • If notifications are turned on for HubSpot, return to Settings and tap Troubleshoot Notifications. In Android, you’ll see Running… under the setting.

  • The diagnostic tool will check if your HubSpot app is correctly registered with the HubSpot servers.

    • If it isn’t, you’ll see a dialog box with the message Something went wrong registering your HubSpot app.., and HubSpot will try to register your app again.

    • If notifications are working correctly, you’ll receive a sample notification on your device.

  • Low: push notification, no vibration, no light, and no sound

Manage user out of office hours for help desk

Super Admins and individual users can set out of office availability based on a user’s timezone. When a user is out of office, their availability will be changed to Away and they will not be eligible for automatic assignment in help desk.

Users can manually change their availability status on the user record page or help desk. When a user manually changes their status, it will be reflected across all of the experiences.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are requires to set users’ office hours and manage their availability status.

Set user out of office hours

To set user out of office hours:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record.
  • Click the Preferences tab. Then, in the left sidebar menu, click Working hours.
  • Click the Timezone dropdown menu to select the correct user timezone. Then click Save.
  • Under Out of office, click + Add dates. To set a a time period for when you will be out of office, click the date picker fields and select dates. Use the dropdown menus to select start and end times. To remove dates, click the delete delete icon.
  • Click Save.
  • At the top of the user record, the user’s availability status and working hours for the day will reflect the start and end date of the user’s out of office period.
    • To manually change the availability status, click the User status dropdown menu, then click Available or Away.
    • To edit the working hours, click Edit working hours.

Manage availability status

  • At the beginning of a user’s out of office, their availability status is automatically set to Away. At the end of a user’s out of office, their availability status is automatically set to Available. Users can manually change their availability status before the end of their out of office period to reflect when they are Available. Doing so will prompt the user to confirm if they want to end their out of office block early or continue to be set as Away.
  • To manually change your availability status, navigate to one of the following:
    • User record:
      • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
      • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
    • In the user table, click a user record.
    • At the top of the user record, click the User status dropdown menu, then click Available or Away.
    • In the dialog box, click Yes, set myself as available.
    • Help Desk:
      • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Help Desk. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Help Desk directly.
      • In the bottom-left corner, toggle the switch on or off to change your availability status.
      • In the dialog box, click Yes, set myself as available.

Sync out of office calendar events with HubSpot

If you’re using HubSpot’s calendar sync with Google or Outlook Calendar, you can automatically sync out of office events between your calendar and HubSpot.

To sync out of office events between HubSpot and your Google or Outlook calendar:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record.
  • Click the Preferences tab. Then, in the left sidebar menu, click Working hours.
  • In the Out of office section, select the Sync out of office with your calendar checkbox.

Once this setting is enabled, any newly created or edited out of office blocks on the user’s calendar will automatically sync with HubSpot, and vice versa. This setting will also be used to determine the user’s availability for automatic assignment.

Manage user out of office hours for inbox and help desk

Set out of office availability based on a user’s timezone. When a user is out of office, their availability will be changed to Away and they won’t be eligible for automatic assignment in inboxes or help desk.

Users can manually change their availability status on the user record page, inbox, or help desk. When a user manually changes their status, it’ll be reflected across all of the experiences.

Set user out of office hours

To set user out of office hours:

Permissions required Super Admins permissions are required to set user out of office hours for another user. Users can set their own out of office hours.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • In the user table, click a user record.

  • Click the Preferences tab. Then, in the left sidebar menu, click Working hours.

  • Click the Timezone dropdown menu to select the correct user timezone. Then click Save.

  • Under Out of office, click + Add dates. To set a a time period for when you will be out of office, click the date picker fields and select dates. Use the dropdown menus to select start and end times. To remove dates, click the delete delete icon.

  • Click Save.

  • At the top of the user record, the user’s availability status and working hours for the day will reflect the start and end date of the user’s out of office period.

    • To manually change the availability status, click the User status dropdown menu, then click Available or Away.
    • To edit the working hours, click Edit working hours.

Manage availability status from inboxes or help desk

At the beginning of a user’s out of office, their availability status is automatically set to Away. At the end of a user’s out of office, their availability status is automatically set to Available if their out of office period ends during set working hours. If their out of office period ends outside of working hours or if working hours aren’t set, Users can manually change their availability status before the end of their out of office period to reflect when they are Available. Doing so will prompt the user to confirm if they want to end their out of office block early or continue to be set as Away.

To manually change your availability status, navigate to one of the following:

  • User record:

    • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

    • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

    • In the user table, click a user record.

    • At the top of the user record, click the User status dropdown menu, then click Available or Away.

    • In the dialog box, click Yes, set myself as available.

  • Inbox:

    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Inbox directly.
    • In the top-left corner, toggle the switch on or off to change your availability status.
    • In the dialog box, click Yes, set myself as available.

  • Help Desk:

    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Help Desk. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Help Desk directly.
    • In the bottom-left corner, toggle the switch on or off to change your availability status.
    • In the dialog box, click Yes, set myself as available.

Sync out of office calendar events with HubSpot

If you’re using HubSpot’s calendar sync with Google or Outlook Calendar, you can automatically sync out of office events between your calendar and HubSpot.

To sync out of office events between HubSpot and your Google or Outlook calendar:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record.
  • Click the Preferences tab. Then, in the left sidebar menu, click Working hours.
  • In the Out of office section, select the Sync out of office with your calendar checkbox.

Once this setting is enabled, any newly created or edited out of office blocks on the user’s calendar will automatically sync with HubSpot, and vice versa. This setting will also be used to determine the user’s availability for automatic assignment.

Manage user permissions

Permissions define how users can work within HubSpot tools they have access to through their seat. Set permissions to control what users can view, create, edit, or delete in an account. For example, you can give a sales rep permission to communicate only with contacts they own, while allowing a sales manager to communicate with all contacts. Learn more about each user permission.

View a user’s permissions history to track their permission changes over time.

Before you get started

Before you begin setting user permissions, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations and potential consequences of editing permissions.

Understand requirements

Permissions required Super Admins or Add and edit users permissions are required to edit a user’s permissions.

To edit existing users, you must do the following:

  • Set up your HubSpot account.
  • Create HubSpot users.
  • If users need access to features that require a paid seat, purchase paid seats.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Users with Add and edit users permissions, can only assign the permissions they have. For example, users must be a Super Admin to assign Super Admin permissions. Saving changes may be blocked if the user is assigning permissions they don’t have.
  • Permission updates can take up to five minutes to take effect across HubSpot’s systems.
  • Users need to log out of the account and back in before updates to their permissions take effect. On mobile, users may need to fully close and reopen the HubSpot app for changes to take effect.
  • Seat assignment and Super Admin permissions are separate. Reassigning a seat doesn’t automatically restore Super Admin permissions.
  • When HubSpot adds new permissions to a permission set, existing users will keep their current access and any new permissions added to the set will be turned on by default for them.
  • If permission changes don’t appear in a web browser, users need to log into HubSpot in a private or incognito window. If the permission changes are effective there, the user needs to clear the browser cache and cookies, then reload HubSpot and try again.
  • HubSpot assets can have limited access, which will override permissions.
  • HubSpot Support can’t change user permissions.

Review user permissions

Review a user’s current access on their user record, without opening the editor. Review their seat, which permissions are turned on, the level of access for each, and how they received that access. Use this view to audit user access or troubleshoot access issues.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record, then click the Access tab.
  • In the Access tab, review:
    • Seat: the seat assigned to the user.
    • Permission Sets: the permission sets assigned to the user. If none are assigned, No permission set appears.
    • Permissions: the user’s permissions, shown in a table.
  • In the Permissions section, click a tab to narrow the list by type of access:
    • All: all permissions.
    • CRM Access: permissions for CRM objects.
    • Tool Access: permissions for HubSpot tools.
    • Admin Access: account administration permissions.
  • To filter the table further, use the following options:
    • Click the Status dropdown menu and select All, On, or Off.
    • Click the Area dropdown menu and select an area, such as CRM objects, CRM tools, Custom objects, or Marketing.
    • Click the search icon and enter a permission name.
  • Click Edit permissions to edit the user’s permissions.

Edit user permissions

To edit permissions for existing users:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record, then click the Access tab.
  • Under Permissions, click Edit permissions. You can use the Current view dropdown menu to review user permissions before and after editing them.
  • On the Editing access screen, click to expand the Choose how to set access and Choose permissions sections.
  • Toggle the permissions on and off as needed. Learn more about what each permission gives access to in HubSpot’s user permissions guide.
  • In the top right, click Save.

Edit user permissions for multiple users at once

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • Select the checkbox next to the users whose permissions you want to edit.
  • At the top of the table, click Edit permissions. You can now edit permissions for the selected users as needed.

Please note: users need to have the same seat type to edit them at the same time.

Copy permissions to another user

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the Copy permissions to another user beta.

Copy permissions of one user to another user. This is useful when onboarding multiple users in the same role or backfilling an existing role.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • Next to the user whose permissions are being copied, click the Actions dropdown menu, hover over Manage permissions, and select one of the following options:
    • Copy permissions to new users. Continue adding new users.
    • Copy permissions to… In the dialog box, click the Search for users dropdown menu, and select the users the permissions should copy to. To remove a user from the list, click the X next to the users name. Click Next. Continue editing user permissions.

Create and edit permission sets

Subscription required An Enterprise subscription is required to create and edit permission sets.

With permission sets, you can define preset permissions for your team. Once you’ve created a permission set and specified certain permissions for it, you can assign new and existing users the permission set to grant them the same permissions.

Learn more about creating and editing permission sets.

Compare permissions

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to compare permissions.

You can compare the permissions of users or permission sets (Enterprise only) to see how access differs across your account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • At the top, navigate to the Users tab or the Permission Sets tab.
  • In the table, click the checkboxes next to the users or permission sets you want to compare, then click Compare access.
  • On the Compare access page, scroll down to review the permission differences between the users or permission sets you selected. To change the user or permission set, at the top of the page, click the dropdown menus under Choose a permission set or user.
  • Click the All sections dropdown menu to filter which permissions or user defaults you see. Toggle off Hide similarities to see all permissions.
  • To change permissions for a user or permission set, hover over the permissions on the side of the specific user or permission set, then click Change [name]’s permissions or Manage this custom permission set.

Manage user preferences with presets

With presets, Super Admins and users with Presets permissions can set up default preferences in their HubSpot account so that users don’t have to set them up individually. For example, you can set up the default dashboard, language, and email signature for a group of users.

Users can later change their preferences individually to override presets.

Permissions required Super Admins or Presets permissions are required to manage presets.

Create a preset

To set up a preset:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • Click the Presets tab.

  • Click Create preset.

  • At the top of the page, click the edit pencil icon and enter a name for your preset.

  • On the Setup screen, configure the preset’s default preferences and email signature:

    • On the General tab, use the dropdown menus to select the preset’s default homepage, default dashboard, language, and date and number format.

Please note: if you are enrolled in the HubSpot Home Page public beta, HubSpot Home will be the default landing page for users, unless you choose a different option from the Default Landing Page dropdown menu (formerly Default Homepage dropdown menu).

- To set up the signature that will be used in [one-to-one emails](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/one-to-one-email/send-and-reply-to-one-to-one-emails) sent through the HubSpot CRM, click on the Email Signature tab.
    - Click to toggle the Email Signature switch on to manage email signatures for all users
    - Enter your email signature in the text box.
        - In the Simple editor, use the formatting tools to create your email signature.
        - You can use personalization tokens to populate values based on the user.

        - In the HTML editor, use HTML to create your email signature. To see the variable names of personalization tokens in the HTML, you must first add personalization tokens in the Simple editor, then click HTML to see the variable names.
        - To assign a [notification profile](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/account-management/create-notification-profiles), click the Notifications tab.
        - Click the Notification profile dropdown menu, and select the notification profile for the preset.

  • To select the users or teams to apply to the preset, click the Users & Teams tab at the top of the page:

    • Click the dropdown menu and select the checkboxes next to the users or teams you want to add to the preset.
    • In the upper right, click Save preset. In the right sidebar, review the preset settings, then click Save.

  • To manage personalization tokens, click the Setup tab at the top of the page. Then click the Email Signature tab and Manage email tokens.

    • On the Manage email tokens right panel, click + Add email token and type a set value in the text box. You can add up to 5 email tokens. Tokens can only have lowercase letters (a-z), numbers (0-9), and underscores. They must start with a letter.

    • Once you have created your email tokens, click Save.

    • To assign an email token to a user, on the Presets tab, hover over the preset, click the Actions dropdown menu, and select Assign Email Tokens.

    • To customize users email tokens, click the checkbox next to the users you want to customize, and then click Edit.

    • Under the email token value, type the name you want to populate on the email token for the user.

    • Click Save.

Once a preset has been created, a user can update their personal preferences to override the preset’s preferences.

Manage presets

To edit or delete a preset:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • Click the Presets tab.

  • Hover over the preset, then click the Actions dropdown menu.

    • To edit the preset settings, select Edit, then update the preset settings.
    • To clone the preset, select Clone. Then, enter a name for the new cloned preset.
    • To assign email tokens, select Assign Email Tokens, then assign email tokens to users.
    • To add or remove users from the preset, select Assign Users & Teams. In the right panel, add or remove users or teams from the preset, and click Save.
    • To delete the preset, select Delete, then click Delete preset. Deleting a preset will not affect default settings for any users in the preset.

Manage user properties and preferences

You can view, customize, and manage user properties and preferences for every user in your HubSpot account. Managing user properties and preferences is essential for setting up organizational structure and ensuring proper feature access. For example, you can assign a user to a team for organizational purposes, add a user’s skill for skill-based routing , and set their working hours to manage their availability. This helps ensure your users are making use of HubSpot in the best way for your business.

Learn how to edit a user’s permissions or seats.

Super Admin permissions are required to manage user properties and preferences in your account.

Before you get started

To manage user properties and preferences, you must do the following:

  • Set up your HubSpot account.
  • Create HubSpot users.

View and filter users

In the Users & Teams settings page, you can view your users and filter them using dropdown filters and views. You can also create custom views and assign your own default view.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Click Users & Teams in the left sidebar menu.
  • To view filtered views provided by HubSpot, at the top of the table, click the view tabs.
    • Click + Add view to select a HubSpot-provided view (All Users, AI Teammates, Pending Invites, Deactivated Users, etc).
    • You can create custom views and clone and delete existing ones. Learn more about creating and managing saved views.
  • To filter your users further, click the Status, AI Teammates, Last active, or Advanced filters. Learn more about setting up advanced filters and saved views.
Edit columns of the users table
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Click Users & Teams in the left sidebar menu.
  • In the top right of the table, click Edit columns.
  • In the dialog box:
    • Add properties: add a property as a column. In the Column options section, select the property’s checkbox.
    • Reorder properties: arrange display of the properties. In the Selected columns section, use the dragHandle drag handle to place properties.
    • Remove properties: remove a column. In the Selected columns section, click the x next to a property. If you want to clear all columns, click Remove All Columns.
    • Freeze column above: retain the left most Name column in the view. In the Selected columns section, click the Frozen columns above checkbox if you want users’ names to always stay frozen on the left when you scroll.
  • Click Apply.

You can also change the position of an individual column by using the dragHandle drag handle on the users table.

Review the user table for user-specific data

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • Click Users & Teams in the left sidebar menu.

  • Below the highlight card, scroll through the user table to view the following user-specific information:

    • Name
    • Seat
    • Permission Sets
    • Access
    • Default Team (formerly Main Team)
    • Extra Teams
    • Invite Status
    • Partner User
    • Last Active
    • SCIM Status (Enterprise only)
    • Email Status (Super Admin only)
    • Calendar Status (Super Admin only)
    • Calendar Sync (Super Admin only)
    • Scheduling Pages (Super Admin only)
    • Last Password Change (Super Admin only)
    • To narrow down the users in the table, click the checkboxes next to the users’ names.
    • To filter your data further, click Invite Status, Last active, or Advanced filters. Learn more about setting up advanced filters and saved views.

Bulk edit user properties

An Enterprise subscription is required to set custom user properties.

You can edit user properties in bulk directly from the users table in addition to editing directly from the user record.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
