Review a specific user record

In a user record, you can see an overview of user-specific data, and change the presets, teams, skills, and preferences assigned to them.

View an overview of user-specific data

Subscription required An Enterprise subscription is required to view a user’s audit log.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • Click Users & Teams in the left sidebar menu.

  • On the Overview tab, you can review the following:

Please note: for EU customers, we recommend following your country’s laws regulating employee monitoring. If you would like to turn off this feature, please contact customer support.

Assign presets and teams

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to assign presets and teams.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • Click Users & Teams in the left sidebar menu.

  • On the Setup tab, you can customize and review the following information:

    • Teams: click the Teams tab, then click the Main Team and Extra Teams dropdown menus to assign the user to different teams for organizational and reporting purposes. Learn more about organizing your users into teams. If an account is opted into the Support Multiple Main Teams for Full Functionality beta, you’ll assign a Default team and Teams.
    • Management hierarchy: click the Management hierarchy tab, then click the Manager dropdown menu to assign a manager to the user. You can also click the Direct reports dropdown menu to assign up to twenty direct reports to the user.
Add user skills

Subscription required A Service Hub Enterprise subscription is required to add user skills.

Set user preferences

An Enterprise subscription is required to set custom user properties.

Set user preferences like job title, phone number, time zones, and working hours. If the user is in multiple HubSpot accounts, some preferences can only be updated by the user separately in each account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • Click Users & Teams in the left sidebar menu.

    • Working hours:

Click the category name to see the specific properties.

Manage user working hours and availability for scheduling pages, inbox, and help desk

Super Admins and individual users can set weekly working hours based on a user’s timezone. When a user is outside of their working hours, their availability will be changed to Away and they will not be eligible for automatic assignment in the conversations inbox or help desk. If the user is the host or a team member for a scheduling page that considers working hours for availability, meetings can’t be scheduled outside of their working hours.

Users can manually change their availability status on the user record page, inbox, or help desk. Those with the Availability Management permission can also change the availability status of other team members.

When a user manually changes their status, it’ll be reflected across all of the experiences.

Set user working hours

To set user working hours:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record.
  • Click the Preferences tab. Then, in the left sidebar menu, click Working hours.
  • Click the Timezone dropdown menu to select the correct user timezone, or if you want the time zone to automatically updated based on the device location, select the checkbox.
  • Click Save.
  • Under General working hours, click + Add hours. Use the dropdown menus to select days of the week, and start and end times. To remove a day, click the delete delete icon.
  • Click Save.
  • At the top of the user record, view the user’s availability status and working hours for the day.
    • To manually change the availability status, click the User status dropdown menu, then click Available or Away.
    • To edit the working hours, click Edit working hours.

Set availability status for team members

Manually set a team member’s status to Available or Away:

HubSpot Credits required Availability Management permissions are required to set a team member’s status to Available or Away.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Inbox & Help Desk > Availability Management.
  • In the table, view each user’s name, current availability status, and if you’ve set ticket capacity limits, the number of assigned tickets alongside their capacity.
  • To filter users, click the filters at the top of the table and select a value. Applied filters are visible to all users accessing this view going forward.
  • To remove filters, click Clear filters.
  • Click the user status, then click Available or Away.

Set your availability status from the inbox or help desk

At the beginning of a user’s working hours, their availability status is automatically set to Available. At the end of a user’s working hours, their availability status is automatically set to Away. Users can manually change their availability status during the day to reflect when they are Away.

To manually change your availability status, navigate to one of the following:

Inbox

To manually change your availability status for Inbox, navigate to one of the following:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Inbox directly.
  • In the top-left corner, click the status dropdown menu and select Update status.
Help desk

To manually change your availability status for help desk, navigate to one of the following:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Help Desk. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Help Desk directly.
  • In the bottom-left corner, toggle the switch on or off to change your availability status.

Manage your user profile and preferences

Use your profile and preferences to manage settings that apply only to your user, including your name and profile image, language and date and number format, phone number, default login page, and time zone.

These settings control how HubSpot appears and behaves for you, so you can work in your preferred language and local time without changing the experience for other users in your account. For example, you can display HubSpot in Spanish and schedule emails in your local time zone while your teammates keep their own settings.

Some commonly related settings are managed in other areas of HubSpot:

  • To change the email address used to send one-to-one CRM emails, learn how to connect an individual work email.
  • To change the signature used when you send one-to-one emails through the CRM, learn how to customize your CRM email signature.
  • To change the email address where you receive HubSpot notifications and log in, learn how to change your email address.

To navigate to your account preferences, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then click Profile & Preferences. This will take you to the General section of account settings.

Profile image and name

The profile image, first name, and last name associated with a HubSpot user can only be changed by the user themselves, or a Super Admin who logs in as the user only if that user is on one HubSpot account. Otherwise, users can’t make edits to other users’ names, even if they have the Add and edit users permission.

To change your profile image and first name and last name:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then click Profile & Preferences.
  • Click your current Profile Image, then select from the available options:
    • Upload image: to upload a new image from your computer. Then select your image and use the slider to adjust the image size so that it fits in the circle. To save your changes, click Save.
    • Use Gravatar: to use a Gravatar photo. If you don’t have a Gravatar photo yet, you can click Set up Gravatar photo to add one. Learn more about Gravatar.
    • Remove image: to remove the current avatar image.
  • In the First name field, enter your first name.
  • In the Last name field, enter your last name.
  • Click Save.

Language and date & number format

The language setting controls the language that displays in HubSpot’s user interface. This setting won’t adjust the language in the HubSpot mobile app. To change the mobile app language, adjust your iPhone or Android language settings. Learn more about HubSpot’s language offerings.

To change the language and number format that displays in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then click Profile & Preferences.
  • Click the Language dropdown menu and select a language. Switching your language will automatically adjust your Date & number format.
  • To change the date and number format, click the Date, time, and number format dropdown menu, then select a region.
  • Click Save.

Please note: the date and number format used in personalization tokens in marketing emails and workflows will use the account default settings instead.

Phone number

To set the phone number that’s used to notify you about security events:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then click Profile & Preferences.
  • In the Phone number field, enter your phone number, then click Save.

Defaults

To set the default page when you login to HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click your profile picture in the top right corner, then click Profile & Preferences.
  • On the Profile tab in the Defaults section, click the dropdown menus and select your default page and Brand. These will only apply to you.
  • Click Save.

Time zone

You can set a time zone for your user to automatically display time data in certain tools in your local time. User time zones apply to the scheduling of email, SMS, and social communication, as well as marketing index pages. For example, a marketing executive in Germany can review an email created by a colleague in Canada, see when changes were made, then schedule that email to go out the following morning without worrying about whose time zone is being used.

By default, your user’s time zone will be set to the time zone of your device.

To manually set your user time zone:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record.
  • Click the Preferences tab.
  • Click Working hours in the left sidebar menu.
  • Clear the checkbox next to Update time zone based on device location.
  • Click the Time zone dropdown menu and select a time zone.
  • In the bottom left, click Save.

If you want to change the time zone used by default in your HubSpot account for tools like workflows and reports, learn more about editing your account’s default settings.

If you previously manually updated your time zone, to revert back to adjusting your time zone based on your device location:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, click a user record.
  • Click the Preferences tab.
  • Click Working hours in the left sidebar menu.
  • Select the checkbox next to Update time zone based on device location.
  • In the bottom left, click Save.

Provision HubSpot users with SCIM through Okta

Provisioning users through SCIM (the System for Cross-domain Identity Management) provides a secure and automated way to create and manage HubSpot users through Okta.

If your identity provider is not Okta or Google, you can set up a custom SCIM integration. This allows you to set up SCIM to provision users from providers like Microsoft Entra ID, PingFederate, OneLogin, and JumpCloud. Learn more about setting up SCIM for your identify provider.

Below, learn how to set up user provisioning through Okta.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand requirements
  • Single sign-on (SSO) must be turned on in your HubSpot account.
  • It’s recommended to set up user permission sets in HubSpot based on your team’s Okta Roles before setting up SCIM.
  • To set user permissions, you must create permission sets in HubSpot. Okta can then assign permissions to a user if their Roles in Okta matches the name of the HubSpot permission set.
  • To verify your domain, you’ll need to update your DNS records. Ensure you have the login details for your DNS provider and have access to the TXT records.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Assigning seats will vary depending on whether you’re on the seats-based pricing model:
    • If you aren’t on a seats-based pricing model: to assign seats for users set up with SCIM, purchase the seats in HubSpot and create a permission set with a paid seat. Navigate back to Okta and set the user’s Roles to be the same as the permission set.
    • If you’re using the seats-based pricing model: when a permission set is assigned through SCIM/API, HubSpot automatically assigns the user to the best available seat that supports all permissions in that set.

Set up SCIM provisioning

To set up SCIM user provisioning through Okta, you’ll need to first add the HubSpot app in Okta, then assign users to the app:

  • Log in to Okta.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Applications > Applications, then browse for and add the HubSpot application in your Okta account.
  • In the HubSpot application screen, click the Provisioning tab, then click Configure API Integration.
  • Select the Enable API integration checkbox, then click Authenticate with HubSpot. A new window will open where you can give Okta access to your HubSpot account.
  • In the HubSpot window, select which account you want to integrate Okta with, then click Choose account.
  • Click Connect app. The window will close, and you’ll be directed to the Okta admin console.
  • Click Save.
  • On the Provisioning tab, select how you want Okta to provision users to HubSpot by clicking Edit.
  • Select the Enable checkboxes next to Create Users, Update User Attributes, and Deactivate Users to configure the integration.
  • Click Save.
  • Then, assign users to the HubSpot app.

Verify your domain

After adding the HubSpot app through Okta, you’ll need to verify your domain in HubSpot by updating your DNS records.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Click Okta SCIM.
  • Navigate to the General Settings tab.
  • In the Domain field, enter your users’ email sending domain.
  • Click Save.
  • Click Verify it now.
  • In the dialog box, select Next.
  • Copy the value in the Value column. You’ll then use this value when creating a new TXT record in your DNS provider
  • Log in to your DNS provider account, then create a new TXT record for the domain you’re verifying. Paste the value copied from HubSpot into the Value/Points To/Target field.
  • After you’ve created the TXT record, navigate back to HubSpot, then click Next. Once the DNS changes propagate, the domain will be verified.

Please note: it can take up to 48 hours for the DNS changes to propagate and reflect in HubSpot.

Sync Okta roles with HubSpot permission sets

To set user permissions, you must create permission sets in HubSpot. Okta can then assign permissions to a user if their Roles in Okta matches the exact name of the HubSpot permission set, including spaces and caps.

To give Okta access to assign permission sets to users:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Under All apps, click Okta SCIM.
  • Toggle Permission Set Management on.

Disable SCIM provisioning

To disable SCIM provisioning in HubSpot, you must uninstall Okta SCIM in HubSpot before making any changes in your Okta account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Connected Apps.
  • Under the Okta SCIM app, click the Actions dropdown menu, then click Uninstall.
  • In your Okta account, users will become editable and will no longer be synced with SCIM.

FAQ

Can users created through SCIM be edited in HubSpot?

Only user permissions can be edited in HubSpot, and only if permission set management is not configured. All other user information, including user name and email address, can only be updated through your identity provider.

Why are my assigned Okta roles not showing up on my user permission set in HubSpot?

You must turn on Permission set management in HubSpot to have Okta roles sync with HubSpot permission sets. The permission set name in HubSpot must match the exact Roles names in Okta, including all spaces and caps.

Can Okta assign users to teams?

No. However, after the user is added to HubSpot, you can update their team manually in HubSpot.

What happens if I delete a SCIM user in HubSpot or Okta?

Deleting a user in HubSpot will not delete the user in Okta. However, if you remove a user’s access to HubSpot from Okta, or deactivate their account in Okta, the user will be deactivated in HubSpot as well. Adding a user to HubSpot will not add the user to Okta.

What happens to existing users in my HubSpot account when I connect Okta?

After setting up SCIM through Okta, any existing HubSpot users that match users in Okta will automatically be converted to SCIM users. HubSpot will attempt to assign the user a permission set based on their Roles in Okta. If the user does not have roles in Okta that match permissions set in HubSpot, the user will have only minimal permissions in HubSpot.

I’m seeing the error “This domain couldn’t be verified,” how do I fix this?

If you are seeing this error, ensure your domain has been entered correctly with no spelling mistakes. Also, check that you have copied the correct value for the TXT record from the Configuration step in HubSpot into your DNS provider.

Request access to Users & Teams settings

Users without permissions can access the Users & Teams settings and request access directly in HubSpot. In the request form, describe what you’re trying to accomplish and select a Super Admin to notify. The Super Admin receives the request and a link to Permissions settings, where they can review user needs and grant the appropriate access.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • Click Request access.
  • In the dialog box, click the Select an admin dropdown menu and select the Super Admin to send the request to.
  • In the What are you working on field? describe why you need access to Users & Teams settings.
  • Click Send request.

The Super Admin receives a notification they can click, which brings them to permission settings so they can manage user permissions.

Set up lead revisit notifications

Lead revisit alerts make connecting with leads easier. When a lead returns to your site, HubSpot will notify you so you can take action.

Please note: you must be a user in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise account to receive lead revisit notifications via email. All users can receive lead revisit notifications via the sales email extension and view these notifications in the activity feed.

How lead revisit notifications work

With the lead revisit feature, you can receive an email in your inbox, an alert in your notification center, or real-time alert via the sales extension when an existing contact visits your website. Notifications will be sent for both HubSpot-hosted pages and external pages that have the HubSpot tracking code installed. The notifications include a link to the contact’s profile page, where you can see a full history of interactions that person has had with your company.

If you assigned a lead to a specific sales rep in Salesforce, that rep will receive the revisit alert when that lead visits the site again.

If you choose to receive notifications for all leads or all of the leads you own, you will receive a revisit alert for all contacts except the following:

For email notifications:

  • Contacts visiting your site for the first time.
  • Contacts created in the last 24 hours.
  • Contacts you do not have visibility to.
  • Contacts for whom you’ve received a lead revisit notification in the past 24 hours.
  • Contacts that you do not own (if you’re only tracking leads that you own).
  • Contacts revisiting your site with a lifecycle stage of Customer. Notifications will still be sent for contacts with all other lifecycle stages, including Evangelist and Other.
  • Contacts who have the same email domain as the assigned owner.

For sales notifications:

  • Contacts you do not have visibility to.
  • Contacts that you do not own (if you’re only tracking leads that you own).
  • Contacts revisiting your site with a lifecycle stage of Customer. Notifications will still be sent for contacts with all other lifecycle stages, including Evangelist and Other.

The email notification you receive will list your lead’s information and the domain that they’ve visited. The domain information in the subject of the email notification is based on the Company domain field in the Account Defaults.

Please note: if the specific page they visited has a unique canonical URL that has a different domain than the domain in its visible URL, the domain in the canonical URL will be displayed in the email instead.

Customize your website revisit notification settings

Select the contacts and companies you want to track and how you want to be notified when they visit your website.

Please note: each individual user must set their own revisit notification preferences. An admin or other user cannot adjust their team member’s preferences.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Notifications.
  • In the Website visits section, configure how you’d like to be notified when a contact or company visits your website.

Update your contact revisit notifications under the Contacts section:

  • Select the radio button next to the contacts you want to track.

    • Contacts you can view: select this option to send yourself contact revisit alert notifications for contacts you can view in your account.
    • Contacts you own: select this option to send yourself contact revisit alert notifications only for the contacts that are assigned to you.

  • Decide how you want to be notified when a lead revisits your site, then select the checkboxes next to the notification type.

    • Email: receive a daily email alert for each contact that has visited your site.
    • Real-time alert in your activity feed: view contact revisit activity in the activity feed.

Update your company revisit notifications under the Companies section:

  • Select the radio button next to the companies you want to track.
    • Companies you can view: select this option to send yourself company revisit alert notifications for companies you can view in your account.
    • Companies you own: select this option to send yourself lead revisit alert notifications only for the companies that are assigned to you.
  • Decide how you want to be notified when a company revisits your site, then select the checkbox(es) next to the notification type.
    • Email: receive a daily email alert for each company that has visited your site.
    • Real-time alert in your activity feed: view company revisit activity in the activity feed.

Please note: if you are not a HubSpot user and no longer want to receive lead revisit notifications, open an old lead revisit notification email and click the unsubscribe link at the bottom of the message.

If you are a lead owner in Salesforce, you will need to unsubscribe after you receive your first email. There is no option to unsubscribe before the first email is received.

If you’re tracking webiste visits, you can receive notifications based on a saved view in the website visits tool. You can turn on website visit notifications in the tool, then manage your notification preferences in the Prospects section by selecting the checkboxes next to the notification type you want to receive for that view.

Set up lead revisit notifications without using the Salesforce integration

If your HubSpot account is integrated with Salesforce, lead revisit alerts will be delivered to the sales rep assigned to the lead in your Salesforce account. If you are not integrated with Salesforce, you can use the default property, Contact owner, to automatically trigger lead revisit notifications for your users. This property will pull the owner name and email address from the users in your account.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to CRM > Contacts.
  • Click the name of your unassigned contact.
  • In left panel in the About section, click View all properties.
  • Use the search bar to locate the contact owner property. Hover over the owner property and click the edit icon, then select an owner from the dropdown menu.

To assign owners to multiple contacts at a time, use a workflow or bulk edit the records from the contacts dashboard. To set up owner assignment rules for future contacts, you can also use a workflow.

Set up user notifications in HubSpot

User notifications keep you informed about important activity in your HubSpot account, such as when you are assigned a record, a form is submitted, or an export is complete. C ustomize which notifications you receive and how you receive them across email, desktop, and mobile, helping you stay focused on the updates that matter most to your work.

For example, you might choose to receive desktop pop-up notifications for new conversations assigned to you, while using email notifications for security activity. Each notification type can be configured independently so you can tailor your experience.

If you’ve turned on email notifications and aren’t receiving them, troubleshoot notification emails.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with notifications, make sure to fully understand the limitations of the feature.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Some notifications (e.g. HubSpot Support or HubSpot Billing emails) can’t be turned off due to the important account management details they provide.
  • Super Admins in Enterprise accounts can set default notification preferences using notification profiles for other users. If default notifications are set up, preferences set by individual users will take precedence over the defaults.
  • Email notifications:
    • Users won’t receive more than 1,000 email notifications per day. When an email notification has been sent 1,000 times in the same day, to the same email address, any additional sends will be dropped.
    • Unsubcribing in an email notifications causes notification preferences to be automatically turned off for that notification type.
    • Default system notification email templates, including standard survey and form submission notification emails, can’t be customized for wording, headers, formatting, field placement, additional fields, or per form from form settings. To send customized notifications, create a workflow.
  • Desktop notifications:
    • If you log in to your HubSpot account in a different browser, you’ll need to turn on notifications in the new browser.
    • If you are unable to view notifications in your browser after clicking Allow notifications, you may also need to grant permission for notifications to display in your OS settings.
    • To edit your Chrome sales notifications, modify your notification settings in the Chrome extension.

Notification channels

The following notification channels are available in HubSpot:

  • Pop-up: notifications appear on screen when you are logged in and active in your HubSpot account. You can set a different sound for each notification.
  • Browser: notifications are be sent to your browser when you’re not active in HubSpot, but your HubSpot account is open in another tab or window of the browser. For example, a notification will be triggered if you have two tabs open, one of which is HubSpot, but you’re active in the non-HubSpot tab. Click Allow notifications to allow HubSpot to display notifications in your browser.
  • Bell: notifications appear as a red badge on the bell in your navigation bar. Click the bell to view your recent notifications. The notifications icon will appear in the browser tabs of favicon-supported browsers.
  • Email: noticiations are sent to your email address.
  • Mobile: push and in-app notifications will be sent to your mobile device once the mobile app is installed. You can configure your notification preferences within the settings on your browser or within the mobile app.
  • Integrations: learn how to set notifications for Microsoft Teams and Slack.

Set channel defaults

In the Set channel defaults settings, Turn on or off a notification channel and adjust the sounds for pop-ups.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Notifications.
  • In the top right, click Set channel defaults.
  • In the right panel click the channel toggle to turn that channel on or off. For example, if you want to temporarily turn off email notifications, click the Email toggle.
    • To adjust the sound that plays for pop-up, notifications, click the Sound dropdown menu and select a song. Click playerPlayPlay to preview the sound.
    • Click View apps to review your connected apps.

Set up and turn off HubSpot notifications

Notification preferences are user-specific, so each user must update their own settings. To set up or turn off your HubSpot notifications:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Notifications.
  • To filter notifications, click one the Most received or All notifications filters. To filter notifications by those that are turned on or off, click the Notification status dropdown menu, and select an option.
  • To expand all notification topics, click Expand all topics at the top of the table. To turn off all notification topics, click Turn off all Topics.
  • To turn on a notification, search for or expand the notification topics, and select the notification checkbox.
  • To turn off a notification, search for or expand the notification topics, and clear the notification checkbox.
  • Click Save. Changes may take a few minutes to take effect.
  • To view details of a notification and select the sound for pop-ups, click Manage.
    • On the notification page, click the toggles to turn on notifications for that channel.
    • When the pop-up toggle is turned on, in the Additional preferences section, click the Default dropdown menu and select a song. Click playerPlayPlay to preview the sound.

Types of notifications

Click the notification topics to expand further or use the search bar in the top left to find the notification topic you want to edit. The following are the notification sections and what notifications they include:

  • Academy: receive a notification when there’s an update about your certifications, awards, and exercises.
  • Account: receive a notification when your account has configured single sign-on (SSO) but doesn’t have the Require Single Sign-on checkbox enabled.
  • Ads: receive a notification when your ad sequence ads are started or paused.
  • Analytics: receive a notification when lists created or updated from a customer journey report finish populating.
  • Audit Logs: receive a notification when there are multiple exports from your account and when a user’s admin permissions are removed.
  • Blog: receive notifications when there’s a new comment on your draft blog post, when a user shares a blog draft with you, when there’s a new comment on your blog post, when HubSpot finishes scanning your blog, and when you receive an @-mention in a comment in a blog post draft.
  • Breeze: receive notifications for agent activity, including completed automated or manual runs, failed automated or manual runs, tool approval requests, data tests, and ABM landing page creation.
  • CRM: receive notifications when installing an app that accesses object types that are currently disabled in the Object library and for when your Custom Data Translations import is completed.
  • Calling: receive notifications when an inbound phone call to your HubSpot phone number has been logged.
  • Chat and email conversations: receive notifications for chat and email conversations from the conversations inbox and help desk. Receive a notification when a conversation is assigned to you, reassigned to you, when there’s a reply on a conversation, when you’re @-mentioning on a conversation, and when there’s a new unassigned conversation in the inbox. Even if these notifications are turned on, a user will only receive a notification if they have previously navigated to the inbox. For users on a team with access to the inbox, only main members of the team will receive the unassigned conversation notifications.
  • Comments: receive notifications on an activity you’re involved in or when you’re @-mentioned in a comment. Learn more about understanding and managing your comment notifications.
  • Contacts and companies: receive notifications when a company or contact is assigned to you, when there’s a duplicate record, when you’re @-mentioned in a company or contact record. Notifications will be received by users selected in the default Contact owner property or Company owner property, and in any custom user properties.
  • Custom objects: receive notifications when a custom object record is assigned to you or when you’re @-mentioned on a custom object record.
  • Dashboards: receive notifications when you’re @-mentioned in a note on a dashboard, or when you’re assigned permissions to view or edit a dashboard.
  • Data quality: receive notifications when a property anomaly is detected or a duplicate record is found.
  • Deals: receive notifications when a deal is assigned to you, when a deal you own or follow moves to a different deal stage, and when you’re @-mentioned on a deal record.

Please note: assignment notifications may be delayed by up to five minutes after the time of the assignment. If you’re assigned multiple records or tasks around the same time and the combined notification exceeds 100 individual assignment notifications, the combined notification will be sent without waiting the full five minutes. This helps balance quick delivery of notifications while avoiding sending too many notifications.

There are also cases where an assignment notification will not be sent. You will not receive a notification if you:

  • manually assign a contact, company, deal or task to yourself.
  • set the Object owner or custom owner property via a contact import or a sync from Salesforce.
  • become the owner of a contact or company record via the ownership sync between contacts and companies.
  • become the record owner due to a logged activity on the record, such as an email, call, or meeting.
  • were assigned to a HubSpot user property on the record prior to the Object Owner assignment (e.g., if a custom property Contact creator exists with the HubSpot user field type and you were already set as the Contact creator before being set as the Contact owner, you won’t receive a notification).

For deals, if you are the Deal owner and you make manual updates to the Deal stage property, you won’t receive a notification.

  • Email: receive notifications when someone clicks, opens, or replies to your email.

  • Exports: receive notifications when changes were made to your export.

  • Feedback surveys: receive notifications when there’s a new customer loyalty, customer satisfaction, customer support, or custom survey submission.

  • Form submissions: receive notifications when a visitor or contact submits your form. This notification type will only appear for users with access to the forms tool.

  • General: receive notifications for certain tools and updates to records including:

    • Marketplace: when a review you’ve written or reported in the Solutions or App Marketplace has been updated, when a cookie scan has finished, and when a rollback of an import has completed.
    • Approvals: when a teammate requests your approval, cancels an approval request, or approves your request.
    • Projects: when there’s an update to a project you’re assigned to, or you’ve been @-mentioned on a project.
    • Record updates: when a record that you own or are following is associated with another record, when there’s a new activity logged on a record you own, or when someone views a document you own. By default you’ll follow records you own, but if you unfollow them, you won’t receive notifications.

  • Growth: receive notifications when your Clip Creator Video cannot be generated.

  • Integrations: receive notifications for integrations installed in your HubSpot account including:

    • Data Sync - Resync previously deleted records: when previously deleted records have been restored and are back in sync.
    • Test sync complete: when a test sync is complete.
    • Integration disconnection: when an integration gets disconnected.

  • Invoices: receive notifications when an invoice you own has been paid.

  • Knowledge Base: receive notifications for your Knowledge Base including:

    • Knowledge base import complete with errors: when your knowledge base import is complete but with some errors.
    • Knowledge base import successful: when your knowledge base imports successfully.
    • Your knowledge base has been updated: when a knowledge base has been successfully migrated.
    • Your knowledge base was not updated: when a knowledge base wasn’t updated.
    • Your knowledge base was updated with errors: when a knowledge base has been migrated with errors.

  • Leads: receive notifications when a lead is assigned to you.

  • Lists: receive notifications when a list has completed processing and is ready to be used.

  • Marketplace: receive notifications for HubSpot Marketplace assets and purchases. Receive notifications when an asset update is available, a refund is requested, a purchase is confirmed, a refund is issued, a refund request is canceled, or a refund request is denied. If you’re an app, theme, or module creator, you can also receive notifications about your listing.

  • Messages: receive notifications when the SMS numbers reformatting task is completed or fails.

  • Partners: receive notifications when you’re an approved Partner Admin.

  • Payments (Super Admin only): receive notifications for when a payment is initiated or fails, when a payment is received, and when a payout is created or fails.

  • Performance and Insights: receive notifications when a dashboard is sent to you.

  • Product Updates: receive notifications about product updates and betas, including:

    • Product Updates: when product updates are available to your account.
    • Beta Request Status: when your beta requests are approved or rejected.

  • Projects: receive notifications when you a project is assigned to you, the stage is updated, the status is updated, and when you receive an @-mention on a project record.

  • Quotes: receive notifications for quotes. Receive notifications when a countersignature is required, a quote is paid, a quote is signed by a customer, a quote you countersigned is fully signed, or a quote you own is fully signed.

Please note: quote notifications will only be sent to the user who owns the quote.

  • SEO scan: receive a notification when an SEO scan is complete for your domain.
  • Security (Super Admin only): receive notifications when a suspicious login occurs on your account, when your portal data backup is complete and ready to be downloaded, when you have recommendations to manage security risks, when you need to confirm access to your two-factor authentication backup codes, and when HubSpot IP ranges change (BETA).
  • Social: receive notifications when new activity is available in your account’s social inbox.
    • Activity in social inbox: when there’s new activity available in your social inbox.
    • New direct message in social inbox: when one of your social profiles receives a direct message.
    • New mention in social inbox: when one of your social profiles is mentioned.
    • New reply in social inbox: when one of your social posts has a new reply.
  • System notifications: receive notifications when your initial data sync has completed, when your export is ready to download, when your import is complete, when your Salesforce integration is paused or there’s a sync error, or when a Salesforce user requests access to a record in HubSpot.

Please note: set up large export notifications in your Import & Export settings.

  • Tasks: receive notifications when you’re assigned a task, when a task assigned to you is due, when a task you’ve assigned someone else is completed, when a task is overdue, or when you’re @-mentioned in a note on a task. You can also opt to receive one email every weekday as a summary of your tasks.

  • Tickets: receive notifications when you’re assigned a ticket, when a ticket you own or follow moves to a different ticket status, or when you’re @-mentioned on a ticket record. Notifications will be received by users selected in the default Ticket owner property, and in any custom user properties.

  • Transcription and Analysis: receive notifications when tracked terms are found in a call, when the transcription from your recording is ready, and when tracked terms are ready for reporting.

  • Upgrades: the account admin will get notifications when a user requests a seat.

  • Website visits (Email only): receive notifications when contacts, companies, and prospects visit your website.

  • Workflows: receive notifications when a “send notification” action is triggered for your user in a workflow or when a workflow “needs review.” You can also opt to receive an email every Friday if a workflow has a change in enrollments. If workflow-based email notifications are turned off, workflows will still enroll records and run, but that user won’t receive internal workflow notifications or form-related workflow emails; turning the workflow on applies only to future notifications and won’t send missed notifications retroactively.

Summarize notifications

Generate an AI-powered summary of HubSpot notifications from the last 24 hours. The summary is available in the Notification sidebar and is also sent by email. The AI Summary feature provides a consolidated overview of recent notification activity, helping users:

  • Quickly catch up after a busy day or time away from HubSpot.
  • Reduce the need to review notifications individually.
  • Identify important updates and follow-up actions.
  • Stay informed without leaving the HubSpot interface.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the On-Demand AI Summary — Notification Sidebar beta.

Access notifications AI summary

To generate a notification summary:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the notifications icon.
  • In the right panel, click the AI icon.
  • If a summary for the last 24 hours isn’t available, click Generate Summary.

To create an updated summary, click Regenerate. Request up to three summaries per 24-hour period. This limit includes both initial generation requests and regeneration requests. A regenerated summary includes the most recent 24 hours of notifications.

View user permissions history

View a user’s permission history to see which permissions were added or removed, who made each change, and when. Use this information to troubleshoot access issues or support security and compliance audits.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to view user permission history.

To view a user’s permission history:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.

  • Hover over the user that you want to view the permission history of, then click the Actions dropdown menu. Navigate to Manage permissions then click View user permission history.

  • On the permission history screen, view the permission history details, which includes the following columns:

    • Permission: the name of the permission.
    • Action: whether the permission was added (Create) or removed (Delete).
    • Updated by: the user that made the update. An Automated Change entry represents a system-initiated change.
    • Date of change: when the change took place.

  • To export the last 90 days of the user permission history click Export Report.

AI: AI

Analyze Breeze Assistant usage

Use Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI, to review its usage across your HubSpot account. Breeze Assistant generates an artifact, an interactive visual output, of total messages sent. By default, the date range is the last 12 months, and you can adjust this in your prompt. Use the analytics to help you track adoption and trends. In this article, learn how to generate and review Breeze Assistant usage analytics.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance..

Understand requirements

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to return an analytics breakdown by HubSpot team.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to review Breeze Assistant usage analytics.

To use Breeze Assistant and generate usage analytics, you must:

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.

  • Prompt Breeze Assistant with a phrase or question from one of four categories to start the analytics process. Review example questions in these categories:

    • Message counts: how many messages have been sent to Breeze Assistant this year?
    • Adoption: how many users are interacting with Breeze Assistant?
    • Team-specific breakdown: which teams have used Breeze Assistant the most?
    • Usage statistics and trends: what’s the Breeze Assistant usage trend for this quarter?

Review Breeze Assistant usage analytics

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Enter a prompt from one of the four categories (e.g., how many users are interacting with Breeze Assistant?).
  • If you’ve configured brand styling, select a response to the report styling question.
  • Breeze Assistant generates an artifact and a CSV with the usage analysis.
  • Click the inline artifact card to view and interact with it in the panel alongside your Breeze Assistant conversation.
  • Click the inline CSV card to open it, then click Download CSV to save it to your computer. The CSV contains information such as first name, email, and total messages.

Build agents with Breeze Assistant

Use Breeze Assistant to build custom agents and agentic automation in the agent builder by describing the agent in plain language. Breeze Assistant proposes a configuration, including goal, tools, and knowledge sources. This gives you a working starting point to review and refine, rather than configuring an agent from scratch.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

After Breeze Assistant generates a configuration, learn how to create and customize agents in the agent builder to further adjust instructions, add actions, and test before publishing.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Agent builder permissions is required to create and customize agents in the agent builder.

Permissions required Users may require additional permissions depending on the agent’s goal. For example, an agent that generates a landing page requires Edit and Publish permission to edit and publish landing pages.

Before you create agents using Breeze Assistant, review the requirements and considerations.

  • A Super Admin must toggle the following switches on in your AI settings:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversion data
    • Files data
    • Give users access to Breeze Assistant
  • For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Build an agent using Breeze Assistant

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • What outcome do you want this agent to produce?
  • What information should the agent use to do that well?
  • What should the agent actually do with the result?

Create an agent that performs the following action and adheres to these instructions: For each new contact, evaluate fit against our ICP using company size, industry, job title, country, and lead source. Return one of three results: High fit, Medium fit, or Low fit, plus a one-sentence reason. If the contact is High fit, mark them for rep review. If Medium or Low fit, keep them out of the rep queue until enriched or reviewed.

To start building the agent with Breeze Assistant:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Enter your prompt and click the send prompt icon.
  • Review Breeze Assistant’s proposed configuration, including the goal, actions, and knowledge sources. Breeze Assistant may ask clarifying questions or suggest refinements before you confirm.
  • Confirm the configuration. Breeze Assistant will provide a link to the agent in the agent builder.
  • Continue customizing the agent in the agent builder.

Choose when to use AI agents or workflows

When you want to automate a process, you can use a workflow, a HubSpot default AI agent, a custom AI agent, or an agentic workflow. Each corresponds to a different type of goal. This article helps you identify which tool aligns with your goal, review implementation examples, and find resources for each.

If your goal requires situational assistance in the flow of work, learn when to use Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Identify the nature of your goal

Before you set up a workflow or using an AI agent, it’s recommended to identify the input, triggers, actions, and output that would define a successful result. Most goals fall into three categories:

  • Rule-based: the goal has a specific set of input data and desired outcomes. When defined criteria are met, a set of actions and optionally branching logic should occur. For example, assign leads to certain owners based on the lead’s geographic location.
  • Judgment-based: the goal requires analysis or parsing of unstructured or ambiguous data in order to be achieved. When data is created or updated, a report, summary, or analysis should take place. For example, identify at-risk deals from logged activities such as call notes.
  • Hybrid: the goal has both rule-based and judgment-based criteria. When defined criteria are met, an analysis of logged data determines whether or how predefined actions occur. For example, assign leads to certain owners based on an analysis of a resume file uploaded to the contact record.

Determine which tool to use

After you identify the category of your goal, navigate through the questions to identify recommended tools.

  • Can the entire process be configured using pre-defined data and fixed outcomes?
    • Yes: Use a workflow, segment, or calculated property.
    • No: Continue.
  • Does the process need to interpret, summarize, classify, or score ambiguous information or generate data from that information?
    • Yes: Continue.
    • No: Use a workflow, segment, or calculated property.
  • Does a user need to start and review each request?
    • Yes: Use Breeze Assistant.
    • No: Continue.
  • Does your goal match the functions of a HubSpot default AI agent?
  • HubSpot agent name
  • Function
  • Prospecting agent
  • Research target companies and generate personalized outreach to leads
  • Customer agent
  • Respond to support conversations and run 24/7 support
  • Data agent
  • Enrich and maintain CRM data quality
  • Campaign agent
  • Plan and generate marketing campaigns
  • Knowledge base agent (BETA)
  • Identify and flag content gaps in knowledge base articles
  • Revenue agent (BETA)
  • Follow-up on invoices
    • Yes: Install and configure the HubSpot default AI agent.
    • No: Continue
  • Does the AI agent need to use specific instructions, accept custom inputs, or take actions beyond the default AI agents?
    • Yes: Build a custom AI agent.
    • No: Review HubSpot default AI agents.
  • Does the AI agent need to run automatically, on a schedule, or after a detected data change?
    • Yes: Add the agent to an hybrid workflow or automation.
    • No: Run the agent from the agent inbox, Breeze Assistant, or CRM cards.

Implementation examples

After you identify the nature of your goal, review implementation examples for each category.

Rule-based goal: workflow

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use workflows.

Permissions required

  • Super Admin or Edit and Publish workflows permissions are required to create and publish workflows.
  • Edit workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows without publish access.

The operations manager at Sprocket Supply Co. has a goal to assign new leads to each sales rep based on the lead’s geographic location. The manager configures a workflow as follows:

  • Select the assign leads to a contact owner workflow template.
  • Add a branch action with paths that branch on the State/Region contact property.
  • Add a rotate record action to each path to assign contacts to owners within an assigned team.

Learn more about:

  • Workflow optimization strategies
  • End-to-end workflow configuration
  • Available workflow triggers
  • Available workflow actions
Judgment-based goal: custom AI agent

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to configure a custom agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required when a custom agent performs work such as thinking, taking actions, and generating content to complete a run. Costs vary by work complexity, so run tests without consuming HubSpot Credits prior to publishing your custom agent. Learn more about HubSpot Credits.

Permissions required Super Admin or Agent Builder permissions are required to create and customize agents in the agent builder.

The operations manager at Sprocket Supply Co. has a goal to identify at-risk deals by analyzing logged call notes. Call notes contain unstructured data such as text, numbers, and technical terms, which require AI interpretation to parse and recommend an action. The manager creates a custom agent with the following configuration:

  • An input that requires the user to select the deal they want to review.
  • A structured scoring guide the agent must follow to determine risk level.
  • A structured output in a bulleted list.
  • A Read your HubSpot CRM records action that analyzes the deal record.
  • A Write to your HubSpot CRM records action that updates the Deal risk level property.

Learn more about:

  • Manual custom agent configuration
  • Assisted agent configuration using Breeze Assistant
  • Custom agent tests that don’t require HubSpot Credits
Hybrid goal: agentic workflow

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to configure a workflow.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to use AI and agentic workflow actions. Learn more about HubSpot Credits.

Permissions required

  • Super Admin or Edit and Publish workflows permissions are required to create and publish workflows.
  • Edit workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows without publish access.

An agentic workflow is an automation that combines pre-defined triggers and actions with AI actions. The operations manager at Sprocket Supply Co. wants to assign leads to the hiring manager when the contact’s resume meets certain criteria. The manager configures an agentic workflow as follows:

  • A Property value changed workflow trigger based on the Resume or CV property.
  • An AI agent action that runs a custom Resume analysis agent.
  • A branch that splits into paths based on the analysis and property value updates performed by the Resume analysis agent.
  • An Edit record action for the path that assigns relevant contacts to the hiring manager.
  • An Edit record action that updates a contact for manual flagging if the attached file wasn’t relevant.

Learn more about:

  • Workflows that use AI actions
  • Available workflow triggers
  • Available AI actions

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to enroll your account in a beta.
