Collaborate in HubSpot Work

Use HubSpot Work to review what needs your attention, complete action items, and collaborate on shared work. Update tables and documents to manage information, coordinate tasks, and keep HubSpot Work projects on track.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

Permissions required An assigned Core, Sales, or Service seat is required to use HubSpot Work.

Understand limitations & considerations

Projects in HubSpot Work aren’t related to the projects object or Breeze Assistant projects.

Collaborate on a table

Permissions required

  • Project Owner permissions are required to customize columns in a table.
  • Project Contributor permissions are required to edit a table.

Update fields, add files, and link CRM records within a table to coordinate on project data. You can also create and use saved views to organize work within a table.

Edit and use a table view
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.
  • In the upper left, click the workspaces dropdown menu, then select a workspace.
  • In the left sidebar, click the name of a table.
  • To use a saved view, click the name of a view tab to navigate between saved views with different filters and display configurations.
  • To edit the table layout, click the New dropdown menu, then select an option:
    • Group: add an organizational category to the table.
    • Column: add data to the table such as a CRM reference field, a HubSpot Work document link, or a dropdown menu.
  • To edit the table color, row height, and text wrapping, click the configure table view icon.
Complete work in a table

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.

  • In the upper left, click the workspaces dropdown menu, then select a workspace.

  • In the left sidebar, click the name of a table.

  • To complete work actions:

    • Add data: click Add item, then fill in the details of the action item.
    • Edit data: click a field in the row to make changes to the action item.
    • Complete items: select the checkbox next to the action item, then select Mark as done.
    • Remove items: select the checkbox next to the action item, then select Delete. In the dialog box, click Delete to confirm.
Collaborate on a document

Permissions required Project Contributor permissions are required to collaborate on a document.

Co-edit documents with other users in the project. Tag users in comments with mentions, resolve feedback, and view line-by-line version history.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.
  • In the upper left, click the workspaces dropdown menu, then select a workspace.
  • In the left sidebar, click the name of a document.
  • Within the document, you can:
    • Edit: modify and style text inline.
    • Add content: add information such as style elements, documents, and media. Click the body of the document, then click the insert content icon to add content.
    • Add comments: mention other users in comments to collaborate on the content. Click and drag to highlight text, then select the comment icon in the context menu to add a comment and mention users.
    • Share: share the document with other users in the workspace or your HubSpot account. In the upper right, click Share, then configure access permissions.
    • View version history: review each iteration of the document in a diff style. In the right sidebar, click the version history icon, then select a timeline to compare or restore.
    • Export: share the document with users outside of the workspace or outside of HubSpot. In the upper right, click the three horizontal dots icon, then select Export as Markdown. The download will start and save the file to your computer.

Create and customize agents in the agent builder

Create custom agents that can analyze data, generate outputs, and take actions based on your business processes. Within the updated builder, you can define what an agent should do, what data it can access, and how it should respond.

Custom agents help standardize how tasks are performed and reduce manual effort by applying consistent logic to your data. This is useful for processes that require reviewing records, generating structured outputs, or making decisions based on multiple data sources.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up your HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required when a custom agent performs work such as thinking, taking actions, and generating content to complete a run. Costs vary by work complexity, so run tests without consuming HubSpot Credits prior to publishing your custom agent.

Before you begin creating and customizing agents in the agent builder, review the requirements and considerations.

  • A Super Admin must toggle the following switches on in your AI settings:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversion data
    • Files data
    • Give users access to Breeze Assistant

Create an agent in the agent builder

Permissions required Super Admin or Agent Builder permission is required to create and customize agents in the agent builder.

Permissions required Users may require additional permissions depending on the agent’s goal. For example, an agent that generates a landing page requires Edit and Publish permission to edit and publish landing pages.

Create a custom agent by defining its instructions, selecting actions, and configuring the data and inputs it’ll use.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • In the upper right, click the Create dropdown menu, then select Agents.
  • In the agent builder, configure your agent’s instructions, actions, knowledge, and inputs.
Instructions

Define what the agent should do and how it should behave. Include the agent’s role, goal, approach, and expected output.

In the agent builder, enter text in the Instructions field. Clearly define the agent’s role, goal, approach, and expected output.

For example, you could add the following instructions:

Role:

You’re a customer onboarding review agent responsible for preparing internal handoffs after a deal is closed.

Goal:

Analyze customer information and summarize key details needed for a successful onboarding process.

Approach:

Review contact and company properties, deal details, and recent activity.

Identify important context such as customer goals, purchased products, timeline expectations, and risks.

Flag any missing or unclear information that may impact onboarding.

Output:

Section 1: Customer summary (3-5 bullet points).

Section 2: Key onboarding considerations.

Section 3: Missing information or risks.

Keep responses concise, structured, and actionable.

Actions

Select the actions the agent can perform. Actions determine what tasks the agent can complete based on instructions.

  • In the agent builder, click Add action.
  • In the right panel, click the HubSpot, Default, or Connectors tabs and select your actions.
    • HubSpot: select from different types of actions (e.g., Get data, Generate, Take action). To filter the types of actions, click the Types dropdown menu and select a type (e.g., Generate).
    • Default: select from default actions such as Browsing the web or Reading your HubSpot CRM records.
      • Browse the web: this gives the agent access to browse the web.
      • Read your HubSpot CRM records: this gives the agent access to read your CRM records.
      • Write to your HubSpot CRM records: this gives the agent access to write to your CRM records.
    • Connectors: connect your agent to external systems using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Learn more about supported MCP servers.
Context

Add specific use case context the agent can reference when generating outputs, such as uploaded documents, brand guidelines, knowledge vaults, or relevant CRM data.

Use the Context section to provide supporting information the agent can draw from when analyzing data or generating responses. Unlike inputs, this context is available to the agent without being redefined each time it runs.

For example, an onboarding-focused agent may rely on deal details, associated company information, and recent activity, while a content-focused agent may use uploaded documents or files.

  • In the agent builder, click Add context in the Context section.
  • In the right panel, click Custom, Default, or Integrations and select your desired data.
    • Custom: select a knowledge vault. Learn more about managing agent context with knowledge vaults.
    • Default: select from default context such as your brand kit or ICPs.
    • Integrations: click an integration to configure what is included.
Inputs

Define the specific data the agent uses each time it runs, such as a record, user-provided value, or information passed from another tool or process.

Use inputs to specify what the agent should act on for a given run. Unlike knowledge, inputs are provided at runtime and can vary depending on the context.

For example, an onboarding-focused agent may use inputs such as deal name, close date, or customer goals, while a content-focused agent may require a topic, audience or key message.

  • In the agent builder, click Add input in the Inputs section.
  • Click the Input type dropdown menu and select an option (e.g., CRM Object).
  • In the Label field, enter a name for the input.
Permissions

Subscription required An Enterprise subscription is required to use permission sets.

Permissions required Super Admin or Add and edit users permissions are required to modify an agent’s permissions from default settings.

By default, the agent can access baseline functionality across your HubSpot account. Customize the permissions for an agent to grant or limit access to desired areas of your HubSpot account. However, the instructions, knowledge, and actions you configure determine what the agent can do within its permissions.

For example, a deal pipeline analysis agent that has Deals View and Edit permissions cannot edit deal records without the Write to my HubSpot records action turned on and instructions to make CRM changes.

Please note: agents don’t count toward your account’s seat assignments.

  • In the agent builder middle card, click Set permissions.
  • In the right panel, review and manage permissions for the agent:
    • Click Edit agent permissions to edit permissions manually in a new tab.
    • Click the Select permission set dropdown menu and select a permission set to apply it to the agent.
    • In the Permissions summary card, click a row to review the agent’s permissions in the selected area.
    • When you’re finished, click Update.

Manage agent access

Control which users have access to each agent. By default, Super Admins can edit agents and all users can run them.

If an agent’s configuration relies on other HubSpot features (e.g., blog or landing pages) that a user doesn’t have access to, the agent can’t be run by that user, even if the user has permission to edit or run the agent.

  • In the agent builder middle card, click Only admins can run.
  • In the right panel, select an access option:
    • Owners and super admins can edit and run: only the user, who created or installed the agent, and Super Admins can edit and run the agent.
    • Owners and super admins can edit, everyone can run: only the user, who created or installed the agent, and Super Admins can edit the agent. Every user can run the agent.
    • Everyone can edit and run: any user can edit and run the agent.
    • Custom team and user access: only selected users and teams can edit or run the agent. If you select this option there will be additional access options:
      • Run and edit: selected users or teams can run and edit the agent.
      • Run: selected users or teams can run the agent.
  • In the right panel, click theOwner dropdown menu, and select a user to optionally change who owns the agent.
  • When finished, click Update.

Test an agent in the agent builder

Test your agent without consuming HubSpot Credits to confirm the output meets your expectations. Review if the agent is using the correct inputs and referencing the correct data. Then, refine your instructions and agent knowledge and test again.

For example, you build a customer onboarding review agent that analyzes closed deals and prepares an internal handoff summary. You create the agent with instructions to review deal details, company info, and recent activity. You run a test that doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits in the builder and identify some changes you want to make. In the agent’s run history, you review the estimated credits per run based on your agent’s configuration. You add the agent to a deal closed workflow, and this month 50 deals close, triggering 50 runs.

Review estimated credit costs and set run limits

After testing the agent, review the estimated HubSpot credits required for the task. You can also set run limits to control how many credits an agent can use during execution, helping you manage credit usage across your account.

  • In the agent builder, click the Run history tab.
  • In the left panel, click an agent run.
  • In the right panel, review the estimated credits.

These estimates are provided for informational purposes only. Actual costs may vary. Learn more about reviewing estimated credit costs for agents and setting monthly run limits.

Publish a custom agent

Once you’ve tested your agent and confirmed the output meets your expectations, save and publish the agent to make it available for use.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • Click Edit on the agent you want to publish.

After publishing, use the agent as part of your broader processes and include agents in other automations. Learn more about adding agents to workflows.

Run agents from other sources

After publishing your agent, you can trigger and run your agents from other sources, such as workflows or CRM cards.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • Hover over an agent, then click Edit.
  • In the Run from section, select a source:
    • Breeze Assistant: run your agent using Breeze Assistant.
      • Click Breeze Assistant.
      • In the right panel, toggle the Enable this agent to be used with Breeze Assistant switch on.
    • Workflow: run your agent from a workflow or automation.
      • Click Automate, then set up your workflow or automation.
      • If you have a Starter account, run your agent from a automation in the automation side panel. Learn how to create automations in Agent Hub.
      • If you have a Professional or Enterprise account, run your agent from a workflow in the Agent Hub workflow builder. Learn how to create workflows in Agent Hub.
    • CRM card: run your agent from a CRM card directly in your CRM records.
      • Click CRM cards.
      • In the right panel, click Add to a CRM card and select the object type that you’d like to run your agent from. You can add your agent to multiple object types.
  • When you’re finished, click Publish updates.

Next steps

  • Run agents and review output in the agent inbox
  • Review estimated credit costs when using agents
  • Manage agent permissions in the users and AI teammates table

Create and manage projects in Breeze Assistant

Use projects to organize related conversations and provide consistent context within Breeze Assistant. Projects are used to group chats, define shared instructions, and add reference materials such as files or HubSpot content. This helps reduce repetitive prompts and ensures Breeze Assistant generates more relevant and consistent responses across related tasks.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: on July 13th, 2026, custom assistants were sunset.

  • Custom assistants you created: were automatically migrated to projects. Welcome messages and conversation starters weren’t automatically migrated.
  • Custom assistants installed from the Marketplace: weren’t migrated to projects and were sunset.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings to use Breeze Assistant.
  • To use a connector in a project, first connect the supported app to Breeze Assistant. Learn more about connecting apps to Breeze Assistant.
Understand limitations & considerations

Projects in Breeze Assistant are not related to the projects object.

Create a Breeze Assistant project

After you create a project, you can also use connectors to access supported third-party apps. For example, add the Amplitude connector to analyze product usage data in a project, or use both Amplitude and Notion together to retrieve metrics and create a summary in Notion.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the panel, click the Breeze dropdown menu, then select Projects.
  • Click New.
Create a project from scratch
  • In the dialog box, enter a name and description for your project.
  • Enter instructions to direct how Breeze Assistant responds.
  • In the Context section, click the file upload area to provide reference files from your computer.
  • In the Context section, click the + upload context icon to add optional context already stored in HubSpot such as knowledge vaults or CRM records.
  • In the Tools section, select the tools that are required for the project:
    • Connectors: under Connectors, click the + button and select the connectors you want to use in the project.
    • Browse the web: Breeze Assistant can search the web to provide responses during conversations.
    • Write to the CRM: Breeze Assistant can create or update records on your behalf during conversations.
  • In the Access section, click the edit edit access icon to set which users in your account can access the Breeze project.
  • Click Create project.
Create a project from a template
  • In the dialog box, select a template.
  • In the Context section, click the file upload area to provide reference files from your computer (e.g., outreach templates for the Sales prospecting template).
  • In the Access section, click the edit edit access icon to set which users in your account can access the Breeze project.
  • Click Create project.

Edit or delete an existing project

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the panel, click the Breeze dropdown menu, then select Projects.
  • To edit an existing project:
    • Click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon on a project you want to edit.
    • Click Settings.
    • In the dialog box, make your desired changes, then click Save.
  • To delete a project:
    • Click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon next to a project you want to delete.
    • Click Delete.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete project.

Start a chat in a project

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the prompt text field, click the use tools icon.
  • In the pop-up menu, hover over Add to project, then click the name of the project you want to use.
  • Chat with Breeze Assistant by:

    • Entering a prompt: in the prompt text field, enter a prompt.

    • Selecting a saved prompt: click the use tools icon, then select Saved prompts.

    • Continuing a previous chat: click View project, then click the name of a previous chat.

Learn how to use Breeze Assistant projects in the HubSpot mobile app.

Manage memory for projects

Breeze Assistant will automatically store relevant information as context for use in future chats. Prompt Breeze Assistant to remember certain details to manually create a memory. Learn more about Breeze Assistant memories.

To review project-specific memories:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the panel, click the Breeze dropdown menu, hover over More, then select Memories.
  • Click the filter memories icon, then select a project to review and delete memories specific to the selected project.

Create and manage prompts in Breeze Assistant

Save prompts in Breeze Assistant to send reusable requests. Use saved prompts for tasks or questions you ask often, such as drafting follow-up emails, summarizing records, or preparing for meetings, then reuse them in future chats. Organize prompts with tags, choose which assistants can access them, and share prompts with your team. Reusing saved prompts saves time on recurring tasks and keeps prompting consistent across your team. To provide Breeze Assistant with specific instruction for how to complete a task, use skills instead.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings to use Breeze Assistant.

Create prompts in Breeze Assistant

Create saved prompts so you can quickly start conversations for common tasks. Share prompts with other users in your account so they have access to prompts you create. Only Super Admins can edit or delete shared prompts created by other users.

To create prompts in Breeze Assistant:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Click the Breeze dropdown menu, hover over More, then select Prompts.
  • Click New.
  • Enter your prompt. Optionally click Add object placeholders (e.g., Contact) to require users to fill before using the prompt.
  • Enter your prompt name. Give the prompt a clear name so users know what it does.
  • To share the prompt with your team:
    • In the Private section, click the edit access icon.
    • In the dialog box, add users to give them access.
    • When you’re finished, click Done.
  • Click Save.
Create a scheduled prompt in Breeze Assistant

Set up prompts that run on a configured schedule. Configure up to five automated prompts that are personal to your user.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Click the Breeze dropdown menu, hover over More, then select Prompts.
  • Click New.
  • Enter your prompt. Optionally click Add object placeholders (e.g., Contact) to require users to fill before using the prompt.
  • Enter your prompt name.
  • Click Schedule this prompt, then in the dialog box configure the following:
    • Click the Frequency dropdown menu, then select an option (e.g., daily).
    • Click the Time dropdown menu, then select a time. You can also enter a custom time.
    • Click Done.
  • Click Save.

Scheduled prompts appear in your chats history with a timeIcon scheduled prompt icon next to the chat name.

Edit or delete prompts in Breeze Assistant

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Click the Breeze dropdown menu, hover over More, then select Prompts.
  • To edit a prompt:
    • Click the name of the prompt you want to edit.
    • Make your desired changes, then click Update.
  • To delete a saved prompt:
    • Click the three vertical dots icon next to the prompt you want to delete, then select Delete.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete prompt.
Edit or delete scheduled prompts in Breeze Assistant
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Click the Breeze dropdown menu, hover over More, then select Prompts.
  • Click the name of a scheduled prompt.
  • To edit the schedule:
    • In the Schedule section, click the editIcon edit icon to adjust the frequency and time.
    • In the Schedule section, click the playerPauseIcon pause icon to stop the prompt from running. Resume a scheduled prompt turn it back on.
    • Click Update.
  • To delete the scheduled prompt:
    • In the Schedule section, click the delete icon.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete to confirm.

Use saved prompts in Breeze Assistant

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the prompt text field, click the use tools icon and select a saved prompt or shared prompt.
  • Click the send prompt icon.

Create and use skills in Breeze Assistant

Create skills to give Breeze Assistant custom instructions for business-specific tasks. Skills store instructions, business context, files, and output behavior that tell Breeze Assistant how to perform a task. This reduces the manual work of entering lengthy instructions and keeps output consistent for repeat tasks. To save a question or request you use often that doesn’t require specific instructions, use saved prompts instead.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Skills only support markdown instructions, not scripts, tools, or external data sources.

Create skills

Skills are specific to your user until you share them. If you’ve built skills for other AI agents, copy them to Breeze Assistant to start from that baseline. You can also prompt Breeze Assistant to build a skill or create it manually.

To create a skill:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the prompt text field, click the use tools icon.
  • In the pop-up menu, hover over Skills, then select Add skill.
  • In the dialog box, click Add skill, then select a method.
Upload a skill
  • Click Upload a skill.
  • Click the file upload area, then select a SKILL.md file or a .zip folder that contains a SKILL.md file.
  • Edit the skill description, if desired.
  • Click Upload skill.
Build a skill manually
  • Click Create a skill.
  • In the Skill name text field, enter a name. You’ll use this when invoking a skill.
  • In the Skill description text field, enter a brief description of the skill’s purpose.
  • In the Skill content text field, enter the skill’s instructions in markdown format. For guidance on format, refer to this markdown cheat sheet.
  • When you’re finished, click Save skill.
Build a skill with Breeze Assistant
  • Click Create with Breeze.
  • Select answers to Breeze Assistant’s configuration questions or select Skip.
  • Enter a prompt that describes the task you want the skill to complete. Breeze Assistant will generate the skill instructions.
  • In the right panel, review the generated instructions.
  • Enter a follow-up prompt to refine the instructions, if applicable.
  • In the right panel, click Save skill.

Use skills

Breeze Assistant doesn’t select and use a skill automatically. You must invoke it in a new or existing conversation.

To use a skill:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Click the prompt text field.
  • Press the / key on your keyboard, then click the name of a skill.
  • Enter any details your skill requires, then click the send prompt icon. Breeze Assistant will respond based on your skill instructions.

Manage skills

Edit a skill to refine its instructions if output isn’t what you expect or delete skills you don’t use. Share skills so your team doesn’t need to create their own.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the prompt text field, click the use tools icon.
  • In the pop-up menu, hover over Skills, then select Manage skills.
Share skills
  • In the dialog box, hover over the skill you want to share.
  • Click the three horizontal dots icon, then select Share.
  • Click the Add people by name or email dropdown menu, then select users and teams.
  • When you’re finished, click Save. Users and teams you added can now use the skill.
Edit skills
  • In the dialog box, hover over the skill you want to edit.
  • Click the three horizontal dots icon, then select Edit.
  • Make desired changes to the skill.
  • When you’re finished, click Save skill.
Delete skills
  • In the dialog box, hover over the skill you want to delete.
  • Click the three horizontal dots icon, then select Delete.
  • Click Delete skill to confirm.

Create rich content with Breeze Assistant

The Breeze Assistant artifact viewer displays generated content in a side panel next to your chat. Each time you ask Breeze Assistant to create or refine rich content, a new version is saved. This preserves your progress across revisions, so you can experiment with different directions without losing earlier versions of the content.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings to use Breeze Assistant.

Create rich content in Breeze Assistant chats

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Enter your prompt, asking Breeze Assistant to generate a piece of rich content (e.g., a document or an email), and then click send prompt icon.
  • Breeze Assistant will generate the requested content and automatically open a side panel displaying the results.
  • Refine the content by sending follow-up messages in the Breeze Assistant chat. Each change is saved as a new version in the artifact viewer.
  • When generating an email, edit the content of the email directly in the canvas.
  • In the upper right, click the X to close the artifact viewer.
  • Click the name of the content to reopen the canvas or to switch to another piece of content.

Review version history

As you’re refining the generated content, review previous versions in the artifact viewer.

  • In the upper left of the artifact viewer, click the version dropdown menu.
  • Select the version you want to review.

Share generated content

When you’ve finished refining the content with Breeze Assistant, share the result via a URL with users in your HubSpot account or external users.

  • Share an artifact with users in your HubSpot account.
  • Share an artifact with the public.
Download artifacts

Download artifacts to save local copies of a specific version. The download method depends on the type of content that was generated:

  • Text documents: in the upper right of the artifact viewer, click Copy markdown to copy the content to your clipboard.
  • Presentations: in the upper right of the artifact viewer, click Save as PPTX.
  • HTML pages: save the HTML code to your clipboard or download the HTML file.
    • In the upper right of the artifact viewer, click Copy to copy the HTML code to your clipboard.
    • In the upper right of the artifact viewer, click the dropdownIcon down arrow icon and then select Save as HTML to save the page.
  • Emails: send the email or copy the email body to your clipboard.
    • Enter an email address in the To: field, and then click Send email in the upper right.
    • In the upper right of the artifact viewer, click the dropdownIcon down arrow icon and then select Copy to clipboard.

Generate data visualizations with Breeze Assistant

Use Breeze Assistant to generate charts and graphs directly in your conversation using natural language prompts. Generate ad-hoc visualizations through conversation to explore your data quickly, without the overhead of setting up a formal report. Breeze Assistant supports multiple chart types, annotations, labels, and formatting adjustments, allowing you to iteratively build visualizations without leaving the conversation.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements to use Breeze Assistant

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.
  • Users must have permissions to the relevant records in your HubSpot account to create visualizations using CRM data.
Understand limitations & considerations when using Breeze Assistant

Data visualizations are unique to your conversation in Breeze Assistant. They can’t be saved to your report library or added to dashboards in HubSpot. For persistent, dashboard-ready reports, learn more about creating custom reports.

How to create a data visualization with Breeze Assistant

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Enter your prompt describing the visualization you want to create.

Show me closed revenue by rep this quarter as a bar chart with a target line at $50K.

Give me a cumulative pipeline chart for Q2, broken out by stage.

  • Click the send prompt icon.
  • Breeze Assistant will generate the visualization directly in the conversation.

How to use external data in a visualization

Include CRM data or external data sources such as a CSV file or web data when generating visualizations.

How to use uploaded spreadsheet data
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Click the attachment icon and select Upload from computer. Then select your CSV file.
  • Enter your prompt describing the visualization you want to create using the uploaded data.

Create a line chart comparing quarterly revenue from the uploaded spreadsheet.

  • Click the send prompt icon.
How to use external web data

Breeze Assistant can also use publicly available web data when generating visualizations. For example, enter a prompt like this:

Compare our quarterly deal growth with recent industry hiring trends.

Refine a data visualization

After Breeze Assistant generates a visualization, continue refining it through a follow-up prompt. For example, enter a prompt like the following:

Change this to a stacked bar chart.

Add a trend line for average deal size.

Update the chart title to “Q2 pipeline growth by stage”.

Export a data visualization

After you’ve finished refining your visualization, click Save to export the visualization as a PDF. Then share the exported PDF with other members of your team.

Install agents from the Agent Marketplace

HubSpot pre-built agents are available in the Agent Marketplace and can be customized in the agent builder. These agents provide a starting point for common use cases, reducing the need to build agents from scratch.

After installing an agent, update its instructions, context, and configuration to align with your business needs. This allows agents to perform tasks using your preferred workflows, messaging, and data.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up your HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Please note: on July 23, 2026 the following agents were sunset. If you’ve previously installed these agents, they will remain in your account. However, these agents can not be installed going forward.

  • Social Post Agent
  • ABM Landing Page Agent
  • RFP Agent
  • Cross-sell/Upsell Agent
  • Sales to Marketing Feedback Agent

Before you get started

  • A Super Admin must toggle the following switches on in AI settings:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversion data
    • Files data
    • Give users access to Breeze Assistant
  • Users may require additional permissions depending on the agent’s goal. For example, an agent that generates a landing page requires Edit and Publish permission to edit and publish landing pages.

Install an agent

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use some HubSpot-built agents.

Permissions required Super Admin or Agent Builder permission is required to create and customize agents in the agent builder.

Please note: Agent Marketplace only lists HubSpot’s pre-built agents. Custom agents created in Agent Builder are not eligible for listing on the Agent Marketplace.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Marketplace. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Marketplace directly.
  • At the bottom of the page, click Explore all.
  • Click an agent card (e.g., Company research agent).
  • On the listing page, review the agent information:
    • Built by: creator of the agent.
    • Overview: summary of the capabilities of the agent. Click See more to view the entire summary.
    • Features: explanation of individual features available in the agent.
    • Agent functionality: which tools the agent uses by default.
    • Pricing: explanation of credit usage. Learn more about HubSpot Credits and billing.
    • More info: additional information about the agent, including links to contact the agent’s creator for support.
    • Feedback: users can provide feedback on the agent to help improve it’s performance and capabilities.
  • Click Add.

Next steps

  • Create and customize agents in the agent builder
  • Run agents and review output in the agent inbox
  • Review estimated credit costs when using agents

Manage AI context

HubSpot’s AI tools use two types of information to inform AI functionality: context and knowledge vaults. Context is foundational information about your business that’s automatically applied across multiple AI tools in HubSpot. Knowledge vaults are sets of information that you manually add to projects or agents for specific use cases.

Keeping your context up to date ensures that AI features across HubSpot reflect your organization’s latest information and communicate in ways that align with your business.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Add or customize AI context

Permissions required Super Admin or Partner Admin permission is required to update most context details, except in the following scenarios:

  • Users with Prospecting Agent Admin permission can also update the Products & Services section for the Business details.

  • Any user can create an email personality and update their user profile in the Personal section. Email personalities can only be edited or deleted by the user who created them.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.

  • Click the Context tab to add and review AI context sections.

Business

Add and edit your company information, such as firmographics, how you monetize, and your product and service offerings.

  • Click the Business tab.
  • In the Identity and classification, Business profile, Technology stack, and Market and ecosystem context sections, click Customize, then select Edit.
    • In the right panel, enter values to provide additional context about your business.
    • When you’re done, click Save.
  • In the Brand kit section, click Manage to navigate to your brand kit settings and define your company’s voice, tone, and brand guidelines. Learn more about managing your brand kit.
  • In the Product and services section, click Customize, then select Add product or service.
    • In the right panel, enter values for the product or service.
    • When you’re done, click Save.
  • To edit or delete a product or service, hover over an existing product or service, then click the edit icon or delete icon.
Customers

Add or edit information about your target audience and customer personas.

  • Click the Customers tab.
  • In the Ideal Customer Profiles section, manage characteristics of companies or buyers that are the best fit for your offerings.
  • To add a new ICP, click Customize, then select Add.
    • In the right panel, enter the ICP details.
    • When you’re done, click Create.
  • To edit an existing ICP, click the name.
  • To delete an ICP:
    • Hover over the profile and click the delete icon.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete.
  • In the Personas section, manage the types of customers your business targets.
  • To add a new persona, click Customize, then select Add.
    • In the right panel, enter the persona details.
    • When you’re done, click Create.
  • To edit an existing persona, click the name.
  • To delete an existing persona:
    • Hover over the profile and click the delete icon.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete.
Team & Processes

Add team processes ,such as sales methodology, so HubSpot’s AI tools understand your team context.

  • Click the Team & Processes tab.
  • Add sales methodology.
Personal

Manage your profile details and email style and tone. You can add an email personality per email type (e.g., one for Closing and one for Cold outreach).

  • In the Your personal info section, click Customize, then select Manage profile to navigate to your user profile settings in a new tab. Learn more about managing your user profile and preferences.
  • In the Email personalities section, update the preferred tone, style, and voice used in email communications.
  • To add a new email personality:
    • Click Customize, then select Add.
    • In the right panel, configure your email personality.
    • When you’re done, click Add personality.
  • To edit an email personality, click the name.
  • To delete an email personality:
    • Hover over the personality and click the delete icon.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete.
Custom

Add files or free-form notes to give HubSpot’s AI tools additional context about your business that doesn’t fit into the other categories.

  • Click the Custom tab.
  • In the Custom context section, click Add, then select an option.
    • Write free-form text: enter custom text and select the visibility. When you’re done, click Add context.
    • Upload files: use existing files from your computer and select visibility. When you’re done, click Add context.
External tools

Add and manage third-party connectors and add instructions to provide AI agents with data on when to use certain third-party apps. Connectors that you add are personal and not turned on for other users in your account.

  • Click the External tools tab.
  • To add a connector:
    • Click Add a connector.
    • In the dialog box, click Connect or Install on an app.
    • Proceed through the connection authentication steps.
    • When connected, click the X to close the dialog box.
    • In the Agent connectors section, click Add instructions to tell AI agents when they should use the connector.
    • In the right panel, click Update connector.
  • To add app-specific instructions:
    • In the Apps & integrations section, click Instructions.
    • In the right panel, enter instructions to tell AI agents when to look for context in the app.
    • Click Update app.
  • To edit existing instructions for connectors:
    • In the Agent connectors section, click the three vertical dots icon, then select Update agent instructions.
    • In the right panel, make your desired changes and save.
  • To edit existing instructions for specific apps:
    • In the Apps & integrations section, click Instructions.
    • In the right panel, make your desired changes and save.
Knowledge vaults

Create or update knowledge vaults that provide projects and AI agents with additional context about your business.

  • Click the Context vaults tab.
  • Add or edit knowledge vaults.

Manage AI context with knowledge vaults

Use knowledge vaults to provide projects and agents with the specific business information they need to generate accurate and relevant outputs for targeted use cases. Add context such as files from your desktop, existing HubSpot assets, or CRM segments so agents reference the appropriate data for each task, rather than relying on broad general context.

In this article, learn how to create, edit, and manage knowledge vaults, control vault permissions, and attach vaults to projects and agents.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • You can have up to 50 separate knowledge vaults at the same time.

  • Projects and agents will use the most recent version of any records added to knowledge vaults.

  • Knowledge vaults can’t be saved without at least one file or CRM object attached.

  • Review the file formats and size limits supported in knowledge vaults:

  • .pdf

  • .md

  • .html

  • .pptx

  • .txt (UTF-8 encoding only)

  • .docx

  • .xlsx

  • .csv

  • .json

  • .xml

  • .jpeg

  • .png

  • .webp

Create knowledge vaults

A default knowledge vault will be created using the context provided on your AI Context page. To create custom knowledge vaults for additional context:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Context tab.
  • Click the Context vaults tab.
  • In the top right, click Create Vault.
  • In the right panel, enter a name for the vault in the Name field.
  • In the Description field, enter a description of the context you’ll be adding to this vault.
  • In the Files section, click Add and select the relevant files from your device. Learn how embedded images in documents are used.
  • In the HubSpot Content section, click the Add dropdown menu and select a content type (e.g., Knowledge base).
    • To choose specific content, select the checkbox next to each asset. For knowledge bases, click the knowledge base to select articles to include or exclude.
    • To select all content, toggle the Select all switch on.
    • Click Add [assets] in the bottom right.
  • In the Segments (Lists) section, click Add.

    • In the search field, enter the name of a segment.

    • To filter the available segments, click the Status (e.g., Active or Static) or Object dropdown menus, and select an option. Available objects include foundational and custom objects.

    • To choose a segment, select the checkbox next to the segment.

    • Click Add segments in the bottom right.

  • To add additional files, content, or segments, click Add, then repeat the relevant sections.
  • When you’re finished, click Create.

How embedded images are used in content

When you add content to a knowledge vault, embedded images are processed alongside the text. This allows projects and agents to retrieve and analyze visual information, such as diagrams, charts, and screenshots, without requiring you to upload image files separately.

This applies to images embedded in:

  • Knowledge articles
  • Blog posts
  • Landing pages
  • Website pages
  • Uploaded documents (e.g., PDF)

When content is published or updated, the knowledge vault automatically extracts qualifying images, generates descriptions, and indexes them with the text. At query time, projects and agents can use these images and descriptions to understand context and respond more accurately.

Ask questions about visual content in your sources, such as diagrams or data shown in a chart.

  • Image limits for pages, posts, and articles: up to 10 images per asset, with a maximum size of 500 KB per image.
  • Document support: PDF, Word (.docx), and PowerPoint (.pptx), up to 50 MB per file.
  • Content scope: only images in the body content are processed (not headers, footers, or decorative elements).
  • HTML limitations: images must be embedded inline (e.g., base64). External image URLs aren’t supported.

Manage knowledge vault permissions

Control access to individual knowledge vaults by assigning permissions to specific users and teams. This helps limit access to only the vaults relevant to each user while allowing designated users to maintain vault content and settings.

Please note: Super Admins can always access and manage all knowledge vaults, regardless of vault-level permissions.

To manage permissions for a knowledge vault:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.

  • Click the Context tab.

  • Click the Context vaults tab.

  • Click a knowledge vault card.

  • In the right panel, click the ellipsesIcon three horizontal dots icon and select Manage Access.

  • In the Manage Access panel, select the users or teams that should have access to the vault:

    • Owners + super admins can edit and use: only vault owners and Super Admins can edit or use the vault.
    • Owners + super admins can edit, everyone can use: all users can use the vault, but only vault owners and Super Admins can edit it.
    • Everyone can edit and use: all users can view, use, and edit the vault.
    • Custom team and user access: select specific users and teams that can view and manage the vault.

  • Click Save.

Edit knowledge vaults

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Context tab.
  • Click the Context vaults tab.
  • Click a knowledge vault card.
  • In the right panel, click the ellipsesIcon three horizontal dots icon and select Edit to customize the name and description. Then click Save.
  • To add a new file, click Add in the Files section, then upload a file.
  • To add content or segments, click Add in the Content or Segments (List) sections and select an option.
    • For knowledge base articles, landing pages, blog posts, and calls, select the checkbox next to each asset you want to add, then click Add [asset].
    • For segments, click Add, clear or select the checkbox next to the segment. Then click Add segments.
  • To remove a file, asset or segment, click the remove remove icon next to its name.
  • When you’re finished, click Save.

Delete knowledge vaults

When you remove a knowledge vault from a project or agent, that knowledge vault stays in your account. To permanently delete a knowledge vault:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Context tab.
  • Click the Context vaults tab.
  • Click a knowledge vault card.
  • In the right panel, click the ellipsesIcon three horizontal dots icon and select Delete.
  • In the dialog box, click Delete vault.

Manage a project or agents knowledge vaults

After you’ve created knowledge vaults, add them to any project or agent.

Manage a project’s knowledge vaults
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the upper left, click the Breeze dropdown menu, then select Projects.
  • Click the three horizontal dots icon next to a project, then select Settings.
  • In the Context section, click the + plus icon and select Add knowledge vault.
  • Select an existing knowledge vault or click Create a knowledge vault.
  • When you’re finished, click Save.
Manage an agent’s knowledge vaults
  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • Click Edit on the agent card.
  • To add a knowledge vault to an agent, click Add knowledge in the Knowledge section. In the right panel, select the knowledge vault.
  • To remove a knowledge vault from an agent, hover over the knowledge vault and click the X icon.
  • In the What this agent knows section of the editor, click Add knowledge.
  • In the right panel, hover over a knowledge vault and click Add. Repeat for each knowledge vault you want to use.
  • To review the contents of a knowledge vault, hover over the knowledge vault and click View details or View in settings.
  • When you’re finished, click X to close the right side panel. Then click Publish in the top right.

Understand knowledge vault citations

When a project or agent references content from knowledge vault documents in its responses, the citation includes specific details from the source file.

Citations display the document name along with the relevant page number or section, when available. This helps you locate and verify the referenced content within the original document. Supported formats include .pdf or .docx.
