Example: Use a segment-based knowledge vault in a project

Build a project that helps users surface insights from recent support tickets. For example, summarizing frequent issues reported in the past week, spotting regional trends, or identifying spikes in certain ticket types.

Create a segment for recent tickets
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • Create an active segment on “Tickets” filtered to only include tickets created in the last 30 days (or “last 7 days,” depending on how fresh you want the data).

Learn more about creating segments.

Create a knowledge vault using the segment
  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Context tab.
  • Click the Context vaults tab.
  • In the top right, click Create vault.
  • In the right panel, enter the knowledge vault details:
    • Name: Recent tickets in [X] region.
    • Description: Support tickets within the last 30 days filed in [X] region.
  • In the Segments section, click Add, and select the new segment. You can add more than one segment to a knowledge vault, but the other segments need to be a different object type. For example, one segment on tickets and one on contacts.
Attach the knowledge vault to a project
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the upper left, click the Breeze dropdown menu, then select Projects.
  • Click the three horizontal dots icon next to a project, then select Settings.
  • In the Context section, click the + plus icon and select Add knowledge vault.
  • Select the knowledge vault.
  • When your’re finished, click Save.

Manage revenue agent

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for invoices are required to manage revenue agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to send invoices using revenue agent. Credits are consumed per invoice associated with a plan. Learn more about how revenue agent uses HubSpot Credits.

Please note: if an individual inbox is connected to revenue agent, only the owner of the inbox can manage revenue agent.

Use revenue agent, part of HubSpot’s AI, to monitor open invoices and automate outreach to buyers. Revenue agent tracks invoice changes and customer communications to suggest personalized outreach plans to help collect payment. Revenue agent adjusts plans based on customer replies and invoice activity and can send escalation emails to internal contacts.

For example, if an invoice is past due and a buyer hasn’t responded, revenue agent can send a personalized follow-up and escalate the case to an internal contact if payment remains outstanding.

Manage revenue agent, including enrolling and unenrolling companies and contacts, manually excluding invoices, reviewing, editing, and approving plans, viewing missing data, changing email addresses, and turning off revenue agent. Learn how revenue agent works and how to set it up.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

View the plan overview

The plan overview displays the outstanding invoice balances revenue agent is managing, the number of agent actions in the last 24 hours, the number of enrolled companies and contacts, companies and contacts that need attention, and active plans.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • The managed balance, agent actions, and companies and contacts enrolled are displayed at the top. To search companies and contacts, in the upper right, in the Search field, enter a company or contact name or email address.
  • The overview table displays enrolled companies and contacts across two tabs, organized by whether their invoices are included or excluded in plans:
    • Needs plan review tab: displays companies and contacts that need plans reviewed or billing contacts added.
    • Active plans tab: view plans that are currently active and their associated companies and contacts. Enrolled companies and contacts are monitored for open invoices, even without an active plan. Learn more about managing active plans.
  • The following columns are displayed in the table:
    • Enrolled entity: company or contact name and billing contact email address.
    • Type: type of enrolled entity (company or contact).
    • Open invoices: number of open invoices and how many are overdue.
    • Last outreach: the last outreach activity. Values include Email (most recent completed action has a sent email. Hover to view the subject and body), Escalate (completed escalation action), or — (no last action).
    • Next step: the next step in the plan, including when it will take place. Values include Add billing contact (billing contact needs adding), Review plan (plan needs reviewing), Email response (scheduled reply to the company or contact), Reminder email (scheduled reminder), Escalation email (scheduled internal escalation), No action (no upcoming actions), or Monitoring account (account is being monitored. Status updates if revenue agent detects customer communication related to the entity’s invoices).
    • Last payment: when the last payment was made.
    • Balance due: the total balance due and overdue for the account.
  • In the Needs plan review tab, review companies and contacts that need your attention. Under Next step, click the action list (e.g., Add billing contact, Review plan).
  • In the Active plans tab, review enrolled companies and contacts with active plans:
    • To view the details of a company or contact, under Enrolled entity, click the name of the company or contact. In the right panel, view the company or contact details, AI summary, open invoices, and activities, including emails sent and received.
    • To view the active plan, including proposed and sent emails, in the Plan column, click View plan.

Enroll and unenroll companies and contacts

After selecting companies and contacts to enroll during setup, you can enroll additional ones or unenroll them.

Manually enroll companies and contacts
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the top right, click Manage enrollment, then click Review entities.
  • To search companies and contacts, in the Search field, enter a company or contact name or email address.
  • To filter by type, click the All types dropdown menu and select the Companies or Contacts checkboxes.
  • To sort, click the sort icon and select # open invoices (sort by number of open invoices) or Alphabetical (sort alphabetically).
  • In the table, select the checkboxes next to the companies and contacts you want to enroll or unenroll.
  • In the bottom right of the dialog box, click Exclusion segments.
  • Add exclusion segments to exclude invoices that meet filtered criteria from plans. Learn more about exclusion segments. To add an exclusion segment:
    • Toggle an existing invoice segment switch on to exclude invoices included in that segment. Review the number of available CRM segments for your subscription in the Product & Services Catalog. Learn more about creating CRM segments.
    • To add a new exclusion segment, click Create exclusion segment.
    • From the list, select invoice properties to filter by.
    • Enter filter criteria, then click Done.
    • To add filter criteria to the same group, click Add filter.
    • To add another filter group, click Add filter group.
    • To add another exclusion segment, click Create exclusion segment again.
  • In the bottom right, click Review & confirm.
  • In the bottom right of the dialog box, click Update enrollment.

Please note: after updating enrollment:

  • Unenrolled entities: unenrolled companies and contacts that were active will no longer receive previously planned emails, and unapproved plans are removed. Any static email reminders configured in settings will resume.
  • Enrolled entities: static email reminders configured in settings are paused as soon as a company or contact is enrolled. If the automation mode is set to Review every email, approve plans for newly enrolled companies and contacts. If the automation mode is set to Send automatically until a customer replies, scheduled and escalation emails for newly enrolled companies and contacts are sent automatically.
Enroll companies and contacts from the invoices index page

Enroll companies and contacts directly from an invoice. Revenue agent must be activated before you can enroll companies and contacts from their invoices. Learn more about company and contact enrollment.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Invoices. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Invoices directly.
  • Click an invoice number.
  • In the right sidebar, under Revenue Agent, click Enroll in Revenue Agent.
  • In the dialog box, select an option:
    • Company: enroll the company in revenue agent.
    • Contact: enroll the contact in revenue agent.
  • Click Enroll.
Manually unenroll companies and contacts
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar, click Manage, then click Companies and contacts.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the companies and contacts to unenroll.
  • Click Unenroll at the top of the table.
  • In the dialog box, click Unenroll.
Unenroll companies and contacts from the invoices index page

Unenroll companies and contacts directly from an invoice.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Invoices. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Invoices directly.
  • Click an invoice number.
  • In the right sidebar, under Revenue Agent, click the Manage dropdown menu.
  • Select Unenroll [company or contact name].
  • In the dialog box, click Continue.

View missing data

View missing data of enrolled companies and contacts. Missing data statuses apply to invoices created in HubSpot, or synced to HubSpot from an integrated platform (e.g., QuickBooks, Xero).

HubSpot and synced invoices

The following errors apply to invoices create in HubSpot orsynced from external providers. Resolve the issue in HubSpot.

No billing contact: update the billing contact of a HubSpot invoice.

Synced invoices

The following errors apply to invoices synced from external providers. Resolve the issue in the integrated platform and re-sync the invoice to HubSpot.

  • Missing invoice URL: URL missing for the invoice.
  • Currency: currency missing from the invoice.
  • Balance due: balance due missing from the invoice.
  • Due date: due date missing from the invoice.

To view missing data and update billing contacts for HubSpot invoices:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar, click Manage, then click Missing data.
  • Click the Grouped by dropdown menu and select an option:
    • Data missing: group missing data by missing data type (e.g., No billing contact).
    • Entity: group missing data by company or contact.
  • To add a billing contact, click Add contact next to a company.
  • In the dialog box:
    • To add an existing contact, click the Billing contact dropdown menu and select a contact.
    • To add a new contact, click Add new. In the fields provided, enter the contact details.
    • Click Add contact.
  • For issues with invoices from external systems, correct the errors in the external system and re-sync them to HubSpot.

Manually include and exclude invoices

Select invoices to include or exclude from plans or the invoices index page. Companies and contacts will remain enrolled with revenue agent. Learn more about exclusions and enrollments.

Manually include and exclude invoices from plans
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • On the Needs plan review or Active plans tab, click Review plan or View plan.
  • In the right sidebar, in the Open invoices section, click the three vertical dots icon, then select Exclude from plan.
  • In the dialog box, click Exclude and regenerate plan.

The plan will be regenerated using the remaining invoices. If you’re excluding an invoice from an active plan, you need to review and approve the new plan for outreach to resume.

Manually include and exclude invoices from the invoices index page
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Invoices. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Invoices directly.
  • Click an invoice number of an enrolled company or contact.
  • In the right sidebar, under Revenue Agent, click the Manage dropdown menu.
  • Select an option:
    • Exclude invoice: exclude a currently included invoice. In the dialog box, click Continue.
    • Include invoice: include the invoice. In the dialog box, click Continue.
  • Included invoices are labeled as Active.
  • Excluded invoices are labeled as Excluded.

Review, edit, and approve proposed plans

Review, edit, and approve proposed plans. You can edit the structure and sequence of plans, edit individual emails within a plan, or propose a new plan. Some invoices may be excluded. Learn more about exclusions and plans.

Review plans
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • On the plan overview page, plans that need reviewing will be displayed on the Needs plan review tab.
  • Click Review plan.
  • Review the suggested plan.
  • In the right panel, review the AI summary of the plan.
Exclude invoices from plans

Select invoices to include or exclude from plans. Companies and contacts will remain enrolled with revenue agent. Learn more about exclusions and enrollments.

  • In the right sidebar, in the Open invoices section, click the three vertical dots icon, then select Exclude from plan.
  • In the dialog box, click Exclude and regenerate plan.

The plan will be regenerated using the remaining invoices. If you’re excluding an invoice from an active plan, you need to review and approve the new plan for outreach to resume.

Edit individual emails within a plan
  • To edit the subject of an email, next to Subject, click the edit icon and enter a subject.
  • To add other recipients, in the upper right of the email, click Cc or Bcc. Enter an email address, then press Return on your keyboard. You can add multiple recipients.
  • To change the scheduled date and time of future emails, in the Schedule section of the email, click the date and time pickers and select a date and time.
  • To edit the email, click the email body and make any updates. Use the formatting toolbar at the bottom of the email to format text and add links.
Edit proposed plans with Breeze Assistant
  • In the upper right, click Edit.
  • Update plans using Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant.
Approve plans

Approve the plan to initiate the scheduled emails. Any emails scheduled to be sent immediately will be sent when you approve the plan.

  • In the upper right, click Approve plan.
  • The plan will move to the Active plans tab on the overview page.

Review and edit active plans

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the Overview table, click the Active plans tab.
  • To view the active plan, including proposed and sent emails, in the Plan column, click View plan.
  • To select invoices to include or exclude from plans (companies and contacts will remain enrolled with revenue agent. Learn more about exclusions and enrollments):
    • In the right sidebar, in the Open invoices section, click the three vertical dots icon, then select Exclude from plan.
    • In the dialog box, click Exclude and regenerate plan. The plan will be regenerated using the remaining invoices. If you’re excluding an invoice from an active plan, you need to review and approve the new plan for outreach to resume.
  • To adjust the plan, in the upper right, click Adjust plan.
  • Update plans using Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant.
  • To edit scheduled emails, at the bottom of an email, click Edit.
  • To edit the subject of an email, next to Subject, click the edit icon and enter a subject.
  • To add other recipients, in the upper right of the email, click Cc or Bcc. Enter an email address, then press Return on your keyboard. You can add multiple recipients.
  • To change the scheduled date and time of future emails, in the Schedule section of the email, click the date and time pickers and select a date and time.
  • To edit the email, click the email body and make any updates. Use the formatting toolbar at the bottom of the email to format text and add links.
  • To save your changes, at the bottom of the email, click Save.

Manage companies and contacts

View all companies and contacts enrolled, whether plans are in review or active.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar, click Manage, then click Companies and contacts.
  • For an overview of a company or contact, click the company or contact name.
  • In the right panel, review company or contact details and their open invoices.
  • For plans in review, click Review plan to review, edit, and approve proposed plans.
  • For active plans, in the Plan column, click View plan to review and edit active plans.

Review revenue agent invoice statuses

Permissions required Super Admin or View permissions for invoices are required to review revenue agent invoice statuses .

Each invoice managed by revenue agent is assigned a status that reflects why it was included, excluded, or paused. To view revenue agent status of an invoice:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Invoices. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Invoices directly.
  • Click an invoice number.
  • In the right sidebar, under Revenue Agent, review the status.
  • Invoices can have the following statuses related to revenue agent. These statuses are separate from invoice statuses.
    • Not managed: the invoice isn’t managed by revenue agent.
    • Managed: the invoice is managed by revenue agent and is using credits.
    • Limit reached: your monthly credits have been used and the plan is currently paused. Credits reset based on when credits were added to your account. You can also add more. Learn more about managing credits.
    • Excluded: the invoice matches an exclusion segment and was automatically excluded or was manually excluded from revenue agent.
    • Processing: a payment for the invoice is currently processing.
    • Failed payment: the invoice was excluded after a payment attempt failed. Revenue agent secures the initial payment attempt but doesn’t follow up on failed payments. The failed payment recovery process handles next steps. Learn more about failed payments.
    • Autopay on: the invoice is excluded because its payment is managed outside revenue agent. The customer will be charged automatically.
    • Missing data: the invoice was excluded because required data is missing. Learn more about reviewing missing data.
    • No billing contact: the invoice was excluded because it’s missing a billing contact. Learn more about adding a billing contact.

Change email and escalation email addresses

Change the email address used to send emails in plans and the email address used for escalations. Changes are automatically saved.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar, click Configure, then click Account details.
  • To update the email address used to send emails in plans, under Email and escalation, select an option:
    • Shared inbox: use a team email address. Click Connect new shared inbox to connect a new team email address.
    • Individual inbox: use an individual email address. Click Connect new inbox to connect a new personal email address.
  • To update the escalation recipient, in the Escalation recipient field, enter the recipient’s email address. Learn more about escalation emails.

Turn off revenue agent

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar, click Configure, then click Account details.
  • Click Turn off Revenue Agent.
  • In the dialog box:
    • Optionally select the Also unenroll all [count] [contacts or companies] checkbox to unenroll companies contacts. Selecting this checkbox ensures no companies or contacts will automatically be enrolled if you turn revenue agent on again in the future. If you don’t select this checkbox, companies and contacts remain affiliated with revenue agent, but their plans are removed.
    • Click Turn off to confirm.

Next Steps

Learn more about setting up revenue agent, including enrolling accounts and starting automated outreach.

Manage workspaces, projects, and assets in HubSpot Work

Manage workspaces, projects, and assets in HubSpot Work as your team’s needs change. Use the AI assistant to rename workspaces, update access, and modify projects, tables, documents, forms, and AI agents with natural-language prompts. Manually delete workspaces, projects, and assets if needed.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

Permissions required An assigned Core, Sales, or Service seat is required to manage HubSpot work.

Understand limitations & considerations

Projects in HubSpot Work aren’t related to the projects object or Breeze Assistant projects.

Manage a workspace

To rename or update access to a workspace:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.
  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter a prompt describing the name of the workspace you want to change and the new name or access level.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.

To delete a workspace:

  • In the upper left, click the workspaces dropdown menu, then select the name of the workspace you want to delete.
  • In the upper right, click the three horizontal dots icon, then select Delete workspace.
  • In the dialog box, click Delete to confirm.
Manage a project

Use the AI assistant to make changes to your project. It’s recommended to be specific about the changes you want or to add a rule such as ask me clarifying questions to your prompt.

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter a prompt describing the changes you want to make.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.
Manage an asset

Use the AI assistant to modify tables, documents, forms, and AI agents. It’s recommended to be specific about the changes you want to make to reduce the number of turns per conversation.

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter a prompt describing the changes you want to make (e.g., create, edit, or delete).
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.

Next steps

Collaborate with your team in HubSpot Work.

Optimize content and improve brand visibility for AI

As a marketer, you want to ensure that your content reaches your target audience. To effectively market your business and generate leads through answer engines (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity), understand and apply the key strategies for Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) when creating marketing content.

For example, a marketer for Sprocket Supply Co., an ecommerce office supply company, wants to ensure their brand is cited when leads search for Best office chair suppliers in my area through an answer engine.

Optimizing for AEO can ensure that Sprocket Supply Co. is surfaced with a link in the generated results. When a lead clicks on the link, they will already have researched and compared different suppliers through the answer engine. Consequently, they are more prepared to purchase, which leads to higher conversion rates.

Below, review the two key strategies used for AEO: content optimization and visibility. Then, learn how you can use different tools in your HubSpot account to optimize your content for AI and build visibility across different channels.

Understand answer engine optimization strategies

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) focuses on two key strategies: content optimization and content visibility across different channels. Each piece of content you create, from pages to social posts, can contribute to the overall success of this strategy.

These two strategies determine whether your content is parsed and surfaced in AI-powered search across answer engines, and consequently, the impact of your marketing efforts in tangible results such as traffic, engagement, and conversions.

  • Content optimization: creating and structuring content in a way that answer engines can find and understand your content. When writing or generating content for answer engines, there are specific strategies that you can use, such as content structure, answer clarity, and multi-format accessibility. Learn more about the key best practices for AEO.
  • Visibility: how likely answer engines are to surface your content. This is determined by a combination of the following:
    • Consistency: whether messaging is aligned across your different channels.
    • Authority: whether the answer engine determines that your content displays subject matter expertise.
    • Density: whether you have a multi-channel presence. This is also impacted by the frequency and saturation (e.g., depth) of your content.

Optimize marketing content for answer engines

To ensure your content is surfaced by answer engines, optimize the structure and format of your written content with these best practices:

  • Incorporate schemas into your pages: add schemas to your pages to provide structured data so that answer engines can interpret your pages. Answer engines will use a page’s schema markup to classify, rank, and display content in search results. Adding schemas will increase the likelihood of your pages being cited. Learn more about incorporating schemas into your page.
  • Use direct, concise, and consistent language and formatting: use action-oriented sentences beginning with verbs and avoid unnecessary adverbs and adjectives. Use clear headings for each section and follow a predictable structure (e.g., H2 header for sections, H3 headers for subsections, and so on).
  • Consider the best formatting for the type of information: use numbered steps and checklists for sequential instructions. Use bulleted lists for options. Use tables for comparisons or lists with multiple sections.
  • Avoid using visuals as the main source of information: only use images (e.g., graphs, charts) as a secondary source to complement written descriptions.
  • Use alt text when adding visuals: when using images, include alt text to help answer engines interpret the image within the page context. The alt text should be specific. For example, use “an ergonomic office chair with armrests in a black mesh fabric” as opposed to “an office chair”.
  • Use conditional statements: write conditional rules (e.g., if, then) for processes to help AI provide actionable answers based on specific scenarios. For example, use the following:
    • If the price of a product is over $500, always include a link to the 5-year warranty offering.
    • If the channel is email, include a ‘Shop Now’ button at the end of the email before the sign-off.
  • Include negative constraints: when documenting rules, be clear about what is not allowed to avoid AI hallucinations. For example, use the following constraints:
    • No exaggerated durability. Do not use words like “indestructible,” “permanent,” or “forever” for consumables like pens or folders. Use “long-lasting” or “heavy-duty”.
    • No speculation on health. Do not claim that furniture “cures” or “fixes” medical conditions (e.g., “cures back pain”). Instead, use “supports spinal alignment” or “designed for ergonomic comfort”.
  • Include examples: where possible, show the agent what’s “good” or “bad.” This is particularly helpful for rule and process documentation. For example, use the following good and bad examples:
    • Good: do always use provided numbers (e.g., 80 GSM).
    • Bad: do not guess or use the term “Heavy-duty” without technical specifications.

For example, if a marketer for Sprocket Supply Co. was creating a blog post, they might include these components:

  • Schema: @type: Article

  • Target title: Building a Home Office: Expert Answers to Your Setup Questions

  • H2 Headers (question-based):

    • What is the ideal height for a home office desk?

    • Is a dual-monitor setup better for productivity?

    • How often should I replace my office chair?

    • What table lighting is best for reducing eye strain at a computer?

  • H3 strategies: this can be used under the What table lighting is best for reducing eye strain at a computer H2 header

    • Is warm or cool lighting better for a work setup?
    • How bright should my office table lighting be?

  • Formatted information: a table comparing the specifications of different table lighting options or the lifespan for different office chairs.

Audit existing content for AEO

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription or a HubSpot AEO subscription is required to use HubSpot AEO.

Well-structured content helps both AI and users understand the information that you’re trying to convey. Unique content that accurately reflects your brand will also help to establish consistency in your messaging.

  • Audit your existing content for AEO:
    • It’s recommended to use HubSpot’s AEO grader as a starting point.
    • Use this audit to determine the key areas and pages that you’d like to optimize.
  • Use HubSpot AEO to analyze your brand AEO: measure how well your brand AEO performs by running your prompts daily against answer engines, then aggregate results into visibility metrics.
    • Use HubSpot AEO metrics to support a comprehensive analysis of brand mentions, prompt coverage, and citation patterns over time. This allows you to track visibiility across different benchmarks such as frequency across answer engines, track your citations with different metrics, compare your visibility metrics with competitors, and more.
    • It’s recommended to track your brand’s AEO metrics before and after making any changes to measure the actual impact of your efforts. For example, review your brand’s citation rate before and after restructuring your home page for AEO.
    • Within AEO, you can then take action based on recommendations, including automatically generating content with AI that you can review before publishing.

It is recommended to use both HubSpot AEO grader and the HubSpot AEO tool to audit your content. HubSpot’s AEO Grader produces a snapshot of your answer engine visibility. Use this data to determine where your brand holds authority and where content may fall short. Then, use HubSpot AEO for ongoing prompt tracking, competitor analysis, and prioritized recommendations to address gaps the HubSpot AEO grader may surface.

Set up and tailor your AI tools

Subscription required A Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use knowledge vaults in projects.

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use brand voice and brand identity.

While you can use Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s AI conversational assistant, to review content, it’s recommended to set up the following tools to refine your outputs for both your branding and answer engines.

  • Set up Breeze Assistant so users can access it for content generation and recommendations.

  • Create a project specifically to optimize your content for AEO:

    • Create a project with added instructions based on the AEO optimization strategies that you’d like to put in place. After publishing your project, access the project from Breeze Assistant across HubSpot.
    • Create a custom knowledge vault to provide additional context to your project. Without a custom knowledge vault, any projects will be limited to the data configured in your AI context. Adding a knowledge vault will allow your projects to generate refined outputs tailored to your brand and audience. When creating source content, follow the same best practices for writing content for AI.

  • Tailor your AI tools in HubSpot to your brand:

    • Set up your brand voice in your HubSpot account to establish consistency in your marketing content. This brand voice will then be applied whenever generating content in your HubSpot account. Learn more about setting up your brand voice to optimize for AI adoption.
    • Set up your brand identity context to provide additional context to AI when creating blogs, landing pages, and case studies. Learn more about setting up your brand identity context to optimize for AI adoption.
    • Set up your buyer personas to determine your target audience when generating content. Learn more about defining sales details to optimize for AI adoption.
Optimize new and existing content for AEO

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use Marketing Studio and AEO.

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use content remix.

After auditing your content and setting up your AI tools, review your data and use recommendations to optimize existing content for AEO. Generate new content based on recommendations to avoid missing potential citation opportunities. When optimizing your content with AI, it is strongly recommended to manually review and edit your content.

  • If you don’t have any existing content: use Breeze Assistant to generate new content. When generating content for the first time, use Marketing Studio to create a high-level overview of your content to ensure alignment across channels and consistency with your brand messaging. You’ll also be able to use campaign templates to get started with content ideas.

  • If you have existing content: use Breeze Assistant to review your written content such as pages and social posts, then generate recommendations to improve AEO.

    • For example, you could use this prompt: “Review the content in this page and optimize and generate suggestions for AEO.”
    • While it is strongly recommended to use Breeze Assistant to optimize your content directly within HubSpot, if you prefer to use another AI tool, use a similar prompt, then use a preview URL of your current content draft for pages or blog posts.

  • If you have existing limited content that has been optimized for AEO: use content remix to create additional pieces of similar content across different channels. Alternatively, you can also use the Recommendations tab in AEO to review potential topics and generate content.

Refine your marketing content based on performance

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use AEO.

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to run A/B tests on your pages.

After optimizing your content for AI, test and review your performance to understand which topics drive leads, identify underperforming content, and make changes to improve your content.

  • Repeat an AEO audit on a regular basis to analyze the affect of your changes on AEO. For example, you may want to do an audit cycle every 3 months.
  • A/B test your pages: test two different versions of your page. While AEO metrics are not tracked through A/B testing, you can track marketing outcomes that can be correlated to organic visibility. Successful marketing outcomes to look for in the “winning” version include a higher number of conversions and a higher citation rate (i.e. that version is being surfaced more often in answer engines). The outcomes of your A/B tests can then be incorporated into your brand voice or used as a consideration when generating or reviewing content moving forward.

For example, a marketer at Sprocket Supply Co. creates an A/B test for two versions of a landing page offering an ergonomic chair guide. They test titles such as The Guide to Ergonomic Seating for 2026 against The Best Ergonomic Office Chairs in 2025. When The Best Ergonomic Office Chairs in 2025 has higher citation and conversion rates, they update the brand voice to recommend similar titles moving forward.

Learn more about A/B testing.

Improve brand AI visibility

After establishing consistency with a brand voice and optimizing content with Breeze, your content should be structured in a way that can be parsed by both humans and AI.

The goal of visibility is to ensure that when an answer engine surfaces an answer, your content is selected over other content that may be similar. The next step in improving your visibility will be to build consistency, density, and authority.

Plan multi-channel campaigns

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use Marketing Studio and AEO.

AI models use content across all platforms to assess brand authority and reputation. Building a presence across different social and media platforms can influence AI visibility. A key strategy for AEO is increasing brand presence across the wider web. For example, if Sproket Supply Co. is regularly mentioned in different social posts or forums.

Providing concise answers on these platforms will build experience, expertise, authoritativeness, and trustworthiness (EEAT), which is used to rate content for quality and determine which content should be cited.

  • Use Marketing Studio (BETA) when planning your campaigns:
    • In the canvas view in Marketing Studio, review all assets to ensure that your marketing strategy has a multi-channel approach and that your content is aligned across these different channels.
    • Generate content directly from within Marketing Studio. For example, review if there are topics that are performing particularly well or a successful piece of content has not been replicated in another channel, such as a social post, video, or podcast.
  • Use content remix to reuse your content and ensure that it reaches multiple channels. For example, you could remix a video about the different office furniture offered in your store into a blog post, an Instagram post, and a YouTube short for customers who look for content on those platforms.
  • Use HubSpot’s AI to help you generate content across multiple channels:

    • Generate images using AI

    • Use AI to generate social post content

    • Generate social posts from blog posts

    • Use AI assistants to create ad campaigns

    • Generate blog posts

    • Generate marketing emails with AI email creation (BETA)

Reach a wider audience with translated content

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to automatically translate multi-language content.

Translate and set up your pages for multiple languages to reach a wider audience. For example, Sprocket Supply Co. has a branch in Miami, a city with both English-speaking and Spanish-speaking communities. A marketer for the company translates the content for the local website to effectively market office supplies to businesses in both populations.

  • Automatically translate page and post content into other languages with Breeze for your website pages, landing pages, and blog posts.
  • Ensure that content is indexed for localized search queries:
    • Tag your language content with hreflang to allow AI to recognize and serve the correct language version. Learn more about using hreflang tag attributes.
    • Adapt content for cultural nuances and local search behaviors. Localizing casual language will improve relevancy for AI models and increase the likelihood of citations. For example, certain puns or idioms may not work in other languages, such as ‘Broken pencils are pointless. That’s why we have a 20% sale on all sharpeners!’. In the translated versions of your content, you’ll want to change the pun used.

Glossary

  • Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): the strategy of optimizing your content to be surfaced by answer engines.
  • Answer engines: AI platforms and answer engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Gemini.
  • Citations: whether your brand appears in the answers provided by answer engines.
  • Channels: different platforms where you can host content or where references to your content may appear. Some examples include websites, social media platforms such as Instagram or Tiktok, video hosting platforms such as YouTube, forums, such as Reddit, and directories such as Yelp.

Review product updates with Breeze Assistant

Use Breeze Assistant to review and understand recent product updates in HubSpot. Instead of manually browsing release notes, ask Breeze Assistant questions in natural language to get summaries of new features, changes, and improvements.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings to use Breeze Assistant.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Some product updates or features may only be available in beta. To access these, learn how to opt your account into a public beta feature.

How to review product updates with Breeze Assistant

Breeze Assistant can answer questions about product updates and give concise summaries. Instead of reviewing full release notes, users can ask natural-language questions and get a high-level overview of recent changes, along with links to relevant product updates when more detail is needed.

What new features were released this week?

To prompt Breeze Assistant about product updates:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • Enter a prompt and then click the send prompt icon.
  • Review the product update information. Breeze Assistant’s response may include:
    • Summaries of the recent releases
    • Filtered information that reflects the user’s available tools
    • Links to relevant tabs on the Product Updates page for deeper review.

Run agents and review output

Run agents, monitor outputs, and take actions in one place using the agent inbox. You can also run agents from other CRM cards, automations, and Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant. Agent output includes the sources used, export options, and sharing settings available for each run. In this article, learn how to run agents, review and filter output, refine results, and export or share agent runs.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

Permissions required Super Admin or agent access permissions are required to run agents.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required when a custom agent performs work such as thinking, taking actions, and generating content to complete a run.

To run agents and review output in the agent inbox, a Super Admin must turn the following switches on in AI Settings:

  • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
  • CRM data
  • Customer conversion data
  • Files data
  • Give users access to Breeze Assistant

Run agents from the agent inbox

Run agents from the agent inbox to execute their configured instructions, inputs, and actions.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.
  • Click the Run agents dropdown menu and select an agent to run on the top left.
  • In the right panel, enter the required inputs for the agent and then click Run agent.
Missing tool
What the error means

The Write to your HubSpot CRM records action isn’t turned on. By default, custom agents only read information, and you must turn on write access.

How to resolve the error

Turn on the Write to your HubSpot CRM records action or edit your agent instructions to remove any write actions.

Unable to run agent
What the error means

A general error message that indicates an issue occurred and the agent couldn’t run.

How to resolve the error
  • Test the agent: run a simulation in the agent builder and review the output.
  • Review access: check the owner of the agent and ensure their user permissions allow the agent to run. For example, the agent owner must have view access to contacts for the agent to synthesize CRM contact data.
  • Review with Breeze Assistant: copy the agent instructions and paste into Breeze Assistant. Prompt Breeze Assistant to review for conflicts in the instructions.
  • Support: if you are still seeing an error, post on the Community (all users) or contact the support team (Starter, Professional, and Enterprise only).

Run agents from other sources

In addition to the agent inbox, run agents from automations, Breeze Assistant, or CRM cards.

Automations

When you run an agent via an automation, the agent owner’s permissions are used. This means if an agent owner doesn’t have access to certain HubSpot tools, the corresponding agent actions may fail. The automation you can run your agent from depends on your subscription:

  • Starter: run your agent from an automation in the automation side panel. Learn how to create automations in agent hub.
  • Professional or Enterprise: run your agent from a workflow. Learn how to create workflows in agent hub.
Breeze Assistant
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the prompt text field, enter @[agent name] then your prompt.
  • Click the send prompt icon and review the output.
Breeze Assistant on the HubSpot mobile app
  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • In the lower right, tap Ask Breeze.
  • In the prompt text field, enter @[agent name] then your prompt.
  • Click the send prompt icon and review the output.
CRM cards

Add an agent to a CRM card to run agents directly from a record. Learn how to run agents from a CRM card.

Review agent output from the agent inbox

Review agent output from the agent inbox when monitoring multiple agents or recent runs. You can also filter the agent output and mark all agent output as read.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.

  • By default, the inbox is filtered to Owners: All agent runs. To filter the inbox, click the Filters dropdown menu and select the filters. Then, click Apply.

    • Unread messages: displays agent runs that haven’t been viewed.
    • Status: displays agent runs based on their current status.
      • Needs approval: runs waiting for tool approval.
      • Success: completed runs without errors.
      • Running: runs currently in progress.
      • Failed: runs that encountered an error.
      • Waiting: runs queued or paused before execution.
    • Agents: displays agent runs for a specific agent (e.g., Company Research Agent)
    • Source: displays agent runs based on how they were triggered (e.g., Breeze Studio or Automation).
    • Owners: displays agent runs based on ownership or sharing context.
      • All agent runs: all runs visible to the user.
      • Shared with me: runs shared by other users or teams.
      • Me: runs owned by the user.

  • In the left panel, click an agent run.

  • In the right panel, review your output. At the top, you can review the following:

    • Run title: the name of the run. To rename a run:
      • In the left panel, click the ellipsesIcon three horizontal dots icon, and select Rename.
      • Then, enter a new name for your run.
    • Where the run was triggered from: whether the run was triggered from Breeze Studio or a different tool.
    • Status: the status of the agent’s run, such as Completed, In progress, and more.
    • User: the name of the user who triggered the run.
    • Estimated credits: the estimated credits cost to run the agent.

  • By default, agent output will be optimized for readability. To view the output in text instead, click the dashboardsIcon Output dropdown menu and select Text Output in the top right.

  • To take further action on your agent output, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon. Then, you can export, share, or maximize your output view.

  • To review the thinking or reasoning steps behind each run, click [x] thinking steps to expand the section.

  • To review the sources the agent used to generate its output, click [x] sources at the bottom of the output. A list of sources used to generate the output will appear.

Refine agent output

When reviewing agent output, you can request additional changes. The agent will re-run with new reasoning steps and produce a revised output. The refined output will appear under the previous output in your agent inbox.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.
  • In the left panel, select a run that you’d like to refine.
  • In the right panel, in the chat box, enter text to refine your output.For example, you can enter “make it shorter” to make your output more concise.

Export agent output

Export your agent’s run output to a PDF file for sharing, record keeping, or offline review.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.
  • In the left panel, select a run that you’d like to share.
  • At the top, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon. Then, click Export PDF or the pdfFileIcon PDF file icon.
  • When the export is ready, click the notification notification icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the right panel, click the export notification to begin the download.

Share agent output

Share agent output with other users or teams by updating run visibility settings and copying a shareable link.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.
  • In the left panel, select a run that you’d like to share.
  • At the top, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon. Then, click Share or the shareIcon Share icon.
  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select from the following:
    • Only me: the agent’s output will only be visible to the user who ran the agent.
    • Everyone in my portal: all users within the account, that have access to the agent, can view the agent’s run output.
    • Specific users and teams: only the selected users and teams that have access to the agent, can view the agent’s run output.
  • When finished, click Copy link and send to your recipients.
  • To unshare an agent’s run output, click Share. In the dialog box, select Only me and then click Done.

Run effective marketing with less manual effort

Streamline your marketing process by reducing manual, repetitive tasks so you can launch campaigns faster. When running marketing with less manual effort, you can focus your time on optimizing content and planning effective strategies.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co., an ecommerce company selling sustainable office supplies, uses HubSpot’s AI tools and content remix to generate assets, instead of creating everything from scratch.

Below, learn how to reduce manual effort when planning a campaign, creating campaign assets, and distributing your campaign assets.

Learn more about this feature by joining a small group coaching session

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Pre-requisites

When using the following recommendations to streamline your marketing efforts, it is recommended to use HubSpot’s AI tools, as well as Breeze Assistant. To ensure the quality of your generated content, it is recommended to:

  • Set up Breeze Assistant: throughout the framework, Breeze Assistant will be used to generate insights and content. Suggested prompts will also be provided. Learn how to configure and use Breeze Assistant.
  • Set up user permissions: assign user permissions for the relevant tools. For example, to create campaigns, users will need Campaign Edit permissions.
  • Define your audience: define your highest-value customers to create an audience profile. You can also use Breeze Assistant to summarize CRM data for this profile. This will be used when setting up your brand identity.
  • Craft a style guide and use it in HubSpot: define a brand style guide to capture your unique branding and how it applies to your target audience. This will be your brand identity context. Input this into the brand identity tool. Then, when creating content with AI, brand-specific context including voice, tone, ideal customer profile, products, and competitive insight will always be applied.
  • Provide context to AI tools: create a project for your marketing campaigns and a knowledge vault to add any additional brand context.
  • Review outputs: review AI outputs throughout the process. Flagging any patterns of errors will help to refine your style guide and prompts.

Plan your campaigns

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use Marketing Studio.

As a marketer setting up a campaign, set up your campaign story before creating any campaign assets. This includes the key ideas and messaging that you’d like to convey, as well as the purpose and plan for your campaign. Learn how to define your campaign story.

Then, use Marketing Studio as a home base to design your campaign, create assets, and execute your plan in a single workspace.

  • When conceptualizing your campaign strategy, use Marketing Studio to create an outline of what your campaign and assets could look like, as a starting point for your campaign planning.
  • Then, use Marketing Studio to make content decisions, such as:
    • Planning the timeline for your campaign and release of campaign assets. For example, if you’re running a social campaign, when each post should be published. You’ll also be able to review the different publish dates for each asset type in the campaign calendar.
    • Manage the progress and performance of each campaign asset. From the Board and Approvals views, you’ll be able to review whether each asset has been set up and is ready for the campaign.
    • Visualizing the distribution of your assets. On the Marketing Studio canvas, you’ll be able to review the count of each asset type, and group different assets together.
  • Use content remix to remix assets directly from Marketing Studio. In the section below, learn how to use content remix to adapt existing assets and create new assets for different channels.

Adapt existing assets for different channels

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use content remix.

Instead of spending time and effort manually recreating and adapting an existing asset for different channels, use content remix to generate multiple assets from a successful piece of content.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. is releasing a new line of ergonomic office chairs. Using content remix, a specification document for these new chairs is used to generate social posts and marketing emails.

The new content can be directly used for promotion across different channels, or used as a more concrete starting point for your marketing content.

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to generate pages with HubSpot’s AI tools.

Run multi-step research with Breeze Assistant

Use Breeze Assistant’s research function to answer a question that either requires analysis across multiple data sources or benefits from a structured plan. Breeze Assistant generates a research plan for you to review, runs it in order, and returns a report. For example, research why form conversion dropped last quarter and compare against the same quarter from last year.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.
  • Turn on the following context switches in your AI settings so Breeze Assistant can use additional sources for research context:
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversation data
    • Files data
Understand limitations & considerations

User permissions determine the data Breeze Assistant can view and use. For example, if your user cannot access marketing campaigns, Breeze Assistant cannot perform research in this area.

Start research

Start research from suggested prompts that use contextual data from your current screen. You can also enter a custom prompt to start research.

To research with Breeze Assistant:

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the prompt text field, click the use tools icon, then select Start research.
  • Start the research:
    • To use a suggested prompt, in the Research card, select a prompt. Breeze Assistant automatically sends a pre-filled prompt.
    • To use a custom prompt, in the prompt text field, enter a prompt that describes what you want to research.
  • Breeze Assistant generates a research plan for you to review.
  • To optionally refine the research plan:
    • Click an item in the research plan, then enter a prompt to refine or ask questions about the selected item.
    • Click Edit plan, then enter a prompt to refine the entire research plan.
    • Breeze Assistant generates an updated research plan.
  • Click Run to start the research.

Once Breeze Assistant completes the plan, the research displays in the artifact viewer panel alongside your conversation. Share or download the research artifact so other users in your account can view it.

Search connected apps with Breeze Assistant

Find relevant information from connected apps (e.g., Slack, Gmail) using Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant . Ask questions in plain language and get synthesized answers drawn from your connected tools, regardless of where the data is stored. This allows you to find data without switching between multiple apps.

In this article, learn how to install and manage apps, structure prompts for connected app searches, and explore example use cases for support, marketing, and sales teams.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

Before you search connected apps with Breeze Assistant you must:

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.
  • Understand that user permissions determine which actions can be performed with Breeze Assistant.
  • Install apps in your HubSpot account before Breeze Assistant can access their data.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Search within filters from apps isn’t supported. To filter app results, use the app’s search syntax. For example, to search Gmail for unread emails from John Smith last month, use m:john is:unread older_than:1m.

Manage apps

Breeze Assistant can analyze information from apps in the App Marketplace. Install or uninstall apps to control which data Breeze Assistant can access.

Install apps
  • Navigate to the App Marketplace.
  • Select the app you’d like to install.
  • On the app listing page, click Install.
  • Complete the app’s installation flow. Review the specific instructions in the app’s setup guide in the Overview section.
Uninstall apps

To prevent Breeze Assistant from using data from an app, learn more about uninstalling apps.

Ask Breeze Assistant questions using connected apps

After installing apps, Breeze Assistant can use information from those apps to generate responses.

Write prompts

Breeze Assistant can answer open-ended questions. To improve response quality, structure prompts using the following elements:

Element

Description

Task

State the action to complete (e.g., summarize notes, write an email, answer a question).

Context

Include background information so Breeze Assistant can look for relevant data and focus the response on the key points based on the context.

Response format

Specify tone, length, and structure (e.g., professional, short answer, report, bullet list).

Search focus

Include specific app names, files, folders, or dates to narrow the search. Add up to five URLs and Breeze Assistant will use them as context to respond to the question.

Select apps to search
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the right panel, click the Apps dropdown menu and select the checkboxes next to the apps you’d like to search.
  • To search all apps, click to toggle the Use all apps as sources switch on.
  • To save the selected apps for future chats with Breeze Assistant so that those apps are searched first, click to toggle the Keep selection for future chats switch on.
  • Continue using Breeze Assistant.

Example: Search connected apps for support, marketing, or sales questions

The following examples show how to search connected apps with Breeze Assistant based on common support, marketing, or sales questions.

Customer support

You’re a customer support representative and you need to write instructions for a customer to reset their password. Relevant information exists in Slack and Google Docs.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the right panel, click the Apps dropdown menu and select the checkbox next to Slack and Google Docs apps.
  • Enter this prompt: How does a user reset their account password?
Marketing

You’re a marketing manager and someone sent you information about a new product in Teams and in Google Docs. You need to create a blog post using the information shared.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the right panel, click the Apps dropdown menu and select the checkbox next to Teams and Google Docs apps.
  • Enter this prompt: Write a blog post about [product]. It should be 5-7 minutes long and about five paragraphs. Use this sytle guide [link], and our blog [link] with other blog posts for reference.
Sales

You’re a sales rep and you need to know what the key differentiators are for a product. You don’t know where to find this information.

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the right panel, click the Apps dropdown menu and toggle the Use all apps as sources switch on.
  • Enter this prompt: What are our key differentiators for [product]?

Set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features

Before you get started with HubSpot’s AI, learn how to set up your account for the best results from artificial intelligence features. The steps below outline processes and best practices for admins adopting AI tools in HubSpot, from initial set up and personalization to using AI features and tracking their impact.

Permissions required Super Admin or Partner admin permissions are required to configure the account and feature settings mentioned throughout the article.

Set up: Turn on AI features and give access to account data

To use basic AI capabilities in your account, turn them on in your AI settings. Turning on these account-wide settings won’t consume HubSpot Credits. Credits are used by specific features, indicated by HubSpot Credits icons shown in your account. Learn how to manage HubSpot credits and refer to HubSpot’s Product & Services Catalog for details about features that use credits.

Turn on the following AI settings:

  • Give users access to generative AI tools and features: allow users to generate content throughout the HubSpot account, including in text editors (e.g., marketing emails, blog posts), the Conversations Inbox, sales emails, templates, Breeze Assistant, and more.
  • Give generative AI tools and features powered by AI service providers access to specific data categories: once generative AI tools and features are turned on, give access to the following sources that provide context to improve AI-generated results. This helps personalize results based on your account’s unique data.
    • CRM data: your account’s CRM data, including contacts, companies, deals, tickets, notes, and feedback.
    • Customer conversation data: data from interactions with customers, including call transcripts, call recordings, emails, and chats.
    • Files data: public files and documents stored in the files and documents tools.
  • Give users access to Breeze Assistant: allow all users to use Breeze Assistant, a conversational AI assistant available throughout your HubSpot account to help with tasks and generate content. Access to Breeze Assistant is turned on by default. To restrict access for certain users, manage individual access in user permissions.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. is an e-commerce office supply company releasing a new line of furniture. Turning on these settings sets up the foundational HubSpot’s AI tools to help Sprocket Supply Co.’s users with their work for the release.

Team

How they can use generative AI and Breeze Assistant

Marketing

Generate copy and hashtags for the social post announcing the new line.

Sales

Summarize calls with prospects interested in the new line.

Support

Draft responses to order inquiries using a professional tone.

Operations

Get recommendations for workflow enrollment triggers and actions to nurture leads interested in the new line.

When you’re ready to use more tools, set them up in their own space.

Control access: Set up permissions for AI tools

After you turn on account-wide AI settings, manage how users can access AI through user permission configuration and feature-specific access. It’s recommended to allow access to Breeze Assistant as it can help with daily tasks without using HubSpot Credits. Agents and assistants should be limited to specific users to avoid unintentional process changes or HubSpot Credits consumption.

Manage user access to Breeze Assistant

By default, Breeze Assistant access is turned on, and all users can chat with it. To manage individual access (e.g., remove access for specific users) or make Breeze Assistant accessible only to admins, update the Breeze Assistant permission for certain users or teams.

For Breeze Assistant features embedded in other tools, users must also have permissions for those tools. For example, to generate content in a blog post, a user must have permissions to use Breeze Assistant and to edit blog posts.

Manage user access to specific features, projects, and agents

Subscription required

  • A Data Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use data studio.
  • A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use customer agent.
  • A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to use agent builder and prospecting agent.

Unlike the default Breeze Assistant, other projects and agents are for specific use cases (e.g., drafting prospecting emails, managing support tickets) and may use HubSpot Credits. For this reason, it’s recommended to limit access to only the teams that need them.

You can customize user permissions and feature settings to ensure the correct users can create, edit, or use projects and agents.

Tip: If a permission uses HubSpot Credits, it means the associated actions consume credits. Limit which users have permission to use features that consume HubSpot Credits until you’re certain about your account’s AI strategy. You can update permissions at any time if users need access later on.

Personalize: Teach HubSpot’s AI tools about your business

Maximize HubSpot’s AI impact by personalizing it to your business. The Personalize phase builds your digital identity, moving from basic automation to a tailored experience that understands your organization’s specific context. Providing this personalization ensures AI-generated content (e.g., blog posts, customer service agents) is accurate, aligned with your business, and consistent across your various teams.

Configure your brand kit

Your brand kit is the foundational source of truth for your business’s visual and verbal identity. In the context of AI, it functions as the definitive instruction manual that prevents assistants and agents from generating generic, robotic content. Brand kits provide:

  • Visual consistency: centralize your logos, color palettes, and typography to maintain a cohesive aesthetic across all social media assets and presentation decks.
  • Verbal identity: formalize your brand voice and lexicon to provide the necessary context that prevents assistants and agents from generating generic or robotic responses.
  • Brand trust: demonstrate professional excellence through cross-platform uniformity, ensuring customers perceive your organization as reliable rather than disorganized.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. can leverage these settings to ensure every email draft for their new products adheres to their technical context. HubSpot’s AI can create social media assets incorporating their brand palettes and addressing the pain points defined in their buyer profiles. This produces a foundational draft that requires minimal manual editing to meet organizational standards.

To get the most out of your brand kit, set up the following:

  • Edit your brand’s logo, favicon, brand colors, fonts, and theme.
  • Set up your brand identity context to crawl your website domain, and establish a voice, tone, ideal client profile, products, and competitive information through website context.
  • Set up your brand voice to tailor generated or written content to your brand’s specific voice.
  • Configure your brand assistant as a quality control measure to verify that all AI-generated content remains consistent with your brand identity.
Complete your company profile

Your company profile serves as the source of truth for your organization’s digital identity for HubSpot’s AI tools, specifying exactly who it represents, its domain, and the market in which it operates.

Accurately configuring these details establishes a framework that prevents HubSpot’s AI from hallucinating foundational aspects of your business. This provides benefits such as:

  • Branding integrity: centralize your company name and domain to ensure that AI-generated content and customer communications consistently reflect your approved professional identity.
  • Contextual accuracy: formalize your industry to provide HubSpot’s AI tools with the necessary logic for navigation; establishing this starting point ensures customer interactions are tailored to your specific sector rather than generic information.

Learn more about how to edit your company profile in your AI settings.

Provide details about your customers and sales process

Add information about your customers, buyers, and sales processes to give AI tools the necessary context to help support consistent sales execution. This information helps HubSpot’s AI tools personalize results and recommendations across a variety of buyers and customers.

For example, the Sprocket Supply Co. sales team is reaching out to prospective buyers for their new line of furniture. With a defined product catalog and unique buying profiles for Executives and Individual Contributors, sales reps can generate emails to target role-specific needs and include tailored product recommendations.

Set up the following:

  • Create ideal customer profiles that define your target markets based on industry, size, region, and other characteristics.
  • Define your product and service offerings, including your value proposition, the pain points your company solves, and the specific product and services available.
  • Create buyer profiles that outline the attributes of certain prospects and explain how to target them.
  • Create selling profiles that define the communication style and tone that AI-generated sales content should use with specific prospects.

Organize: Clean up data to improve results

Subscription required A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to use data quality tools.

HubSpot’s AI tools use your CRM data to retrieve information and generate responses. If your data is incomplete or inconsistent, AI outputs may be inaccurate or irrelevant. Maintaining clean, structured data helps ensure reliable results.

Follow these best practices to maintain good data hygiene in your HubSpot account:

  • Fill in and standardize property values: incomplete or inconsistent property values can lead to inaccurate or generic AI responses. Set up property validation rules to enforce consistent property value formatting, mark important properties as required when creating records, and archive properties with low fill rates.
  • Identify and merge duplicate records: if multiple records exist for the same object (e.g., two HubSpot company records), HubSpot’s AI tools may reference outdated, conflicting, or incomplete information. Use the duplicate management tool to find duplicates and merge them to maintain one source of truth.
  • Capture missing or unstructured data: HubSpot’s AI tools reference unstructured data, such as emails and call transcripts. Ensure teams are logging their customer conversations in HubSpot, including sending or logging emails in HubSpot and recording calls. Use clear and descriptive language when writing email subject lines and activity titles.

For an overview of your account’s data quality and recommended next steps, learn how to use data quality tools.

Add context: Connect documentation and external sources

Combined with personalized context and an organized CRM, documentation and external data gives HubSpot’s AI tools the full picture of how your business and its employees work.

Connect files and written content

Accurate and well-structured context is foundational to the quality of AI-generated outputs. For projects and agents, such as the sales coach assistant, context about your business processes and rules help provide personalized recommendations to account users. For customer facing agents, such as the customer agent, context about your products, services, and policies help provide accurate answers to customers.

When customizing AI features, such as assistants and agents, connect sources such as files, knowledge base articles, blog posts, and landing or web pages. Learn more about best practices when writing content for AI tools:

  • Optimize content for AI engines
  • Prepare content for the customer agent
  • Best practices for agent content sources
Connect external data

To allow assistants and agents to access data from third-party apps, connect apps from the HubSpot Marketplace. For example, add Google Calendar to connect your calendar data, Zoom to connect Zoom meeting recordings, or Asana to connect your tasks. You can also use AI connectors, such as the HubSpot Gemini connector, to allow other AI models to access your HubSpot data.

Connecting your tools and data sources with HubSpot provides all the relevant context for personalized AI outputs from HubSpot’s AI. Review available apps and their capabilities in the HubSpot Marketplace.

  • A Sales or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use meeting notetaker.
  • A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use marketing studio.
  • A Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use knowledge base agent and reply recommendations.
  • A Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to use prospecting agent and smart properties.
  • A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use customer agent.

Monitor: Test and improve AI tools and processes

While the above recommendations prepare you to adopt AI features in HubSpot, you should track results and iterate over time to continue improving your AI outputs.

For example, the Sprocket Supply Co. sales team uses Breeze Assistant to prepare for calls. The sales manager tracks time spent on call prep and rep confidence in Breeze Assistant responses. For most reps, there’s a decrease in time spent on prep and responses are accurate, which is a positive indicator for the tool’s adoption. For some reps, the answers are too general. The sales manager should recommend that these sales reps record their calls in HubSpot to give the assistant personalized context about their call strategies.
