Glossary

  • Breeze Assistant: an AI companion that supports users in HubSpot, using account context to give relevant recommendations and insights. Breeze Assistant can be used for a variety of tasks, such as refining or generating content, preparing for meetings, and summarizing data.
  • Agents: AI agents that help automate work across HubSpot. Use pre-built a gents from the Marketplace or customize agents in the agent builder.
  • Agent builder: a workspace to manage and customize Agents.
  • Projects: configurable AI experiences created in Breeze Assistant to help with specific tasks or processes. They follow instructions, tools, and knowledge set by admins and can be seen inside Breeze Assistant or other HubSpot-supported areas..

Set up and use the company research agent

With the company research agent, you can view important information about a companies funding signals, changes in the company’s structure, tech stack, and more. The agent consolidates company research from your CRM data, public web sources, and industry trends into one structured summary, reducing the manual research needed before outreach or meetings. For example, sales reps can prepare for a meeting with a prospect’s latest news and company overview.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

  • On the Company Research Agent details page, click Add beta agent.

Configure the company research agent

Once the company research agent is added, Super Admins can manage access, add extra instructions, and automate the agent.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to configure the agent.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Hub. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub directly.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • On the Company Research Agent card click Edit.
  • To continue configuring the agent, learn more about customizing agents in the agent builder..

Please note: by default, Super Admins can edit the agent and all users can run the agent. Learn more about managing agent access.

Use the company research agent

The company research agent gathers and evaluates data from sources that are accessible to the public, such as news and information on products or services. Additionally, the agent presents an overview of competitors, industry patterns, and data from your own CRM.

You can use the company research agent from the Agent Inbox and from company records.

Subscription required A Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the company research agent from company records.

Agent Inbox
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.
  • In the upper left, click the Run agents dropdown menu, then select the Company research agent.
  • In the panel, enter the required inputs for the agent and then click Run agent.

Learn more about running agents and reviewing output in the agent inbox.

Company records

To add the company research agent card:

  • Click the name of a company.
  • In the upper right of the middle column, click Customize. You’ll be directed to the Record Customization tab for companies your settings.
  • Create the Agent card and select Company Research Agent.
  • Finish your customizations and then click Save.

To use the company research agent card:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.
  • Click the name of a company.
  • On Company research agent card, click Start research.
  • Once the agent has researched the company, view the output on the Company research agent card.

Set up and use the customer health agent

With the customer health agent, you can assess the health of an account based on logged CRM activities, call transcripts, and public information available on the internet. This allows service teams to identify at-risk accounts and prioritize retention efforts based on a synthesized health assessment, rather than manually reviewing CRM activities and transcripts.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Set up the customer health agent

Permissions required Super Admin permission is required to set up the agent.

Once the customer health agent is added, Super Admins can manage access, add extra instructions, and automate the agent.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Hub. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub directly.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • On the Customer Health Agent card click Edit.
  • To continue configuring the agent, learn more about customizing agents in the agent builder.

Use the customer health agent

The health of an account can be assessed by the customer health agent. The agent will assess logged CRM activities, call transcripts, and publicly accessible information on the internet.

Seats required An assigned Service Seat is required to use the customer health agent.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Agents > Agent Inbox directly.

Set up and use the deal loss agent

With the deal loss agent, you can analyze how and why deals were marked as closed lost. The agent reviews closed-lost deals and their associated records across the timeline you set up. It automatically surfaces loss patterns across your CRM data, so your team can act on the recommendations without manually reviewing individual deal records. You can also share the generated reports or download them as PDFs.

Set up HubSpot Work

Summary

Set up HubSpot Work to manage cross-functional projects and operational processes in one place. Create workspaces, configure projects and access levels, and use the AI assistant to generate the tables, documents, forms, and AI agents you need to collect information, coordinate work, and automate recurring actions.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

Permissions required An assigned Core, Sales, or Service seat is required to use HubSpot Work.

A Super Admin must:

  • Enroll in the HubSpot Work public beta to use the features outlined below.
  • Turn on the Give users access to generative AI tools and features setting in your AI settings.
Understand limitations & considerations

Projects in HubSpot Work aren’t related to the projects object or Breeze Assistant projects.

Set up a workspace

A workspace contains all of your projects and assets. Use a single workspace for cross-functional processes such as client onboarding. Use separate workspaces for compartmentalized processes or unrelated work such as IT management or marketing campaign operations. When you set up a workspace, you’ll also configure the starting project that contains the assets for a specific goal (e.g., client onboarding).

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.
  • Click Create your first workspace. If you already created a workspace, click the workspaces dropdown menu, then select Add workspace.
  • Enter a name for your workspace, then click Continue.
  • Click the Add people or teams dropdown menu, then select users and teams to grant access to the workspace.
  • In the People with access section, click the access dropdown menu, then select an option:
    • Admin: grants access to modify anything within the workspace. Learn more about access levels.
    • Member: grants access to view and contribute to projects and assets within the workspace. Members cannot modify the workspace configuration or share the workspace with other users. Learn more about access levels.
  • Click the General access dropdown menu, then select an option:
    • Private: only users or teams you’ve given access to can interact with the workspace.
    • Organization can view: all users in your account with Work permissions can view.
    • Organization can edit: all users in your account with Work permissions can view and edit.
  • Select a pre-defined workspace name (e.g., Client onboarding) or select Other to enter a custom name.
  • Click Next.
  • On the What kind of project do you want to create? page, select from the following to configure a project and assets:
    • Custom prompt: start from your own context.
      • In the How can I help text field, enter a prompt describing in detail what you want the project to accomplish.
      • To return a line, press and hold the Shift key, then simultaneously press the Enter key on your keyboard.
      • To add context the AI assistant should use, click Import files.
    • Template prompt: start from a project template.
      • Below the text field, select a HubSpot default prompt option. The prompt automatically fills the text field.
      • In the text field, navigate the prompt to review what will be built and best practices when submitting future prompts.
    • Start from scratch: start from a blank workspace. Learn how to set up a project from scratch.
  • When you’re finished with your prompt or template prompt, press the Enter key on your keyboard.
  • If applicable, select answers to questions, then click Submit.
  • The AI assistant will generate a plan for you to review and edit before content is created.
  • Click Approve to allow the agent to build the listed content.
  • Click the X to minimize the conversation and keep the AI assistant running in the background.

After the AI assistant completes the build process, it will list the actions it took and display clickable links to each asset.

Manage access to HubSpot Work

By default, user access to projects and assets is inherited from workspace permissions. Customize access at a workspace, project, or asset level to restrict access on a large or granular scale. Use the table below to review inherited access defaults.

Access level

Project access

Asset access

Private workspace + workspace admin

Inherits project owner when the project is open to the workspace.

Inherits asset owner when the asset is open to the project.

Private workspace + workspace member

Inherits project contributor when the project is open to the workspace.

Inherits asset contributor when the asset is open to the project.

Organization can view

Users in your HubSpot account with Work permissions can view projects that are open to the workspace.

Users in your HubSpot account with Work permissions can view assets that are open to the project.

Organization can edit

Users in your HubSpot account with Work permissions can view and edit projects that are open to the workspace.

Users in your HubSpot account with Work permissions can view and edit assets that are open to the project.

Invite-only project

Overrides workspace inherited access. Only directly added users can access the project.

Added users can view or edit based on their project access.

Invite-only asset

N/A

Overrides project inherited access. Only directly added users can access the asset.

Manage user permissions for HubSpot Work

Grant users HubSpot Work user permissions so they can access workspaces set to Organization can view/edit.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • In the user table, hover over a user’s name, then click Edit permissions.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Work Management.
  • Toggle the Work Management access switch on or off.
  • In the upper right, click Save.

Set up a project

Projects track specific initiatives for a team to collaborate on within a workspace. Each project contains its own assets: tables, documents, forms, and AI agents. Set up multiple projects for organization, access management, and scope. For example, in a customer success workspace with a client onboarding project, create an onboarding operations project and add assets such as process playbooks and onboarding templates.

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • What specific outcome should this project achieve?
  • Who needs to own, contribute to, and use this project?
  • What structure and process will the work in the project need?

Create a project called onboarding operations. Only the customer success managers team should have access to it. Ask me clarifying questions before finalizing the build.

To set up a project:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.
  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter your prompt.
  • The AI assistant will begin generating the project.
Configure project permissions
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Work Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Work Management directly.
  • In the upper left, click the workspaces dropdown menu, then select a workspace.
  • In the left sidebar, click the name of a project.
  • In the upper right, click Share.
  • In the dialog box, manage the following:
    • Click the Add people or teams dropdown menu, then select users and teams to grant access to the project.
    • In the People with access section, click the access dropdown menu, then select an option:
      • Owner: grants access to modify the project configuration and all assets within it.
      • Contributor: grants access to create and edit assets, including agents.
      • Viewer: grants access to view the projects and assets within it. Viewers cannot modify the project or anything within it.
    • Click Save.
Create a table

Tables are the fundamental asset within a project. They contain the data needed to build other assets, run agents, and collaborate on work.

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • What is the goal of the table, and how is each column defined?
  • What rows should be present and how are they defined (e.g., enumeration, CRM lookup)?
  • Which teams or users should have access to the table?

Build a Client Onboarding Tracker to manage each new client from signed agreement through successful onboarding and handoff to the account team. Create columns for client name, onboarding stage, onboarding owner, kickoff date, target completion date, key contacts, products or services purchased, implementation status, outstanding tasks, risks or blockers, handoff date, and notes. Use dropdowns for onboarding stage and implementation status, and use CRM lookups for the client and key contacts. Create one row for each newly signed client, using CRM data where available. Give the Client Success and Implementation teams edit access, the Sales team view access, and managers full administrative access.

To generate a table:

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter your prompt.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.
  • Enter additional prompts to refine the table’s details.

After the AI assistant completes the build process, it will list the actions it took and display a clickable link to the table.

Create views in a table

Within a table, use views to keep track of item statuses and collaborate with users in your HubSpot account. For example, create a calendar view to track due dates for client onboarding deadlines.

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • Which table should the view be created in? (Use @ to reference it by name.)
  • What type of visualization do you want (e.g., table, board, calendar), and what data should it display?
  • What is the goal of the view (e.g., track all open items and sub-items)?

Create a board view in the @Client Onboarding Tracker table. Group clients by onboarding stage and display the client name, onboarding owner, target completion date, implementation status, and any risks or blockers. The goal is to give the Client Success team a clear view of every active onboarding and quickly identify clients that are delayed or need attention.

To set up a view:

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter your prompt.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.

To manually set up a view:

  • In the left sidebar, click the name of the table you want to create a view for.
  • Below the table name, click the add view icon, then select a visualization option (e.g., board).
  • Click the configure view icon to customize the display of the view. Your changes are automatically saved.
Create a document

Create documents for information that doesn’t fit into a table format, such as briefs, operational playbooks, or meeting recaps. You can also create summary documents that use tables as their sources.

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • Who is the intended audience?
  • What source material should be used to generate the document, if any?
  • What format should the document follow (e.g., checklist, brief, proposal)?
  • What tone or writing style should be used?
  • Which teams or users should have access to the document?

Create a Client Onboarding Playbook for the Client Success and Implementation teams. Use the @Client Onboarding Tracker table as the source material, including its onboarding stages, required tasks, owners, timelines, and escalation criteria. Format the document as a practical checklist organized by onboarding stage. Use a clear, concise, and professional tone. Give the Client Success and Implementation teams edit access, the Sales team view access, and managers full administrative access.

To generate a document:

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter your prompt.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.
  • Enter additional prompts to refine the document’s details.

After the AI assistant completes the build process, it will list the actions it took and display a clickable link to the document.

Create a form

Create a form to collect relevant information for a project goal and send the data to a specific table. Form submissions sync to one table only to keep the table rows consistent and optionally trigger automations. For example, create an intake form with a custom routing assignment rule that syncs to your client onboarding table.

Please note: HubSpot Work forms are displayed alongside other forms in the marketing form tool, but submission data is sent to the configured HubSpot Work table.

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • What is the goal of the form (e.g., onboarding questionnaire)?
  • Which HubSpot Work table should receive the form submissions?
  • What information should the form collect, and which fields are required?
  • What should happen after the form is submitted (e.g., show a confirmation message, send a notification to a specific user)?

Create a Client Onboarding Questionnaire to collect the information needed to begin onboarding a new client. Send all submissions to the @Client Onboarding Tracker table. Collect the client name, primary contact, contact email, products or services purchased, preferred kickoff date, onboarding goals, key requirements, and any known risks or concerns. Require the client name, primary contact, email address, and onboarding goals. Use the submission to create a new onboarding record with the initial stage set to New. Keep internal tracking fields—such as onboarding owner, implementation status, target completion date, blockers, handoff date, and internal notes—out of the questionnaire for the onboarding team to complete later. After submission, show a confirmation message.

To generate a form:

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter your prompt.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.
  • Enter additional prompts to refine the form’s details.

After the AI assistant completes the build process, it will list the actions it took and display a clickable link to the form.

Create an AI agent

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to use AI workflow actions within a HubSpot Work AI agent. These actions are indicated by the icon.

Create an AI agent to automate actions for a specific goal. It’s recommended to align each agent with a goal and create automations within the agent that represent the goal. An onboarding status agent would monitor milestones, identify delays, and generate recurring status summaries.

For example, you build an onboarding status agent that manages active client onboardings in the Client Onboarding Tracker table through record review and updates every weekday at 9:00 AM. Each morning, the agent’s AI workflow actions, which include ownership assessment and interpretation of at-risk onboardings, consume HubSpot Credits. The agent’s other rule-based actions such as updating a table value and sending an email notification don’t consume HubSpot Credits.

Review the below questions to guide your prompt:

  • What is the goal of the AI agent (e.g., keep onboarding requests moving)?
  • What should trigger the AI agent, and how often should it run?
  • What context should the AI agent consider before taking action?
  • What must it never change?
  • What should it create or modify?

Create an agent to manage active client onboardings in the @Client Onboarding Tracker table. Review new records immediately and review records in the New, In Progress, or At Risk stages every weekday at 9:00 AM Eastern.

Use the table and CRM data to assess ownership, dates, services, tasks, risks, and blockers, but preserve client-submitted information when sources conflict. Create the standard onboarding subitems—Kickoff scheduled, Requirements confirmed, Implementation plan approved, Training complete, and Handoff complete—with due dates 2, 5, 7, 14, and 21 business days after creation. Assign them to the onboarding owner and never duplicate existing tasks.

If a target date is missed or a blocker persists for two business days, set the implementation status to At Risk, add an internal note, create one urgent follow-up task, and notify the owner. If required information or an owner is missing, do not guess. Never delete records, change client-submitted data, or modify Completed or Handed Off onboardings.

To set up an AI agent with a template prompt:

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, press the / key on your keyboard.
  • In the template prompts panel, navigate to the Agents section, then click the name of a prompt.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.

To set up an agent with a custom prompt:

  • At the bottom of the screen, click the prompt bar.
  • In the prompt text field, enter your prompt.
  • Press the Enter key on your keyboard.
  • If desired, enter additional prompts to refine the agent’s details.

After the AI assistant completes the build process, it will list the actions it took and display clickable links to each created asset.

Next steps

  • Collaborate with your team in HubSpot Work.
  • Manage your HubSpot work workspaces, projects, and assets.

Set up revenue agent

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for invoices are required to set up revenue agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to send invoices using revenue agent. Credits are consumed per invoice associated with a plan. Learn more about how revenue agent uses HubSpot Credits.

Use revenue agent, part of HubSpot’s AI, to monitor open invoices and automate outreach to buyers. Revenue agent tracks invoice changes and customer communications to suggest personalized outreach plans to help collect payment. Revenue agent adjusts plans based on customer replies and invoice activity and can send escalation emails to internal contacts.

For example, if an invoice is past due and a buyer hasn’t responded, revenue agent can send a personalized follow-up and escalate the case to an internal contact if payment remains outstanding.

Set up revenue agent and enroll companies and contacts to start automating outreach. Learn more about how revenue agent works.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Understand requirements
  • The Give users access to generative AI tools and features toggle must be switched on in the AI settings of your account.
  • You must have an individual or team email address connected to your account to activate and use revenue agent.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Revenue agent tracks invoice status (open, paid, overdue, etc.) regardless of how the invoice was created or which tool generated it (e.g., contracts, quotes, or subscriptions created in HubSpot or invoices from external sources). If invoices originate from an external source, they must be synced to HubSpot first.

Turn revenue agent on

Turn on revenue agent to enroll entities (companies and contacts) and generate plans. You can enroll additional companies and contacts and update automation settings after setup (whether emails to buyers are manually reviewed or automatically sent) can be updated after setup. Learn more about enrollment and automation settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • Under Sending inbox, select an option:
    • Shared inbox: use a team email address.
    • Individual inbox: use an individual email address.

Please note: if you select Individual inbox, only the owner of the individual inbox can edit and approve proposed plans or edit active plans.

  • Click Done.
  • Under Enroll companies or contacts, the agent automatically selects companies and contacts based on their current open invoices and total due. You can enroll additional companies and contacts after activating revenue agent. To update the selection:
    • Click Add company or contact.
    • Up to 20 companies will be shown in the dialog box. Click the Contacts tab to view contacts.
    • To search companies and contacts, in the Search by name field, enter a company or contact name or email address.
    • Click Add next to the company or contact to enroll.
    • To remove a company or contact, click Remove.
  • Click Continue to agent overview.
  • In the dialog box, click Review plans. Learn more about reviewing, editing, and approving proposed plans.

Manage how companies and contacts are enrolled

Configure whether companies and contacts are enrolled automatically or manually. Learn more about enrollment.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the top right, click Manage enrollment.
  • Select an enrollment option:
    • Leave the Auto enroll new companies and contacts switch off to manually enroll companies and contacts. Learn more about manually enrolling entities.
    • Toggle the Auto enroll new companies and contacts switch on to auto-enroll companies and contacts.

Set an escalation recipient

Set an internal recipient to send escalation emails to. Revenue agent evaluates the invoice status, customer messages, prior outreach, and prior decisions before deciding whether to escalate. Learn more about escalations.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Configure, then select Account details.
  • In the Escalation recipient field, enter their email address.

Set the automation mode

Automation modes control whether emails to buyers are manually reviewed or automated. Learn more about automation modes.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Configure, then select Automations.
  • Select an automation mode:
    • Review every email: you must review and approve plans.
    • Send automatically until a customer replies: revenue agent automatically sends initial and follow-up emails to the buyer and escalation emails. Neither requires approval. Any billing-related email from the buyer, whether it’s a reply or a new message, regenerates the payment plan and sends it to you for approval. Invoice updates, such as partial or full payments, regenerate the plan automatically without requiring approval.

Set agent instructions

Set instructions for revenue agent to follow when writing emails in plans. You can specify tone, sentence structure, email length, number and timing of follow-ups, and phrases to avoid. Instructions can’t change invoice amounts, payment terms, customer and account data, or attached files and documents.

When you update agent instructions, existing plans are updated as follows:

  • New emails: use the updated instructions automatically. No additional action is required.
  • Plans awaiting approval: don’t update automatically when you save. You’ll be prompted to:
    • Regenerate all proposed plans: update all plans in review with the new instructions.
    • Save without regenerating: save the instructions and apply them to individual plans during plan review.
  • Approved plans and scheduled emails: aren’t affected by instruction changes.

To set agent instructions:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Revenue > Revenue Agent directly.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Configure, then select Agent instructions.
  • In the Instructions field, enter instructions for the agent to follow.
  • Click Save instructions.
  • In the dialog box, select an option:
    • Save and regenerate [x] plans: update all plans in review with the new instructions.
    • Save without regenerating: save the instructions and apply them to individual plans during plan review.

Next Steps

Learn more about managing revenue agent, including viewing active plans, unenrolling companies and contacts, viewing plan history, and editing the enrollment mode and filters.

Summarize and review data with Breeze Assistant

Use Breeze Assistant to summarize and review data across your HubSpot account, including CRM records, and reporting tools such as marketing emails, campaigns, and reports. Instead of manually reviewing metrics or activity timelines, generate summaries that highlight key trends, performance insights, and important context. You can also ask follow-up questions to explore specific details to better understand your data.

Before using Breeze Assistant, review how it uses your account context and responds to prompts.

For an overview of configuring your account for AI features, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements to use Breeze Assistant

To summarize data with Breeze Assistant you must:

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.
  • Have access to the relevant HubSpot tools (e.g., feedback surveys).

Summarize records with Breeze Assistant

  • Navigate to your records:
    • Contacts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • Companies: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Companies. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Companies directly.
    • Deals: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.
    • Tickets: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Tickets. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Tickets directly.
  • Click the name of the record you want to summarize.
  • In the left sidebar title card, click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Summarize. In the Breeze Assistant panel, review the record summary. Learn more about summarizing records with Breeze Assistant.

Summarize marketing email performance with Breeze Assistant

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Hover over a sent marketing email, then click the Actions dropdown menu and select Summarize performance. Learn more about summarizing marketing email performance.

Summarize campaign performance with Breeze Assistant

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to summarize campaign performance.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Campaigns. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Campaigns directly.
  • Click the name of a campaign.
  • Click the Actions dropdown menu and select Summarize on the top left. Learn more about summarizing individual campaign performance.

Review campaign data with Breeze Assistant

Review and analyze campaign performance, assets, and budget details directly from the campaign tool with Breeze Assistant. This helps you access key information without navigating between multiple tabs or reports.

  • What's the goal progress for the campaign?
  • What's the attributed revenue for the campaign?
  • What's the budget and spending?

To prompt Breeze Assistant about marketing campaigns:

  • Click the name of a campaign.
  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the panel, enter a question about the campaign.
  • Click the send prompt icon.

Summarize reports with Breeze Assistant

Use Breeze Assistant to interpret report data. Some reports such as funnel reports cannot be summarized.

To summarize a report:

  • In the upper left, click the dashboard dropdown menu, then select the name of the dashboard you want to view.

Summarize survey responses with Breeze Assistant

Subscription required A Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to summarize survey responses.

Summarize ticket survey responses to review the themes of received feedback. The summary can only be generated after receiving at least three submissions.

Summarize average rating for Ticket owner Leslie Knope.

Test and control agent credit usage

Simulate AI agent runs without consuming credits to estimate HubSpot Credit costs. Then, set guardrails to cap HubSpot Credit usage per agent. Since credit costs vary by agent complexity, simulating runs before going live helps you plan usage and avoid unexpected charges.

Learn more about using agents and assistants in HubSpot.

Before you get started

Estimated credit costs per run are calculated based on the agent’s current run and complexity. This can sometimes vary from the actual costs of each agent’s run.

Please note: on July 23, 2026, all AI agents started consuming HubSpot Credits. It’s strongly recommended to run agent simulations to estimate credit costs per run and avoid unexpected charges.

Run agent simulations without consuming credits

Run simulations for individual agents. This allows you to test an agent, including reading CRM context, without consuming credits. You’ll see the input, agent reasoning and activity, and the agent output. The output display mirrors a regular agent run, without taking CRM actions or making any changes. If configured, the agent may run MCP tools, so it’s recommended to use sample input data.

To run an agent simulation:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • Click Edit on an agent card.
  • In the upper right, click Test.
  • Enter the required details to test the agent.
  • Click Test agent to start the agent run.

To review previous agent simulation runs:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • Click the Agents tab.
  • Click Edit on an agent card.
  • In the upper right, click Test.
  • In the Test agent panel, click View history.
  • Click the name of a simulation to review details such as the estimated number of credits consumed, the timestamp of the run, and the output.

Set monthly run limits per agent

Set the number of times an AI agent can run per month to cap HubSpot Credit usage. These limits apply on a per-agent basis, and the agent stops running once it reaches the set limit.

To turn on a monthly run limit for an agent:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.

  • At the top, click the Agents tab.

  • Click Edit on an agent card.

  • In the agent builder, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon and select Edit run limit.

  • In the Agent run limits panel, review the average estimated credits per run.

  • Toggle the Monthly agent run limit switch on to set a monthly run limit for the agent.

  • In the Agent run limit text field, enter the number of times you want the agent to run this month.

  • Review the estimated credit usage range. The range will automatically update as you adjust the run limit (e.g., 900–1,000 credits/month) based on the average credits consumed per run.

  • In the lower right, click Update.

Understand Breeze Assistant

Review how Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant, uses your account context to generate responses to your prompts. This article covers the context types Breeze Assistant uses, the available interaction methods, and what to expect from responses.

For an overview of configuring your account for HubSpot’s AI, review how to set up a HubSpot account to adopt AI features.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • Turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Breeze Assistant responses and actions depend on your user permissions. As a Super Admin, review user access to HubSpot AI tools.
  • Breeze Assistant doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits, but triggering an AI agent run with Breeze Assistant may cost HubSpot Credits. Learn more about HubSpot Credits.

Understand the context Breeze Assistant uses for responses

Breeze Assistant draws on three types of context when generating a response and may not use all three types each time. Depending on your account configuration, your permissions, and your specific request, Breeze Assistant uses varying levels of context. If a response seems incomplete or lacks key details, you can review the types below to determine what additional context to provide:

  • Account-level business context: information configured in the context section of agent hub, such as your company profile, ideal customer profiles (ICPs), personas, and team processes like sales methodology. You can also create knowledge vaults that store more specific information for targeted use cases, such as product details or support guidance.
  • Task-level context: information available for the specific request, such as the CRM record you’re asking about, files you’ve added to a prompt, results from a connected app search, or knowledge vault content. Breeze Assistant accesses only information that’s relevant to the request and available within your user’s permissions.
  • Personal and project context: information Breeze Assistant stores as memories, such as output preferences, tone, and recurring instructions. When you chat with Breeze Assistant within a project, those instructions, tools, and reference materials persist across conversations in the project.

Review ways to interact with Breeze Assistant

  • Prompt: regular text-based input. Use regular prompts for research, general questions, and feature exploration.
  • Saved prompt: regular prompts saved for repeat use. Save prompts for tasks, questions, or template prompts to save time writing out instructions each time you chat with Breeze Assistant. You can also automate a saved prompt to automatically start a chat with Breeze Assistant on a recurring basis. For example, save a weekly deal pipeline summary question to review a consistent weekly report.
  • Skill: a specific set of instructions. Build or upload skills that instruct Breeze Assistant how to complete a business-specific task and use them in new or existing conversations. For example, build a skill with instructions to generate alt text descriptions for uploaded files that uses the WC3 guidelines.
  • Project: a folder of instructions, specific context, knowledge vaults, and tools. Start chats within a project and Breeze Assistant uses the saved set of materials. Use projects for conversations that share the same instructions, reference materials, or goals. For example, a project for a specific marketing campaign could include background documents, a target persona, and tone guidance that applies across every conversation in that project.
  • Voice (BETA): voice-based conversation. Speak to Breeze Assistant, and it responds verbally. Use voice input when you want to share your thoughts aloud or be hands-free. For example, start voice mode after an in-person meeting with a client to save meeting notes to their contact record.

Understand the structure of a Breeze Assistant response

Each Breeze Assistant response varies based on your prompt and the context used. If a response appears to lack direction or not provide information you expect, review your context settings or iterate on your prompt. Based on your prompt, a response may include one or all of the following:

  • Plain text output: answers to your questions or synthesis of research.
  • Confirmation: a card displayed in the chat when a prompt requests CRM changes, with the option to confirm or cancel before the action runs.
  • Follow-up questions: when more information is needed to complete your request, you may receive single, multiple choice, or free-text questions.
  • Artifact: for eligible content types (e.g., email, report, spreadsheet) output appears as a saved and versioned piece of content.
  • Sources: for prompts involving research, analysis, or data interpretation, citations appear inline or as footnotes in the response.

Use-case: use Breeze Assistant to analyze deals that need attention

A sales rep at Sprocket Supply Co. prompts Breeze Assistant: Review my open deals this week, identify the one at highest risk, and draft a re-engagement email for that contact. Breeze Assistant returns a plain text summary and generates a draft email artifact. Breeze Assistant uses the rep’s saved email signature and connected calendar to add personalization to the drafted email. The rep notices that the deal record wasn’t cited in the summary and prompts Breeze Assistant: always cite sources, regardless of if I asked about a specific CRM record. Then, the rep follows up on that prompt with Mark that deal as at-risk, and a confirmation card appears in the chat for manual approval before the Deal risk property is updated.

Understand revenue agent

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for invoices are required to set up and manage revenue agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to send invoices using revenue agent. Credits are consumed per invoice associated with a plan. Learn more about how revenue agent uses HubSpot Credits.

Use revenue agent, part of HubSpot’s AI, to monitor open invoices and automate outreach to buyers. Revenue agent tracks invoice changes and buyer communications to suggest personalized outreach plans to help collect payment. Revenue agent adjusts plans based on buyer replies and invoice activity and can send escalation emails to internal contacts.

For example, if an invoice is past due and a buyer hasn’t responded, revenue agent can send a personalized follow-up and escalate the case to an internal contact if payment remains outstanding.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Understand requirements
  • The Give users access to generative AI tools and features toggle must be switched on in the AI settings of your account.
  • You must have an individual or team email address connected to your account to activate and use revenue agent.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Revenue agent tracks invoice status (open, paid, overdue, etc.) regardless of how the invoice was created or which tool generated it (e.g., contracts, quotes, or subscriptions created in HubSpot or invoices from external sources). If invoices originate from an external source, they must be synced to HubSpot first.

Company and contact enrollment

When you set up revenue agent for the first time, it will suggest companies and contacts to enroll based on their current open invoices and total due. You can review the suggested outreach plans and email schedules before any emails are sent, or configure revenue agent to send emails automatically until a contact replies. After setting up revenue agent, you can manually enroll additional companies and contacts or turn on auto-enrollment:

  • Auto-enrollment: revenue agent enrolls companies and contacts and monitors them for open invoices, including future invoices. Plans will be created for matching companies and contacts with open invoices that aren’t configured for automatic payments.
  • Manual enrollment: select up to 1,000 companies and contacts to enroll. Revenue agent continuously monitors enrolled records and creates plans for current and future open invoices that aren’t configured for automatic payments. Companies and contacts added to HubSpot later aren’t enrolled automatically and must be enrolled manually.

Learn more about how companies and contacts are enrolled.

Exclusions

Invoices may be excluded based on manual exclusions or exclusion segments. Excluded invoices won’t be included in plans. Learn more about types of exclusions below.

Manual exclusions

You can manually exclude individual invoices. Learn more about how to manually exclude invoices.

Exclusion segments

You can configure invoice exclusion segments to exclude invoices that meet filtered criteria when enrolling companies and contacts. The exclusion segment automatically applies its filters to invoices and excludes matching invoices from plans.

Learn more about setting up exclusion filters when enrolling companies and contacts.

Plans

Plans are personalized email schedules generated from CRM context about the buyer, their invoices, and their account. Actions can include proactive reminder emails and replies to buyer invoice inquiries. A plan considers the open invoices associated with the enrolled companies or contacts. The plan is regenerated when an invoice changes or a buyer contacts you about an invoice.

Learn more about action types.

When revenue agent regenerates a plan

A plan can be regenerated when:

  • A new invoice is created or associated.
  • An invoice is paid, voided, reopened, or otherwise has its status changed.
  • The invoice amount or balance changes.
  • The invoice becomes past due.
  • The due date changes.
  • An invoice is disassociated.
  • An external invoice link changes.
  • A relevant buyer email is received.
  • A scheduled reevaluation runs.
  • A prior plan expires.
  • A plan is manually adjusted or regenerated.
  • Enrollment or invoice-exclusion settings change and affect the account.

A plan isn’t regenerated when the change does not materially affect collection, or when the existing plan remains valid. Revenue agent cancels plans when no actionable invoices remain.

Action types in plans

Within plans, revenue agent can suggest the following actions:

  • Reminder emails: scheduled emails sent to the buyer about open invoices, including upcoming and overdue amounts and due dates. Revenue agent can send proactive outreach before an invoice is due, as well as follow-up emails for overdue invoices. Multiple invoices can be combined in one email when more than one invoice is open or when their due dates are close together.
  • Escalation emails: emails sent to an internal recipient when escalation is required. Revenue agent evaluates the invoice status, buyer messages, previous outreach, and previous decisions before deciding whether escalation is appropriate. Escalation is triggered in either of the following cases:
    • Time-based conditions:
      • The invoice must be at least 90 days past due.
      • Revenue agent must have made at least two outreach attempts. If two attempts are completed before day 90, escalation is triggered on the 90th day. If the invoice reaches 90 days past due before two attempts are completed, the agent completes the remaining outreach, then escalates three days after the second attempt.
    • Unresolvable buyer response: The agent escalates anytime it receives a response it can’t handle, such as when a buyer disputes the invoice or states they won’t pay.
  • Reply emails: when a buyer emails about an invoice, revenue agent reviews the message and may draft a response. Replies must be reviewed before they are sent.

Learn more about reviewing and editing proposed plans and active plans.

Plan automation

Automation modes control whether emails to buyers are manually reviewed or automated. You can select from the following modes:

  • Review all emails: you must review and approve each plan before revenue agent sends emails.
  • Review only when a customer replies: revenue agent automatically sends escalation emails and buyer emails, except when a buyer emails about billing.
    • Billing emails from the buyer are routed for review by a user. This includes any billing-related email from the buyer, not only replies to emails sent by revenue agent.
    • If a buyer changes an invoice, such as by making a partial or full payment, the plan regenerates automatically.

Learn more about configuring the automation mode.

Scheduled reevaluation

Scheduled reevaluations review a plan at a future time and update it if needed. It checks for changes such as payments, invoice status updates, buyer replies, or elapsed time, then regenerates the plan if needed. Scheduled reevaluations are time-based triggers that complement reevaluations caused by invoice updates and email activity. Scheduled reevaluations are labeled with Wakeup in active plans.

Set instructions for revenue agent

Set instructions for revenue agent to follow when writing emails in plans, so it matches your brand’s tone of voice. Use instructions to define the email tone, sentence structure, length, number and timing of follow-up emails, and phrases to avoid. You can’t change invoice amounts, payment terms, buyer, or account data, or attached files and documents with instructions.

Learn more about setting instructions for revenue agent.

How revenue agent uses HubSpot Credits

Revenue agent uses HubSpot Credits when it starts payment collection outreach for an invoice. Credits are consumed per invoice when outreach begins, not when the buyer pays the invoice.

For example, you have 1,000 overdue invoices, of which 30 have outstanding balances greater than $5,000. You decide to use revenue agent to collect payment for those 30 invoices. When revenue agent starts payment collection outreach for the 30 invoices, HubSpot Credits are consumed for each invoice.

Learn more about how many HubSpot Credits revenue agent uses in the Product & Services Catalog.

The following activities don’t consume credits:

  • Actions within plans, including escalation emails.
  • Scheduled reevaluations.

Next Steps

  • Learn more about setting up revenue agent, including enrolling accounts and starting automated outreach.
  • Learn more about managing revenue agent, including viewing active plans, unenrolling companies and contacts, viewing plan history, and editing the enrollment mode and filters.

Use AI to close deals faster

To close deals faster, prioritize the right accounts, reduce preparation time, and maintain momentum between touchpoints.

In HubSpot, use AI-powered tools and automation to identify high-fit prospects, streamline outreach, and guide deals through your pipeline more efficiently. For example, Sprocket Supply Co., an ecommerce company selling sustainable office supplies, focuses on companies already researching environmentally-friendly vendors. Instead of manually qualifying every lead, their sales team prioritizes accounts showing buying signals, automates outreach, and prepares for meetings using AI-generated insights.

This article focuses on using these tools throughout the sales process after they’re set up. If you’re a Super Admin or sales leader who wants to configure AI-powered prospecting for your account, learn how to get started with AI-powered prospecting.

Find high-fit leads using prospecting agent

Subscription required A Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, Data Hub, or Content Hub Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription or a Smart CRM Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use prospecting agent.

The fastest way to shorten your sales cycle is to focus on companies already showing buying signals instead of researching every potential prospect.

If you’re using the Prospecting Agent Gets Smarter: Buying Signals and Contact Sourcing (BETA), the prospecting agent monitors companies for buying signals, recommends high-fit companies for outreach, sources relevant contacts from third-party sales intelligence providers (e.g. ZoomInfo, Apollo, Surfe, etc.), and generates personalized outreach based on your plays.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co.’s sales team monitors mid-sized ecommerce companies for buying signals such as researching sustainability topics, launching new products, or receiving funding. When those signals are detected, the prospecting agent recommends companies for outreach and suggests contacts that match the company’s target personas.

To find high-fit leads:

  • Create plays that define your target audience, buying signals, personas, selling context, outreach strategy, and automation preferences.
  • Review recommended companies based on detected buying signals, or monitor all companies included in your selected audience segments.
  • Review suggested contacts for each company and enroll contacts or companies in a play to begin outreach. Configure automatic enrollment based on criteria such as page views, form submissions, list membership, or time since last engagement.

Learn more about using buying signals in the prospecting agent (BETA).

Research leads and plan outreach with the prospecting agent

Subscription required A Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, Data Hub, or Content Hub Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription or a Smart CRM Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use prospecting agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are consumed when the agent generates personalized email outreach for each lead (a recommended or manually enrolled lead), with additional steps based on your play settings. Review how Breeze Agents use HubSpot Credits.

After identifying high-fit accounts, use the prospecting agent to research prospects and generate personalized outreach at scale. Instead of sales reps spending 20–30 minutes manually researching each company, the prospecting agent analyzes CRM data and instructions outlined in plays to draft tailored and consistent outreach messages.

To set up and use the prospecting agent:

  • Enroll high-fit leads in the prospecting agent. Add contacts manually or automatically to generate outreach emails and follow-ups based on your plays.
  • Review, edit, and send emails if using Review before sending. Ensure generated messages align with your tone, positioning, and outreach goals before sending.

For example, if a company announces new funding or begins researching topics related to sustainable office supplies, Sprocket Supply Co. uses that context to generate relevant outreach related to those events.

Learn more about how to use the prospecting agent.

Generate meeting agendas with Breeze Assistant

When a contact replies to an email or books a meeting, they’re automatically unenrolled from the prospecting agent. At this point, the focus shifts from outreach to meeting preparation. In HubSpot, use Breeze Assistant to automatically generate a meeting agenda so you can enter the conversation with clear talking points, relevant context, and defined next steps.

To prepare for a call or meeting:

  • Open the contact or company record. Review recent activity, including emails, page visits, and previous interactions. If you have Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise, do this directly in the sales workspace.
  • Generate a call agenda with Breeze Assistant. Use the assistant to summarize key information and suggest discussion topics based on CRM data. Connect apps to Breeze assistant (BETA) if additional information stored in apps is helpful for your meetings.
  • Review and refine the agenda. Add questions, relevant talking points, or notes based on the prospect’s industry, company size, or use case.
  • Use the agenda during the meeting. Guide the conversation through discovery, key challenges, and potential solutions.

For example, a prospect schedules a meeting after reviewing bulk pricing options, so the Sprocket Supply Co. sales rep prepares to discuss order volume, delivery timelines, and supplier requirements.

Learn more about using Breeze Assistant and the sales workspace.

Review and apply next-step recommendations for calls or meetings

Seats required

  • An assigned Sales seat is required to use Notetaker.
  • If you’ve opted into the Meeting Notetaker with Smart Deal Progression beta, an assigned Sales or Service seat is required.

Subscription required A Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use meeting notetaker.

After a meeting or call, the next step is to review follow-up actions and update your deal. HubSpot analyzes meeting recordings and transcripts to recommend follow-up actions and CRM updates, eliminating the need to manually review transcripts and decide what to do next.

If you’re using meeting notetaker (BETA), or syncing recordings and transcripts from Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, or Zoom to HubSpot, HubSpot can automatically generate recommendations based on your meetings. If you’re using AI call summaries, or if call transcripts are provided through a connected app, HubSpot can also generate recommendations based on your calls.

These recommendations help you follow up with prospects and keep deals progressing through your pipeline.

After a meeting or call:

  • Review recommended next steps (BETA). HubSpot analyzes meeting and call transcripts to identify action items and suggest deal updates.
  • Generate follow-up emails. Create a draft follow-up email based on the meeting conversation, then review and edit it before sending.
  • Approve CRM updates. Review suggested property updates, such as deal stage or next activity, and approve or reject them.
  • Create tasks from action items. Save recommended action items as tasks to ensure follow-up steps are completed. If your sales process includes additional manual follow-up tasks (e.g., routing approvals, preparing handoffs), consider creating custom agents to automate them.

For example, after a meeting with a company evaluating new suppliers, the Sprocket Supply Co. sales team’s recommended next steps are to send pricing details, schedule a follow-up, and update the deal stage. The sales rep updates the deal, then creates tasks to put together the pricing information and schedule the follow-up meeting.

Learn more about reviewing recommended next steps for deal.

Analyze prospecting and sales reports

Review your sales analytics to understand what’s working and where your sales process can improve. For example, measure outreach performance, track deal progression, and identify bottlenecks in your pipeline.

Analyze prospecting agent performance

Subscription required A Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, Data Hub, or Content Hub Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription or a Smart CRM Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use prospecting agent.

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are consumed when the agent generates personalized email outreach for each lead (a recommended or manually enrolled lead), with additional steps based on your play settings. Review how Breeze Agents use HubSpot Credits.

Review prospecting agent enrollment outcomes data to understand how your automated outreach is doing.

From the Analyze tab, filter the data to enrollments made by you. Then, review metrics such as:

  • Open rates to measure how often prospects open outreach emails.
  • Reply rates to understand how prospects respond to outreach.
  • Meeting bookings to track how often outreach leads to scheduled meetings.
  • Enrollment performance to identify which plays or segments perform best.

These insights help you refine plays, adjust messaging, and improve targeting for future outreach.

Learn more about how to analyze prospecting agent enrollments.

Analyze sales performance with sales analytics reports

Subscription required A Sales Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to analyze sales performance with sales analytics reports.

Use the sales analytics suite to monitor deal progression and identify where deals slow down in your pipeline.

For example, review reports that measure your:

  • Deal stage conversion rates.
  • Deal velocity.
  • Time spent in each deal stage.
  • Revenue performance.

Review these reports regularly to identify patterns in your sales process. For example, if deals frequently stall after the first meeting, you may need to improve discovery conversations or follow-up strategies.

Continuously reviewing sales analytics helps you refine targeting, improve outreach strategies, and remove friction from your sales process over time.

Learn more about creating sales reports in the sales analytics suite.

Use insights to improve performance

Use performance reports to:

  • Improve targeted outreach.
  • Refine a selling profile in prospecting agent.
  • Refine AI-generated emails.

For example, you could use the following benchmarks to help you evaluate and improve performance:

Metric

Definition

Benchmark to aim for

What it means if not meeting the benchmark

Actions to improve performance

Response rate (reply or meeting)

Replies from contacts to agent outreach with at least one email send across all plays.

4%

A low response rate means contacts aren’t replying to play emails or booking meetings.

Edit a selling profile or play in prospecting agent so the message is more tailored.

Edit and send emails to ensure the messaging is tailored.

Meeting rate

Contacts who were unenrolled from a play because a meeting was booked, or who had a meeting booked within 7 days after being unenrolled. Only meetings scheduled after the contact was enrolled are counted.

1%

A low meeting rate means contacts enrolled in a play still aren’t booking meetings.

Use data agent to segment and deep research the prospect before enrolling in prospecting agent.
