Please note: there must be at least one Super Admin in the client account. If you are the only Super Admin in the client account, it will not be possible to change yourself or others to a Partner Admin.

Manage shared partner deals

Shared deals create a centralized space for HubSpot Partners and HubSpot sales representatives to collaborate. Learn more about creating shared deals and collaborating using messages on shared deals.

Permissions required The deals you have access to depend on your CRM object permissions for deals.

Track registered deals

When reviewing deals in your account, you can filter for the deals your HubSpot sales representative has registered for you:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.
  • At the top of the table, click More to add a quick filter.
  • In the pop-up box, select Number of Active Deal Registrations.
  • At the top of the table, click the Number of Active Deal Registrations filter.
  • In the pop-up box, click the dropdown menu and select is greater than or equal to.
  • In the right field, enter 1.

Set a sales contact for shared deals

You can set a sales contact who will be notified of partner matching opportunities and the creation of assisted deals. It’s recommended to select whomever manages HubSpot selling opportunities for your team.

If you don’t set a sales contact, the Primary POC for your account will receive these notifications instead.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Partners > Shared Deals.
  • Click the Default sales contact dropdown menu and select a user.
  • In the bottom left, click Save.

Manage a shared deal’s users

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.

  • Click the name of a shared deal.

  • In the Shared deal information section of the deal record, hover over the Deal team field and click Edit. If the Shared deals section isn’t present on the record, customize your record layout.

  • In the dialog box, click the Deal team dropdown menu and select a user from your own account.

  • Click Save.

Set a default pipeline for shared deals

In your partner settings, you can set a default pipeline for shared deals created in the future. This will not affect existing deals.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Partners > Shared Deals.
  • Click the Default pipeline for shared deals dropdown menu and select a pipeline.

Manage Solutions Directory reviews

When a customer works with a Solutions Partner, they can leave a review in the Solutions Directory to reflect their experience with that partner. Good reviews build trust, while bad reviews offer an opportunity for you to showcase how you respond to critical feedback.

This article covers steps for Solutions Partners to request and reply to reviews for their listings in the Solutions Directory. Learn more about leaving a review on the HubSpot Marketplace.

Permissions required Solutions Directory permissions for partner tools are required to access your Solutions Directory profile.

Generate a review link

When asking customers to leave you a review, you can include a direct link for them to create the review. Only customers that meet HubSpot’s review guidelines should leave reviews.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Partner > Directory Profile. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Partner > Directory Profile directly.
  • In the All Customer Reviews section, click Copy review link in the top right.

Reply to a review

If a customer leaves a review, you can leave a single reply to that review addressing their comments. The customer will then receive an email with the content of your reply, which will be posted on the public listing page.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Partner > Directory Profile. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Partner > Directory Profile directly.
  • At the bottom of the review, click Reply.
  • In the dialog box, enter a reply in the Reply field.
  • Click Send.

Request review or reply removal

If a review or reply is offensive, uses profane language or violates HubSpot’s review guidelines, you can request that it be removed. HubSpot will review the request within ten business days.

If the review is removed, its rating will no longer be factored into the listing’s rating, and the customer will be able to leave a new review.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Partner > Directory Profile. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Partner > Directory Profile directly.
  • At the bottom of the review, click Report.

Manage upcoming client renewals

You can view any upcoming renewals for clients you are managing on your partner dashboard. This is helpful for initiating conversations with clients about their experience using HubSpot.

Permissions required Partner dashboard permissions for partner tools are required to access the partner dashboard.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Partner > Dashboard. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Partner > Dashboard directly.
  • In the Upcoming HubSpot Renewals section, you can view the following information for clients who have upcoming renewals:
    • Client: name of the client, with a link to their client record.
    • Products: the client’s HubSpot subscriptions.
    • MRR Change: the anticipated change in the client’s monthly recurring revenue based on their renewal status.
    • Last active employee: the user who was last active in the client’s HubSpot account.
    • Renewal Manager: the HubSpot employee who is managing the client’s renewal.
    • Time to Renewal: when the client’s contract will renew.

Reply to Solutions Directory reviews

If you’re a member of HubSpot’s Solutions Partner Program or an inbound certified agency that has created a profile on HubSpot’s Solutions Directory, customers can leave reviews on your profile. Good reviews build trust, while bad reviews offer an opportunity for you to showcase how you respond to critical feedback.

Permissions required Solutions Directory permissions for partner tools are required to access your Solutions Directory profile.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • Review replies may take a few minutes to appear on the Solutions Directory.
  • Review replies cannot be edited after they’ve been submitted.

Reply to reviews

  • In your HubSpot partner account, navigate to Partner > Directory Profile.
  • In the Reviews section, click Reply under a review.
  • In the dialog box, enter a reply in the Reply field.
  • Click Send.

Review commission statements and payments

As a HubSpot Solutions Partner, you can review your commission statements and payments, as well as a forecast of predicted future commission earnings. You can then export commission statements to CSV or PDF for your records or to share with others in your organization.

Permissions required Super Admin or Partner commission access permissions are required to review commission statements and payments.

View commission statements

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Commission.
  • Click the statement you would like to review.
  • To export your statement, click the Export dropdown menu and select Export to CSV.
  • To save the statement as a PDF, click the Export dropdown menu and select Print/Save as PDF.

View commission payments

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Commission.
  • Click the Payments tab.
  • Review the payments HubSpot has made to your organization.

View commission forecasting

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Commission.
  • Click the Forecasting tab.
  • Click the From dropdown menu and select the starting month of the forecasting range.
  • Click the To dropdown menu and select the ending month of the forecasting range.
  • Review the commission forecasting data in the reports, including:
    • Total Projected Commission: projected commission across all clients for the date range specified.
    • Clients: number of clients generating commissions in the date range specified.
    • Commission Line Items: projected products generating commissions across all clients for the date range specified.
    • Monthly Commission: commission earned each month for a specific client.
    • Commissions: total separate products generating commissions for a specific client. To view more information about a client’s commissions, click the down arrow next to the client name.
    • Projected Total: projected commission for a specific client for the date range specified.
    • Status: whether the commission is still active or will be expiring during the next period.

Set up partner lead notifications

Set up email notifications to be sent when a registered lead or current client takes a high-value action like viewing HubSpot’s pricing page, requesting a demo, or signing up for HubSpot’s free tools.

There are two types of notifications that you’ll receive through this setting:

  • Partner lead notifications: notifications triggered by high-value actions taken on HubSpot’s website by leads already registered to you.
  • Partner deal notifications: notifications triggered by leads on a shared deal signing up for a free HubSpot account. This type of notification will be sent to the deal owner and all users on the deal team, as long as the following criteria are met:
    • The contact must be associated with a company owned by a HubSpot Growth Specialist.
    • The contact’s company must have an associated co-sold deal that is shared with you.

Please note: only the first partner to be added to the shared deal will receive partner deal notifications.

Set up partner lead notifications

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Notifications.
  • Click to expand the Leads section.
  • Next to Activity on a lead you follow, select the checkbox in the column of each type of notification you want to receive. If you select Pop-up, click the dropdown menu in the Pop-up Sound column and select a sound option.

Set up partner deal notifications

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Notifications.
  • Click to expand the HubSpot Partners section.
  • Next to Co Selling Prospect Activity, select the checkbox in the column of each type of notification you want to receive. If you select Pop-up, click the dropdown menu in the Pop-up Sound column and select a sound option.
  • In the bottom left, click Save.

Submit bank and tax documentation through your partner account

If you’re a HubSpot partner, you need to submit your banking information and an appropriate tax form to receive commission payments for the HubSpot products that you sell.

You can submit these documents directly through your partner account. HubSpot uses a third-party service, Dropbox Sign, to process your submission.

Please note: Dropbox Sign uses a trusted partner for e-signature compliance in the EU and will not explicitly show up on the eIDAS website of trusted partners.

Submit a bank form

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right corner, then click Account & Billing.

  • Click the Documents tab.

  • Next to the bank form, click Edit in the Actions column.

  • In the dialog box, click Get started. HubSpot uses a third-party service called Dropbox Sign to process your submission.

  • Fill in the form with your information. If you exit the form, the bank form status should change to In Progress. To continue filling out the form, hover over the form and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Edit.

  • Once you’ve entered all required information, click I agree.

  • You’ll be redirected to the document list in HubSpot. The bank form’s status will change to Pending approval. When the form is accepted, its status will change to Approved.

  • To download the completed document, hover over the form and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select View.

  • If the document is rejected, you’ll be notified via email and the status will change to Rejected.

    • To learn more about the reason for the rejection, hover over the status in the documents list.
    • To redo the submission, hover over the rejected form and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Start again.

Submit a tax form

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right corner, then click Account & Billing.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select Documents.
  • If this is your first time visiting the documents section to submit a tax form, click Setup tax form in the yellow banner at the top of the page.
  • Complete each step to determine which tax form you need to submit. If the resulting document is correct, select the I agree to submit a form [W-9, W-8BEN, W-8BEN-8] checkbox, then click Go to tax form.
  • Your company may not need to submit a tax form to receive commissions. If no tax form is required, click Finish.
  • If you do need to submit a tax form, HubSpot uses a third-party service called Dropbox Sign to process your submission. In the dialog box, click Get started.
  • Fill in the form. You can exit the form at any time. The tax form status should change to In Progress. To continue filling out the form, hover over the form and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Edit.
  • Once you’ve added all required information, click I agree.
  • You’ll be redirected to the document list in HubSpot. The bank form’s status will change to Pending approval. When the form is accepted, its status will change to Approved.
  • To download the completed document, hover over the form and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select View.
  • If the tax form is rejected, you’ll be notified via email or will see the status changed to Rejected.
    • To learn more about the reason for the rejection, hover over the status in the documents list.
    • To redo the submission, hover over the rejected form and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Start again.
  • If your company’s tax circumstances change, click Reconfigure tax form in the upper right. You’ll be redirected to the setup process to re-determine the required tax form.

Track partner goals with the Mutual Action Plan

With a Mutual Action Plan (MAP), you as a Solutions Partner can collaborate with your Partner Development Manager to set annual goals and establish targets for deals created, deals won, and monthly recurring revenue.

It’s recommended to set goals at the beginning of each year, then collaborate with your Partner Development Manager to review them quarterly.

Please note: MAP goals are intended for program alignment and performance tracking only. Achievement of these goals does not guarantee any particular business outcome or level of success for partners, and HubSpot accepts no liability in that regard. HubSpot does not warrant the completeness or accuracy of any MAP data, metrics, or reports, and partners are solely responsible for their own business decisions and outcomes.

Set annual goals

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Mutual Action Plan.
  • In the Set your partner goals section, click Set goals for the year.
  • In the Company goals section, enter the goals you want to achieve this year:
    • Organizational goals: goals for your company, such as “sell the business in the next 12 months.”
    • Revenue goals: goals related to generating revenue that help you work toward your organizational goal, such as “increase revenue by 20% in the next 12 months.”
    • People goals: goals related to hiring or growth, such as “hire a new sales rep in the next 6 months.”
    • Market goals: goals related to interacting with the market, such as “expand into a new vertical or market.”
    • HubSpot partnership goals: goals related to working with HubSpot, such as “Get to platinum in the next 3 months.”
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • Review your performance from the previous year, then enter goals for each month in each of the following areas:
    • Sourced deals created: deals you create that will generate revenue directly.
    • Sourced deals closed won: deals you create that have been closed and generate revenue directly.
    • Sourced deal MRR: monthly recurring revenue from your deals.
    • Assisted deal MRR: monthly recurring revenue from deals where you assisted HubSpot.
  • To apply a uniform growth % to your goals, click the Apply growth percentage dropdown menu and select a percentage from 5% to 30%.
  • In the bottom right, click Save and exit.

Your goals will be shared with your Partner Development Manager and can be changed during quarterly reviews.

Review progress

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Mutual Action Plan.
  • In the HubSpot goals, you can review your progress toward each goal you set. Each goal will display the following for each month and for the year:
    • Current performance (e.g. you closed five sourced deals in January.)
    • Target goal (e.g. you set a goal to close six sourced deals in January.)
    • Percentage to goal (e.g. you got 83% of the way to your sourced deals goal in January.)
  • By default, performance will be displayed monthly. To view quarterly performance, click Quarterly at the top of the page.
  • In the Data highlights section, review reporting on your performance, such as average selling price and inflight deals.

Create action tasks

You can work with your Partner Development Manager to create action tasks that will help you achieve your goals. Any action tasks created will be visible by your Partner Development Manager.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Mutual Action Plan.
  • In the Go to market section, click the Create task dropdown menu, then click Create open task. You can also select a default task instead.
  • In the right panel, enter a name for the task in the Task Title field.
  • If you have already completed the task, click the check icon to mark it as complete.
  • Click the Task type dropdown menu and select Call, Email, or To-Do.
  • Click the Priority dropdown menu and select a priority for how important the task is.
  • Click the Assigned to dropdown menu and select either your user or your Partner Development Manager.
  • Click the Due date dropdown menu and select a date. To select a different date, click the Due date dropdown menu and select Custom Date, then select a date in the date picker.
  • In the Due date section, click the second dropdown menu and select the time the task will be due.
  • Click the Reminder dropdown menu and select the time the reminder will be sent. To set a custom reminder time:
    • Click the Reminder dropdown menu and select Custom date.
    • In the date picker, select a date.
    • In the Reminder section, click the second dropdown menu and select the time the reminder will be sent.
  • In the Task Notes field, enter any notes with context or additional information about the task.
  • Click Create.

Set up quarterly reviews

You and your Partner Development Manager should set aside time to do the following every quarter:

  • Review your performance against the goals you’ve set.
  • Update future goals, if adjustments are needed.
  • Document any changes to your strategy or the areas where you’re focusing your effort.
  • Update progress of existing action tasks, then create new action tasks.

Update your partner employee email domain

As a HubSpot Solutions Partner, your partner employee email domain allows HubSpot to identify your employees that are active on your customers’ accounts.

Having a unique partner employee email domain that matches your employees’ email domain ensures the following:

  • Your partner account is attributed with managed tier points earned from providing services to your customers.
  • Your employees can access free Partner Seats to work in your customers’ HubSpot accounts.
  • Your employees are assigned accurate partner permissions for working in your customers’ HubSpot accounts.

This feature is available to all HubSpot Solutions Partners, regardless of the tier.

If you have users working in your customers’ HubSpot accounts with different email domains from your own (for example, external contractors), use the Client Access Manager to assign them to your customers’ accounts.

The domain must be unique and cannot be a shared email domain, such as gmail.com. If your employees are using a shared email domain, use the Client Access Manager to assign them to your client’s account. You will also need to add a unique domain to the partner employee email domain setting to prevent further notifications from being sent.

Update partner employee email domains

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to update partner employee email domains.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar, navigate to Partners > Automation.
  • In the Partner employee email domain field, enter your email domain.

If you have multiple employee email domains, enter the email domain for majority of the employees working in your customer accounts.

Use Partner Clients

Partner Clients is a HubSpot CRM object that makes it easier for HubSpot Solutions Partners and HubSpot employees to work together to drive product activation and retention for customers.

You can also use the Partner Client API to integrate Partner Client records with other external applications such as Asana Clickup. Learn more about using the Partner Clients API.

Permissions required View permissions for the Partner Client object are required to access Partner Clients.

Review Partner Clients

To review your Partner Clients:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to CRM > Partner Clients.
  • In the table, review your Partner Client records.

For customer data privacy protection, when reviewing individual Partner Client records, the Partner Client properties displayed and the available property groups will vary based on the Solution Partner’s relationship with each client.

Manage Partner Client records

The Partner Clients object is like other HubSpot CRM objects such as contacts and companies. With this object, you can do the following:

  • Edit the Partner Client record.
  • Associate the record to other object records like companies.
  • View and filter records for segmentation purposes. For example, you could create a view or segment that shows your relationship type with each client and the amount of associated Sold MRR . Learn more about filtering records and creating segments.
  • Create custom object properties.
  • Use Partner Client properties in workflows. For example, you could create a workflow that will send a notification to the record owner based on the Managed relationship estimated expiration date property.
  • Create custom reports. For example, create a report showing the number of services set to expire in the next 90 days. Learn how to create custom single object reports and how to use the custom report builder.
  • Customize client record layout (Super Admin or Customize record page layout permissions required).

Client record cards

The information on the Partner Client record can help you ensure your clients are getting the most out of HubSpot. The available cards for clients you are directly managing include:

  • Credits & Capacity: usage against limits for features like seats, contacts, and marketing emails, as well as credit usage.
  • Partner Tier Points Records: points received for managing this client.
  • Unified Usage Score: how much value the client is currently getting from HubSpot. Learn more about the Unified Usage Score on the HubSpot Academy.

Please note: you must be logged into your partner account to view partner-specific HubSpot Academy content.

View and manage your partner dashboard

As a HubSpot Partner, you can use the partner dashboard to view and manage your clients, understand your partner tier, and reach the HubSpot team that supports you as a partner.

Permissions required Partner dashboard permissions for partner tools are required to access the partner dashboard.

Review the Partner Center dashboard

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Partner > Dashboard. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Partner > Dashboard directly.
  • In the Program Progress section, you can review the following:
    • Tier information, including your current credited tier and your current tier performance.
    • Your total points, the total points needed to reach the next tier, your total twelve month source dollar amount, your rolling twelve month sourced MRR $ amount, and your 12 month average C$R (customer dollar retention.
  • In the Tier Progression section, review your current performance towards the next tier. To change your tier goal, click the Get to dropdown menu and select a tier. You can review the following metrics:
    • Total points: the total overall points required to reach the selected next tier.
    • Sourced minimums: the sourced minimums required to reach the selected next tier.
    • Managed minimums: the managed minimums required to reach the next tier.
  • In the Tier Point Changes section, understand how your points are changing in certain date ranges and the different Partner Clients associated with these changes.
    • To filter your data by date, click the Date range dropdown menu and select a range.
    • To review a report about each metric, click the number of new sold points, lost sold points, new managed points, or lost managed points. In the dialog box, you can do the following:
      • To create a segment of clients, click Use in segments. In the dialog box, select Create a new segment or Add to an existing static segment. Then, click Submit.
      • To export the report data, click Export unsummarized data. Enter a name for your export, and select a file format. Then, click Export.
      • To save the data as a new report, click Save as report. In the right panel, configure your report details and click Save or Save & add.
  • In the Shared Selling section, track trends in your sales pipeline within specific date ranges and review deal information in your Shared Selling pipeline.
    • Click the Date range dropdown menu and select a range for your data.
    • To review a report about each metric, click the number of HubSpot deals created, sourced inflight deals, or closed won HubSpot deals. In the dialog box, you can do the following:
      • To create a segment of clients, click Use in segments. In the dialog box, select Create a new segment or Add to an existing static segment. Then, click Submit.
      • To export the report data, click Export unsummarized data. Enter a name for your export, and select a file format. Then, click Export.
      • To save the data as a new report, click Save as report. In the right panel, configure your report details and click Save or Save & add.
  • In the Commission section, review past and future commission payments. Learn more about reviewing commission payments.
  • In the Upcoming HubSpot Renewals section, you can review key information for clients with upcoming renewals. To view a client’s record, click the client name in the Client column.

Review your partner tier points

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Tier.
  • At the top of the dashboard, view your solutions partner tier.
  • In the Tier Performance section, view your current partner tier performance and how the current number of sold points and managed points add up to the credited tier. Sold points are earned by selling to new or existing customers and managed points are earned by servicing your existing customers.
    • The tier progress chart shows a breakdown of your Sold and Managed points, along with your progress for each track. The chart includes a line indicator along with the number of points required to move to the next tier.
  • The Tier Insights section shows your partner tier progress based on your current points, along with the minimum points required to maintain your tier and the points needed to move up to the next tier.
  • The Account Performance section shows your median tool usage and whether or not you’re Partner Certified. To qualify for a partner tier, you must have a valid Solutions Partner Certification.
  • To view your combined sold and managed points by client, click the Points Breakdown tab, then view the Points Breakdown table.
    • Click the Deal type dropdown menu to filter clients by their deal type.
    • Click the Market type dropdown menu to filter clients by their market type.
    • Click a client to view more details about the client, including a breakdown of the sold and managed history, sold sales history and active managed points, and which points are active or expired.
  • You can also view how your points have changed over the months with the Progress Over Time chart.

Preview sold and managed points with the points calculator

Using the points calculator tool on your partner dashboard, you can estimate how many sold and managed points you can earn from different subscription levels.

To use the points calculator:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Partner > Tier.
  • In the right sidebar, click the firstlet left arrow icon to reveal the points calculator.
  • In the points calculator tool, enter the following details:
    • Sold amount: based on the selected Client currency, enter the amount you would like to convert to points.
    • Client market: select the country that the client is located in. Clients in growth markets will result in point multipliers.
    • Client currency: select the client’s currency.
    • Will you also manage this client?: select whether you’ll be managing the client.
    • How many other partners will manage this client?: if you’ll be managing the client, enter how many other partners will be managing them. Managed points will be split among the specified number of partners.
  • Below the fields, view the estimated Total points, Sold points, and Managed points.
  • To convert points to and from different currencies, click the Currency tab, then enter the following details:
    • Conversion method: select whether you’d like to convert points to currency, or currency to points.
    • Client market: select the country that the client is located in. Clients in growth markets will result in point multipliers.
    • Client currency: select the client’s currency.
    • Sold points: if you’re converting points to currency, enter the number of sold points to convert to currency.
    • Managed points: if you’re converting points to currency, enter the number of managed points to convert to currency.
    • Sold value: if you’re converting currency to points, enter the amount of sold value to convert to points.
    • Managed value: if you’re converting currency to points, enter the amount of managed value to convert to points.

View and reach your HubSpot Team

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Partner > Dashboard. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Partner > Dashboard directly.
  • Click the HubSpot Team tab. Your HubSpot Partner Development Manager (PDM) will be listed along with a brief description of how they help you.
  • Click Send email to send your PDM an email with your queries from your default email client.

View contacts in HubSpot’s default partner segments

As a HubSpot Partner, you can consult default partner segments to gain insight into the overall status of your registered leads.

Permissions required View permissions for segments are required to view default partner segments.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.

  • In the search bar, enter HubSpot Partner.

  • The following HubSpot Partner segments will be displayed:

    • HubSpot Partner – Expired: contacts that have expired and are no longer registered.

    • HubSpot Partner – Invalid Data: contacts that cannot be registered because they are missing required contact information for registration. This can include: First name, Last name, Website URL, Email, and Company.

    • HubSpot Partner – Pending Registration: contacts that you have requested to register but have not yet been processed by HubSpot.

    • HubSpot Partner – Registered: contacts that have been processed in HubSpot’s sales database and are owned by your company until the listed expiration date.

    • HubSpot Partner – Unavailable: contacts that cannot be registered under your company as they are being pursued by HubSpot or have already been registered by HubSpot or another HubSpot Partner.

View default partner registration properties

As a HubSpot Solutions Partner, your account has five default partner registration contact properties that track important information about registered leads.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Properties.
  • Click the Select an object dropdown menu and select Contact properties.
  • Click to expand the Partner Registration Information section and review the following properties:

    • Expiration Date: date your claim on this contact expires.

    • Registered Domain: domain associated with this contact.

    • Registration Action: action to perform on this contact, which will be performed on the next sync with the HubSpot sales database.

    • Registration Message: more details on why a contact was not registered during the sync to the HubSpot sales database.

    • Registration Status: status of this contact as of the last sync with the HubSpot sales database.

Miscellaneous

Import memories to Breeze Assistant

Import memories from AI assistants that allow memory export such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini to Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s conversational AI assistant. This allows you to copy over contextual data so you spend less time explaining your preferences to Breeze Assistant.

Learn more about how Breeze Assistant uses your HubSpot account context.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand requirements

  • To use Breeze Assistant, you must turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.

Import memories from another AI assistant

  • In the top navigation bar, click Breeze Assistant.
  • In the upper left, click the Breeze dropdown menu. Then, hover over More and select Memories.
  • Click Import.
  • In the Copy this prompt text field, click Copy.
  • In a new tab, navigate to your desired external AI assistant, then paste the copied prompt.
  • Copy the output from the external AI assistant.
  • In the Breeze Assistant tab, in the Paste the result text field, enter the external AI assistant’s output.
  • Click Import memories. A new Breeze Assistant chat will open with the data from the Paste the result text field so the imported memories are saved.

Imported memories will apply to all future Breeze Assistant conversations.

Set up markets

Establish markets to define and discover what companies are the best fit for your business, using key company attributes like industry, company location, number of employees, and more.

You can utilize markets in buyer and research intent to segment for high-fit companies that are visiting high-intent pages on your website and researching topics that align with what your business sells. You can also utilize markets in target accounts to identify what existing company records you’d like to assign as target accounts, or what net-new companies you’d like to add to HubSpot as target accounts.

Please note: when you define a market, HubSpot searches within our own database to find companies that meet your criteria, and then determines which of those records already exist in your CRM and which can be added as net-new company records.

Add a market

When adding a market, a company must meet at least one criteria in all selected categories to be added as part of that market. For example, if the target Industries has been set to Accounting or Energy, and the target Company country has been set to France, the market will include specifically accounting companies in France or energy companies in France.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar. In the left sidebar menu, under Data Management, click Markets.
  • On the Markets screen, click Create new market.
  • In the right panel, write the name of the market. Then, click Add next to the category you’d like to use to define your market. Then, configure the following target categories:
    • Industries: the industry these companies belong to, such as Accounting or Manufacturing.
    • Company keywords: use keywords with industries to narrow your market to specific companies within industries. Company tags can also be used to identify companies that match specific keywords or terms, such as B2C, healthcare, or more.
    • Employee range: the range of employees in each of your target companies.
    • Company country: the country that these companies are based in.
    • Company state/province/region: the state, province, or region that these companies are based in.
    • Company city: the city that these companies are based in.
    • Web technologies: the technologies currently used by these companies internally and for their websites.
    • Revenue: the revenue for each of your target companies.
  • To manage your market criteria:
    • To add another criteria within each category, click the dropdown menu and select or enter another criteria.
    • To remove a criteria within a category, click the X icon next to the criteria.
    • To remove a category, click Remove.
  • To exclude specific criteria:
    • In the category section, click + Add [category] to exclude.
    • Click the dropdown menu and select your criteria.
    • To remove an exclusion criteria within a category, click the X icon next to the criteria.
  • After setting up your market, at the bottom, click Create market.

Manage markets

Users have a limit of 20 markets. Once 20 are created, you must delete an existing one to make a new one. HubSpot protects against deleting markets that are used in existing buyer intent saved views.

  • To edit an existing market:
    • Hover over a market you want to edit, then click Edit.
    • In the right panel, edit the market’s details.
    • At the bottom, click Save market.
  • To rename your market:
    • Hover over a market you want to rename, then click Edit.
    • Under Market name, type the market name.
    • Click Save market.
  • To clone your market:

    • Hover over a market you want to clone, then click Edit.

    • In the right panel, at the bottom, click More and select Clone market. A clone market will appear in the market table. By default, it will be named [market name] (Copy). To rename the market, see above.

  • To delete an existing market:

    • Hover over a market you want to delete, then click Edit.

    • In the right panel, at the bottom, click More and select Delete market.

    • In the dialog box, click Delete.

  • You can view your total addressable markets on the Markets screen in settings or the Configuration tab in Buyer Intent. If a specific company appears in more than one target market, the company will only be counted once. As a result, the total count of companies may be lower than expected.

    • On the Markets screen, it will display the message: HubSpot has identified [x] companies that fit into the saved markets you’ve defined. Of that total, approximately [x]% are in your CRM.

    • On the Configuration tab in Buyer Intent, it will display the message: We’ve identified [x] companies in your TAM.
